At his memorial service, the Dallas Symphony Orchestra played the second movement of Beethoven's Third Symphony. After the service, I visited his home. His daughter sought me out specially and told me: "Dad always thought very highly of you, did you know that?" In 1980, my standing at TI had already begun its irreversible decline. Hearing those words from this beautiful young woman, though a thousand emotions surged within me, I could only keep them in my heart.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Brief conversations as assessment—简短谈话评估法，指通过简短的、非正式的对话来评估一个人的理解深度和思路清晰度；这是一种高效的人才评估技巧，也是高层管理者最常用的「快筛」工具。
Irreversible decline—无可挽救地下滑，指地位或处境已经恶化到无法逆转的地步；在职业叙事中，「下滑」往往比「失败」更难书写——因为它不是一次性的事件，而是一个缓慢的过程。
Recognition of my worth—知遇之恩，指上级对下属的赏识和提拔；在中国传统文化中，「知遇」是一种需要用忠诚和表现来回报的道德债务。
修辞赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

「爸爸一直非常重视你，你知道吗？」——这是张忠谋自传中最为温柔的一句话。在海格底的追思仪式上，他的女儿对已经「无可挽救地下滑」的张忠谋说出了这句迟到多年的认可。张忠谋写道：「虽然万千感慨，也只好留在心里。」这种克制——把万千感慨留在心里而不是写在纸上——是他作为传记作者最特出的品质。他不煽情、不渲染、不利用读者的情感。他只是把一个珍贵的瞬间呈现给读者，然后让它自己发光。 "Dad always thought very highly of you, did you know that?" — This is the gentlest line in Chang's autobiography. At Haggerty's memorial, his daughter spoke these words of overdue recognition to Chang, whose standing at TI was already in irreversible decline. Chang writes: "Though a thousand emotions surged within me, I could only keep them in my heart." This restraint — keeping the surge of emotion in the heart rather than on the page — is what most distinguishes Chang as a biographical writer. He does not sentimentalize, does not dramatize, does not exploit the reader's emotions. He simply presents a precious moment and lets it shine on its own.

德仪篇·第五章｜四个上司

海格底退休时选择夏伯特为他的继承董事长。事后看来，这是海格底一生稀有的败笔。但当时（一九七六年）看来，却是当然的事。夏伯特在二十五岁加入德仪（一九四八年）后就追随海格底。当海格底把全公司赌在半导体业上时（一九五二年），夏伯特主管半导体部。夏伯特与海格底一同把德仪推上半导体霸主宝座。此后，夏伯特的事业一帆风顺，升到执行副总裁兼营运长，再 CEO；到一九七六年，继承海格底的董事长职位已是水到渠成。

夏伯特正直、直爽、相当聪明，但也有大缺点：他刚愎自用，有了成见后就不再听别人的意见。在一九七二年他决定进入「消费者产品」（计算机、电子表、教育玩具、家庭电脑等）后，虽然几年内就开始亏本，几位董事及他的下属（包括我）开始劝他退出，但他仍坚持下去，一直撑到几乎拖垮整个公司。

还有，他与半导体技术脱节。当公司渐渐庞大，领导高层的内务、外务逐渐增加，但大半与技术无关。为了「日理万机」，自己倒与快速进步的技术脱节了。以夏伯特为例：五〇年代他是半导体行家；六〇年代提升为主管全公司业务的执行副总，开始与半导体逐渐脱节；到了七〇年代，他已成半导体外行——更可悲的是，他自己还不知道已脱节，仍以为七〇年代的半导体业与二十年前一样。

ReadShift 双语翻译

When Haggerty retired, he selected Shepherd as his successor as Chairman. In hindsight, this was one of the rare misjudgments of Haggerty's career. But at the time (1976), it seemed the natural choice. Shepherd had joined TI at twenty-five (1948) and had followed Haggerty ever since. When Haggerty bet the entire company on semiconductors (1952), Shepherd ran the semiconductor division. Shepherd and Haggerty together had propelled TI to semiconductor dominance. After that, Shepherd's career had risen steadily — Executive VP and COO, then CEO. By 1976, succeeding Haggerty as Chairman was the natural culmination.

Shepherd was upright, straightforward, and quite intelligent. But he had a major flaw: he was rigidly self-opinionated. Once he had formed a view, he would no longer listen to others' input. In 1972, he decided to enter "consumer products" (calculators, electronic watches, educational toys, home computers, and so on). Although losses materialized within a few years, and several board members along with his subordinates (myself included) urged him to exit, he persisted — carrying on until it nearly bankrupted the entire company.

Moreover, he grew disconnected from semiconductor technology. As the company expanded, the internals and external obligations of senior leadership multiplied — most of them unrelated to technology. In order to "manage a thousand things a day," he lost touch with fast-advancing technology. Take Shepherd as an example: in the 1950s, he was a semiconductor expert. In the 1960s, promoted to Executive VP overseeing all company operations, he began to gradually lose touch with semiconductors. By the 1970s, he had become a semiconductor layman — and more tragically, he himself did not know he had lost touch, still believing that the semiconductor industry of the 1970s was the same as it had been twenty years earlier.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Rigidly self-opinionated—刚愎自用，指一旦形成观点就拒绝接受反馈；在组织行为学中，这种特质在创始人或长期任职的 CEO 中尤为常见，且与「企业衰退」高度相关。
Consumer products misadventure—消费者产品歧途，指B2B企业盲目进入B2C市场的战略错误；在德仪的案例中，这不仅消耗了资源，更使公司从核心业务中失焦。
Disconnected from technology—与技术脱节，指管理者因行政事务而失去对技术前沿的感知；在科技驱动型产业中，「技术脱节」是管理者最危险的能力退化。
修辞赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

「更可悲的是，他自己还不知道已脱节，仍以为七〇年代的半导体业与二十年前一样。」——张忠谋用这句冷静的判断，提出了一个管理学中最为致命的现象：「无意识的无能」（unconscious incompetence）。夏伯特不是故意忽视技术——他是真心以为自己还懂技术。这种「不知道自己不知道」的状态，比「知道自己不知道」危险得多。因为它消除了学习的原动力。张忠谋对夏伯特的这段分析，不仅是对一个人、更是对所有「在位太久、脱节太久」的管理者的深刻警示。 "And more tragically, he himself did not know he had lost touch." — With this calm judgment, Chang identifies one of the deadliest phenomena in management: "unconscious incompetence." Shepherd was not deliberately ignoring technology — he genuinely believed he still understood it. This state of "not knowing that you don't know" is far more dangerous than "knowing that you don't know," because it removes the motivation to learn. Chang's analysis of Shepherd is not merely about one man — it is a profound warning to all managers who have "stayed too long and disconnected too deeply."

背景知识延伸 · Beyond the Text

一九七〇年代德仪半导体的两个技术挑战：张忠谋指出，七〇年代德仪半导体面临两个最大技术挑战：如何追上（日本及美国）竞争者的 MOS 记忆体，以及如何追上英特尔的微处理器。这两个挑战都是技术问题。当张忠谋与这两个技术问题时，夏伯特始终不了解他的需要——他不但不给资源，反而为公司设立了新焦点（消费者产品），把公司的资源都给了新焦点。张忠谋总结道：「德仪自此失焦迷途。」这五个字浓缩了德仪从半导体霸主走向衰退的核心原因。

第五章小结：四个上司、两种遗产

张忠谋在德仪的二十年间，经历了四种截然不同的管理风格。吕斯的「非正式、一对一、建设性」让他学会了信任和沟通；彪希的「正式、集体会议、书面报告」让他学会了如何在层级中保持效率；海格底的「远见和勇气」让他看到了最高管理者应该如何押注未来；夏伯特的「刚愎自用」则让他警惕：一个管理者如何在权力中失去学习的能力。

对张忠谋而言，这四个上司带来的最大遗产不是知识，而是一种「镜鉴」——他从每个人身上都看到了自己想成为和不想成为的样子。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Over twenty years at TI, Chang experienced four distinct management styles. Lewis's "informal, one-on-one, constructive" taught him trust and communication. Shep's "formal, group-based, written" taught him how to maintain efficiency in a hierarchy. Haggerty's "vision and courage" showed him how top leaders should bet on the future. Shepherd's "rigid self-opinion" warned him how managers can lose the ability to learn amid power.

The greatest legacy of these four bosses was not knowledge, but a mirror — from each person, Chang saw both what he wanted to become and what he did not.

德仪篇·第五章｜四个上司

一九七〇年代德仪半导体部的两个最大技术挑战是：如何追上（日本及美国）竞争者的 MOS 记忆体，以及如何追上英特尔的微处理器。这两个挑战都是技术问题。当我在与这两个技术问题挣扎时，夏伯特始终不了解我的需要。他不但不给我资源，反而为公司设立了新焦点——消费者产品（计算机、电子表、家庭电脑等）——把公司的资源都给了新焦点。德仪自此失焦迷途。

除了这两个缺点外，夏伯特还有一个迷思：他认为一个好的经理人可以经营任何行业。在一九七二年，虽然德仪没有任何拥有消费者产品经验的经理人，夏伯特认为别的行业的经理人也可以成功经营消费者产品事业。

ReadShift 双语翻译

The two greatest technical challenges facing TI's semiconductor division in the 1970s were: how to catch up with competitors' (both Japanese and American) MOS memory, and how to catch up with Intel's microprocessors. Both were technical problems. As I struggled with these two challenges, Shepherd never understood my needs. Not only did he deny me resources, he established a new corporate focus — consumer products (calculators, electronic watches, home computers, and so on) — and diverted corporate resources to this new focus. From that point on, TI lost its way.

Beyond these two flaws, Shepherd had another myth: he believed a good manager could run any industry. In 1972, even though TI had zero managers with consumer product experience, Shepherd believed managers from other industries could successfully run a consumer products business.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Lost its way—失焦迷途，指企业因战略摇摆而失去了原有的核心竞争优势；在商业叙事中，「失焦」往往比「失败」更常见也更危险——因为它意味着企业在「做很多事」中逐渐忘记了「什么事最重要」。
Good manager can run any industry—好经理人可以经营任何行业，这是一种「管理普世主义」的迷思；在张忠谋看来，这种信念忽视了行业专业知识的壁垒——尤其是在技术驱动型产业中，「通用型管理者」往往不如「行业专家型管理者」。
MOS memory vs. Microprocessor—MOS 记忆体 vs. 微处理器，一九七〇年代半导体产业最核心的两个战场；英特尔凭借在这两个领域的领先奠定了「矽谷之王」的地位，而德仪因「失焦」失去了这个机会窗口。

第五章小结

张忠谋在德仪的二十年间经历了四位上司，每一位都在他身上留下了印记。他从吕斯学会了「非正式沟通」；从彪希学会了「如何在层级中生存」；从海格底学会了「远见与勇气」；从夏伯特学会了「刚愎自用」的危险。这四种遗产，构成了张忠谋日后管理台积电的「隐性基因」——他此后在台积电的管理风格，既包含吕斯的亲和力、彪希的组织力、海格底的远见，也刻意规避了夏伯特的刚愎自用。

一个伟大的管理者，不是天生的，而是从他的上司——无论是好是坏——身上「选择性地继承」的结果。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Over twenty years at TI, Chang had four bosses, each leaving a mark. From Lewis, he learned informal communication. From Shep, he learned how to survive in a hierarchy. From Haggerty, he learned vision and courage. From Shepherd, he learned the danger of rigid self-opinion. These four legacies became the "hidden DNA" of Chang's management of TSMC — his later style incorporated Lewis's warmth, Shep's organizational discipline, Haggerty's farsightedness, and deliberately steered clear of Shepherd's inflexibility.

A great manager is not born — he is the result of "selective inheritance" from his bosses, both good and bad.

章节

德儀篇第六章

张忠谋

德仪篇·第六章｜实现「美国梦」

集成电路的发展，先自「双极」集成电路开始，再从「双极」走到「MOS」。我在一九六六年秋接管「集成电路部」时，正值「双极」集成电路盛世——市场上的集成电路几乎全是「双极」，「MOS」集成电路还在实验室内，而德仪的「MOS」研发也不在我辖下。但是，虽然「双极」集成电路市场成长神速，德仪的「双极」集成电路业务却萎靡不振。

我被赋予的使命就是要重振德仪威风。

我第一发现的是：我的前任史厥特（已在第四章介绍）在他任内最后一年深受压力——一部分是他上司道森给他的，另一部分是他好强性格自我产生——已把这压力放大后全部转移到他的属下身上。在我接任时，他的属下（现在变成我的属下）已到「民不聊生」地步。我立刻放松压迫，与属下单位个别讨论并设定每一单位合理的目标。这个举动，在几星期内就见效——士气提升了！

我在十一月接任，十二月底圣诞节前后，我上司吕斯就满脸笑容来看我，说他刚与几位同事（我的属下）谈话，他们都带着已半年看不到的笑容。吕斯问我：「你施了什么魔术？」

ReadShift 双语翻译

The development of integrated circuits began with "bipolar" ICs, then progressed from "bipolar" to "MOS." When I took over the Integrated Circuit Division in the fall of 1966, bipolar ICs were at their zenith. Nearly all ICs on the market were bipolar; MOS ICs were still confined to the laboratory, and TI's MOS R&D was not under my jurisdiction. But although the bipolar IC market was growing at breakneck speed, TI's bipolar IC business was languishing.

The mission given to me was to restore TI's prestige.

The first thing I discovered was that my predecessor Strat (introduced in Chapter 4) had been under immense pressure in his final year — partly from his boss Dawson, partly self-generated by his competitive nature — had amplified that pressure and passed it all down to his subordinates. By the time I took over, his subordinates (now mine) had reached a state of utter despondency. I immediately eased the pressure and met with each department individually to set reasonable targets. This move showed results within weeks — morale improved!

I took over in November. Around Christmas at the end of December, my boss Lewis came to see me with a big smile. He said he had just spoken with several of my team members — all carrying smiles unseen for half a year. Lewis asked me: "What magic did you perform?"

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Restore TI's prestige—重振企业威风，指在业绩低迷后重建市场信心和竞争地位；在组织行为学中，「重振」通常从「提升士气」开始——因为士气是绩效的先导指标。
Utter despondency—民不聊生，指团队士气极度低落、丧失希望的状态；在管理失败的前任遗产中，这种情绪创伤往往比业绩下滑更难修复。
Reasonable targets—合理目标，指既有挑战性又可达成的绩效指标；在目标管理理论中，「合理目标」是恢复团队信心的第一步——它让员工重新体验「赢」的感觉。
修辞赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

「你施了什么魔术？」——吕斯的这句玩笑话，是自传中罕见的喜剧时刻。张忠谋没有用什么魔术，他只是做了一件最简单也最难的事：停止压迫、设定合理目标、让团队重新体验成功的滋味。这种「去魔法化」的管理叙事，正是张忠谋自传中最为珍贵的特质——他从不把自己的成功归因于天才或运气，而是归因于一些任何人都可以做到、但很少有人真正做到的基本动作。 "What magic did you perform?" — Lewis's playful question is a rare comic moment in the autobiography. Chang used no magic. He simply did the simplest and hardest thing: stop the pressure, set reasonable targets, let the team experience success again. This "de-magicked" management narrative is among the most precious qualities of Chang's autobiography — he never attributes his success to genius or luck, but to basic moves that anyone can do but few actually do.

背景知识延伸 · Beyond the Text

MSI策略与台积电的前兆：张忠谋在自传中做了一个精彩的「历史对照」：「明眼读者读至此，也许可以依稀看到二十年前台积电的前兆。」他把德仪的MSI策略（做竞争少的高价值产品、开发能充分利用产品价值的客户）与台积电的「专业晶圆代工」策略进行了类比——两者的核心逻辑完全相同：「没有什么竞争，但是我们要开发客户，如果能找可以充分利用我们价值的客户，我们应该可以开出利润较高的价格。」这种跨越二十年的战略一致性，在台积电一九八七年成立时得到了完整的验证。

德仪篇·第六章｜实现「美国梦」

我的双极集成电路策略（一）

当然，光是提振部下士气，不足以重振德仪集成电路威风。就如我在第三章〈总经理的学习〉里所说，一个好的领袖一定要有人跟，而且要带领他的团队赢。提振士气表示我的团队开始跟我。怎么赢？这就是策略了。

我的策略的第一部分是「技术」。当时简单的集成电路只合几个晶体管，这类集成电路在市场上已是「标准式商品」，竞争激烈，价格及利润均低。但是德仪颇有技术实力，可以做得出一百多个晶体管的集成电路——我们称此类集成电路为「中程整合」（Medium Scale Integration）或 MSI。此类集成电路没有什么竞争，但是我们必须开发客户。如果能找到可以充分利用 MSI 价值的客户，我们应该可以开出利润较高的价格。

明眼读者读至此，也许可以依稀看到二十年前台积电的前兆。把上段最后几句换几个名词，变成：「专业晶圆代工没有什么竞争，但是我们要开发客户，如果能找到可以充分利用台积电价值的客户，我们应该可以开出利润较高的价格。」——这就是台积电成立时的策略。

ReadShift 双语翻译

My bipolar IC strategy (1)

Of course, boosting morale alone was not enough to restore the prestige of TI's IC business. As I said in Chapter 3 "A General Manager's Learning," a good leader must have people follow him — and must lead his team to win. Boosting morale meant my team was beginning to follow me. How to win? That was strategy.

The first part of my strategy was "technology." At that time, simple ICs contained only a few transistors. These were already "standard commodities" in the market — fierce competition, low prices and margins. But TI had the technical capability to produce ICs with over a hundred transistors — what we called "Medium Scale Integration," or MSI. This segment had little competition, but we had to develop customers. If we could find customers who could fully exploit the value of MSI, we should be able to command higher-margin prices.

Astute readers may already glimpse the foreshadowing of TSMC, twenty years later. Replace a few terms in the last sentences above: "Pure-play foundry had little competition, but we had to develop customers. If we could find customers who could fully exploit TSMC's value, we should be able to command higher-margin prices." — That was TSMC's founding strategy.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Medium Scale Integration (MSI)—中程整合，指集成电路按整合度划分的一个等级（一百至一千个晶体管）；在六〇年代末期，MSI 是德仪通过「高技术差异化」获得高利润的关键产品线。
Standard commodity—标准商品，指多家供应商都能生产的通用产品；在半导体产业中，标准商品化意味着价格战和毛利率下滑——唯一的出路是向更高阶产品迁移。
Foreshadowing of TSMC—台积电的前兆，指德仪时期的策略逻辑与二十年后台积电的商业模式的镜像关系；张忠谋是自传的「先知」——他在德仪的一举一动，都在为未来的创业埋下伏笔。
修辞赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

「明眼读者读至此，也许可以依稀看到二十年前台积电的前兆。」——这句话是张忠谋自传中最为精彩的「元叙事」瞬间之一。他打破了时间与自传的边界，直接从德仪的MSI策略跳到台积电的专业晶圆代工策略。这个「跳跃」不仅是叙事技巧，更是张忠谋对自身生涯「内在逻辑一致性」的自信宣示：他在一九六七年做的事，和他在一九八七年做的事，本质上是同一件事——找到高价值、低竞争的市场定位。 "Astute readers may already glimpse the foreshadowing of TSMC, twenty years later." — This is one of the most brilliant "metanarrative" moments in Chang's autobiography. He breaks the temporal boundary, leaping directly from TI's MSI strategy to TSMC's pure-play foundry strategy. This "leap" is not merely a narrative flourish but a confident declaration of the "internal logical consistency" of his career: what he did in 1967 and what he did in 1987 were, at their core, the same act — finding a high-value, low-competition market position.

背景知识延伸 · Beyond the Text

设计明星的凋零：张忠谋在自传中讲了一个令人伤感的故事：在MSI发展过程中，有两位「设计明星」——是一对兄弟。他们在一九六六至一九七二年获得了大量晋升和加薪。但几年后 MOS 发展远快于双极体。当张忠谋苦于寻找MOS设计人才时，得到的回答是：「这两位不会设计MOS。」二十几年后张忠谋重访德仪，发现他们早已默默无闻。张忠谋的评论只有五个字：「过时真是所有工程师最可怕的敌人。」

德仪篇·第六章｜实现「美国梦」

我的双极集成电路策略（二）

扩张高技术产品（MSI）是我策略的一部分，另一部分是减低的成本。在一九六〇年代后期，集成电路良率大约在二〇%之下。这样低良率的确有不少改善空间。升高良率更是降低生产成本最有效的办法。但在我接管后的一年半内（一九六六年秋至一九六八年夏），良率进步很少。

一九六八年夏——大灾难发生！良率忽然从一五%至一七%掉到一〇%。这时正值景气不错，客户需求很高，但我们交不出货。客户的压力，先是对我，再延伸到对彪希，再延伸到对夏伯特，甚至延伸到对海格底——大家都慌张了。一〇%低良率持续一个多月。在这一个多月中我每天早上开技术会议，有时彪希也来参加，但他可说完全不懂半导体技术，所以在我们会议中「加忙」远过于「帮忙」。

一个多月、成千成万「工程师人时」后，终于找到低良率的主因——在几十个制程步骤中，有一步做错了。找到原因后，立刻把这制程步骤复原。良率很快回到一五%至一七%，大家都松了一口气。

ReadShift 双语翻译

My bipolar IC strategy (2)

Expanding high-technology products (MSI) was part of my strategy; another part was reducing production costs. In the late 1960s, IC yields were below 20%. Such low yields certainly left plenty of room for improvement. Raising yields was the most effective way to reduce production costs. But in the year and a half after I took over (fall 1966 to summer 1968), yield improvement was minimal.

In the summer of 1968 — disaster struck! Yields suddenly collapsed from 15-17% down to 10%. The economy was booming and customer demand was high, but we could not deliver. Customer pressure flowed first to me, then up to Shep, then up to Shepherd, and even up to Haggerty — everyone was in a panic. The 10% yield persisted for over a month. During that month, I convened technical meetings every morning. Shep sometimes attended, but he understood virtually nothing about semiconductor technology, so his presence was more of a hindrance than a help.

After a month and thousands of engineer-hours, we finally identified the root cause — one step out of dozens of process steps had been done incorrectly. Once found, we immediately restored that process step to its pre-disaster configuration. Yields quickly recovered to 15-17%, and everyone breathed a sigh of relief.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Yield collapse—良率崩溃，指半导体生产中的良品率突然大幅下降；在半导体制造中，良率每下降一个百分点的损失都可以用「每天数十万美元」来衡量。
Root cause analysis—根本原因分析，指通过系统化方法找到质量问题源头；在本张忠谋的叙事中，「几十步制程中一步做错了」是半导体制造中经典的「single-point failure」模式。
Hindrance vs. help—加忙 vs. 帮忙，指因缺乏专业知识而给团队造成额外负担而非支持；在组织管理中，「不懂装懂的上级参与技术讨论」是降低决策效率的常见原因。
修辞赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

「彪希也来参加，但他可说完全不懂半导体技术，所以在我们会议中『加忙』远过于『帮忙』。」——张忠谋用「加忙」和「帮忙」这种口语化的对比，不动声色地描绘了一个技术盲上级参与技术会议的尴尬场景。他既不批评彪希也不为他辩护，只是忠实地记录了这种「外行参与内行会议」带来的效率损失。这种克制的幽默是张忠谋自传中难得一见的轻松笔触。 "Shep sometimes attended, but he understood virtually nothing about semiconductor technology, so his presence was more of a hindrance than a help." — Chang uses the colloquial contrast of "hindrance" versus "help" to quietly depict the awkward scene of a technically illiterate superior sitting in on a technical meeting. He neither criticizes Shep nor defends him, but faithfully records the efficiency loss from "laypeople participating in expert discussions." This restrained humor is a rare light touch in Chang's autobiography.

背景知识延伸 · Beyond the Text

一个危机、两个英雄：一九六八年的「良率之灾」直接、间接地产生了两个英雄：直接英雄是工厂总工程师布鲁克（Brook），他发现错误制程而把它矫正。十年后他获得德仪副总裁头衔，再离开德仪成为快捷半导体（Fairchild）的 CEO，一九九一年被张忠谋聘为台积电总经理。间接英雄是史坦（Alfred Stein）——张忠谋在休斯顿建新晶圆厂让他当家，与达拉斯老厂竞争。一年多后新厂良率在四〇%以上，超出达拉斯厂一倍。史坦后来也成为德仪副总裁，再成为另一家半导体公司 CEO——这家公司后来成为台积电的重要客户。张忠谋总结道：「有竞争才有进步，这是商场的真理。」

德仪篇·第六章｜实现「美国梦」

我的双极集成电路策略（三）

我在第三章〈总经理的学习〉说过，半导体产品可分为两类：「标准式商品」和「客制品」。「标准式商品」卖给许多客户，竞争者也多，利润往往不高。「客制品」只为客户而製，规格往往由客户定，竞争者少或没有，利润通常较高。

我任「锗」、「矽」部总经理时就有过许多「客制品」。集成电路部当然也竭力争取「客制品」。在六〇年代后期及七〇年代早期，德仪「集成电路部」有三个大「客制品」客户——两个是我争取的。

其中之一是 IBM。当年 IBM 在资讯界的地位，比今日苹果在消费者的地位还高。我争取到的客製品每年销售金额也在几千万美元之谱，利润也不错。我尤其记得，一九七〇年集成电路市场萧条，但这个「客制品」的需求没有大波动，为我们一九七〇年的业绩增色不少。

另一个原来就有的大客户是国防商北美航空（North American Aviation）。我们的「客制品」为国防部所用，非常重视品质及可靠度。

第三个「客制品」客户是拍立得相机公司（Polaroid）——也是我争取到。我们的「客制品」专为拍立得最先进的相机 SX70 设计。在数码相机还相当遥远的七〇年代，拍立得「即刻洗出照片」的技术深受社会大众欢迎，新的 SX70 尤有重要创新。为这个「客制品」计画，我多次去波士顿拍立得总部与他们协商，深深感受到拍立得全体员工对 SX70 的兴奋和期待，也借此机会认识拍立得董事长兰德（Edwin Land）——一位当代的科技怪杰。

这几个「客制品」都为德仪带来不少营收和高于「标准式商品」的获利率。更重要的，它们赋予德仪同仁一种特别使命感——因为这几个「客制品」的终端产品——IBM 的新电脑、北美航空的导弹、拍立得的 SX70——都是当时社会闻名的产品。每次在报纸杂志看到这些产品的报导，我们「与有荣焉」！

ReadShift 双语翻译

My bipolar IC strategy (3)

As I discussed in Chapter 3, semiconductor products fall into two categories: "standard commodities" and "custom products." Standard commodities were sold to many customers with numerous competitors, often yielding thin margins. Custom products were made for specific customers, with specs usually defined by the customer, fewer or no competitors, and typically higher margins.

As GM of the Germanium and Silicon divisions, I had managed many custom products. The IC division certainly pursued them aggressively. In the late 1960s and early 1970s, TI's IC Division had three major custom-product customers — two of which I had won myself.

One was IBM. IBM's position in the information industry then was analogous to Apple's in consumer electronics today. The custom product I had won generated tens of millions of dollars annually in revenue with healthy margins. I especially remember that during the IC market recession of 1970, demand for this custom product barely wavered — it bolstered our 1970 results considerably.

Another, pre-existing major customer was North American Aviation, a defense contractor. Our custom products went into Defense Department systems, where quality and reliability were paramount.

The third custom-product customer was Polaroid, which I also won. Our custom product was designed specifically for Polaroid's most advanced camera, the SX70. In the 1970s, when digital cameras were still a distant prospect, Polaroid's "instant photo" technology was enormously popular with the public, and the new SX70 represented a significant innovation. For this project, I traveled repeatedly to Polaroid's Boston headquarters to negotiate. I felt firsthand the excitement and anticipation that pervaded Polaroid for the SX70, and had the opportunity to meet Polaroid's chairman, Edwin Land — a technological wunderkind of his era.

These custom products brought TI substantial revenue and margins well above standard commodities. More importantly, they gave TI employees a special sense of mission — because the end products — IBM's new computers, North American Aviation's missiles, Polaroid's SX70 — were all celebrated products in their day. Every time we read about them in a newspaper or magazine, we felt a shared pride!

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Custom product mission—客製品使命感，指员工因参与知名终端产品而产生的归属感和荣誉感；在 B2B 企业中，这种「使命感」是比薪酬更有效的留任因素。
Edwin Land (兰德)—Edwin Land（一九〇九—一九七一），拍立得公司创始人，即时成像技术的发明者；他是乔布斯之前矽谷最受崇拜的「科技怪杰」之一——兼具科学家、发明家和企业家三重身份。
Shared pride—与有荣焉，指因参与而闻名产品而产生的间接荣誉感；在组织行为学中，这种「间接荣誉」是企业文化的重要组成部分——它让员工觉得自己的工作「有意义」。
修辞赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

「每次在报纸杂志看到这些产品的报导，我们『与有荣焉』！」——张忠谋用一句古语，精准地捕捉了 B2B 企业员工最珍贵的情感资产：间接荣誉感。德仪的员工不是终端消费者直接看到的品牌，但他们知道 IBM 的电脑里有他们的芯片、拍立得的相机里有他们的电路。这种「藏在幕后的荣耀」，是 B2B 企业文化的核心价值一一它告诉员工：你不不需要做你需要做的事，你的产品使那些产品成为可能。 "Every time we read about them in a newspaper or magazine, we felt a shared pride!" — Chang uses a classical Chinese phrase to capture the most precious emotional asset of B2B employees: indirect pride. TI employees were not the brand that end consumers saw directly, but they knew their chips were inside IBM's computers and their circuits inside Polaroid's cameras. This "behind-the-scenes glory" is the core value of B2B corporate culture — it tells employees: you do not need to be visible; your product makes those products possible.

背景知识延伸 · Beyond the Text

定期减价策略（一九七二年）：张忠谋在第三章中提到与BCG的合作后，最具冲击力的应用是德仪在一九七二年公开宣布的双极集成电路「定期每季减价」政策。德仪在双极集成电路的市场占有率已领先所有竞争者，製造成本也是同业中最低。公开「定期减价」让竞争对手疲于奔命：「他们眼前与德仪竞争，已因为成本较高而疲于奔命，德仪的定期减价更使他们连将来都没有指望。他们唯一的出路是退出这个市场。」张忠谋保存了一份一九七四年《电子新闻》的报导，标题大意是「市场已供不应求，英理士·张仍宣布德仪继续定期减价」。照片中他一脸凶悍。

德仪篇·第六章｜实现「美国梦」

一九七〇年裁员——一九六〇年代，世界半导体市场快速成长，市场规模成长了二.三倍，平均年复合成长率一八%。一九六四年（我初任业务单位总经理的一年），世界半导体市场为十亿美元；到一九六九年，市场已成长到二十三亿美元。但一九七〇年市场仅有微幅成长（二%）。对习惯高速成长的半导体业，二%成长率是一个大灾难——因为这行业一直快速增添员工和产能，一旦成长停顿，立刻就有产能过剩、员工过多的问题。

一九七〇和七一年，大部分半导体公司都亏损，继而裁員。有些公司的裁员幅度高达全部员工的三〇%、四〇%。许多半导体公司的 CEO 都被撤换，许多副总级人员都被裁。基层员工被裁更是稀松平常的事。记得我在那时期有一次德仪董事会上，以「废立的皇帝（指被撤换的 CEO）、蒙羞的将军（指被裁的副总）、屠杀的兵士（指被裁员的基层人员）」为题，报告竞争者的状况——深为董事会欣赏。一位德仪共同创办人还要了一份複印本，说「要给他朋友看」。

ReadShift 双语翻译

The 1970 layoffs —

The 1960s saw the world semiconductor market grow rapidly — from $1 billion in 1964 (the year I first became a business unit GM) to $2.3 billion by 1969: a 2.3x increase at an 18% compound annual growth rate. But in 1970, the market grew only marginally (2%). For an industry accustomed to hypergrowth, 2% was a catastrophe — because the industry had been rapidly adding headcount and capacity. When growth stalled, overcapacity and overstaffing hit instantly.

In 1970 and 1971, most semiconductor companies lost money and laid off staff. Some firms cut as much as 30-40% of their workforce. Many CEOs were replaced; many vice presidents were let go. Front-line workers were laid off as a matter of course. I remember during that period, I once delivered a presentation to the TI board on competitor conditions under the title "Deposed emperors (the replaced CEOs), disgraced generals (the laid-off VPs), slaughtered soldiers (the laid-off rank-and-file)" — much appreciated by the board. A TI co-founder even asked for a copy to "show his friends."

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Stalled growth catastrophe—成长停滯灾难，指习惯高成长的产业在增速骤降时面临的系统性危机；在半导体产业中，「停滯」往往比「下滑」更危险——因为产能扩充的惯性仍在前行。
Deposed emperors, disgraced generals, slaughtered soldiers—废立的皇帝、蒙羞的将军、屠杀的兵士，张忠谋用三个递进的比喻来描写产业衰退期的裁员潮；这个生动的排比是他自传中罕见的文学笔触，也是管理层向董事会传递坏消息的一个经典修辞手法。
Moat erosion through layoffs—裁员导致的护城河侵蚀，指企业在衰退期流失关键人才而长期损害竞争力；在半导体产业中，「裁员容易、复职难」是一条铁律。
修辞赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

「废立的皇帝、蒙羞的将军、屠杀的兵士」——张忠谋用三个递进的比喻，把一场行业裁员潮写成了一幅史诗级的画面。这个排比不仅是修辞技巧，更是管理层向董事会传递「坏消息」的一种高超策略：用生动的比喻让听众产生共鸣，同时在笑声中减轻了信息的残酷性。张忠谋的叙述能力在这里达到了高峰——即便是最悲惨的产业衰退，也能被他讲成一个让人印象深刻且「深为董事会欣赏」的故事。 "Deposed emperors, disgraced generals, slaughtered soldiers." — Chang uses three ascending metaphors to render an industry-wide layoff wave as an epic panorama. The triadic structure is not merely rhetorical flourish but a sophisticated strategy for delivering "bad news" to the board: vivid metaphors evoke empathy while their theatricality cushions the information's brutality. Chang's narrative prowess peaks here — even the most tragic industry downturn can become a story the board finds "much appreciated."

背景知识延伸 · Beyond the Text

裁员标准的争议：虽然集成电路部门不需要裁员，但德仪其他部门（锗、矽等）面临严重人满为患。夏伯特和彪希决定：所有半导体部门一致裁员，幅度大约十分之一。张忠谋在裁员标准上采取了坚定立场——他反对以考绩为准（因为「每个上司打考绩标准都不一样」），坚持采用「年资」为标准（最后进来的最先被裁）。这个「年资标准」虽然在逻辑上最公平，但也产生了几个月前才被告知「公司很需要你」的新员工突然要走路的荒诞剧。张忠谋只把责任归给高阶经理人：「他们雇人太快！」

德仪篇·第六章｜实现「美国梦」

承接 MOS 新任命——一直到一九六〇年代后期，几乎所有的集成电路都是双极体，MOS 只是实验室的一个研究案。理论上，MOS 的密度可以较双极体高，但速度较双极体低，而且制造技术比双极体更不穩定。六〇年代的一般认知，MOS 在密度上的优点抵不过它在速度及制造技术上的缺点，所以一直到一九六〇年代晚期，MOS 都不被看好。

不看 MOS 的人士包括杰克·基比（Jack Kilby）——集成电路发明人，也是当时德仪半导体技术的「教主」。在德仪半导体技术研究中，基比有「一槌定案」的权威。在一九六〇年代中期及晚期，基比「一槌定案」的方向不是 MOS，而是另一个双极体方向——后来没有成功。基比是我认识的人中最富有想像力和创意者之一，但是在评估 MOS 潜力上面，他错了。

他低估 MOS 的潜力，使得德仪当时只有八名工程师的小团队从事 MOS 研发。而且这八个工程师相当苦闷——他们觉得公司不重视他们的工作，他们也不在我带领的士气高昂的集成电路部门，而是被冷落在研究单位里。

终于，他们的苦闷爆发了一九六八年，这八个工程师——德仪唯一的 MOS 团队——集体辞职！导火线是彪希要求他们搬到休斯顿去。实际原因是他们认为不受公司重视，更重要是——他们已在外面获得支持，要到外面自开公司了。

彪希很想留他们，但发现他们要自开公司后，雷霆大怒，勒令这八个工程师缴出公物、即日离开、不得再返回。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Assumption of the MOS portfolio —

Through the late 1960s, nearly all ICs were bipolar. MOS was merely a laboratory research project. In theory, MOS offered higher density than bipolar but at lower speed, and its manufacturing technology was more unstable. The conventional wisdom of the 1960s held that MOS's density advantage did not offset its disadvantages in speed and manufacturability. So through the late 1960s, MOS was not taken seriously.

Among the MOS skeptics was Jack Kilby — coinventor of the integrated circuit and the high priest of TI's semiconductor technology. In TI's semiconductor R&D, Kilby had the authority of "the final word." In the mid-to-late 1960s, Kilby's "final word" pointed to a different bipolar direction — one that ultimately failed. Kilby was among the most imaginative and creative people I have ever known. But in assessing MOS's potential, he was wrong.

His underestimation of MOS meant TI had only a tiny team of eight engineers working on MOS R&D. And these eight engineers were deeply frustrated — they felt the company did not value their work. They were not part of my high-morale IC division but were marginalized in a research unit.

Finally, their frustration erupted. In 1968, these eight engineers — TI's only MOS team — resigned en masse! The trigger was Shep's demand that them move to Houston. The real reason was that they felt unappreciated by the company, and more importantly — they had already secured support on the outside and were leaving to start their own company.

Shep wanted badly to keep them, but when he learned they were founding a company, he flew into a rage and ordered the eight engineers to turn in their company belongings, leave that same day, and never return.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Jack Kilby vs. MOS—杰克·基比（Jack Kilby，一九二三—二〇〇五），集成电路共同发明人，诺贝尔物理学奖得主；即使是基比这样的技术天才，也会因为「过度自信」而低估技术路线的潜力。这是所有技术驅動型公司必须警惕的「创始人盲区」。
Eight engineers → Mostek—八名工程师 → Mostek 公司，指集体离职后创立的公司；Mostek 后来成为 MOS 记忆体领域的重要竞争者，也是七〇年代德仪最头疼的对手之一。
"The final word" authority—一槌定案的权威，指技术组织中拥有最终决定权的人；在技术规范中，「final word」是必要的效率保障，但当权威者判断错误时，整个组织都会付出代价。
修辞赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

「基比是我认识的人中最富有想像力和创意者之一，但是在评估 MOS 潜力上面，他错了。」——张忠谋用「但是」这个转折词，完成了一次对诺贝尔奖得主的「公正审判」。他没有因为基比是集成电路的发明人就回避他的错误——他对基比的最高评价是：他是一个富有想像力的人，但在这个关键判断上错了。这种「对事不对人」的评价风格，在东方文化中极为罕见——因为我们对权威人物的评价往往是「非颂即斥」，而非「在肯定的前提下指出错误」。 "Kilby was among the most imaginative and creative people I have ever known. But in assessing MOS's potential, he was wrong." — Chang uses the conjunction "but" to deliver a "fair verdict" on a Nobel laureate. He does not shy away from Kilby's error because Kilby coinvented the IC. His highest praise of Kilby: a highly imaginative man who, on this particular judgment call, was wrong. This "issue-focused, not person-focused" evaluative style is rare in East Asian culture, where assessments of authority figures tend toward "either praise or condemnation" rather than "pointing out error within a context of respect."

背景知识延伸 · Beyond the Text

计算器 IC 与 MOS 归来：MOS 研发团队被驱逐后，德仪重建 MOS 研发，开始重视 MOS——不是因为对 MOS 技术有新的洞察，而是忽然有客户找上门来。客户要的不是旧 MOS 团队孜孜念念的记忆体，而是一个新花样：计算器 IC。七〇年代初期，计算器刚刚问世，零售价在一百美元以上——实际成本只有二三十美元。许多商人成立计算机公司，急着要买计算器用 IC。德仪新的 MOS 团队乐意应付计算器 IC 生意——因为设计制造都比记忆体简单。一九七一年，MOS 归张忠谋管辖。他接手的 MOS 团队扩充到二三十名工程师，处在得意洋洋的状态中。但张忠谋知道：严峻的挑戰即将来临，得意洋洋的笑容也即将关闭。

德仪篇·第六章｜实现「美国梦」

集团副总裁暨半导体——一九七二年五月的一个上午，我应召到彪希办公室。「好消息，」彪希说——接着他就告诉我：公司要我接他的职位，负责全球半导体业务。我的头衔是「集团副总裁」（Group Vice President）。他又说：「这是在公司董事长、总裁和我以下最重要的职位。海格底、夏伯特和你都很有信心，希望你好自为之。」他做什么呢？他成为「执行副总裁」，管理德仪所有业务。

对我，这是一个大升级。我进入德仪后有过许多次小升级，但只有两次大升级。第一次是本书第二章所述的「工程师一跃为总经理」，这次是第二次。

在一九七二年，德仪的半导体集团是全球半导体业的领袖：市占率十几%，营收三亿美元左右（半导体业最高）；营业利润一八%左右（较大部分同业为优）；员工共四万人左右，分布全球。

那天是很高兴的一天。假使有任何隐忧，恐怕也只是 MOS 技术实力吧。计算器 IC 的成功掩饰了我们 MOS 其他的产品的弱点。在记忆体上，我们才从一九七一年接管 MOS 后重新开始努力；而我知道英特尔的「一一〇三」记忆体是市场的热门货，甚至我们「叛将」组成的 Mostek 也已推出新记忆体产品。在逻辑产品方面，英特尔已发明了微处理器，而我们根本连影子都没有。

让我明天再想吧——今天且尽情庆祝。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Group VP of Worldwide Semiconductors —

One morning in May 1972, I was summoned to Shep's office. "Good news," Shep said — and then he told me: the company wanted me to take over his position, running worldwide semiconductor operations. My title would be "Group Vice President." He added: "This is the most important position below the Chairman, the President, and myself. Haggerty, Shepherd, and I all have great confidence in you. We hope you will do your best." What did Shep do? He became "Executive Vice President," overseeing all of TI's businesses.

For me, this was a major promotion. I had received many smaller promotions since joining TI, but only two major ones. The first was the "Engineer Leaps to General Manager" described in Chapter 2; this was the second.

In 1972, TI's Semiconductor Group was the global leader in semiconductors: market share in the mid-teens, revenues of roughly $300 million (the highest in the industry), operating margins of approximately 18% (superior to most peers), and approximately 40,000 employees worldwide.

It was a happy day. If there any lingering worry, it was perhaps MOS technological capability. The success of calculator ICs masked the weakness of our other MOS products. In memory, we had only restarted our efforts in 1971 after taking over MOS, and I knew that Intel's "1103" memory was the market's hot product. Even the company our "traitorous defectors" had founded — Mostek — had already introduced new memory products. In logic, Intel had invented the microprocessor, and we didn't even have the faintest trace of one.

Let me worry about that tomorrow. Today, I celebrate.

Group Vice President (GVP)—集团副总裁，指管理一个跨多个 Divison 的业务集群的高级职位；一九七二年的德仪半导体集团是全球该行业的「最高职位」之一——掌管四万名员工、三亿美元营收。
Market share in the mid-teens—市占率十几个百分点，指在整体市场中占有十至十九个百分点的份额；在高度分散的半导体市场中，「十几%」已是绝对的领导地位。

修辞赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

「让我明天再想吧——今天且尽情庆祝。」——这句话在张忠谋自传中极为罕见——他几乎从不在自传中流露出「先享受、后烦恼」的态度。但这一天不同：四十一岁，从工程师到集团副总裁——掌管全球半导体业的领袖——他用了十六年走过了很多人一辈子都走不完的路。他有权庆祝，也有权暂时忘记那些隐忧。这种罕见的情感流露，让读者看到了张忠谋坚硬外壳下那个曾经年轻、充满梦想的工程师。 "Let me worry about that tomorrow. Today, I celebrate." — This line is almost unheard of in Chang's autobiography — he virtually never shows a "celebrate now, worry later" attitude. But this day was different: forty-one years old, from engineer to Group VP — steward of the world's leading semiconductor operation. He had covered in sixteen years what took most people a lifetime. He had the right to celebrate and the right to momentarily forget the worries. This rare emotional glimpse lets the reader see, beneath Chang's hardened exterior, the young, dream-filled engineer he once was.

背景知识延伸 · Beyond the Text

隐忧二则：张忠谋的两个隐忧——记忆体（英特尔 一一〇三）和微处理器（英特尔发明，德仪连影子都没有）——精准地预测了此后三十年半导体产业的竞争格局。英特尔将在这两个领域成为统治者，而德仪将因为对这两个领域的投入不足而逐渐失去领导地位。张忠谋在庆祝的当天就看到了问题的所在，但他无力改变一切——因为他刚刚接手 MOS，而 MOS 不是他此前二十年的专长。这种「预见问题却无法解决」的无力感，是高级管理者最痛苦的职业体验。

德仪篇·第六章｜实现「美国梦」

实现「美国梦」——「美国梦」这个名词，在我长住美国时（一九四九—一九九五年）相当普遍。我稍加研究后，发现这个名词大约来自十九世纪末、二十世纪初欧洲到美国的移民。他们到美国时贫穷、无畏惧、有希望的自由劳动者。他们的「美国梦」是要在美国至少做到中产階級——而实现「美国梦」的途径，往往是高等教育。

刚到美国时，我是一个穷外国学生——和美国的穷人一样，同有「美国梦」。「美国梦」的终点只是中产阶级的收入——那我在希凡尼亚开始工作时就已实现「美国梦」。但现在（一九七二年）更不一样了：以收入和财富言，我已在全美顶尖百分之一以内；以事业地位言，我掌管数万员工，是全球半导体业的领袖；以社会地位言，我和妻也在达拉斯上流社会内。

有了一点钱的一个好处，就是可以帮助父母亲。父母亲于一九五〇年到美国——起初父亲还到哥伦比亚大学商学院读了一个管理硕士，以为有了这个学位可以找到适宜的工作。但得到学位后求职的结果，只得到两个聘雇机会，薪水都很低。他决定不接受。一直到一九五五年在百老汇住家附近顶了一家礼物杂货小店。父母亲两人亲自打理——父亲整年应付外界，母亲整年招呼顾客。双亲已有疲态。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Realizing the "American Dream" —

The term "American Dream" was quite common throughout my long residence in the United States (1949–1995). After a little research, I found that the term likely originated with European immigrants to America at the turn of the twentieth century. They arrived poor, fearless, hopeful, free laborers. Their "American Dream" was to reach at least the middle class in America — and the path to achieving it was often higher education.

When I first arrived in America, I was a poor foreign student — like America's poor, I too had an "American Dream." If the endpoint of the "American Dream" was merely middle-class income, then I had already achieved mine when I started working at Sylvania. But by 1972, things were quite different: by income and wealth, I was in the top 1% of the nation; by professional status, I led tens of thousands of employees as the head of the global semiconductor industry; by social standing, my wife and I had entered Dallas high society.

p class="en-para">One benefit of having some money was the ability to help my parents. My parents came to America in 1950 — at first my father even enrolled at Columbia Business School for a master's in management, believing the degree would lead to a suitable job. But upon graduating, he received only two offers, both at low salaries. He declined them. Not until 1955 did he take over a gift and grocery shop near their Broadway home. My parents ran it themselves — my father managing external affairs year-round, my mother greeting customers year-round. Both were showing signs of weariness.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Top 1% income threshold—顶尖百分之一收入门槛，指进入全美收入最高的百分之一行列；一九七二年的门槛约在三万美元以上——对一位四十一岁的企业高管来说，这是「美国梦」最直观的答案。
MBA underemployment—硕士学位低聘，指高学位持有者因就业市场、年龄歧视或文化障碍而无法找到匹配学历的工作；张忠谋父亲的故事是移民家庭最为心酸的现实——知识和学位并不直接等于经济回报。
Social ladder through education—教育攀升社会阶梯，指通过高等教育实现阶层跃迁的「美国梦」经典路径；张忠谋在自传中承认自己的路线是这条——并且他在父母未能完成的路上走了更远。
修辞赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

张忠谋在自传中插入了一段关于父亲的心酸叙事：一位哥伦比亚大学商学院硕士，在美国求职只得到两个低薪聘雇机会，最后选择自己经营一家小店。这个细节是张忠谋自传中最为心碎的「隐藏叙事」——它不仅解释了张忠谋对教育的执着（因为他亲眼看见父亲的高学历如何被浪费），也解释了他对「机会」的珍视（因为他知道父亲不是不够优秀，只是没有机会）。父亲的不得志，是张忠谋这一代人「美国梦」叙事中最常见的副产品。 Chang inserts a poignant narrative about his father: a Columbia Business School master's who, job-hunting in America, received only two low-salary offers and ultimately chose to run a small shop. This is the crushed "hidden narrative" of the autobiography — it explains not only Chang's devotion to education (having witnessed a father's advanced degree go to waste) but also his cherishing of "opportunity" (knowing his father was not untalented, merely unlucky). A father's frustration was the most common byproduct of the "American Dream" narrative for Chang's generation.

父亲的天伦礼物

一九七一年，张忠谋首次拥有价值一百万美元德仪股票。他决定赠与父母十分之一——十万美元。在那样重重安全网下，父母决定退休。一九七二年他们出顶小店。「以后父亲过了九年、母亲过了二十几年健康、自由、舒适的生活——一直到父亲在一九八一年中风，母亲在二〇〇〇年代渐渐失记忆力。」张忠谋写道：「一九七二年是我人生的一个重要瞻前顾后点。我已实现了我的『美国梦』，前途看起来一片光明——下一步应该是德仪公司总裁的职位。」

ReadShift 双语翻译

In 1971, Chang first acquired $1 million in TI stock. He gave one-tenth — $100,000 — to his parents. With this and other safety nets, they retired. In 1972 they sold the shop. "Father enjoyed nine more years, and mother more than twenty years, of healthy, free, comfortable life — until Father had a stroke in 1981 and mother gradually lost her memory in the 2000s." Chang wrote: "1972 was an important looking-back-and-forward point in my life. I had realized my 'American Dream'; the road ahead looked bright — the next step should have been the presidency of TI."
