A few weeks later, my suspicion was answered. On an occasion with just the three of us (Shepherd, Shep, and me), Shepherd suddenly asked me: "Are you really working on 64K?"

This question horrified me. After my numerous reports to him about the 64K, after my repeated expressions of high expectations for this new product, after his personal visit to Houston to listen to the engineers discuss the project — he still asked: "Are you really working on it?"

Such a bewildered Chairman of the Board — my boss's boss — was there any hope for me?

Two unpleasant events brought 1977 to a close.

The first occurred in the fall, just as we were planning the following year's operating plan and capital expenditures. Shep suddenly said to me: "You must plan for $1 billion in revenue next year, with sufficient capital expenditure to support $1 billion in revenue."

A billion dollars in revenue would represent nearly 50% growth. The market wasn't growing that fast, and we didn't have enough new products to grow that fast either. I protested, but Shep completely ignored my protests. His simple command to me: "Do it."

The result? In January of the following year (1978), I requested a transfer. My successor took over production equipment sufficient to support $1 billion in revenue, but in 1978 achieved only $800 million — proving he had inherited a "mess." This "mess" was not of my making.

The second incident occurred in November. I had accepted an invitation from Ben Rosen, then the semiconductor industry's most prominent analyst, to attend his December semiconductor conference in New York. Rosen had been hosting this annual event since 1975. He invited only executives from the three semiconductor companies he considered most important (TI, Motorola, and Intel) as guests of honor, with an audience from Wall Street investment circles. I had attended in 1975 and 1976 and thoroughly enjoyed debating with Grove (who alternately represented Intel).

At the end of this dissonant and absurd year, I was still looking forward to this minimal pleasure. But even this minimal pleasure Shep was unwilling to grant me. In November, when he learned I was attending, he immediately canceled my plans. His reason: "You're too busy here to have time for this conference."

修辞赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

「你们真的在做64K吗？」——这句话的杀伤力不在于它的内容，而在于它的语境。张忠谋已经多次汇报、多次表达期望、甚至带夏伯特亲自去休士顿旁听——而董事长仍然问出这个问题。张忠谋用「惊骇莫名」四个字来形容自己的反应，这四个字背后是一个职业经理人对「外行领导内行」最深的恐惧：不是反对，不是质疑，而是根本不知道你在做什么。 "Are you really working on 64K?" — The devastating power of this question lies not in its content but in its context. Chang had reported repeatedly, expressed expectations repeatedly, and even brought Shepherd to Houston to listen in person — and the Chairman still asked this question. Chang uses "惊骇莫名" (horrified beyond description) to characterize his reaction. Behind these four words lies a professional manager's deepest fear of "the ignorant leading the knowledgeable": not opposition, not questioning, but a fundamental unawareness of what you are doing.

在一九七七年圣诞节至七八年新年的假期中，我检讨了我的工作处境：我在德仪已十九年半，头十七、八年可说是一帆风顺，最近两、三年我的业绩仍然亮丽，但是夏伯特和彪希，因为他们自己的错误决定——进入「消费者产品」事业——对我的态度已达到荒诞无理，甚至侮辱的程度。半导体总经理这个职务，我做不下去了。

也许连德仪都待不下去了？

但是当时我以为我无处可去。也许因为业界都以为德仪半导体集团总经理已是半导体业最高位置，我已好久没有收到同业的挖角邀请，我也从未收到当时还在萌芽期创业投资家的邀约。先辞职、再找，似乎是很大的风险。

一九七七年，我才四十六岁，退休还太早。

况且，我对德仪还抱了一丝希望；毕竟，德仪让我发出了我的光芒；也许，今日的逆境只是暂时的、短期的，也许，我在德仪还能东山再起。

七〇年代的德仪经营委员会（以总裁彪希为主席，大约三、四个集团总经理组成）习惯在新年假后立刻举行长达一星期的「排列」会议。「排列」会议的任务，是依绩效优劣次序排列前一百名德仪人，并且决定这一百人每人的奖金及股票认购权。

就在这「排列」会议会期中，有一天我在会后到处希办公室，自请调职。

During the Christmas-to-New-Year holiday of 1977–78, I reviewed my work situation: I had been at TI for nineteen and a half years. The first seventeen or eighteen had been smooth sailing. In the most recent two to three years, my performance had still been brilliant. But Shepherd and Shep, because of their own wrong decision — entering the "consumer products" business — had treated me with an attitude that reached the point of absurdity, unreason, even humiliation. The Semiconductor GM role — I could no longer do it.

Perhaps I could no longer stay at TI at all?

But at the time I believed I had nowhere to go. Perhaps because the industry viewed the TI Semiconductor Group GM as the highest position in the semiconductor industry, I had long stopped receiving poaching offers from competitors. I had never received invitations from venture capitalists, who were then still in their infancy. Quit first, then look — that seemed like enormous risk.

In 1977, I was only forty-six. Retirement was too early.

Moreover, I still held a glimmer of hope for TI. After all, TI had let me shine. Perhaps today's adversity was only temporary, short-term. Perhaps I could still make a comeback at TI.

In the 1970s, TI's Operating Committee (chaired by President Shep, composed of roughly three or four Group GMs) customarily held a week-long "Ranking" meeting immediately after the New Year holiday. The Ranking meeting's task was to rank the top one hundred TI people in order of performance, and to determine each of these one hundred people's bonuses and stock options.

During one of these Ranking meeting days, I went to Shep's office after the meeting and requested a transfer.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
"Ranking" meeting (「排列」会议)—指企业一年一度的绩效排名与薪酬决定会议；在通用电气等公司推行「活力曲线」（Vitality Curve）后，这种强制排名机制成为全球大企业通用的管理工具——它既是激励手段，也是组织达尔文主义的制度化体现。
Perceived highest position in the industry (业界认知的最高位置)—当整个行业都认为你已到达最高位置时，外部机会的认知信道就被关闭了——张忠谋已在德仪半导体做到顶，猎头不会来找他，创投也不会来找他。这个「无选择」的处境恰恰是他内心最大的困境。

听了我的要求，彪希面无表情，甚至没有问我为什么要自请调职。我想，他早已规划了过去半年对我的言语和态度，今天我的请求，只是他规划的结果而已。他唯一的回答是：让他考虑一下，而且要跟夏伯特谈谈。

ReadShift 双语翻译

[1] *The Man Behind the Microchip: Robert Noyce and the Invention of Silicon Valley* by Leslie Berlin (Oxford University Press, 2005), p.158.

一星期后，彪希的回答来了：准许我的请求。至于我的新职，我可在两个职位中选择一个：消费者产品集团总经理，或「公司成长」资深副总裁。

「公司成长」是一个幕僚职位，我不认为我适宜做幕僚，那么唯一的消费者产品集团总经理——这又是多么讽刺性的给予！

自从一九七二年后，我一直认为消费者产品集团是公司的「祸根」：第一，它分散了德仪对半导体的专注；第二，它变成半导体集团最大的「内部客户」及最大的负担，大大地削弱半导体集团对外发展的能力；第三，它的亏损倍增了夏伯特和彪希对半导体集团和对我的压力。

但是现在，夏伯特和彪希要我去经营这个「祸根」。

我在苦笑中同意了。我的德仪缘分还有五年多寿命。我几乎爬到德仪巅峰，现在我开始下山——「消费者产品」总经理是我的「下山驿站」。

Hearing my request, Shep was expressionless. He didn't even ask why I wanted a transfer. I think he had already planned the words and attitude toward me over the past six months; today's request was merely the result of his planning. His only response: let him consider it, and he needed to discuss it with Shepherd.

A week later, Shep's answer came: my request was granted. As for my new role, I could choose between two positions: Consumer Products Group GM, or Senior Vice President of "Corporate Growth."

"Corporate Growth" was a staff position. I didn't consider myself suited for staff work. So the only choice was Consumer Products Group GM — what an ironic offer!

Ever since 1972, I had considered the Consumer Products Group the company's "bane": first, it dispersed TI's focus on semiconductors; second, it became the Semiconductor Group's largest "internal customer" and greatest burden, severely weakening the Semiconductor Group's ability to develop externally; third, its losses multiplied the pressure Shepherd and Shep placed on the Semiconductor Group and on me.

But now, Shepherd and Shep wanted me to run this "bane."

I agreed with a bitter laugh. My TI fate had a little over five more years to live. I had nearly climbed to TI's peak; now I was starting my descent — "Consumer Products" GM was my "downhill station."

修辞赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

「我几乎爬到德仪巅峰，现在我开始下山——『消费者产品』总经理是我的『下山驿站』。」——这是张忠谋自传中最为苍凉的自喻之一。整部上册读到这里，读者已经跟着他经历了从麻省理工的艰难求职、德仪的破格提拔、半导体的黄金时代，到此刻的「下山」。「下山驿站」四个字，既是对现实的接受，也是对德仪黄金时代的最终告别。但历史的反讽在于：正是这个「下山」决定，让张忠谋彻底离开了半导体制造的最高战场——而十年后，他回到台湾，创办了台积电，重新定义了整个产业。 "I had nearly climbed to TI's peak; now I was starting my descent — 'Consumer Products' GM was my 'downhill station.'" This is one of the most elegiac self-metaphors in Chang's entire autobiography. By this point in Volume 1, the reader has followed him through the difficult job search at MIT, the unconventional promotion at TI, the golden age of semiconductors, and now — the "descent." These four words ("downhill station") represent both acceptance of reality and a final farewell to TI's golden age. The historical irony is that this "descent" decision led Chang to permanently leave the highest battlefield of semiconductor manufacturing — and ten years later, he returned to Taiwan and founded TSMC, redefining the entire industry.

第九章小结：奋斗与挣扎的六年

一九七二至一九七八年的六年，是张忠谋在德仪半导体集团总经理任内最艰苦的奋斗与挣扎。这六年中：

第一，英特尔以股票承购权和矽谷地理优势，在人才争夺上对德仪形成结构性压制。

第二，记忆体战役先胜后挫：4K大胜（市占率超50%），16K失败（被迫摹仿Mostek），64K雪耻（但成功来太晚）。

第三，波玛案和德仪进入消费者产品事业，让张忠谋从「半导体领袖」变成「内部客户优先」政策的执行者——他撕了彪希的电邮，但无法撕掉整个公司的战略转向。

第四，拉吧厂、自研设备、微处理器多头马车——每一项决策都是彪希和夏伯特以个人偏好或过时经验替代商业理性的结果。

最终，一九七七年冬，四十六岁的张忠谋自请调职，从半导体巅峰走向「消费者产品」这个他眼中的「祸根」。他以为这是「下山驿站」——但历史证明，这是一个时代的结束，和另一个时代的开始。

ReadShift 双语翻译

The six years from 1972 to 1978 were Chang's most arduous struggle as TI Semiconductor Group GM. During these six years: Intel structurally suppressed TI in talent recruitment through stock options and Silicon Valley geography. The memory battle saw victory then setback — 4K triumph (over 50% share), 16K failure (forced to copy Mostek), 64K redemption (but too late). The Bowmar case and TI's entry into consumer products transformed Chang from "semiconductor leader" into an enforcer of the "internal customer first" policy — he shredded Shep's email but couldn't shred the company's entire strategic pivot. The Lubbock fab, self-developed equipment, and the microprocessor multi-head horse — each decision was Shepherd and Shep substituting personal preference or outdated experience for business rationality. Finally, in the winter of 1977, the forty-six-year-old Chang requested a transfer, descending from the semiconductor peak toward the "bane" he had always despised. He thought it was a "downhill station" — but history would prove it the end of one era and the beginning of another.

章节

德儀篇第十章

张忠谋

德仪篇·第十章｜消费者的长征

仍抱一丝希望在德仪「东山再起」，我认真地开始消费者产品集团（以下简称消费者集团）总经理的工作。

在我开始做总经理时（一九七八年二月），消费者集团有三宗主要产品：（一）消费者计算机（简单加减乘除），这宗产品占集团营收最大，但平均价格已跌至十几美元，是亏损生意；（二）科学计算机营收不大，但售价甚高，只有惠普（Hewlett Packard, HP）一个竞争者，是集团中唯一赚钱的生意；（三）电子表，大部分是十几美元一只的廉价表，但也有很小一部分高价表（一百美元以上），整个电子表部门呈亏损状态。

除了这三宗现有产品，我们正在努力开发教育玩具和家庭电脑：从夏伯特到集团里的工程师，我们一致希望这两个新产品会赚钱，也会为德仪在消费者产品领域建立创新形象。

半导体的附加价值来自晶体管或集成电路的设计和制程创新和效率；消费者集团的附加价值来自满足消费者实际需要的系统设计，以及取悦消费者的工业设计。半导体集团的客户是装在他们系统里的系统公司（计算机公司、国防武器、其他电子设备公司等）；消费者集团的客户却是零售商（百货公司、电子产品连锁店等）。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Still clutching the faint hope of making a comeback at TI, I threw myself into the work of Consumer Products Group GM.

When I started as GM in February 1978, the Consumer Products Group had three main product lines: (1) Consumer calculators (simple arithmetic) — the largest revenue contributor but with average prices plummeting to around $10, a losing business; (2) Scientific calculators — modest revenue but high prices, with only HP as a competitor, the only profitable business in the group; (3) Electronic watches — mostly cheap watches at around $10, but also a small number of high-end watches ($100+), with the entire watch division in a loss position.

Beyond these three existing products, we were working hard to develop educational toys and home computers: from Shepherd to the engineers in the group, we all hoped these two new products would be profitable and establish TI's innovative image in consumer products.

Semiconductors added value through transistor or IC design and process innovation and efficiency. The Consumer Products Group added value through system design that met consumers' practical needs and industrial design that delighted them. The Semiconductor Group's customers were system companies (computer manufacturers, defense weapons, other electronics companies); the Consumer Products Group's customers were retailers (department stores, electronics chains).

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Three product lines with different economics (三条产品线、三种经济逻辑)—指同一集团内不同产品线的商业模式差异——消费性计算机是「营收大但亏损」、科学计算机是「营收小但赚钱」、电子表是「全面亏损」；这种组合在企业管理中叫「产品组合管理」（Product Portfolio Management），需要不同的资源配置逻辑。
Value chain positioning (附加价值来自不同环节)—半导体和消费者产品处于产业链的不同位置——前者以技术创新和制造效率为核心竞争力，后者以工业设计和渠道触达为核心竞争力。张忠谋清晰地认识到：他能做好前者，但后者的游戏规则完全不同。

消费者计算机

消费者计算机的问题是成本。在日本及台湾厂商激烈竞争下，德仪已毫无订价力，盈亏全靠成本。成本又分两类：元件（半导体和液晶显示器），及封装。元件都是德仪自己半导体集团供应的。供应消费者集团是我任半导体总经理时的大头痛，我也知道在这宗生意上半导体的利润很低，现在我易位而处，无颜也无立场要他们再让价。

封装成本呢？的确有机会。一九七八年我们已把大部分封装工作外包给日本东芝公司，但东芝既是竞争者，而且为我们封装的价格也不低。那么为什么不找一家更便宜的台湾厂商呢？

简单的答案是：德仪不够信任台湾厂商的品质。那时德仪台湾已封装测试集成电路近十年，也获得总部的信任，但那信任是老师（美国德仪）对徒弟（德仪台湾）的信任；在计算机封装上，美国德仪既无资格做任何厂商的老师，也不轻易信任任何代工商。但对日本厂商的一般品质相当佩服，所以就让东芝代工。

假使海格底没有在一九七六年退休，那么计算机的封装成本问题，恐怕在一九七八年就解决了。那一年，海格底（虽已从董事长职位退休，但仍为董事）受孙运璿院长、李国鼎政务委员之邀，来台湾访问一周。孙、李给了他「红地毯」待遇：每晚必宴，每演讲必满座；孙、李讨教不尽，而且请海格底组织「行政院科技顾问团」，每年来台湾开会一周。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Consumer Calculators

The consumer calculator problem was cost. With fierce competition from Japanese and Taiwanese manufacturers, TI had no pricing power at all — profit or loss depended entirely on cost. Costs broke down into two categories: components (semiconductors and LCD displays), and packaging. Components were all supplied by TI's own Semiconductor Group. Supplying the Consumer Products Group had been a major headache when I was Semiconductor GM, and I knew semiconductor margins on this business were razor-thin. Now that I had switched seats, I had neither the face nor the standing to ask them to lower prices further.

Packaging costs? There was indeed an opportunity. In 1978, we had already outsourced most packaging work to Japan's Toshiba, but Toshiba was both a competitor and their packaging prices weren't low. So why not find a cheaper Taiwanese manufacturer?

The simple answer: TI didn't trust Taiwanese manufacturers' quality enough. By then, TI Taiwan had been packaging and testing ICs for nearly a decade and had earned headquarters' trust — but that trust was a teacher's (American TI) trust in its apprentice (TI Taiwan). In calculator packaging, American TI had no qualification to be anyone's teacher, and was not inclined to trust any contract manufacturer lightly. But TI held Japanese manufacturers' general quality in high regard, so they let Toshiba do the contract work.

Had Haggerty not retired in 1976, the calculator packaging cost problem would likely have been resolved by 1978. That year, Haggerty (though retired from the Chairman role, still a Director) was invited by Premier Sun Yun-suan and Minister Lee Kuo-ting to visit Taiwan for a week. Sun and Lee gave him the "red-carpet" treatment: dinner every night, packed auditoriums for every lecture. They sought his counsel extensively and asked Haggerty to organize the "Executive Yuan Science and Technology Advisory Group," which would meet in Taiwan for one week each year.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Pricing power vs. cost control (订价力 vs. 成本控制)—在激烈竞争的市场中，企业失去「订价力」（pricing power）后，唯一的生存之道就是成本控制；德仪的消费者计算机业务正是这种「无订价力、只能拼成本」的典型处境。
Trust gradient in outsourcing (外包中的信任梯度)—指企业在选择代工商时的信任层级——「老师对徒弟的信任」>「对日本厂商的佩服」>「对台湾厂商的不够信任」；这种信任梯度直接决定了外包决策，即使成本差异明显。

海格底回达拉斯后约我到他家晚餐，对台湾的经济、科技发展称赞不绝。给他印象最深刻的，却是一家叫Cal-Comp的计算机公司，他对我说：「我们必须小心，别人已经追上来了。」数十年后，我发现CalComp就是金宝，也认识了许胜雄和林百里：许胜雄当年在金宝工作，现在已是金宝的老板；林百里当年也在金宝工作，后来创办广达。我对他们提起数十年前海格底的访问，他们的眼睛都睁大了，他们两位都记得海格底的访问，但不知道他们给了海格底那么美好的印象！

我在第六章曾提及，海格底相当反对德仪去低工资地区设厂，而认为基本解决方案是自动化。他原则上的反对，延迟了德仪集成电路海外封装测试厂的设立。现在，他对台湾及Cal-Comp称赞不绝，我想假使他还是董事长，他会赞成计算机部门去台湾封装，但他已退休，不做此类的指示或建议了。

科学计算机

这是消费者集团唯一赚钱的部门，营收不如消费者计算机，但利润不错；它也及时开发新的机种，持续增加科学计算机的功能，功能逐渐增加，市场也更普遍化。

这部门的成功，当然与部门总经理有关。他是彼得·邦菲（Peter Bonfield），英国籍，工程师出身，但已是优秀的企业经理人。在我消费者集团总经理任内（一九七八年二月至八〇年十二月），我在拉吧找了一个公寓，星期一至五住拉吧。在那时期中，我有时找邦菲和他太太吃饭，与他们结上了那时不知道、但后来变成很长时期的友谊。

二十几年后邦菲从英国大企业（英国电信公司, British Telecom）总裁位退休，而且已被英国女皇封为爵士，我又找上他了——和邀聘为台积电独立董事，并主持审计委员会，他也欣然接受。邦菲至今还是台积电董事会审计委员会主席。我和邦菲的友谊是我在德仪消费者集团短短任内的一个获得吧。

ReadShift 双语翻译

After returning to Dallas, Haggerty invited me to dinner at his home and praised Taiwan's economic and technological development profusely. What impressed him most, though, was a calculator company called Cal-Comp. He said to me: "We must be careful — others have caught up."

Decades later, I discovered that CalComp was actually Kingcomp (金宝), and I came to know Sheng-Shiong Hsu (许胜雄) and Barry Lam (林百里). Hsu had worked at Kingcomp and was now its owner. Lam had also worked at Kingcomp before founding Quanta. When I mentioned Haggerty's visit decades earlier, their eyes widened. Both remembered the visit but had no impression of the favorable image they had made!

I mentioned in Chapter 6 that Haggerty opposed TI building plants in low-wage regions, believing automation was the fundamental solution. His principled opposition delayed TI's establishment of overseas IC packaging and test facilities. Now, praising Taiwan and Cal-Comp profusely, I think had he still been Chairman, he would have approved the calculator division packaging in Taiwan. But he was retired and made no such directives or suggestions.

Scientific Calculators

This was the Consumer Products Group's only profitable division. Revenue was lower than consumer calculators, but margins were healthy. It timely developed new models and continuously expanded the scientific calculator's functionality; as features increased, the market broadened.

The division's success was, of course, tied to its division GM — Peter Bonfield, British, an engineer by training but already an outstanding business manager. During my tenure as Consumer Products GM (February 1978 to December 1980), I kept an apartment in Lubbock, staying there Monday through Friday. During that period, I sometimes invited Bonfield and his wife to dinner, forging a friendship whose longevity I didn't then realize.

Over twenty years later, Bonfield retired from his role as CEO of a major British corporation (British Telecom) and had been knighted by the Queen. I sought him out again and invited him to serve as an independent director of TSMC and chair the Audit Committee. He gladly accepted. Bonfield remains Chairman of TSMC's Audit Committee to this day. My friendship with Bonfield was one of the genuine rewards from my brief tenure at TI's Consumer Products Group.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
"Others have caught up" (别人已经追上来了)—海格底在一九七八年对台湾计算机产业的评语；在竞争分析中，「追上来」意味着技术差距的缩小和竞争格局的改写——这是企业对新兴市场竞争力最简洁也最准确的判断。
Long-term friendship from short tenure (短短任期中的长期人脉)—张忠谋在德仪消费者集团仅短短近三年，却结识了日后台积电董事会的重要成员（邦菲）；在职业发展中，「人脉复利」的表现之一就是——短期关系在几十年后以意想不到的方式变现。

机器人之旅

在我们正为计算机装配成本困扰、又不能决定是否继续外包东芝之时，忽然夏伯特引进一位「机器人专家」。此人来源我已记不清楚，花了约三年时间（正与我任消费者集团总经理时间重叠），他是德仪公司相当「红」的人。夏伯特让他成立了一个机器人开发组。公司高级主管包括我，几乎每月都被召去听他的进展报告。老实说，当时我认为他的研发进度距离真正应用在计算机或电子表的封装上，至少十年、二十年（事实上，四十年后的现在，还没有大规模的机器人封装），但夏伯特似乎认为机器人的应用已近在眉睫。

在这位专家报告时，我坐在第二排想打瞌睡。我最深的印象是，他常伸缩、弯曲他的左右手臂来模拟机器人。姿势倒很好。

电子表和巴黎行

德仪的电子表业务以高价（两百美元以上）的LED表开始，后来发现高价表需要「品牌」，而「德仪」品牌显然不足。再后来，德仪开发了低成本的液晶显示器（LCD），就开始进攻低价电子表市场。在我接任消费者集团时，大部分电子表营收已属低价电子表类，而低价电子表又有东南亚厂商的激烈竞争——德仪的整个电子表业务已在亏损状态。

高价表倒引起了董事会的兴趣。我发现，几乎每一位董事（都男性）都戴了一只名牌手表。董事会的兴趣集中在手表的图形设计上，他们要求：每一个新设计样本都要先让他们审视。结果，没有一个设计能让大家都喜欢。

多年戴中阶Seiko手表的我，一开始就被董事会认为是手表外行人，并没有与他们讨论的资格。讲到高价手表需要「品牌」，有一位拥有法国葡萄园的德仪董事，运用了他在时尚界的关系，替我去巴黎与皮尔·卡登（Pierre Cardin）见面。卡登的名字就是名牌，我见他的目的，就是奉董事会命要求他授权德仪把名字放在我们高价表上。

The Robot Venture

Just as we were mired in calculator assembly costs and couldn't decide whether to continue outsourcing to Toshiba, Shepherd suddenly brought in a "robotics expert." I can no longer remember this person's background. He spent about three years on this (overlapping precisely with my tenure as Consumer Products GM) and was a highly "famous" figure within TI. Shepherd had him set up a robotics development group. Senior executives, including me, were summoned nearly monthly to hear his progress reports. Frankly, I believed his R&D progress was at least ten to twenty years away from real application in calculator or watch packaging (in fact, forty years later, there is still no large-scale robotic packaging). But Shepherd seemed to think robotics application was imminent.

During this expert's presentations, I sat in the second row fighting sleep. My deepest impression was how he frequently stretched and bent his left and right arms to simulate a robot. The gestures were quite good.

Electronic Watches and the Paris Trip

TI's electronic watch business began with high-end (over $200) LED watches. Later, it was discovered that high-end watches required "brand," and the "TI" brand was clearly insufficient. Still later, TI developed low-cost LCD displays and began attacking the low-end electronic watch market. By the time I took over the Consumer Products Group, most watch revenue came from low-end electronic watches, and the low-end market saw fierce competition from Southeast Asian manufacturers — TI's entire watch business was already in a loss position.

The high-end watches, however, captured the Board's interest. I discovered that nearly every director (all male) wore a luxury brand watch. The Board's interest focused on the watch's graphic design. They demanded that every new design sample be submitted to them for review first. The result: no design pleased everyone.

Having worn a mid-range Seiko for many years, I was immediately dismissed by the Board as a watch outsider with no standing to participate in their discussions. When it came to luxury watches requiring "brand," one TI director who owned a French vineyard used his connections in the fashion world to arrange for me to meet Pierre Cardin in Paris. Cardin's name was the brand. My purpose in meeting him was, at the Board's behest, to request that he license his name for our high-end watches.

修辞赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

「姿势倒很好」——这是张忠谋式的冷幽默。在整段关于机器人专家冗长而无望的叙述中，他以这四个字做结。没有愤怒，没有批评，只有一个旁观者对一场荒诞剧的简短评语。这种「冷幽默」是张忠谋自传中反复出现的修辞策略：面对不合理的人事和决策，他不直接批评，而是以一个细节（伸缩手臂模拟机器人）让读者自行判断其荒谬。 "The gestures were quite good." This is classic Chang deadpan humor. After an entire passage about the robotics expert's interminable and hopeless presentations, he closes with these four words. No anger, no criticism — just a brief reviewer's note on an absurd performance. This "deadpan humor" is a recurring rhetorical device in Chang's autobiography: faced with unreasonable people and decisions, he doesn't criticize directly but offers a single detail (stretching arms to simulate a robot) and lets the reader draw their own conclusions about its absurdity.

我如期赴约，巴黎原是我喜爱的城市，但这次去，却有冷冷的感觉。我没有见到卡登，只见到了他的助理。我准备的德仪电子表品质、设计、技术资料，他一概没有兴趣。他唯一有兴趣的是权利金。我带了他的要求回拉吧。

我已不记得后来的细节，总之，德仪的名贵表一直没有成功。日本的低价表倒是维持了好几年。但是，访问皮尔·卡登的巴黎行，是我职业生涯中最接近「时尚界」的一点，特在此记。

「发音与拼字母」及其引起的「公司政治」

「发音与拼字母」（Speak and Spell，让我们简称它为S&S吧），是一个教育性玩具，对象是五至六岁儿童；这玩具会自动发一个字音，让儿童拼这个字的字母。如儿童拼对了，玩具会夸奖他（或她）；如儿童拼错了，玩具鼓励他再试。这一个玩具售价五十美元，虽稍嫌贵，但仍在中上阶级重视儿童教育家庭的负担能力内。事实上，在一九七八年秋德仪把此玩具引入市场后，它的销路相当好。

S&S在我任消费者集团总经理第一年推出，不但是我任内，甚至可以说是德仪消费者集团整个历史（约二十年）内推出最具创意的产品，大家应该高兴才是。但想不到的，因为S&S，公司政治（应该说：夏伯特与彪希的关系）却变得恶劣。

为什么呢？德仪进入消费者市场的决定（一九七二年），并非基于缜密策略考量，而只是一个机会性的决定。那时夏伯特知道他要继承海格底大位，彪希也知道他是「暂定」的夏伯特继承人（彪希比夏伯特年轻六岁），两人都想做些大事。恰巧德仪的计算机IC非常吃香，看起来计算机生意很容易做，他们就借这个机会进入了计算机市场；后来也因为同样的机会（德仪的电子表IC、LED和LCD），又进入了电子表市场。

ReadShift 双语翻译

I kept the appointment as planned. Paris had always been a city I loved, but this trip, I felt a chill. I never met Cardin — only his assistant. The TI watch quality, design, and technical materials I had prepared interested him not at all. The only thing that interested him was the royalty. I brought his demands back to Lubbock.

I no longer remember the details, but in any case, TI's luxury watches never succeeded. The low-end Japanese watches, however, sustained for several years. Still, the Paris trip to visit Pierre Cardin was the closest I ever came to the "fashion world" in my career — worth recording here.

"Speak and Spell" and the Company Politics It Provoked

Speak and Spell (let's call it S&S) was an educational toy for children aged five to six. The toy would automatically pronounce a word and ask the child to spell it letter by letter. If the child spelled it correctly, the toy would praise him (or her); if incorrect, the toy would encourage another try. Priced at $50, though slightly expensive, it was still within the reach of upper-middle-class families who valued children's education. In fact, when TI introduced it to the market in the fall of 1978, it sold quite well.

S&S launched in my first year as Consumer Products GM. It was not only the most innovative product launched during my tenure — it could be argued the most innovative product in the entire history (roughly twenty years) of TI's Consumer Products Group. Everyone should have been delighted. But unexpectedly, because of S&S, company politics (or rather: the relationship between Shepherd and Shep) deteriorated.

Why? TI's decision to enter consumer markets (1972) was not based on careful strategic analysis — it was purely opportunistic. Shepherd knew he would inherit Haggerty's throne; Shep also knew he was the "provisional" heir to Shepherd (Shep was six years younger). Both wanted to do great things. As it happened, TI's calculator ICs were highly sought after, and the calculator business looked easy to enter. They seized the opportunity and entered the calculator market. Later, seizing similar opportunities (TI's watch ICs, LED and LCD), they entered the watch market.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Opportunistic entry vs. strategic entry (机会性进入 vs. 策略性进入)—德仪进入消费者市场不是因为有一个缜密的产业分析，而是因为「计算机IC正热，看起来容易做」；在战略管理中，「机会性进入」和「策略性进入」的差距在于：前者看到的是短期利润窗口，后者看到的是长期竞争壁垒。
Royalty negotiation (权利金谈判)—皮尔·卡登的助理对德仪手表的品质和设计毫无兴趣，只关心权利金——这是品牌授权（licensing）交易的典型特徵：授权方关心的不是产品品质，而是品牌溢价能力和最低保证授权收入。

他们没有看到的，就是计算机和电子表的「人为障碍」不高。最重要的「人为障碍」就是计算机和电子表的IC，但德仪老早就公开销售此类IC给其他计算机和电子表的竞争者，何况别的IC公司也已销售同类IC。

但是现在，S&S导入了一个新局面——以「人为障碍」高！S&S的心脏是一组「语言合成」IC，这是一组甚具创意、设计难度高、竞争者不易复制的IC，也是德仪半导体集团开发出来的。只要德仪限制这组IC给自己用，S&S竞争者就不易入场了。

虽然S&S营收并不大（远低于消费者计算机），但它在市场上的创新形象似乎为郁问中的德仪指点了了一个新的方向——高科技消费品的创新。

彪希看到这点了，他本人也在郁问中。一九七五年，他升为总裁，但没有CEO头衔。夏伯特保留了CEO头衔和权力。现在，彪希想借S&S的成功，为德仪增添创新形象，同时也为自己增添领袖形象。

没有与夏伯特商量，彪希邀请美国《商业周刊》来德仪访问，不但自己与记者长谈，而且让记者访问好几位重要经理人，但并不包括夏伯特，也没包括我。结果是美国《商业周刊》一九七八年九月十八日的封面故事——封面是德仪的S&S，封面标题是〈德州仪器指导美国企业如何在一九八〇年代生存〉。

全篇报导长达十一页，主角是彪希。彪希阐述德仪的策略：德仪是高科技创新者，当然，如必要，我们也会运用我们强大的制造实力。同时被访问者也包括半导体集团的新人（这篇封面故事发生在自请调职后七个月，科技界对我记忆犹新，所以这封面故事也不忘对我放了一记马后炮）：「英理士·张有一个名誉：他用无懈可击的逻辑，摧毁下属的建议。他的下属不易与他沟通。」

ReadShift 双语翻译

What they hadn't foreseen was that the "man-made barriers" for calculators and watches were not high. The most important barrier was the calculator and watch ICs — but TI had long been openly selling these ICs to competing calculator and watch manufacturers, and other IC companies were selling similar ICs too.

But now, S&S introduced a new dynamic — the "man-made barrier" was high! The heart of S&S was a set of "speech synthesis" ICs — highly creative, difficult to design, hard for competitors to copy — also developed by TI's Semiconductor Group. As long as TI restricted these ICs to its own use, S&S competitors could not easily enter the market.

Though S&S revenue was modest (far below consumer calculators), its innovative image in the market seemed to point a new direction for the beleaguered TI — high-tech consumer product innovation.

Shep saw this. He himself was also frustrated. In 1975, he was promoted to President but without the CEO title. Shepherd retained the CEO title and authority. Now, Shep wanted to leverage S&S's success to enhance TI's innovative image — and simultaneously burnish his own leadership image.

Without consulting Shepherd, Shep invited Business Week to visit TI. He not only spoke with reporters at length but also arranged for them to interview several key managers — but not Shepherd, and not me. The result was Business Week's September 18, 1978 cover story — the cover featured TI's S&S, with the headline: "How Texas Instruments Tells America How to Survive the 1980s."

The full article ran eleven pages, with Shep as the protagonist. Shep articulated TI's strategy: TI is a high-tech innovator; of course, when necessary, we will also deploy our formidable manufacturing strength. Among those interviewed was also the new Semiconductor GM: this cover story came seven months after my self-initiated transfer. The tech world still remembered me, so the article also took a passing shot at me: "Morris Chang has a reputation: he uses impeccable logic to destroy his subordinates' suggestions. His subordinates don't find it easy to communicate with him."

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
"Man-made barrier" as competitive moat (人为竞争壁垒)—指企业通过限制关键技术外溢来构建的竞争壁垒；与「自然壁垒」（如规模经济、专利期）不同，「人为壁垒」是策略性的——S&S的语言合成IC不外售，使竞争者无法复制产品，正是这种壁垒的典型案例。
CEO vs. President: the split of titles (CEO与总裁头衔的分离)—夏伯特保留CEO而只让彪希当总裁，是权力保留的经典安排——CEO拥有最终决策权，President负责日常运营；这种「头衔分离」是过渡期常见的权力格局，但实际制造了权责不清的摩擦。

全篇报导稀少提到海格底和夏伯特，报导的讯息是：彪希在成功地主导德仪的高科技创新方向，同时也为别的美国企业树立未来如何生存的楷模。

当时我读了这报导后大为惊讶：第一，德仪当时士气低落、创意缺乏，人情形绝不如报导描述的那么好；第二，对德仪内部人来说，夏伯特仍是最高长官，公司的方向与策略还轮不到彪希来阐述；至于对我的马后炮，当然使我更为心冷一点。

几天后，在一个集会遇到海格底，他把我拉到一边，说那篇报导——海格底没有对我说的是：他和夏伯特都感觉到他们受了委屈。这个真相，要等彪希三十多年后在自传中暴露。在其自传中，彪希叙述：「我（在那篇文章内）有三张照片，他们（夏伯特和海格底）各只有一张。」看到报导后，海格底要他和夏伯特「谈谈」这事，但夏伯特拒绝与他谈。一直到二〇一〇年，两人都早已离开德仪，夏伯特也快要过世，他们才又提起这事。

两个强悍的德州佬！我可以想像他们心里不开心，但为了各自的地位，又僵硬地合作了七年；我也可以想像，两人各自的自尊和自大会因美国《商业周刊》的那篇封面故事而使两人的关系变质。

家庭电脑

我任半导体总经理时，就知道夏伯特和彪希要求消费者集团开发家庭电脑，也要求半导体集团遵照消费者集团的规格，开发并提供特定用途微处理器及其他集成电路。一旦我任消费者总经理，我也视家庭电脑为我需要开发的最重要新产品。

ReadShift 双语翻译

The article mentioned Haggerty and Shepherd only sparingly. The message was: Shep was successfully directing TI's high-tech innovation and simultaneously serving as a model for other American companies on how to survive the future.

When I read this article, I was astonished: first, TI's morale was low and creativity lacking — the internal reality was nothing like the article described. Second, to TI insiders, Shepherd was still the top executive; the company's direction and strategy were not yet Shep's to articulate. As for the passing shot at me, it certainly chilled me further.

A few days later, I ran into Haggerty at a gathering. He pulled me aside and said that article —

What Haggerty didn't tell me was: both he and Shepherd felt wronged. This truth wouldn't emerge until Shep revealed it in his autobiography over thirty years later. In his autobiography, Shep recounted: "I had three photos in that article; they (Shepherd and Haggerty) each had only one." After seeing the article, Haggerty asked Shep to "talk about it," but Shepherd refused to discuss it with him. It wasn't until 2010 — long after both had left TI, and when Shepherd was near death — that they brought it up again.

Two strong Texans! I could imagine their displeasure, but for the sake of their respective positions, they had stiffly cooperated for seven years. I could also imagine how each man's pride and ego, inflamed by that Business Week cover story, had poisoned their relationship.

Home Computers

During my time as Semiconductor GM, I knew that Shepherd and Shep wanted the Consumer Products Group to develop home computers, and they also wanted the Semiconductor Group to develop and supply dedicated microprocessors and other ICs to the Consumer Products Group's specifications. Once I became Consumer Products GM, too, I regarded the home computer as the most important new product I needed to develop.

修辞赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

「两个强悍的德州佬！」——张忠谋以一声叹息式的感叹句，为夏伯特和彪希之间长达七年的权力对峙做了总结。他没有用任何管理学术语（如「权力斗争」「代理冲突」），而是用了一个极其生动、带有地域文化色彩的称呼——「德州佬」。这个称呼既亲切又疏离，既理解又无奈。它让读者看到：即使在美国最顶尖的科技公司里，驱动高层行为的仍然是人的自尊、骄傲和地域性格。 "Two strong Texans!" — Chang concludes the seven-year power standoff between Shepherd and Shep with an exclamatory sigh. He uses no management jargon ("power struggle," "agency conflict") but instead a vivid, regionally inflected term — "Texas men." This epithet is simultaneously intimate and detached, understanding and resigned. It shows the reader: even in America's most elite technology companies, what drives senior behavior is still human pride, ego, and regional character.

实际上，家庭电脑只是夏伯特「到处都有计算」（Ubiquitous Computation）理念的一部分。夏伯特的理念中，家庭电脑用来算家庭帐、报个人所得税、教育儿童、储藏食谱等等；「商业电脑」放在办公室，用来做专业工作。

夏伯特的理念很有远见，但比现实世界至少早了十几年！在现实世界里，IBM在一九八一年推出「个人电脑」，把「个人电脑」正统化及普遍化，但八〇年代的「个人电脑」，还只是用在工作场合。一直到九〇年代，「个人电脑」才跑到家庭里去，而且也还是叫做「个人电脑」，并无「家庭电脑」之名。当然，到了二〇〇七年，苹果公司更革命性地推出iPhone，iPhone事实上是一个可以放在衬衫口袋里的电脑；现在（二〇一九年），我们真正在一个「到处都有计算」、「到处都有电脑」的时代，但是「现在」是七〇年代的四十年后！

为什么夏伯特与现实脱节？关键是集成电路的功能。集成电路的功能与成本在二十世纪一直遵守「摩尔定律」——每两年一个「摩尔世代」。一直到九〇年代中期，集成电路才足够低价，而低价集成电路的功能才足够驱动电脑的家庭应用。在一九七八年要求有用而又合理价格的家庭电脑，至少早了六、七个「摩尔世代」，也就是十二至十四年。

上章我描述夏伯特对64K记忆体的「茫然」——听了我们几小时后，他还问：「你们真的在做吗？」就是这对技术现实的茫然，加上他刚愎自用的性格，使他高估我们能开发出「家庭电脑」的应用。他要「家庭电脑」算家帐，我们的「家庭电脑」只会算简单的家帐，而不会算他很在意的「现金流量」；他要「家庭电脑」报个人所得税，我们的「家庭电脑」只能报最简单的个人所得税，而买得起我们「家庭电脑」（零售价一千一百五十美元）的个人，其所得税没那么简单；他要「家庭电脑」教育小孩，我们「家庭电脑」的教育游戏不见得比售价五十美元的S&S高明。

ReadShift 双语翻译

In reality, the home computer was only part of Shepherd's "Ubiquitous Computation" vision. In Shepherd's vision, home computers would balance household budgets, file personal income taxes, educate children, store recipes, and so on. "Business computers" would sit in offices doing professional work.

Shepherd's vision was farsighted — but at least a decade ahead of reality! In the real world, IBM launched the "personal computer" in 1981, legitimizing and popularizing the PC. But 1980s "personal computers" were still used only in work settings. It wasn't until the 1990s that "personal computers" made their way into homes — and they were still called "personal computers," not "home computers." Of course, by 2007, Apple more revolutionarily launched the iPhone — a computer that could fit in a shirt pocket. Now (2019), we are truly in an era of "computation everywhere" and "computers everywhere" — but "now" is forty years after the 1970s!

Why was Shepherd disconnected from reality? The key was IC functionality. IC functionality and cost throughout the 20th century followed "Moore's Law" — one "Moore generation" every two years. It wasn't until the mid-1990s that ICs became cheap enough, and cheap ICs powerful enough, to drive home computer applications. Demanding a useful and reasonably priced home computer in 1978 was at least six or seven "Moore generations" too early — twelve to fourteen years.

In the previous chapter, I described Shepherd's "bewilderment" about the 64K memory — after listening for hours, he still asked: "Are you really working on it?" It was this bewilderment about technological reality, combined with his stubborn personality, that caused him to overestimate our ability to develop "home computer" applications. He wanted the home computer to balance household budgets — ours could only do simple budgeting, not the "cash flow" analysis he cared about. He wanted it to file personal income taxes — ours could only handle the simplest returns, and the individuals who could afford our home computer ($1,150 retail) had far more complex taxes. He wanted it to educate children — its educational games were arguably no better than the $50 S&S.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Ubiquitous Computation (到处都有计算)—夏伯特在七〇年代提出的「普适计算」愿景——比英特尔和学术界正式提出类似概念早了十多年；但「远见」和「时机」是两回事——早了十二年的远见不是先知，而是灾难。
Moore generations as timing metric (以摩尔世代计算时机)—张忠谋用「摩尔世代」（每两年一代）来量化夏伯特的愿景与现实之间的时间差——六到七个世代即十二至十四年；这种「以技术节奏度量商业时机」的框架，是半导体产业分析独有的方法论。

我在半导体总经理任内，总是在烦恼消费者集团种种（我认为）不合理的要求，并没太注意所谓「家庭电脑」到底多么有用。到了消费者集团，很快就发现正在如火如荼开发的家庭电脑，实在用途不大；而且限制它的因素相当基本：集成电路的功能还不够成熟，成本也还太高。

怎么办？假使我那时（一九七八年）有现在的勇气，我会说：取消家庭电脑案！等集成电路和电脑软体技术更成熟（也就是说：做出来的家庭电脑更有用）后再议。

但是我那时没有这勇气。事实上，即使我有勇气对夏伯特及彪希建议取消家庭电脑，我也一定当场被严厉驳回。只要看后来家庭电脑彻底失败后，他们还坚持继续做，一直到一九八三年，搞得整个德仪公司几乎被拖垮，他们才停止家庭电脑业务就可以知道。

夏伯特早已宣告了他「到处都有计算」的理念。一九七八年九月美国《商业周刊》的封面故事，虽被彪希抢去了光采，但在「高科技创新」理念方面，却更固化夏伯特对「家庭电脑」的期待。

在我的岗位上，既没有勇气取消家庭电脑，还是尽力做吧！我把我手下最懂技术、最能干的经理人——彼得·邦菲（原任科学计算机总经理）调任为家庭电脑总经理；我给他一切他要求的人力经费。彼得的希望不见得比我的高，但我们要幹一番——也许奇迹会出现。

一九七九年六月，我们正式宣布德仪「家庭电脑」（TI99/4）问世，零售价一千一百五十美元。

宣布后两、三个月内，彼得和我就知道奇迹没有出现，通路和初期买主的反应已纷纷进来：应用有限，售价太高。最具讥笑意义的评论来自当时最红的半导体分析师罗森（他曾在一九七五、七六、七七年邀请我参加他举办的「三巨头座谈」）：

「巨山咆哮，出来的却是一只老鼠。」

ReadShift 双语翻译

As Semiconductor GM, I had always fretted about the Consumer Products Group's various (in my view) unreasonable demands and hadn't paid much attention to how useful the "home computer" really was. Once I moved to the Consumer Products Group, I quickly discovered that the home computer being developed so fervently was of quite limited use. And the constraints were quite fundamental: IC functionality wasn't mature enough yet, and costs were still too high.

What to do? Had I possessed the courage then (1978) that I have now, I would have said: cancel the home computer program! Revisit the topic when IC and computer software technology matured (that is: when a home computer could actually be made useful).

But I didn't have that courage then. In fact, even if I'd had the courage to suggest canceling the home computer to Shepherd and Shep, I would have been soundly rejected on the spot. One only needs to look at how, after the home computer's thorough failure, they still insisted on continuing until 1983 — nearly dragging the entire company down with them — before finally stopping the home computer business.

Shepherd had already proclaimed his "Ubiquitous Computation" vision. The September 1978 Business Week cover story, though its spotlight was stolen by Shep, further cemented Shepherd's expectations for the "home computer" in terms of "high-tech innovation" ideology.

In my position, having neither the courage to cancel the home computer nor the standing to challenge the program, I gave it my best. I assigned my most technically savvy and capable manager — Peter Bonfield (the former Scientific Calculator GM) — to be Home Computer GM. I gave him all the headcount and budget he requested. Bonfield's hopes were no higher than mine, but we were going to give it our all — perhaps a miracle would occur.

In June 1979, we officially announced the TI Home Computer (TI99/4), with a retail price of $1,150.

Within two or three months of the launch, Bonfield and I knew the miracle hadn't happened. Feedback from distributors and early buyers was pouring in: limited applications, price too high. The most derisive comment came from Ben Rosen, then the most prominent semiconductor analyst (who had invited me to his "Trio Summit" in 1975, 1976, and 1977):

"The mountain roared, and out came a mouse."

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
"Ubiquitous Computing" premature by 12–14 years (提前十二年的普适计算愿景)—夏伯特的「到处都有计算」与学术界在九〇年代提出的「普适计算」（Ubiquitous Computing, Weiser 1988）概念高度吻合——但超前了不止一代；在创新管理中，「早一代」是先驱，「早三代」则是先烈。
"The mountain roared, and out came a mouse" (巨山咆哮，出来一只老鼠)—分析师罗森对TI99/4的尖锐评语，也成为科技史上最著名的嘲讽之一；在营销中，「产品期待」和「产品现实」之间的差距直接决定口碑——越是大力造势的产品，一旦不如预期，反噬越强。

寂寞的七十寿辰

一九七九年农历正月，是母亲农历七十寿辰。那时我正在赶「家庭电脑」的开发，孤单地住在拉吧。母亲寿辰前的几个礼拜，我打电话给住在纽约的父母亲，告诉他们我工作忙得很，不能去纽约庆祝母亲的七十寿辰了。父母亲说，那就让他们到拉吧来过母亲的七十岁生日吧，顺便看看我在拉吧的生活情形。

我的拉吧公寓虽然够大，但除了我卧室和客厅有几件必要的家具外，没有别的家具；所以我把父母亲安顿在一个汽车旅馆里。父母亲来了几天，我还是每天照常上班；母亲寿辰那天，我们三人去附近一家中国餐馆点了几道菜，算是庆祝母亲寿辰。

我记得母亲四十寿辰，是在香港过的，那时我们刚从上海逃难到香港，但在母亲生日那天，还是摆了好几桌麻将，晚上有好几桌宴席；母亲五十寿辰在纽约过，那时我在德仪已有初期的成功，我请假到纽约，买了一件貂皮短大衣送给母亲，参加了母亲热闹的寿宴，母亲好高兴，穿了新大衣赴宴，告诉朋友这是她儿子送给她的；母亲六十寿辰，我刚升德仪副总裁不久，请父母同去迈阿密及牙买加度几天愉快的假期。

现在母亲七十寿辰，我在德仪的下山路上，父母亲知道，也痛惜我在下山路上。在陈旧的中餐厅用了晚餐后，三人在冷寂的拉吧街道上，暗淡欲熄的路灯下，无言步回父母亲的旅馆。母亲在餐馆里强颜为笑，但在路灯下已凄然欲泣了。

ReadShift 双语翻译

A Lonely Seventieth Birthday

In the first lunar month of 1979, it was my mother's seventieth lunar birthday. At the time, I was racing to develop the home computer, living alone in Lubbock. A few weeks before her birthday, I called my parents in New York and told them I was too busy with work to travel to New York to celebrate my mother's seventieth birthday. My parents said they would come to Lubbock instead to celebrate her seventieth birthday and see how I was living.

My Lubbock apartment was spacious enough, but beyond a few essential pieces of furniture in my bedroom and living room, it was unfurnished. So I settled my parents in a motel. They stayed for several days; I still went to work every day as usual. On my mother birthday, the three of us went to a nearby Chinese restaurant and ordered a few dishes to mark the occasion.

I remember my mother's fortieth birthday was celebrated in Hong Kong. We had just fled Shanghai for Hong Kong, but on her birthday, we still set up several tables of mahjong and hosted multiple dinner parties in the evening. Her fiftieth birthday was in New York. By then I had achieved initial success at TI. I took time off to go to New York, bought a mink jacket for my mother, and attended her lively birthday banquet. Mother was so happy — she wore the new jacket to the party and told her friends it was a gift from her son. Her sixtieth birthday came shortly after I was promoted to TI Vice President. I took my parents to Miami and Jamaica for a pleasant vacation.

Now, my mother's seventieth birthday — I was on the downhill path at TI. My parents knew it and grieved for me on that downhill path. After dinner at a dated Chinese restaurant, the three of us walked in silence along the desolate Lubbock streets, under the dim, flickering streetlights, back to my parents' motel. My mother had forced a smile at the restaurant, but under the streetlights she was already on the verge of tears.

修辞赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

「母亲在餐馆里强颜为笑，但在路灯下已凄然欲泣了。」——这是张忠谋自传中最为沉痛的个人场景。整部自传以理性和克制著称，但这一段关于母亲七十寿辰的叙述，几乎打破了这种克制。从四十寿辰的热闹、五十寿辰的貂皮大衣、六十寿辰的迈阿密假期，到七十寿辰在拉吧汽车旅馆前的无声漫步——张忠谋用一组递减的「寿辰蒙太奇」，把一个职业经理人的「下山」与一个家庭的情感代价并置，让读者看到：在那些宏大的商业决策背后，是具体的人、具体的牺牲、具体的无法弥补的遗憾。 "My mother had forced a smile at the restaurant, but under the streetlights she was already on the verge of tears." This is one of the most devastating personal scenes in Chang's entire autobiography. The entire memoir is known for its rationality and restraint, but this passage about his mother's seventieth birthday nearly breaks that restraint. From the liveliness of the fortieth, the mink jacket of the fiftieth, the Miami vacation of the sixtieth, to the silent walk in front of a Lubbock motel at the seventieth — Chang uses a descending "birthday montage" to juxtapose a professional manager's "descent" with a family's emotional cost, showing the reader: behind those grand commercial decisions are real people, real sacrifices, real irreparable regrets.

至今我仍不能原谅我那年的不孝。为什么我不能去纽约，热热闹闹地与父母亲的朋友们庆祝母亲生日？为什么我还紧紧抱着其实已不值一钱的「东山再起」希望，留在拉吧赶做即将失败的「家庭电脑」？而让父母亲到遥远的、没有朋友的拉吧，寂寞度过母亲的七十岁生日？

这是我最后一次机会，趁双亲都还健康，庆祝他们的大生日。两年后父亲就中风，后来一直没完全康复。母亲八十寿辰，我在纽约设宴庆贺，但那时父亲已中风多年，大家心情远不如昔；母亲九十寿辰我也为她在纽约设宴庆祝，但那时母亲自己也开始健忘，心情当然更不如昔。

德仪第一版「家庭电脑」（TI99/4）的失败，无疑地敲响我德仪生涯的丧钟。「东山再起」的一线希望，已随TI99/4的失败而完全消灭。唯一剩下的问题：德仪会怎么处理我？

初步答案在一九八〇年三月到达。彪希召见我，告诉我他即将派席克（William Sick）任消费者集团美国总经理，我仍留任全球总经理，所以名义上席克对我报告，但事实上彪希告诉我，他预备在几个月后让席克替代我。这几个月只是过渡时期而已。

至于我以后的工作？彪希说，夏伯特和他正在考虑成立一个新的业务部门，主要任务为机器人，做给自己用，也卖给别的公司。他们考虑我做这个新部门的总经理。

我无言地聆听彪希的话。两年前，我自请调职；现在，我已没有自请做什么事的立场，一切都是被动，一切都是唯命是从。

几个月后，彪希又召见我。他告诉我：夏伯特和他已决定于年底任命席克为全球消费者集团总经理。几个月前考虑开设的新（机器人）事业部门，现在因公司财务拮据已决定不做。自明年（一九八一）一月一日起，我的新职将是：全公司「品质与生产力总监」。

ReadShift 双语翻译

To this day, I still cannot forgive myself for that year's filial impiety. Why couldn't I go to New York and celebrate Mother's birthday with a lively gathering of her friends? Why did I still cling to the worthless hope of a comeback, staying in Lubbock racing to develop a doomed home computer — while letting my parents travel to a distant, friendless Lubbock to spend my mother's seventieth birthday in loneliness?

This was my last chance to celebrate a parent's milestone birthday while both were still healthy. Two years later, my father suffered a stroke and never fully recovered. For my mother's eightieth birthday, I hosted a celebration in New York, but by then my father had suffered from stroke for years and everyone's spirits were far from what they had been. For her ninetieth birthday, I also hosted a celebration in New York, but by then my mother herself had begun to lose her memory, and the mood was even less joyful.

The failure of TI's first-generation "home computer" (TI99/4) unmistakably sounded the death knell of my TI career. The faint hope of a "comeback" had perished completely with the TI99/4's failure. The only remaining question: what would TI do with me?

The preliminary answer arrived in March 1980. Shep summoned me and told me he was soon appointing William Sick as Consumer Products GM for the US. I would remain Global GM, so nominally Sick would report to me. But in fact, Shep told me, he intended to have Sick replace me within a few months. These few months were only a transition period.

As for my future role? Shep said Shepherd and he were considering establishing a new business unit focused on robotics — for TI's own use and for sale to other companies. They were considering me as GM of this new unit.

I listened to Shep's words in silence. Two years earlier, I had requested a transfer. Now, I no longer had standing to request anything. Everything was passive. Everything was obedience.

Several months later, Shep summoned me again. He told me: Shepherd and he had decided to appoint Sick as worldwide Consumer Products GM by year's end. The new robotics business unit considered a few months earlier was now canceled due to the company's financial constraints. Effective January 1 of the following year (1981), my new position would be: worldwide "Quality and Productivity Director."

修辞赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

「一切都是被动，一切都是唯命是从。」——这句话是张忠谋在德仪二十二年职业生涯最精准的墓志铭。从MIT的艰难求职、德仪的破格提拔、半导体的黄金时代、半导体总经理的奋斗与挣扎，到消费者集团的荒诞与失败，「被动」与「被命」最终定义了他在德仪的终局。但正是在这个最低谷中，张忠谋开始重新思考自己的下一步——而这一步，将彻底改变全球半导体产业的历史。 "Everything was passive. Everything was obedience." These words serve as the most precise epitaph for Chang's twenty-two-year TI career. From the difficult job search at MIT, the unconventional promotion at TI, the golden age of semiconductors, the struggle as Semiconductor GM, to the absurdity and failure in Consumer Products, "passive" and "commanded" ultimately defined his denouement at TI. But it was precisely at this lowest ebb that Chang began rethinking his next move — a move that would completely change the history of the global semiconductor industry.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
"Quality and Productivity Director" as exile (作为流放的「品质与生产力总监」)—这是一个典型的「明升暗降」安排——头衔好听，但远离业务核心；在企业管理中，将高阶主管调离利润中心、安排至幕僚职位，是「体面地驱逐」的常见手段。
Death knell of a career (职业生涯的丧钟)—TI99/4的失败不仅是产品层面的失败，更是张忠谋在德仪内部政治资本彻底耗尽的信号；在组织行为学中，「丧钟」敲响代表人在组织内的影响力曲线已跌入不可恢复的区段。

第十章小结：消费者的长征

一九七八年至一九八一日的近三年，是张忠谋在德仪的最后一站。从半导体总经理调任消费者集团总经理，他以「东山再起」的心态接受了一个自己原本认为「祸根」的职位。

这三年中，消费者集团经历了计算机的成本困境、科学计算机的稳健盈利、S&S玩具的创新成功、机器人的荒诞尝试、知名品牌的手表梦、以及TI99/4家庭电脑的彻底失败。张忠谋以几近自省的诚实，记录了每一次成功和失败背后的逻辑——尤其是他在家庭电脑项目上「没有勇气取消」的自我剖析。

最终，母亲寂寞的七十寿辰和TI99/4的失败，共同构成了张忠谋德仪生涯最沉痛的一页。一九八一年，他被调任全公司「品质与生产力总监」——远离了业务核心，等待下一个机会。而那个机会，将在太平洋对岸的土地上等候他。

章节

德儀篇第十一章

张忠谋

德仪篇·第十一章｜品质与生产力总监

「品质与生产力总监」在德仪是一个新的职位；在我之前，没有这个职位，所以也可以说这职位是夏伯特为我而创设。但事实上，在一九八〇年代的美国，创设这个职位是相当「时尚」的举动。在一九六〇、七〇年代，日本企业（尤其电子和半导体）异军突起，美国公司深深感受到他们的威胁。惠普公司一位工程经理在一学术论文刊列日本记忆体品质胜于美国的数据；日本企业内流行的「品质圈」也在美国被摹仿；几位素以品质为业的「品质大师」——戴明（Edwards Deming）、裘兰（Joseph Juran）、克罗斯比（Philip Crosby）——忽然红了起来，每个人都收到无数演讲或顾问邀请。在这节骨眼上，德仪任命一个「品质总监」，也是很自然的事。

我的新职在一九八〇年十二月就宣布，夏伯特在口头宣布时，还加上了一句：「在品质问题上，英理士代表我」，算是十足给了我面子。在新职，我只有一个秘书，没有别的属下，所以要想做事，必须经过我的同事——公司的集团总经理以及他们的属下。我相当自信我有能力经过同事追求公司品质目标，因为我相信绝大部分同事都相当尊敬我——后来的发展，证实了我的自信。

一九八〇年除夕，我寄了一封电子信给德仪所有高级经理（大约百人左右），祝贺他们新年健康、快乐、成功，而且告诉他们我下周就开始与他们合作改善他们产品的品质。这封信得到相当好的反应。最起码的反应是：「这人没灰心，他还是想做事。」

ReadShift 双语翻译

"Quality and Productivity Director" was a new position at TI — no one had held it before me, so one could say the position was created for Shepherd for me. But in fact, in 1980s America, creating such a position was quite a "fashionable" move. In the 1960s and 1970s, Japanese companies (especially in electronics and semiconductors) had risen with stunning force, and American corporations deeply felt the threat. An HP engineering manager published a paper in an academic journal listing data showing Japanese memory quality surpassed American. The "quality circles" popular within Japanese companies were being imitated in America. Several "quality gurus" — Edwards Deming, Joseph Juran, Philip Crosby — suddenly became famous, each receiving countless invitations to lecture or consult. At this juncture, TI's appointment of a "Quality Director" was quite natural.

My new position was announced in December 1980. When Shepherd made the oral announcement, he added: "On quality matters, Morris represents me" — giving me full face. In my new role, I had only one secretary and no other subordinates, so to get things done I had to work through my colleagues — the company's Group GMs and their people. Quite confident in my ability to pursue company quality goals through colleagues, because I believed the vast majority of colleagues held me in considerable respect — later developments proved my confidence well-founded.

On New Year's Eve 1980, I sent an email to all of TI's senior managers (about a hundred or so), wishing them health, happiness, and success in the new year, and telling them I would be working with them next week to improve their product quality. This email received quite a good response. At minimum: "This man hasn't lost heart. He still wants to get things done."

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Quality circles / 品质圈—日本企业推行的员工自愿参与品质改善活动的小组；「品质圈」是七〇至八〇年代日本制造业崛起的核心武器之一——它将品管责任从专门的品管部门扩散到每一位员工。
Staff position without direct reports (没有直接下属的幕僚职位)—张忠谋的「品质与生产力总监」只有一个秘书，没有直接下属——这种「幕僚」职位需要通过影响力（influence without authority）来推动工作；在组织行为学中，「没有职权的领导」（leading without authority）是管理中最高难度的技能之一。

瀑布式品质训练

虽然我在工程师、工程经理、业务总经理时期，都很注意品质，但我从未做过品质专业；现在我是品质专业人了。头三个月，我要密集地学习。

首先，我打听了谁最具权威性，决定到三位「大师」的教室上课。他们是克罗斯比（Philip Crosby）、裘兰（Joseph Juran）和戴明。

每一位大师的课都是两天或三天。在这些课里，我学到了不少技术方面的知识；但与品质总监职务直接相关，我学到最重要的一课就是：「品质不是一个人的事，也不是几个人的事；品质观念必须渗透整个组织，到每一个员工。」凭着我这一课，我在德仪创立了「瀑布式」（Cascade）品质训练。

所谓瀑布式训练，有以下几个步骤：

（一）所有集团总经理（最高层经理人）都去克罗斯比「品质学校」，上两天观念性的课。

（二）所有Division总经理（次高层经理人）都去上裘兰的三天兼具观念和技术的课；裘兰的课有教材和习题。

（三）每一Division总经理受训回来后，再用裘兰的教材，教他的直接下属（Department Managers）。

（四）每一Department Manager上课后，又教他的直接下属。

（五）如此类推，一直教到管理二、三十作业员的生产线领班。国外工厂，也是一样做法。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Cascade Quality Training

Although I had paid close attention to quality as an engineer, engineering manager, and business GM, I had never worked in quality as a specialty; now I was a quality professional. For the first three months, I studied intensively.

First, I found out who was most authoritative and decided to attend classes from three "gurus": Philip Crosby, Joseph Juran, and Deming.

Each guru's class lasted two or three days. In these classes, I learned considerable technical knowledge. But the most important lesson directly relevant to the Quality Director role was: "Quality is not the work of one person or a few people; the quality concept must permeate the entire organization, reaching every employee."

With that single lesson, I created "Cascade" quality training at TI.

The cascade training worked as follows: (1) All Group GMs (top-level managers) attended Crosby's "Quality School" for two days of conceptual training. (2) All Division GMs (next-level managers) attended Juran's three-day course combining concepts and technical skills, with textbooks and exercises. (3) After returning from training, each Division GM used Juran's materials to teach his direct reports (Department Managers). (4) After attending class, each Department Manager then taught his direct reports. (5) And so on, down to production line supervisors managing twenty to thirty operators. Foreign factories followed the same approach.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Cascade training (瀑布式训练)—指从最高层开始逐层向下传递的培训模式——每一层受训后即成为下一层的教师；在组织发展中，「瀑布式训练」是「知识内部化」的高效手段——它同时解决了「知识传递」和「教师资格认证」两个问题。
Quality gurus: Deming, Juran, Crosby (三位品质大师)—对七〇至八〇年代美国产业界影响最大的三位品质管理大师。戴明（Deming）侧重统计品管和高层承诺；裘兰（Juran）侧重品质三部曲（规划、改善、控制）；克罗斯比（Crosby）侧重「零缺陷」和「品质免费」。张忠谋在德仪的瀑布式训练以裘兰的教材为基础——是三人中唯一将其方法论系统教材化的一位。

这样做法，每班学生大约十来人（都是教师的直接下属），教师和学生都相当认真。每一个学生知道接下来他就要当他下属的教师，当然不想在下属面前出丑；而且「同学」都是工作上熟悉的同事，互动格外直接。

训练经费方面，我们以拿来的教材（印刷品）计算，每一副教材付裘兰一个相当合理的价钱。

每个月，我从每一集团收到已受训人数的报告。慢慢地，品质观念渗透全公司；慢慢地，品质技术穿入公司各阶层。我开始「瀑布式训练」后一年，德仪全球领班以上员工大约三万人，已经有一万多人受过裘兰品质训练。

夏伯特感觉到了。在他主持或参与的会议里，经理人的报告和多了一点品质话题。夏伯特在每次会议中，常会做少少的笔记，记他自己的感觉。会后他常把他的笔记传给彪希；如笔记关系到我，彪希也会让我看。一九七七年，彪希就曾给我看：「英理士不再好好经营半导体。」一九八二年，彪希又让我看：「英理士已在对的位置上。」我心酸了。夏伯特是在称赞我在品质上的表现，但他显然认为我以前的位置（半导体总经理、消费者产品总经理）是错的，我不配做那两个位置。

这样看待我的老板，我为什么要继续替他工作？

ReadShift 双语翻译

With this approach, each class had about ten students (all direct reports of the instructor), and both teachers and students took it quite seriously. Every student knew that next he would be the teacher of his own subordinates — certainly not wanting to lose face in front of them. Moreover, "classmates" were all familiar colleagues from work, making the interaction particularly direct.

For training costs, we paid Juran a reasonable fee per set of materials (printed) used.

Every month, I received reports from each Group on the number of people trained. Gradually, the quality concept permeated the entire company. Gradually, quality techniques penetrated every layer of the organization. A year after I started cascade training, of TI's roughly 30,000 supervisor-level and above employees worldwide, over 10,000 had received Juran quality training.

Shepherd noticed. In meetings he chaired or attended, managers' reports carried a bit more quality vocabulary. Shepherd often took brief notes during meetings, recording his own impressions. Afterward, he frequently passed his notes to Shep; if the notes concerned me, Shep would show them to me too. In 1977, Shep had shown me: "Morris no longer runs the semiconductors properly." In 1982, Shep showed me again: "Morris is finally in the right position."

My heart ached. Shepherd was praising my performance on quality — but he clearly believed my former positions (Semiconductor GM, Consumer Products GM) were wrong for me; I wasn't qualified for those roles.

A boss who saw me this way — why should I continue working for him?

修辞赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

「我心酸了。」——张忠谋用三个字回应了一个看似正面的评价。一九八二年，夏伯特透过彪希的笔记传递的「称赞」——「英理士已在对的位置上」——实际上是一个残酷的判断：你做半导体总经理不合格，做消费者产品总经理也不合格，你只适合做品质总监。对张忠谋这样一个从半导体一路做到集团副总裁的天才而言，这种「称赞」比批评更令人心寒。这种「赞美中的否定」是组织内部最隐蔽也最具杀伤力的政治语言。 "My heart ached." — Chang responds to a seemingly positive assessment with three words. Shepherd's 1982 "praise" — relayed through Shep's notes — "Morris is finally in the right position" — was in fact a devastating judgment: you were unqualified as Semiconductor GM, unqualified as Consumer Products GM; you're only suited for Quality Director. For a talent who had risen from Semiconductor GM all the way to Group VP, this kind of "praise" was more chilling than any criticism. This "negging within praise" is the most covert yet damaging form of organizational political language.

品质蓝皮书及巡回视察

在我任「品质总监」的第一年，除了开始大规模「瀑布式训练」外，我又开始了「品质蓝皮书」和巡回视察。

什么是「品质蓝皮书」？先解释德仪的「蓝皮书」。「蓝皮书」就是一个业务单位的盈亏表，每月出版。每一业务单位，从基层一直到全公司，都有它的「蓝皮书」。夏伯特和彪希的「蓝皮书」厚厚一本，除了全公司的盈亏表外，公司百来个业务单位的盈亏表都在他们的「蓝皮书」内。

现在，我要求每一业务单位的「品质经理」编辑他单位的「品质蓝皮书」。品质蓝皮书的数据是「品质成本」——品质成本观念来自正统的品质理论：完美品质等于无瑕疵或无错误；任何瑕疵或错误都代表成本。品质蓝皮书就是这些品质成本的报导。

每一业务单位的「品质经理」都非常倡导我的到来。平常在他们同僚间（研发经理、工程经理、生产经理等等），品质经理往往不受重视，现在，我变成他们的「虚线」上司，他们有我为他们撑腰了。他们对编辑品质蓝皮书充满热忱，也热心地看管他们单位的瀑布式训练。

我也开始巡回视察。在八〇年代，德仪工厂已遍布欧、美、洲。在我任品质总监的三十四个月内，我到过所有工厂地点——有的每季一次，有的半年一次，有的年一次。在这三十四个月内，我超过一半时日都在旅行！

ReadShift 双语翻译

Quality Blue Book and巡回视察

In my first year as "Quality Director," in addition to launching the massive cascade training, I also introduced the "Quality Blue Book" and巡回视察.

What was the "Quality Blue Book"? First, let me explain TI's "Blue Book." The "Blue Book" was a profit-and-loss statement for each business unit, published monthly. Every business unit — from the lowest-level shop floor to the entire company — had its own Blue Book. Shepherd and Shep's Blue Book was a thick volume containing not only the companywide P&L but also the P&L statements for the company's hundred-odd business units.

Now I required each business unit's "Quality Manager" to compile a "Quality Blue Book" for their unit. The Quality Blue Book reported "quality cost" data — the quality cost concept coming from orthodox quality theory: perfect quality equals zero defects or zero errors; every defect or error represents a cost. The Quality Blue Book was the reporting vehicle for these quality costs.

Every business unit's Quality Manager enthusiastically welcomed my initiative. Among their peers (R&D managers, engineering managers, production managers), quality managers had often been undervalued; now I became their "dotted-line" boss, and they had me backing them. They threw themselves into editing their units' Quality Blue Books with zeal and also diligently monitored their units' cascade training.

I also began touring the factories. In the 1980s, TI factories spanned Europe, America, and Asia. During my thirty-four months as Quality Director, I visited all factory locations — some quarterly, some semi-annually, some annually. In those thirty-four months, I spent more than half my time traveling!

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Quality cost (品质成本)—企业因品质失败而产生的所有成本，包括内部失败成本（报废、返工）、外部失败成本（退货、赔偿）和预防/鉴定成本；「品质成本」的概念由裘兰和克罗斯比系统化——它让「品质」从一个主观的「好东西」变成了一个可量化的财务指标。
Dotted-line authority (虚线职权)—指组织中跨正式指挥链的报告关系——「实线」是直接主管，「虚线」是业务指导关系；张忠谋以「品质总监」身份成为各业务单位品质经理的「虚线」上司，这种安排赋予了幕僚对专业职能线的横向影响力。

美日记忆体良率差异分析

一九八一年，德仪日本美浦厂开始生产德仪休士顿厂已在生产的记忆体。忽然，消息传来——美浦厂的良率是休士顿厂的一倍以上（那时休士顿厂良率大约百分之二十几，美浦厂却做到四、五〇%）。

夏伯特震惊了！命令休士顿厂立即改进！把休士顿的工程师弄得人仰马翻，不知道做什么才能改进。我作为「品质与生产力总监」也被嘱「看一下」。

其实我早已预测到日本厂良率会比美国厂高，只是实际的差异比我想象的更大。既然被嘱「看一下」，我就与日本厂和休士顿厂的同事（都是我的旧属）讨论了几次。我的结论如下：

差异在TAG——先从作业员说起，日本厂的作业员流动率每年二人左右，「除非她要结婚了，否则她不会离开」；休士顿作业员在经济景气好、找别的工作容易时流动率高达每年25%，即使在经济不景气时也高达10%。高流动率造成公司常要聘雇无经验的作业员，但是这些无经验作业员经手的晶圆往往是零良率。还有，当我进入日本工厂时，作业员都专心工作，毫不理会我；但当我进入德州工厂时，作业员都转过头来看我——日本作业员显然比较专心工作。

再谈生产线领班，日本厂雇进的领班，至少有工程技职教育，还有许多还是正式大学工程毕业生；美国已雇不到工程毕业的领班。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Japan-US Memory Yield Gap Analysis

In 1981, TI's Miho, Japan fab began producing memory devices that TI's Houston fab was already making. Suddenly, news arrived — Miho's yields were more than double Houston's (Houston was at roughly 20%-plus yields; Miho achieved 40%-50%).

Shepherd was shocked! He ordered Houston to immediately improve! Houston engineers were turned upside down, with no idea what to do to improve. As "Quality and Productivity Director," I was also asked to "take a look."

Actually, I had long predicted that Japanese fab yields would be higher than American — but the actual gap was even larger than I'd imagined. Having been asked to "take a look," I discussed several times with colleagues at both the Japan and Houston fabs (all former subordinates). My conclusion:

The difference was in TAG —

Starting with operators: Japan had an annual operator turnover rate of around 2%. "Unless she gets married, she won't leave." Houston operators had turnover rates as high as 25% annually in good economic times when other jobs were easy to find, and even in bad times it ran 10%. High turnover meant the company constantly hired inexperienced operators, but wafers handled by these inexperienced operators often had zero yield. Also, when I entered the Japanese plant, operators focused on their work and completely ignored me. But when I entered the Texas plant, operators turned their heads to look at me — Japanese operators were clearly more focused on their work.

As for line supervisors: Japan hired supervisors with at least engineering vocational education, and many were full university engineering graduates. America could no longer hire engineering graduates as supervisors.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Yield gap as mirror (良率差距作为一面镜子)—美浦厂的良率是休士顿厂的两倍以上——这个数字背后的不是技术差距，而是人力资本差距（作业员流动率、领班教育水平、工程师素质）；在半导体制造中，「良率」是一个综合性的组织能力指标——它反映的不是单一环节，而是整个工厂的人力品质系统。
Operator turnover rate as quality killer (作业员流动率作为良率杀手)—日本厂作业员流动率约2%/年 vs. 休士顿厂高达25%/年——高流动率是新进无经验作业员比例的直接来源；在制造业中，「作业员流动率」是良率波动的第一大来源——新入职工人经手晶圆往往是零良率。

再谈设备工程师，这是晶圆厂很重要的一环，因为晶圆厂的生产设备几乎都是刚研发出来的精密仪器，操作并不稳定。美国厂能雇到的设备工程师大半都只有修理汽车、或自行车、或机车经验；日本厂却雇到年轻有工程背景的技师，经过训练之后，都变成非常专业。结果：日本厂的新设备平均运转率90%多，美国厂的设备却常处于半运转状态——在前面堆积了一大堆待处理晶圆。我可以断言，从来不曾有一条经常有瓶颈的生产线会有好良率。

再谈生产线上的工程师，七〇、八〇年代的美国优秀工程科系毕业生都想做研发、或市场、或行销，已很少愿意当生产线工程师；日本厂却还能雇到正牌工程科系毕业生。

我找了一个方便的机会，把我以上的分析向夏伯特做了一个口头报告。我还没讲完，就看得出他不耐烦的神气；我一讲完，他立刻说：「我要的是可以立刻改进良率的方案，你的分析对我毫无用。」我的确没有可以立刻改进良率的办法。他倒以为他有——他的办法就是把日本厂长调到休士顿做休士顿厂长。

日本厂长了，但并不拒绝，他也知道这是一个升职的机会，他要求带几个日本工程师一起来休士顿，夏伯特也同意了。但是，立刻的效果并不是夏伯特所想的良率改进，而是日本厂长和几个人地生疏、水土不服，病的病了，想回日本的要求调回。

我的分析报告成为我在德仪的最后哀鸣。我对夏伯特报告后，没有人再提起它；在德仪的池塘里，它没有掀起任何涟漪。讽刺地，它成为几年后我创办台积电的灵感和凭借。

【注释】

[1] TAG = Turnover, 领班教育, 设备工程师, 产线工程师——此为张忠谋自创的缩写记忆法。

ReadShift 双语翻译

As for equipment engineers: this is a critical part of any wafer fab, because fab production equipment is almost always newly developed precision instrumentation that's not stable in operation. The best equipment engineers America could hire mostly had only experience repairing cars, bicycles, or motorcycles. Japan hired young technicians with engineering backgrounds, who after training became highly professional. Result: Japan's new equipment averaged over 90% uptime; America's equipment was often in semi-operational state — with a large pile of wafers waiting in front of it. I can assert: there has never been a production line with frequent bottlenecks that achieved good yields.

As for production line engineers: in 1970s–80s America, top engineering graduates all wanted to do R&D, marketing, or sales; very few were willing to be production line engineers. Japan could still hire properly credentialed engineering graduates.

I found a convenient opportunity and made an oral report of the above analysis to Shepherd. Before I finished, I could see impatience on his face. The moment I finished, he immediately said: "I want a solution that can improve yields immediately. Your analysis is of no use to me."

Indeed, I had no way to improve yields immediately. He thought he did — his solution was to transfer the Japan fab manager to Houston as Houston fab manager.

Japan fab manager was shocked but didn't refuse — he knew this was a promotion opportunity. He asked to bring several Japanese engineers with him; Shepherd agreed. But the immediate result was not the yield improvement Shepherd envisioned, but the Japanese manager and engineers struggling with unfamiliar surroundings, unaccustomed to new conditions — some fell sick, some requested transfer back to Japan.

My analysis report became my final lament at TI. After I delivered it to Shepherd, no one ever mentioned it again. In TI's pond, it created no ripple. Ironically, it became the inspiration and foundation for founding TSMC a few years later.

修辞赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

「在德仪的池塘里，它没有掀起任何涟漪。讽刺地，它成为几年后我创办台积电的灵感和凭借。」——这是张忠谋自传中承上启下的关键句。整个第十一章以「品质总监」的任命始，以「美日良率分析」终。报告中那条由作业员流动率、领班教育、设备工程师素质、产线工程师来源所定义的「良率差距」，在德仪的池塘里没有激起任何水花——但它在一个人的心里种下了一颗种子。六年后，那颗种子在台湾破土而出，长为台积电。 "In TI's pond, it created no ripple. Ironically, it became the inspiration and foundation for founding TSMC a few years later." This is a pivotal pivot in Chang's autobiography. Chapter 11 opens with the appointment as "Quality Director" and closes with the Japan-US yield analysis. That yield gap defined by operator turnover, supervisor education, equipment engineer quality, and line engineer sourcing — it stirred no water in TI's pond. But it planted a seed in one person's heart. Six years later, that seed broke ground in Taiwan and grew into TSMC.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Transfer of Japanese manager as panacea (调日本厂长如休士顿视为万灵丹)—「把日本厂长调过去就好了」——这是管理者的直觉反应（复制成功），但忽略了「成功是系统的产物而非个人的产物」。一个优秀厂长离开其赖以成功的系统（作业员、领班、工程师、供应商），其个人能力在新的系统中往往无法复制旧系统的绩效。
TAG framework (TAG分析框架)—张忠谋自创的TAG缩写（Turnover流动率、领班教育、设备工程师工程师素质、产线工程师来源）——这是一个简洁且完整的工厂良率分析框架。四十年后，台积电的工厂管理仍然沿用类似的人力品质评估维度。
章节

德儀篇第十二章

张忠谋

德仪篇·第十二章｜最后的吶喊与离去

就在我还在德仪做「最后的吶喊」时，我和前妻决定分居及办理离婚手续。我们两人同年，在二十岁时（她在波士顿大学，我在麻省理工）相恋，二十二岁就结婚——结婚得太早了。两人的爱大约继续了十几年，但当我史丹佛读博士时，就已渐渐消散；到四、五十岁时，两人几乎已成陌路人了。

我们都没有外遇，但三十年时光，人总会变的。幸运的夫妻一起变，我和前妻没有这么幸运；至少有十年时间，「分居」、「离婚」就常在心上和口中，但女儿还小，为了她，还是一起过日子吧。我们五十岁时，女儿已去波士顿念大学（她母亲的母校），而且即将毕业自立，我们分手的时间也已到了。

我早已有相当积蓄，但从未享受过物质上舒服的家。我找了一个宽敞（七十坪）的公寓：客厅、饭厅、两个卧房，再加一个很大（三十坪）的起居室兼书房。找室内设计师布置，买了舒服的现代化家具，装了一流音响……一九八一年底，我满五十岁，独自搬入新寓。

华丽的周围，不能补偿内心的寂寞；孤独的夜晚里，萦绕在我心的是三十年的恋爱和婚姻：

记得那日花底相遇，我问你心中有何希望？ 你向我轻轻私语：「要你，要你，要你！」记得那夜月色迷离，你问我心中有何秘密？ 我向你轻轻私语：「爱你，爱你，爱你！」

ReadShift 双语翻译

Even as I was making my "final outcry" at TI, my ex-wife and I decided to separate and begin divorce proceedings. We were the same age — we fell in love at twenty (she at Boston University, I at MIT) and married at twenty-two. Too young. Our love lasted perhaps a dozen years or so. But by the time I was at Stanford pursuing my Ph.D., it had already begun to fade. By our forties and fifties, we were practically strangers.

Neither of us had affairs. But thirty years — people always change. Fortunate couples change together. My ex-wife and I were not so lucky. For at least ten years, "separation" and "divorce" were constantly on our minds and lips. But our daughter was still young, so for her sake, we stayed together. By the time we were fifty, our daughter was at Boston University (her mother's alma mater) and about to graduate and stand on her own. The time for us to part had come.

I already had substantial savings but had never enjoyed a materially comfortable home. I found a spacious (roughly 230 square meters) apartment: living room, dining room, two bedrooms, plus an expansive (roughly 100 square meters) living room-cum-study. I hired an interior designer, bought comfortable modern furniture, installed top-tier audio... At the end of 1981, at fifty years old, I moved into my new apartment alone.

The splendid surroundings could not compensate for the loneliness within. In the lonely nights, what lingered in my heart was thirty years of love and marriage:

I remember that day meeting beneath the flowers — I asked you, what hope was in your heart?

You whispered softly to me: "Want you, want you, want you!"

I remember that night under the hazy moonlight — you asked me, what secret was in my heart?

I whispered softly to you: "Love you, love you, love you!"

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Personal divorce as professional inflection point (个人离婚作为职业转折点)—婚姻关系的结束将与职业转型形成共振——张忠谋在一九八一年底离婚、独自搬入新公寓，与他在德仪的职业下行同步；在传记研究中，「个人生活的断裂」往往是「职业重新定位」的触发事件。

但是今夕何夕，你我为何不交一语？ 我不知你有何希望，你也不问我心底秘密。

「不如离去！」回肠荡气的歌剧——奥芬巴哈的《霍夫曼的爱情故事》、歼米洛……都是悲凉又美丽的曲调和歌词。静坐在宽敞起居室一张沙发上，听到疲倦了，挣扎走回卧房，昏然入睡。

骆驼背上最后一根稻草

与我「分居」平行的是我在德仪每况愈下的际遇。终于，最后一根稻草掉落在骆驼背上——终于，这代表我对德仪已「缘尽债还」了。

没有预警，没有解释，在一九八二年九月，也就是我任「品质总监」一年九个月后，也就是夏伯特认为我已在「对的位置」几个月后，我在「内部邮件」中接到人事处通知：我的薪资不变，但我的职阶被降四级——自四十二级降至三十八级！四十二级是仅次于公司总裁的职阶，三十八级是我任副总裁暨集成电路总经理时的职阶。从三十八级升到四十二级，又从四十二级降回到三十八级，在德仪组织里「上山、下山」前后十年，占据了我四十一岁至五十一岁的年华！

当时德仪高级经理的待遇有三种：（一）薪资；（二）奖金，最高可与薪资相等；（三）股票承购权：如股票涨价，股票承购权可使高阶经理人富有，我就是以此途径实现「美国梦」。

ReadShift 双语翻译

But what day is it today — why do you and I not exchange a word?

I don't know what hope is in your heart, and you don't ask what secret is in mine.

"Better to leave!"

The soul-stirring operas — Offenbach's *The Tales of Hoffmann*, Giordano... all poignant yet beautiful melodies and lyrics. Sitting alone on the sofa in the spacious living room, listening until exhausted, I would struggle back to my bedroom and fall into a stupor of sleep.

The Last Straw on the Camel's Back

Parallel to my "separation" was my deteriorating situation at TI. At last, the final straw fell on the camel's back — at last, this signified that my karmic connection with TI had "run its course and been repaid."

Without warning, without explanation, in September 1982 — one year and nine months into my tenure as "Quality Director," and just a few months after Shepherd declared I was "finally in the right position" — I received a notice from Human Resources via "internal mail": my salary would remain unchanged, but my job grade would be demoted four levels — from Grade 42 to Grade 38! Grade 42 was the second-highest rank in the company, just below the President. Grade 38 was the rank I had held as VP and IC GM. From Grade 38 up to Grade 42, then back down from Grade 42 to Grade 38 — ten years of "ascending and descending" the TI organization, spanning my forty-first to fifty-first years!

At that time, TI senior managers had three forms of compensation: (1) salary; (2) bonus, up to 100% of salary; (3) stock options: if the stock price rose, stock options could make senior managers wealthy. This was the path by which I had achieved my "American Dream."

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Four-level demotion as organizational signal (四级降职作为组织信号)—职阶从四十二级降至三十八级——薪资不变但职阶大幅下调，这是组织中最具羞辱性的处置之一；在企业管理中，「明降」（薪资不变但级别下调）通常意味着「你被边缘化了，但我们不想付遣散费」。
Stock options as American Dream vehicle (股票承购权作为美国梦的载体)—指高阶主管通过股票承购权实现财富积累的路径；在半导体产业的黄金时代，「股票承购权」是吸引和留住高阶人才的核心工具——张忠谋正是通过这一途径实现了他三十年前来到美国时憧憬的「美国梦」。

自我「自请调任」从半导体到消费者产品后，我就没有拿过股票承购权；自我被调到「品质总监」后，我的奖金也被大打折扣。现在，我职阶被降四级。

以后会怎样？我可以很清晰地看到我在德仪的未来：薪资会被调降，奖金和股票承购权永远绝缘；一旦经济不景气，我还会被要求提早退休。

我才五十一岁，距离我计划六十五岁退休年龄，还有十四年！我不愿意！

那么只有一条路：辞职！

看起来价值百万美元。但是我还有尚未到期的股票承购权，那些承购权一年后才到期。

忍一忍吧，忍到领到那些承购权后辞职。

一九八三年十月初，所有股票承购权都拿到了。我口头对彪希辞职，十月底生效。几天后，夏伯特召见我：

「听说你要辞职？」「是。」「我们很满意你现在做的工作。」「但我不满意我的职位。」「那你要做什么？」「我想经营一个事业。」「你还是想要经营半导体？」「不一定是半导体，但我要经营一个事业，而不是做一个幕僚。」「我们没有这样的空缺。」他停顿了一下，继续说：「看来你所需要的和我们所能给你的没有交集。我很遗憾。」谈话显然结束了。我起立，十分痛心，但也十分真诚。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Ever since my "self-initiated transfer" from semiconductors to consumer products, I had received no stock options. Since being moved to "Quality Director," my bonus had also been sharply reduced. Now, my job grade was slashed four levels.

What lay ahead? I could clearly see my future at TI: salary would be cut; bonus and stock options would be permanently out of reach; and once a recession hit, I would be asked to take early retirement.

I was only fifty-one, fourteen years away from my planned retirement age of sixty-five! I was not willing!

Then there was only one path: resign!

It appeared to be worth a million dollars. But I still had unvested stock options that wouldn't vest for another year.

Endure it. Endure until those options vested, then resign.

In early October 1983, all stock options had vested. I verbally resigned to Shep, effective end of October. A few days later, Shepherd summoned me:

"I hear you're resigning?"

"Yes."

"We're very satisfied with the work you're doing now."

"But I'm not satisfied with my position."

"Then what do you want to do?"

"I want to run a business."

"You still want to run semiconductors?"

"Not necessarily semiconductors, but I want to run a business, not be a staff officer."

"We don't have that kind of opening." He paused, then continued: "It seems what you need and what we can offer have no intersection. I regret this."

The conversation was clearly over. I stood up — deeply pained, yet utterly sincere.

修辞赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

「看来你所需要的和我们所能给你的没有交集。我很遗憾。」——夏伯特用一句极其克制的话，结束了张忠谋在德仪的二十二年。没有挽留，没有加薪，没有新的安排——只有「没有交集」四个字。在组织行为学中，这种「没有交集」的对话是最高级别的拒绝——它不是「你不够好」，而是「你的存在方向与组织的方向已经平行」。张忠谋以「十分痛心，但也十分真诚」回应——这是两个骄傲的人之间最后的体面。 "It seems what you need and what we can offer have no intersection. I regret this." Shepherd ended Chang's twenty-two years at TI with an extraordinarily restrained sentence. No attempt to retain, no salary increase, no new arrangement — only "no intersection." In organizational behavior, this "no intersection" conversation is the highest form of rejection: it's not "you're not good enough," it's "your direction and the organization's direction have gone parallel." Chang responded with "deeply pained, yet utterly sincere" — the final courtesy between two proud men.

此后，两三个星期，我辞职的消息在内部传出，零零落落地有人来道别，但也不是很多。一个已走了几年下坡路的人忽然辞职，已不是什么新闻。何况，一九八三年的德仪兵荒马乱，比我早辞职的副总以上人员已有十几个。

有一位道别者是德仪共同创办人，也是荣誉董事长。过去在董事会曾多次称赞和鼓励我，他在走廊上遇见我，止步，把手臂围在我肩膀上：「可惜啊！」叹了口气，「天下无不散的筵席」，他用英文讲这句中国谚语。

十月三十一日，我照常上班；十一月一日，我不再上班，待在家里。

家里的电话铃声也开始响了——是猎头者（Headhunter）的电话铃声。

【注释】

[1] 出自琼瑶《庭院深深》。

[2] 猎头者是专为企业罗致高阶人员之组织。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Afterward, for two or three weeks, news of my resignation spread internally. A few people came to say goodbye — not many. A man who had been on a downhill path for several years suddenly resigning was no longer news. Besides, 1983 TI was in turmoil; over a dozen people at VP level or above had already resigned before me.

One well-wisher was TI's co-founder and Honorary Chairman. He had praised and encouraged me many times in Board meetings. Encountering me in the hallway, stopped, put his arm around my shoulder: "What a pity!" sighed, "There is no feast that does not end." He rendered this Chinese proverb in English.

October 31: I went to work as usual. November 1: I no longer went to work, staying home.

The home phone also began to ring — the ring of headhunters.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Headhunter as career transition catalyst (猎头者作为职业转型的催化剂)—专业为企业罗致高阶人员的组织；在成熟产业中，「猎头」是高层人才市场的核心中介——他们的电话铃声代表「市场对你的能力有另一种定价」。
VP-level exodus as organizational signal (副总级以上离职潮作为组织信号)—在张忠谋辞职前已有十几位副总级以上人员离职——这是组织危机的明确信号；在组织健康度评估中，「高阶主管离职率」是最敏感的先导指标之一。

第十二章小结：德仪的终结

一九八三年十一月一日，张忠谋结束了在德仪的二十二年生涯。他在自传中精确记录了这一天的细节：十月三十一日上班，十一月一日不再上班，待在家里——电话铃响了，是猎头者。

这最后一天的色彩不是告别同事（已提前完成），不是交出手上的工作（早就没有太多工作可交），也不是感慨万千（二十二年已经感慨够了）——而是电话铃声。这种「电话铃声」是市场对张忠谋能力的另一种认可，也是一个时代的最终句号。

ReadShift 双语翻译

On November 1, 1983, Morris Chang ended his twenty-two-year career at TI. He precisely recorded the details of that day in his autobiography: October 31 went to work; November 1 no longer went to work, staying home — the phone rang; it was headhunters.

The color of this final day was not bidding farewell to colleagues (already done), handing over work on hand (there wasn't much left), nor deep reflection (twenty-two years was enough for reflection) — but the phone ring. This "phone ring" was the market's alternate validation of Chang's abilities, and the final period on an era.

章节

德儀篇第十三章

张忠谋

德仪篇·第十三章｜从德仪到通用

找工作

我在德仪辞职的消息，在一、两天内就在《华尔街日报》、达拉斯两份日报及《电子新闻》发表。此后一、两星期，家中电话铃声响不停。我那时家里电话号码公开，所以陌生人要打电话给我只要查达拉斯电话簿或向电话公司询问就可以。而且我装了答话机，如我不在家，答话机可录下对方的讯息。

头两星期，大约有七、八个「接触」，就是对方试探我对他所提供的「机会」有无兴趣。这类试探大部分来自猎头者。经过一两次通话后，有好几个接触都被我谢绝了。

接下来两个月（一九八三年十一月下旬、十二年月及次年一月上旬），我与四个公司举行十几次面谈（光是通用器材公司就与我面谈了五次）。一九八四年一月三日，我收到凡爱创投的聘请；一月十日，我收到通用的聘请；一月十六日，我接受了通用的聘请。

另外两家公司与我面谈但后来没聘我。其中一家是因为董事会不能决定大策略（继续经营？卖掉？了结掉？）。另一家是柯达（Eastman Kodak，著名照相软片公司）。我与他们面谈经过，值得在此一提。

在二十世纪大部分，柯达是一家非常出色的公司。随著一般人民生活渐趋富裕，摄影愈普遍，柯达的软片生意也蒸蒸日上。我开始有些积蓄投资股票时，曾订阅一份很畅销的股票分析师的定期报告，柯达几乎每月都是「必须持有」的蓝筹股。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Job Hunting

News of my resignation from TI appeared in The Wall Street Journal, both Dallas daily newspapers, and Electronic News within a day or two. For the next week or two, my home phone rang constantly. My home phone number was publicly listed — anyone could find it through the Dallas phone directory or by calling the phone company. I had also installed an answering machine to record messages when I was out.

In the first two weeks, there were about seven or eight "contacts" — parties testing my interest in "opportunities" they could offer. Most of these probes came from headhunters. After one or two phone calls, I declined several.

Over the next two months (late November and December 1983, and early January 1984), I held over a dozen interviews with four companies (General Instruments alone interviewed me five times). On January 3, 1984, I received an offer from a venture capital firm; on January 10, an offer from General Instruments; on January 16, I accepted the General Instruments offer.

Two other companies interviewed me but did not extend offers. One couldn't decide on its board-level strategy (continue operating? Sell? Wind down?). The other was Eastman Kodak, the renowned photographic film company. My interview experience with them is worth recounting.

For most of the 20th century, Kodak was a superb company. As ordinary people's lives grew more prosperous and photography became more universal, Kodak's film business thrived. When I had begun investing in stocks, I subscribed to a popular analyst's periodic reports. Kodak was almost every month a "must-hold" blue chip.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Headhunter probes (猎头者的试探)—猎头者在得知高阶主管离职后，以「机会」为饵进行的初步接触；在猎头行业中，「接触」（contact）是正式招聘的前奏——它的目的是评估候选人对机会的兴趣程度，而非立即提供具体职位。
Blue chip "must-hold" (蓝筹股「必须持有」)—指分析师对柯达的评级——「必须持有」是最强的买入建议；在投资分析中，「蓝筹股」（blue chip）指那些历史悠久、财务稳健、长期表现优异的大型上市公司。

有了这样心理背景，当一个「猎头者」在一九八三年十一月上旬打电话给我，问我对柯达即将新设「电子摄影」部门总经理职有无兴趣时，我毫不犹豫地说：「有兴趣」。在下一个电话中，我们就约定了我去纽约州罗彻斯特市柯达总部面谈的日期。

那时德仪有一位董事，是刚从柯达退休的执行副总。我跟他不熟，但认识。我打电话告诉他我要去柯达面谈的消息，他倒很客气，到罗彻斯特机场接我，并约我当晚到他家晚餐。我去了，但他在饭桌上的谈话倒是出我意料的悲观。他的大意是：柯达现在很乱，公司里有少数人以为电子摄影会渐渐取代现在的软片摄影，但多数人不以为然。若我在这个节骨眼上介入，他并不看好。

第二天我进柯达面谈，情况比这位退休副总讲的还糟。我见了好几位副总，最后又见了柯达总裁，几乎没一个谈话可以谈得上「投机」；而且，大部分面谈者给我的感觉是：与我谈话是是浪费时间，他们根本不需要「电子摄影」。

柯达的面谈没有下文。我甚至不知道他们后来有没有设立「电子摄影部」，我也不知道他们后来有没有试图转型。从外面看来，他们死守软片照相；在后来几十年中，随著软片照相的衰退，他们默默地被淘汰。

最近几年，在台湾常听到「转型」的口号：「转型！转型！」但是，又有几家公司转型成功呢？

ReadShift 双语翻译

With this psychological backdrop, when a "headhunter" called in early November 1983 asking if I'd be interested in the GM position for a new "electronic photography" division at Kodak, I said "interested" without hesitation. In our next call, we set a date for me to interview at Kodak's headquarters in Rochester, New York.

At the time, one TI director was a recently retired EVP from Kodak. I didn't know him well but was aware of him. I called to tell him about my Kodak interview, and he was gracious enough to pick me up at the Rochester airport and invite me to his home for dinner. I went. But his dinner conversation was unexpectedly pessimistic: Kodak was in turmoil. A few people inside believed electronic photography would gradually replace film photography. Most did not. If I stepped in at this juncture, he was pessimistic about the prospects.

The next day I went to Kodak for interviews — and it was worse than the retired EVP had described. I met with several VPs and finally the Kodak CEO. Almost none of the conversations felt "in sync." Most of my interviewers gave the impression that talking to me was a waste of time — they didn't need "electronic photography" at all.

The Kodak interview went nowhere. I never even learned whether they eventually created the "electronic photography" division, or whether they ever attempted to transform. From the outside, they clung to film photography. In the decades that followed, as film photography declined, they quietly faded away.

In recent years in Taiwan, I frequently hear the slogan "Transform! Transform!" But how many companies have truly succeeded in transforming?

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Organizational indifference as rejection (以组织冷漠作为拒绝)—柯达面谈者的态度不是敌意，而是冷漠——「与我谈话是浪费时间」；在面试情境中，「冷漠」比「拒绝」更具毁灭性——它不是否定你的能力，而是根本否定你存在的必要性。
"Transform! Transform!" slogan vs. reality (「转型！转型！」口号 vs. 现实)—柯达死守软片照相而最终被数字摄影颠覆，成为「转型失败」的全球标杆案例；在战略管理中，「转型」之所以困难，是因为它要求企业否定自己最熟悉的商业模式、放弃最确定的现有收入。

现在回到一九八四年的我，以及我收到的两个邀聘了。

第一个邀聘来自一位当时很著名、总部在纽约曼哈顿的创业投资人，他与我在三次相当投机的面谈后就邀聘我为创投基金的「高级合伙人」（General Partner），而且开出很优渥的条件：（一）只比德仪略低的固定收入；（二）在他现有的大基金里我会有不错的「附带利益」（carry interest）；（三）在他刚投资的一家半导体公司，他要求我做董事，而且享有股票承购权；（四）他要我主持他想成立的达拉斯分处，他会帮助我募集该分处的基金，而我会在这基金上享受巨大的附带利益。

一星期后我就收到第二个邀聘——通用的邀聘。

通用在一九八三年「财星五百大」（即美国营收最高的五百家公司）的排名，大约居于三百至四百之间（德仪在一百名内）。它是一家多元公司：宽频、半导体、赌注产品（例如跑马场用的赌注机器、政府卖彩票的机器等），还有「电脑产品」（都是购并过来的小公司，准备整理后把它们上市，或卖给别人）。

通用的董事长是歇基。在两个月内，他和我面谈了五次——他似乎要测验我在不同场合的举止。这五次谈话，有两次在他的亚利桑那乡村俱乐部；两次在他办公室或会议室；一次在上等餐厅。五次面谈主要讲话者是我，我叙述了我的一生经历以及我的抱负。他也简单地说了他如何达到通用的颠峰。

对我更有兴趣的，他说他长我四岁并预备几年内就退休，而我将为他的当然接班人。我甚至问他：「你有这个指定你接班人的权力吗？」他的回答：「我绝对有。」

ReadShift 双语翻译

Now, back to me in 1984 and the two offers I had received.

The first offer came from a prominent venture capitalist headquartered in Manhattan, New York. After three highly compatible meetings, he offered me a "General Partner" position in his VC fund, with very attractive terms: (1) Fixed income only slightly below my TI level; (2) A generous "carry interest" in his existing large fund; (3) In a semiconductor company he had just invested in, he wanted me as a director with stock options; (4) He wanted me to head a Dallas office he planned to open. He would help me raise capital for that office, and I would receive substantial carry interest from that fund.

A week later, I received the second offer — from General Instruments.

In the 1983 Fortune 500 rankings, GI sat approximately between 300th and 400th (TI was within the top 100). It was a diversified company: broadband, semiconductors, wagering products (e.g., betting machines at racetracks, government lottery machines), and "computer products" (all acquired small companies, to be spruiced up and either taken public or sold to others).

GI's Chairman was Frank Griek. Over two months, he interviewed me five times — apparently testing my demeanor in different settings.
