Two of these five conversations were at his Arizona ranch; two were in his office or conference rooms; one was at an upscale restaurant. In all five interviews, I was the main speaker, relating my life experience and ambitions. He also briefly told me how he had reached the pinnacle of GI.

What interested me more: he said he was four years older than me and planned to retire within a few years, and I would be his natural successor. I even asked him: "Do you have that authority to designate your successor?" His answer: "I absolutely do."

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
General Partner and carry interest (高级合伙人与附带利益)—创投基金中，「普通合伙人」（GP）负责基金运营，享有约20%的投资收益作为「附带利益」（carry）；「附带利益」是创投和私募基金行业最核心的激励机制——它让基金经理的回报与投资人利益高度对齐。
Natural successor (当然接班人)—歇基宣称将指定张忠谋为他的接班人——这是一个极为诱人也极为危险的承诺；在接班政治中，「口头承诺」和「实际执行」之间往往存在巨大鸿沟——尤其是当「承诺者」不再掌权时。

除了花那么多时间与我面谈，歇基还专程去达拉斯拜访我以前的德仪上司——董事长夏伯特和总裁彪希，询问他们对我的意见。

他开出的邀聘条件也很优渥：（一）薪资及花红比我在德仪颠峰时期还高；（二）我的头衔是总经理暨营运长（President and COO）；（三）我也是董事；（四）相当优厚的股票承购权。

现在要比较通用和创投基金了，到底接受哪一个邀聘？我以兴奋的心情考虑这问题，因为看起来，两者之中无论哪一个都比我在德仪最后处境要好得多。从经济层面看，创投基金机会比较「无限」，因为有「附带利益」；但从我能否「适任」层面考量，似乎通用的机会对我比较适宜——毕竟这是一个公司经营的工作，我已有二十几年经验。

撇开经济，考量「前途」，那么通用的前途就是通用的颠峰——董事长暨CEO，一个相当规模公司的首长。这不是一向的目标吗？而创投的前途，只是赚更多钱而已。

我考虑了几天，也与两位我尊敬的前德仪同事讨论。几天后我决定：接受通用的邀请！

一九八四年一月十六日，我以电话告诉歇基我接受他的聘请。他立刻的反应是：「我今天要喝个半醉，因为找到你了！」我的职位——董事、总经理暨营运长——都需要通用董事会通过，而通用下次董事会是二月二十一日，所以我们决定我在二月十九日抵纽约，二十一日董事会通过我的职务后就上任。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Beyond investing all that time in interviewing me, Griek traveled to Dallas to visit my former TI superiors — Chairman Shepherd and President Shep — to ask their opinions of me.

His offer was also very generous: (1) Salary and bonus higher than my TI peak; (2) Title of President and Chief Operating Officer; (3) Board directorship; (4) Very generous stock options.

Now to compare GI and the VC fund — which offer should I take? I considered the question with excitement because either option was vastly better than my final situation at TI. Economically, the VC fund offered more "unlimited" upside through carry interest. But in terms of "fit," GI seemed more suitable — it was a operating business role, and I had over twenty years of experience running businesses.

Putting economics aside and considering "future prospects" — GI's future peak meant its chairmanship and CEO position: the head of a substantial company. Wasn't this always my goal? The VC path was just about making more money.

I deliberated for several days and discussed with two respected former TI colleagues. A few days later, I decided: accept GI's offer!

On January 16, 1984, I called Griek to say I accepted. His immediate reaction: "I'm going to get half-drunk today, because I found you!" My positions — Director, President, and COO — required board approval. The next board meeting was February 21, so we decided I would arrive in New York on February 19, and upon board approval on the 21st, I would assume office.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Operational role vs. financial role (运营角色 vs. 财务角色)—张忠谋在「运营公司」和「做创投入」之间选择了前者——这反映了他对自己核心能力的认知：他是经营者，不是投资者；在职业选择中，「做什么」比「赚多少」更能决定长期满足感。
References from former bosses (以前上司的背书)—歇基专程拜访夏伯特和彪希，询问他们对张忠谋的评价；在高阶招聘中，「背景调查」（reference check）是最后也是最重要的一步——前上司的评价往往决定最终录用。

通用器材公司

上任的头几个月，我本来预备是「学习」时期。几个月后我就知道，通用总经理并不那么好做。

第一，虽然通用的十几个不同事业遍布全美国——例如宽频的总部在马里兰，半导体总部在纽约长岛，公司最大的工厂又在中国台湾——在头几个月内，我到了每个事业的总部，试图熟悉每一事业的业务，但并不很成功。例如宽频是通用最大的事业，但其业务在我过去经验之外。

我不是有四个资深副总，每人负责几个事业吗？他们不是都应该熟悉各自的事业吗？的确，他们相当熟悉各自的事业单位；但前文已提到，这四位中两位「接受」我，两位反对我。在头几个月内，我就发现：即使「接受」我的两位，对我也不过持敷衍态度而已；而反对我的，的确相当敌对。况且，假这四位副总都能好好经营各自的事业单位，歇基为什么要我？

这最后问题——「歇基为什么要我」的答案，也在我上任的头几个月发现了，与我想像的很不一样。

我的认知是：从众多的通用事业内，选择几个可出成长的（我起初想的是半导体和宽频），再从技术层面着手，扩展研发，把这几个事业培养起来，把通用建立为一个大公司。

这与歇基的期待完全不同！歇基对我在我在上任后的几个月才渐渐透露出来。他要我做他的伙伴，买进小公司，整顿一下，再以高价卖出或上市；他的最高目标，是在他退休前，把整个通用都卖出去！

ReadShift 双语翻译

General Instruments

The first few months in office were meant to be a "learning" period. Within months I discovered that being GI GM was not so easy.

First, though GI's十余 different businesses were scattered across America — broadband HQ in Maryland, semiconductor HQ on Long Island, the company's largest factory in Taiwan — in the first months I visited each business's HQ and tried to become familiar with each one, with limited success. For example: broadband was GI's largest business but outside my prior experience.

Didn't I have four Senior VPs, each responsible for several businesses? Weren't they supposed to know their own units? Indeed, they knew their own units well. But as noted earlier, two of the four "accepted" me and two opposed me. Within the first months, I found that even the two who "accepted" me treated me with barely concealed perfunctoriness, while those who opposed me were genuinely hostile. Besides, if all four VPs could manage their units well, why did Griek need me at all?

The answer to that final question — "Why did Griek want me?" — also emerged within my first few months, and it was quite different from what I had imagined.

My understanding was: among GI's many businesses, select a few that could grow (I initially thought semiconductors and broadband, as both were foundational information industries), then approach them from a technology perspective, expand R&D, and nurture these businesses to build GI into a major company.

This was completely different from Griek's expectations! Griek's expectations of me only became apparent months after I took office. He wanted me to be his partner in buying small companies, turning them around, then selling them at a premium or taking them public. His ultimate goal was to sell the entire company before his retirement!

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Strategic intent mismatch (战略意图错配)—张忠谋想「建立大公司」，歇基想「把公司卖掉」——这两种意图在根本上是对立的；在并购和重组中，「builder vs. flipper」是最致命的认知错配——双方在入职前从未对「成功」的定义达成共识。
VP hostility as organizational immunity reaction (副总敌意作为组织免疫反应)—组织中的资深主管对空降总经理产生敌意，类似于生物体的「排异反应」；在高管空降案例中，「2接受 vs. 2反对」是危险信号——它意味着变革推动者尚未形成足够的多数联盟。

其实「买卖公司」是「私募基金」的正常业务，八〇年代在美国也已有好几家「私募基金」出现。只是，以科技公司之名行「私募基金」之实，在当时还是相当新的做法。

在我「密集学习」期间，歇基就正在积极进行购买一家小公司。我们的办公室相邻，他常到我办公室，并随意打断我的思考，告诉我他的进展，询问我的意见。他也常提起通用的几个赔钱单位：「什么时候你能把它们整理好？让我们把它卖掉？」、「要不要再换这个赔钱单位的总经理？」歇基是爱尔兰裔，当时和我一样是单身。在我上任后的头半年，通用业绩不错，我与歇基相处尚称愉快。他常在下午六、七时走到我办公室，看见我还在，邀我一起去一家百老汇爱尔兰裔人开的牛排餐厅。几杯酒後，歇基会对我说：「英理士，也许你的经营能力超过我；但在金融方面（买进卖出公司），你可以从我这边学到一点东西。」就在这个时期，我与一位麦肯锡公司顾问有一次有趣的谈话。这位顾问常常来通用，但是他的客户似乎只是歇基，对我只是碰见时「哈罗」而已。这次他特别找我喝咖啡，在喝咖啡时说：「你好像很有战略思想，与歇基恰恰相反，他富有战术思想。」我回答：「我们两人互补，不很好吗？」他猛烈地摇头：「不。CEO有战略思想，COO富有战术思想，才算互补。你们两人的位置恰恰相反，是很坏的配合。」这是很高的智慧！对我当时是新闻，但我后来一直记得。只是直到现在，我还不知道，这位顾问是否已接到歇基的指示，要给我第一个警告！

ReadShift 双语翻译

Buying and selling companies was, in fact, standard "private equity" business, and several PE firms had already emerged in 1980s America. It was still relatively novel, however, to operate a PE-like strategy under the banner of a technology company.

During my "intensive learning" period, Griek was already actively pursuing the acquisition of a small company. Our offices were adjacent. He would frequently drop into my office, interrupting my train of thought, to update me on his progress and solicit my views. He also often brought up GI's several money-losing units: "When can you turn these around so we sell them?" or "Should we replace this unit's GM?"

Griek was Irish-American and, like me, single at the time. In my first half-year, GI's performance was decent, and Griek and I got along reasonably well. He would often come to my office around 6 or 7 pm, see I was still there, and invite me to an Irish-owned steakhouse on Broadway. A few drinks in, Griek would say to me: "Morris, perhaps your operating ability exceeds mine; but in finance — buying and selling companies — you could learn a thing or two from me."

Around this time, I had a revealing conversation with a McKinsey consultant. This consultant came to GI frequently, but his client appeared to be Griek alone — he'd just say "hello" when he ran into me. This time, however, he specially asked me for coffee. During the coffee, he said: "You seem to have a strategic mind. Griek is the exact opposite — he has a tactical mind."

"We complement each other. Isn't that good?"

He shook his head vigorously: "No. The CEO having the strategic mind and the COO the tactical mind — that's complementarity. You two have it exactly backwards. That's a very poor fit."

This was profound wisdom! It was news to me at the time, but I never forgot it. To this day, though, I don't know whether this consultant had already received instructions from Griek to deliver me a first warning!

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Strategic mind vs.战术思维的错配 (Strategic vs. Tactical mind mismatch)—麦肯锡顾问的核心判断——张忠谋有战略思维而歇基有战术思维，但公司职位安排（张为COO、歇基为CEO）恰恰要求相反的组合；在管理理论中，「CEO定战略、COO定战术」的经典分工在两人身上完全反转。
Private equity model inside a tech company (科技公司外壳内的私募模式)—以科技公司的躯壳行私募基金的买卖——这在八〇年代是一种创新（或伪装的）商业模式；「公司风险投资」与「私募收购」的界线，在于前者以战略协同为目的，后者以财务回报为目的。

在通用最后的几个月

一九八四年第三季起，市场渐不景气，通用业绩逆转。歇基的注意力马上从「买卖公司」转移到「维持业绩」。当然我也想维持业绩，但当我面对敷衍或敌视我的下属，自己又不熟悉大部分业务，无力回天时，歇基和我的关系很快地转坏了。

歇基富有战术思想，战术精髓在于反应快。在业绩逆转之时，他立刻雇回了一位与他战术思维差不多的前副总（名乔治），把乔治塞在我下面，而且要我手里的事业单位分几个给乔治。我从命。

乔治的确「新官上任三把火」，一上任就飞到他负责的事业单位所在地（加州、亚利桑那州、马里兰州），我很少在见到他，只有打电话。他常有好消息报告，但他的好消息都是治标性的，例如：「我把光电部门一些存货以廉价卖掉了」、「我得到某客户的同意把他们下个月要的货这个月就运出了」。当我问：「那下个月怎么办？」他居然说：「下个月再想办法。」其实下个月的「办法」，也不过与这个月一样——寅吃卯粮。

至于我谆谆教诲的「基本面」，乔治似乎毫不在意。

另一人事变更：负责半导体的资深副总辞职了。此人起初就反对我，后来也没有和我合作，所以我并不惋惜他的辞职，而且立刻任命半导体部门第二号人接位。但歇基似乎很不舍得此人，而且认为此人的离开是我不能留人，在歇基心目中，这是我不适任总经理的又一证据。

一九八五年二月八日，距我上任不到一年，我接到歇基从他亚利桑那州农场以「特邮」寄来的「绝对机密」备忘录（长达三页）：

「你与我对如何解决公司里六个单位的惊人亏损，并无共识。结论：Chang的精力太分散了。我要你集中精力在半导体和光电上；我要乔治集中在电脑产品上；我自己则主要集中在宽频和赌注产品上。」

ReadShift 双语翻译

The Final Months at GI

From the third quarter of 1984, the market turned, and GI's performance reversed. Griek's attention immediately shifted from "buying and selling companies" to "maintaining performance." Of course I wanted to maintain performance too, but facing subordinates who were either perfunctory or hostile, and myself still unfamiliar with most of the businesses, I was powerless to reverse the tide. Griek and my relationship quickly deteriorated.

Griek had a tactical mind, and tactical thinking prized fast reaction. Amid the performance reversal, he immediately rehired a former VP whose tactical mindset mirrored his own — named George — and inserted George beneath me, demanding that I transfer several business units from my purview to George. I complied.

George indeed "hit the ground running" — upon starting, he flew to where his businesses were located (California, Arizona, Maryland) and I rarely saw him in New York, only hearing him by phone. He frequently reported good news, but his good news was all symptomatic treatment, such as: "I sold off some optoelectronics inventory at a fire-sale price" or "I got a customer to agree to take next month's shipment this month." When I asked, "Then what happens next month?" he would actually say, "We'll figure out next month when we get there." In reality, next month's "solution" was no different from this month's — borrowing from next year's harvest to feed this year.

As for the "fundamentals" I earnestly taught, George seemed utterly uninterested.

Another personnel change: the Senior VP in charge of semiconductors resigned. This person had opposed me from the start and never cooperated with me, so I did not regret his departure and immediately appointed the semiconductor division's #2 person as his replacement. But Griek seemed quite reluctant to lose this person and viewed his departure as evidence that I couldn't retain people — in Griek's mind, further proof that I was unsuitable as GM.

On February 8, 1985 — less than a year into my tenure — I received an "absolute confidential" memorandum (three pages long) from Griek, sent via "special mail" from his Arizona ranch:

"You and I have no consensus on how to address the staggering losses in six of our units. Conclusion: Chang's attention is too scattered. I want you to focus on semiconductors and optoelectronics; I want George to focus on computer products; I myself will focus primarily on broadband and wagering products."

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Tactical vs. strategic in downturn (不景气时的战术与战略)—不景气时歇基转向「战术」——卖存货、催客户提货；但这些都是「治标」而非「治本」；在不景气时，「治标」是战术，「治本」是战略——张忠谋认为真正该做的是改善基本面（研发、产品力），歇基则认为先撑过眼前再说。
Special-mail memorandum as conflict escalation (特邮备忘录作为冲突升级)—歇基以「特邮」寄出「绝对机密」备忘录——这是正式的组织警告，也是对张忠谋职权的公开削限；在企业管理中，书面备忘录通常意味着「口头谈判已失败，转入正式冲突程序」。

四天后我答覆（四页）：

一、让乔治集中在电脑产品，我不反对。

二、要我只集中在半导体和光电上，我不接受；我加入通用，是做全公司的总经理，而不是来做半导体和光电部门总经理。

三、你自己要集中在宽频和赌博产品上——我认为这不是你最好利用时间的办法，但如你坚持要这样做我也不反对。只是，你的角色是支持我，而不是代替我。

歇基的要求和我的答覆当然是南辕北辙。他要把我的角色削减到半导体和光电；我却坚持继续做我的总经理。我的答覆等于与他决裂。

五天後，歇基回到纽约，我们有一次长谈，但长谈也解决不了问题。这样的局面又僵持了一个多月。终于，三月二十六日，歇基召我一早到他的办公室，见面就说：「我要你自动辞职。」「为什么？」「你的下属通通都不要你。」一个多月我以为是「僵持」的时间，已让歇基有充分时间与每一个我的直接下属谈话（除资深副总外，还有好几个副总），而且唆使他们叛离我。离开歇基办公室後，我打电话给每一个直属部下「告别」，只有两人肯接我的电话。

当天下午法务长就让我看即将发出的新闻稿：

「通用器材公司董事长暨CEO弗兰克‧歇基今天宣布他已达成共识，在此共识下，总经理暨营运长张博士将辞去他现有职务，生效期为四月十五日。此后张博士将继续为通用咨询。」歇基先生说：「我们非常遗憾做此宣布，因为董事会都尊敬且钦佩英理士‧张。我们很高兴张博士将继续为我们咨询。」这新闻稿不愧是歇基和法务长的精心傑作——既表达了我的辞职是他主动（「共识」），又为我留了一点面子（「尊敬、钦佩」、「咨询」）。

我的辞职新闻在次日《纽约时报》及《华尔街日报》就出现了。我又失业了。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Four days later, I replied (four pages):

1. Letting George focus on computer products — I don't oppose.

2. Asking me to focus only on semiconductors and optoelectronics — I do not accept. I joined GI to be GM of the entire company, not GM of the semiconductor and optoelectronics divisions.

3. You yourself want to focus on broadband and wagering — I don't think this is the best use of your time, but if you insist, I won't oppose. Only, your role is to support me, not replace me.

Griek's demands and my response were diametrically opposed. He wanted to reduce my role to semiconductors and optoelectronics; I insisted on continuing as GM of the whole company. My response was tantamount to a break with him.

Five days later, Griek returned to New York and we had a long talk, but even a long talk couldn't resolve the impasse. This stalemate dragged on for over a month. Finally, on March 26, Griek summoned me to his office first thing in the morning, and upon seeing me, said: "I want you to resign voluntarily." "Why?" "None of your subordinates want you."

The month I thought was "stalemate" had given Griek ample time to talk with every one of my direct reports (and several VPs beyond the senior VPs) and orchestrate their defection. After leaving Griek's office, I called each of my direct reports to "say goodbye." Only two would take my calls.

That afternoon, the General Counsel showed me the press release about to go out:

"General Instruments Corporation Chairman and CEO Frank Griek announced today that he has reached a consensus with President and COO Dr. Morris Chang, under which Dr. Chang will resign his current positions, effective April 15. Dr. Chang will continue as a consultant to General Instruments."

"Mr. Griek stated: 'We are very sorry to make this announcement, as the Board and I hold Dr. Chang in high regard and high esteem. We are pleased that Dr. Chang will continue to consult for us.'"

This press release was a masterful product of Griek and the General Counsel — it presented my resignation as his initiative ("consensus"), while preserving some face for me ("high regard, high esteem," "consult").

The resignation news appeared in the next day's New York Times and Wall Street Journal.

I was unemployed again.

修辞赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

「你的下属通通都不要你。」——歇基以这句话作为辞退张忠谋的理由。这句话的残酷在于：它不仅是一个管理判断，更是一个人格鉴定——「你作为一个领导者，已经众叛亲离」。一个月前还以「我今天要喝个半醉，因为找到你了」欢迎张忠谋的歇基，现在又以「共识」的面具将其驱逐。张忠谋在短短一年中经历了从被追捧到被驱逐的剧烈跌宕——这也是他职业生涯中最短、也最惨烈的一段。 "None of your subordinates want you." — Griek used this as his reason for removing Chang. The cruelty of this statement lies in the fact that it is not merely a management judgment but a character indictment: "As a leader, you have been universally abandoned." The same Griek who a month earlier had welcomed Chang with "I'm going to get half-drunk today, because I found you" now expelled him behind a mask of "consensus." Chang experienced, in a single year, a dramatic rollercoaster from being courted to being expelled — the shortest and most brutal chapter of his career.

IC设计公司（无晶圆厂）先驱

在通用最后几个月的凄风苦雨中，我接触了两位「IC设计公司」创业者，并且为通用做成了第一笔「晶圆代工」生意。这段经验值得在此一提。

一九八四年十一月，戈登·坎普（Gordon Campbell）来访。我们不熟，但互相知道对方是谁。他找我的目的是要通用投资他现在想办的公司——「要五千万美元投资。」我问：「你有营运计画吗？」他说：「没有。」但又指指他的脑袋说：「都在这里。」我告诉他通用应该有兴趣投资，但所有投资案必须经过董事会，我要有一份正式营运计画才能提到董事会去。坎普说：「没问题，我回去後就写，两星期内寄给你。」两星期过去了，三星期过去了，没有收到计画。我就打电话给坎普。坎普回答：「啊，对不起，英理士，我不需要你投资了。」「为什么？」「因为我不需要五千万，只要五百万就成；五百万我随便凑凑就凑得起来。」「为什么只要五百万？」「因为我不建晶圆厂了，把晶圆制造包给别人。」对此，这个投资案就这样无疾而终。後来坎普创办了Chips and Technologies，果然是最无晶圆厂的IC设计公司，相当成功，後来也是台积电的客户。

坎普访问後几星期，一位素昧平生的创业者——经由通用半导体总经理的介绍——也来看我，他名叫乔治·布雷果思（George Perlegos），已创办了Atmel，也是无晶圆厂的IC设计公司，现在要通用替他做晶圆代工。那时我们的晶圆厂正缺订单，所以我立刻指示半导体总经理与乔治谈条件。此後两个月，我常常听到总经理的埋怨：「乔治在我们工厂里指指点点，侮辱我们的工程师」、「乔治要改变我们的制程」、「这是我们的厂，好像乔治认为是他的」。虽然很多埋怨，但案子仍在进行，而且最後，我听说要开始「试片」了。一直到我辞职前六天，总经理很紧张地打电话给我：「乔治大喊大骂，情绪失去控制，说我们建议的合同太苛刻。」次日，我亲自电话乔治，与他谈判。在那天的日记上，我记下：「我稍作让步」。但是五天后我就离开通用。後来听说这桩「晶圆代工」案子继续下去，而且通用和Atmel双方都还算满意。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Pioneers of IC Design (Fabless) Companies

During the windy, rain-drenched final months at GI, I met two "IC design company" entrepreneurs and closed GI's first "foundry" deal. This experience merits recounting.

In November 1984, Gordon Campbell visited. We didn't know each other well but knew of each other. His purpose in seeing me was to ask GI to invest in the company he was starting: "I need $50 million in investment." I asked: "Do you have a business plan?" He said: "No." But pointing to his head: "It's all here here." I told him GI should be interested, but all investments required board approval, and I would need a formal business plan before taking it to the board. Campbell said: "No problem, I'll write it and send it within two weeks."

Two weeks passed, three weeks passed — no plan received. I called Campbell. He replied: "Oh, sorry, Morris, I don't need your investment anymore." "Why?" "Because I don't need $50 million — $5 million will do. I can scrape together $5 million easily." "Why only $5 million?" "Because I'm not building a fab. I'm outsourcing wafer manufacturing to others."

With that, the investment deal came to nothing. Campbell went on to found Chips and Technologies, indeed one of the earliest fabless IC design companies, quite successful, and later a TSMC customer.

A few weeks after Campbell's visit, a stranger — introduced by the GI semiconductor GM — also came to see me. His name was George Perlegos. He had founded Atmel, also a fabless IC design company, and now he wanted GI to do wafer foundry work for him. Our fab was short on orders at the time, so I immediately directed the semiconductor GM to negotiate terms with George. Over the next two months, I frequently heard the GM's complaints: "George points and pokes around our fab, insulting our engineers." "George wants to change our process." "It's our fab, but George acts like it's his." Despite many complaints, the deal progressed, and eventually, I heard they were about to begin "test runs." Until six days before my resignation, the GM nervously called me: "George is yelling and cursing, emotionally out of control, saying our proposed contract was too harsh." The next day, I personally called George to negotiate. In my diary that day, I wrote: "Made minor concessions." But five days later I left GI. I heard later that the foundry deal went forward, and both GI and Atmel were reasonably satisfied.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Fabless IC design company (无晶圆厂IC设计公司)—指只从事IC设计而不自建晶圆厂的公司；「无晶圆厂」（fabless）模式是半导体产业专业化分工的起点——它需要一个可信赖的「纯代工」夥伴，而这正是台积电後来扮演的角色。
Foundry as contract manufacturing (晶圆代工作为契约制造)—指代工厂为其他公司的设计制造晶圆；「晶圆代工」的商业模式在台积电之前并不成熟——IDM（整合组件制造商）通常只为自己制造，而「纯代工」的概念在八〇年代中期还是一个崭新的、未被验证的商业模式。

半年後（一九八五年九月）我就在台湾决定台积电的「专业晶圆代工」商业模式。在思考台积电商业模式时，我也想起了戈登和乔治——他们并不是我决定台积电模式的主要原因（主要原因要请你继续读下去），但在我脑海中，戈登和乔治也是推动「专业晶圆代工」的一股小小力量。

从「经营顾问」到「天使投资人」

我从通用辞职新闻在各大报发表後，家中及办公室电话又是铃声不断，但这次我不急著找工作了。通用的经验，对我是很大的刺激——短短一年，从歇基的「我今天要喝个半醉，因为找到你了」，到他的「与张博士达成共识，在此共识下张博士将辞去他现有职务」——短短一年，有这么大的变化！

当然，这也不能完全怪歇基，我根本就不应该接受这个职位！我没搞清楚歇基和通用董事会要的是什么，我根本不适任他们所需要的！

我需要沉淀下来，给我自己充分时间考虑下一个工作。我失业时则是初春，纽约的春天是最宜人的季节——至少在纽约度过春天吧！暂时，先做一下「经营顾问」。

我印了一盒名片：「英理士‧张，经营顾问」，办公室就是我的家——纽约市第五大道、川普大厦——很光鲜的地址；我也为自己订了顾问费——每天一千八百美元。

两件顾问案倒是接踵而来：第一件来自一位企业主要我去加州跑一趟，了解一下他在那边的研究室，回来告诉他我的感想。我照他的意思做了，收了他两天的顾问费，但後来没有下文。第二件来自一位创投家，他要我列席一次他最近投资的半导体公司的董事会。我去了，也依他的要求发表了一些意见。会后，这位创投家要我当这公司的董事——他说他付不起每天一千八百美元的顾问费，但可以让我以创办者价格投资这公司的股票（这就是所谓「天使投资人」）。我算了一下，觉得可能获利远大于可能损失，所以就接受了创投家的条件。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Half a year later (September 1985), in Taiwan I would decide on TSMC's "dedicated foundry" business model. When contemplating the TSMC model, I also thought of Gordon and George — they were not the primary reason for the TSMC model (the primary reason will emerge as you keep reading), but in my mind, Gordon and George were also a small force pushing me toward the "dedicated foundry" concept.

After the resignation news ran in major newspapers, phones at home and office rang constantly, but this time I wasn't in a hurry to find a job. The GI experience was a tremendous shock — in a single year, from Griek's "I'm going to get half-drunk today, because I found you" to "reached a consensus with Dr. Chang, under which Dr. Chang will resign his current positions." In a single year, such a dramatic change!

Of course, I couldn't entirely blame Griek. I should never have accepted this position! I hadn't understood what Griek and the GI board wanted — I fundamentally wasn't suited for what they needed.

I needed to settle down and give myself ample time to consider my next move. When I became unemployed, it was early spring — New York's spring is the most pleasant season. At least spend spring in New York! For the moment, I would do some "management consulting."

I printed a box of business cards: "Morris Chang, Management Consultant." My office was my home — Fifth Avenue, Trump Tower, New York — a very prestigious address. I also set my consulting fee: $1,800 per day.

Two consulting engagements came my way: The first was from a business owner who wanted me to visit California to review his R&D lab and report back my impressions. I did as asked, collected two days' fees, but there was no follow-up. The second was from a venture capitalist who asked me to attend a board meeting of a semiconductor company he had recently invested in. I attended and offered some observations as requested. After the meeting, the VC asked me to join the company's board — he said he couldn't afford $1,800 per day in consulting fees but could let me invest in the company's stock at founder's price (this is what's known as an "angel investment"). I evaluated it and concluded the potential upside far outweighed the potential loss, so I accepted the VC's terms.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Angel investor (天使投资人)—指以个人资金投资新创公司，通常在新创公司成立初期；天使投资人的典型回报是「以创办者价格获得股权」（founder's price equity）——如果公司上市，初始投资的回报可达数十倍甚至数百倍。
Management consultant as unemployment bridge (经营顾问作为失业桥梁)—张忠谋以「经营顾问」身份度过失业期，每天一千八百美元；这是一种典型的「过渡期策略」——给伤者时间疗愈、给思考者时间反思。

第十三章小结：通用之後

一九八五年春天，张忠谋失业了——他第二次失业了。在德仪被边缘化辞退是一次；在通用被歇基以「共识」驱逐是第二次。这次失业後，他没有立即找工作。他印了「经营顾问」名片，每天收费一千八百美元。他接了几个小案子，做了几个天使投资。他花了五个月时间疗愈通用的创伤，也与父母和女儿享受了最後一段频繁相处的时光。

这五个月的停顿不是懈怠，而是深思。张忠谋在等待一个真正属于自己的机会——这个机会不在美国创投圈，不在美国大企业的董事会，而在太平洋对岸的一个蕞尔小岛。

一九八五年八月，在美国待了三十六年又一个月後，张忠谋要到台湾去了。

序言

台積電篇一卷首

台积电篇一·卷首｜与命运的约会（一九八五－一九九○）

ReadShift 双语翻译

TSMC Part I — Prologue: A Date with Destiny (1985–1990)

章节

台積電篇一第十四章

张忠谋

台积电篇一·第十四章｜我与台湾的渊源

来自台湾的同学

一九六一年前，我不认识任何来自台湾的人。一九六一年，德仪派遣我到斯坦福读博，在与他们的交谈中，我在斯坦福认识了从台湾来的同学，对台湾有初步的认识。

那时，半导体公司已纷纷到低工资的东南亚设立封装测试厂，他们选择的地点大部分在香港。德仪比较保守，还没有到东南亚设厂，但我已认识来自台湾的同学，也问他们对跨国公司利用低工资劳力的见解。他们异口同声地认为：对低工资地区，跨国公司去设厂绝对是好事，因为低工资地区有优秀的大学工程职校毕业的技工人才，也有勤奋的作业员——总之，跨国公司去香港而不去台湾，大概是因为并不知道台湾的好处。

那时我虽不认识台湾，但认识香港；香港给我的印象是一个商业城市，似乎很不适合发展工业，所以我也下意识地接受了同学对台湾的偏见。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Classmates from Taiwan

Before 1961, I did not know anyone from Taiwan. In 1961, TI sent me to Stanford for my PhD, and during my time there, I met several classmates from Taiwan. Through conversations with them, I gained a preliminary understanding of Taiwan.

At that time, semiconductor companies were already rushing to set up assembly and test facilities in low-wage Southeast Asia, mostly in Hong Kong. TI was more conservative and had not yet established factories in Southeast Asia, but I had gotten to know classmates from Taiwan and asked their views on multinational companies exploiting low-wage labor. They unanimously believed that for low-wage regions, it was absolutely a good thing for multinationals to build factories there, because these regions had excellent technical talent graduating from universities and vocational schools, as well as diligent workers. In short, the reason multinationals went to Hong Kong rather than Taiwan was probably that they simply did not know Taiwan's advantages.

At that time, although I did not know Taiwan, I did know Hong Kong. Hong Kong impressed me as a commercial city, seemingly quite unsuitable for industrial development, so I subconsciously accepted my classmates' bias against Taiwan.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Assembly and test facility (封装测试厂)—半导体后段工序工厂，负责将晶圆切割成芯片并进行封装和测试；在半导体产业链中，封装测试是劳动力密集的环节，因此最早向低工资地区转移。
Vocational school talent (职校人才)—指职业学校培养的技术工人；在半导体制造业中，职校毕业生通常担任技术员角色，是产线运转的关键人力。

德仪新加坡与台湾设厂

一九六八年德仪终于决定去东南亚设厂，德仪总裁夏伯特先选了香港，但我推荐台湾，总裁也接受了。他与我一起到台北见经济部长李国鼎，想不到遇到困难，只好暂时搁置在台湾建厂计划。

一年后（一九六九年），台湾设厂的困难解决，德仪就来台湾建厂，但那时德仪的海外厂已不归我管；直到一九七二年，我当上了半导体集团总经理，全球所有德仪半导体单位，包括海外厂，都在我属下。此后直到一九七七年，我大约每年都来台湾视察一次，总是与东京、吉隆坡、新加坡同一旅程，每次在台湾逗留一两天，匆匆来、匆匆走，停留的地方通常只有机场、旅馆，位在中和的德仪台湾厂。

夏伯特与我转程去新加坡，几乎立刻与新加坡政府谈妥，就把原本要到台湾设厂的计划，包括在达拉斯待命出发的厂长及干部一并移到新加坡。

ReadShift 双语翻译

TI's Singapore and Taiwan Factory Decisions

In 1968, TI finally decided to build a factory in Southeast Asia. TI President Shepherd initially chose Hong Kong, but I recommended Taiwan, and the President accepted. He and I traveled together to Taipei to meet Minister of Economic Affairs Li Guoding. Unexpectedly, we encountered difficulties and had to shelve the Taiwan factory plan temporarily.

A year later (1969), the difficulties for building in Taiwan were resolved, and TI came to build a factory in Taiwan. However, by then TI's overseas factories were no longer under my management. It was not until 1972, when I became General Manager of the Semiconductor Group, that all TI semiconductor units worldwide — including overseas factories — came under my authority. From then until 1977, I visited Taiwan about once a year, always on the same trip as Tokyo, Kuala Lumpur, and Singapore. Each time I stayed only a day or two, coming and going in a hurry, typically visiting only the airport, the hotel, and the TI Taiwan factory in Zhonghe.

Shepherd and I diverted to Singapore and almost immediately reached an agreement with the Singapore government. We moved the entire plan originally intended for Taiwan — including the factory manager and staff already on standby in Dallas — to Singapore.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Semiconductor Group General Manager (半导体集团总经理)—德州仪器公司半导体事业群的最高负责人，管辖全球所有半导体设计、制造、销售单位；这是张忠谋在德仪职业生涯的最高职位。
P&L responsibility (损益责任)—Profit and Loss responsibility，指管理者对业务单位的收入、成本及利润负责；拥有完整P&L责任的总经理是真正意义上的业务一把手。

工研院IC计划的开始

一九七五年，在我德仪半导体集团总经理任内，大约是营销部的属下告诉我德仪收到一封台湾工研院的「招标」函——征求IC技术移转，以及相关知识产权的授权。德仪当时政策不卖技术（十几年后，德仪窃此政策改变），所以我毫不犹豫地决定不投标。许多年后，我才知道工研院当年发了不少招标函，但只有少数厂商投标。

一九七六年一月，一位已自美国RCA退休、但仍住在普林斯顿的潘文渊先生要来达拉斯「请教」我，说是为了台湾IC计划招标。我在电话上又对潘先生讲了一遍德仪不卖技术的政策，但潘说他不是要德仪移转技术，而是有别的问题要「请教」，我就与他约了一月二十二日下午在我达拉斯办公室见面。

那天潘与另一位工研院顾问凌君同来。潘的主要问题是：「CMOS是不是最有希望的IC技术？」对这问题，我有一个肯定的答复：「是。」在一九七一年我接手德仪MOS部门后，我历经「PMOS」、「NMOS」，最后「CMOS」。站在一九七六年一月的立足点，CMOS成为最终胜出的技术，在我心中，已没有什么疑问。

潘、凌两位似乎很满意的答复。多年后，我才知道我对潘的肯定答复的确是台湾买RCA CMOS技术的最后关卡（至少是最后关卡之一）。紧接着潘的达拉斯行，四十二天以后（一九七六年三月五日），工研院就与RCA签约，再一个多月后（四月二十六日）工研院就派出第一批工程师去RCA实习。后来几十年IC技术的发展，的确以CMOS为主流，所以我一九七六年给潘者的答复没有错。

ReadShift 双语翻译

The Genesis of ITRI's IC Program

In 1975, during my tenure as TI's Semiconductor Group General Manager, I was informed by someone in marketing that TI had received an "invitation to bid" from Taiwan's Industrial Technology Research Institute (ITRI). The solicitation sought IC technology transfer and related intellectual property licensing. TI's policy at the time was not to sell technology (a policy TI would quietly change a decade later), so I decided without hesitation not to bid. Many years later, I learned that ITRI had sent out numerous bids that year, but only a handful of companies responded.

In January 1976, a Mr. Pan Wen-yuan, retired from RCA but still living in Princeton, wanted to come to Dallas to "consult" me, saying it was about Taiwan's IC program bidding. On the phone, I repeated TI's no-technology-sales policy, but Pan said he wasn't asking TI to transfer technology — he had other questions to "consult" me about. We scheduled a meeting for the afternoon of January 22 in my Dallas office.

That day Pan came with another ITRI consultant, Mr. Ling. Pan's main question was: "Is CMOS the most promising IC technology?" I gave an affirmative answer: "Yes." After taking over TI's MOS division in 1971, I had journeyed through PMOS, NMOS, and ultimately CMOS. Standing at the vantage point of January 1976, CMOS had emerged as the definitive winning technology — of this I had no doubt.

Pan and Ling seemed satisfied with my answer. Years later, I learned that my affirmative response to Pan was indeed the final checkpoint (or at least one of them) for Taiwan's decision to purchase RCA's CMOS technology. Just 42 days after Pan's Dallas visit (March 5, 1976), ITRI signed with RCA, and a little over a month later (April 26), ITRI dispatched its first batch of engineers to RCA for training. The subsequent decades of IC technology development confirmed CMOS as mainstream — so my answer to Pan in 1976 was correct.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Technology transfer (技术移转)—指将技术知识、专利、工艺流程从一方转移给另一方的商业行为；在半导体产业中，技术移转通常以授权金或权利金的形式进行。
CMOS (Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor，互补金属氧化物半导体)—一种低功耗的IC制造技术，将成为全球半导体产业的主流制程；张忠谋在1976年即预判CMOS的最终胜出，这是他技术判断力的早期体现。
Invitation to bid (招标函)—政府或公共机构为特定项目向潜在供应商发出的正式邀请；工研院以招标方式寻求IC技术移转，体现了当时台湾政府推动产业升级的决心。

一九七六年近代工程技术讨论会

与潘文渊会面的同月，秘书忽然告诉我有一位自称是台湾行政院秘书长的人从洛杉矶打电话给我，要和我讲话，我满腹怀疑地接起电话。对方自我介绍他是费骅，行政院秘书长，也是中国工程师学会会长，电话目的是邀请我参加当年七月在台北举行的近代工程技术讨论会，并做专题演说。我在电话上答应考虑，挂了电话后就打电报给德仪台湾，嘱他们打听一下费秘书长及近代工程技尤讨论会的来历。德仪台湾很快就给我正面回音，七月会期也正值德仪假期，我就答应了。

那会议是我与台湾关系的真正开始。我利用德仪的假期赴会。记得我在演说前一天早上就到台北，在圆山大饭店登记后就到山下圆山联谊会，坐在游泳池旁，准备我次日的演讲。虽然台北七月相当炎热，但我来自更炎热的达拉斯，并不觉得不舒服。

一九七六年我还在德仪事业的「高原」上，还是总公司「成长委员会」主席，理论上负责全公司的成长发展策略。那时人们正大做价格一半的电子表，我的演讲就以「电子表」为题，阐述德仪如何先从「市场研究」决定「目标电子表」的性能、设计，以及最利推销的价格；然后，如何动员内部研发、工程、生产部门，不但要做到目标的性能和设计，而且要做到使得公司能在二十美元零售价赚到合理利润的成本。

这场演讲相当受欢迎。在一九七六年的台湾，科技产业相当落后。我所讲的世界级科技公司如何有计划地推出新产品的故事，绝大听众是第一次听到。

听众中有一位是李国鼎政务委员。此时离我一九六八年因筹备德仪台湾而来台拜访时任经济部部长的他，已经有八年之久。李政委当时六十六岁，一生服务政府，历任行政院美援运用委员会秘书长、经济部部长、财政部部长等财经要职，但在一九七六年，他刚经历了重大的心脏手术。据他自己告诉我，蒋经国行政院院长为了减轻他的负担，请他担任科技方面的政务委员。国鼎先生虽在大学时修物理，但已离开科技多年，现在做了科技政委，当然想与世界级的科技公司建立关系；德仪正是这样的公司，何况里面还有一个华裔的高阶主管！

我演讲后李政委就趋前称赞，并约我午餐，此后无论我来台湾，或他去美国，他总会约我见面；每次他去美国，他总会要来德仪参观，看看有什么新发展。他也结识了刚自德仪董事长职位退休的海格底。

ReadShift 双语翻译

The 1976 Engineering Conference

In the same month as my meeting with Pan Wen-yuan, my secretary suddenly told me that someone claiming to be the Secretary-General of Taiwan's Executive Yuan was calling from Los Angeles and wished to speak with me. I picked up the phone full of skepticism. The caller introduced himself as Fei Hua, Secretary-General of the Executive Yuan and President of the Chinese Institute of Engineers. His purpose was to invite me to speak at the upcoming Engineering Conference in Taipei that July. I said I would consider it, and after hanging up, I cabled TI Taiwan to investigate the background of Secretary-General Fei and the conference. TI Taiwan quickly gave me a positive assessment. The July timing coincided with TI's holiday period, so I accepted.

That conference marked the true beginning of my relationship with Taiwan. I used TI's holiday to attend. I remember arriving in Taipei the morning before my speech, checking into the Grand Hotel, then going down to the Yuan Shan Club by the swimming pool to prepare for the next day's presentation. Although Taipei in July was quite humid and hot, I came from the even more sweltering Dallas and didn't find it uncomfortable.

In 1976, I was still on the "plateau" of my TI career, serving as chairman of the corporate Growth Committee, theoretically responsible for the company's growth and development strategy company-wide. At that time, everyone was making electronic watches at half the prevailing price. My speech took "the electronic watch" as its topic, describing how TI used market research to define the target watch's performance, design, and optimal selling price, and then mobilized internal R&D, engineering, and manufacturing not only to meet those performance and design targets but to achieve costs that would allow reasonable profit at a $20 retail price.

The speech was well received. In 1976 Taiwan, the technology industry was quite backward. The story of how a world-class technology company systematically brings new products to market was something most of the audience had never heard before.

Among the audience was Kuo-Ting Li (Li Guoding), a Minister without Portfolio. By then, eight years had passed since my first visit to Taiwan in 1968, when I had met him as Minister of Economic Affairs to discuss building the TI Taiwan factory. Minister Li was then 66, a lifelong government veteran who had served as Secretary-General of the Council for International Economic Cooperation, Minister of Economic Affairs, and Minister of Finance. But in 1976, he had just undergone major heart surgery. As he himself told me, Premier Chiang Ching-kuo had asked him to serve as Minister without Portfolio for technology to lighten his load. Although Mr. Li had studied physics in college, he had left technology behind long ago. Now as technology minister, he naturally wanted to build relationships with world-class technology companies. TI was precisely such a company — and what's more, it had a Chinese senior executive!

After my speech, Minister Li came forward to compliment me and invited me to lunch. From then on, whenever I visited Taiwan or he visited the United States, he would arrange to see me. Every time he came to the U.S., he would visit TI to see what new developments there were. He also became acquainted with Eric Haggerty, who had recently retired as TI's Chairman.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Growth Committee (成长委员会)—德仪最高管理层级的事业策略委员会，由董事长及总裁担任委员、主席负责全公司成长发展策略；张忠谋在一九七六年担任此委员会主席，但并无实权。
Market research → cost targeting (市场研究→成本目标法)—一种逆向定价方法——先通过市场研究确定消费者可接受的零售价，再反推各环节可容忍的成本上限；这是德州仪器在消费电子产品中常用的「按价值定价」方法。
MITI-style technology Minister (科技政委)—台湾政府中负责科技政策规划的政务委员；李国鼎担任此职期间，正是台湾从劳力密集产业向技术密集产业转型的关键期。

海格底与一九八一年台湾访问

此后李政委结识了刚自德仪董事长职位退休的海格底。一年后（一九七八年），海格底应李政委邀请，专程访问台湾一周，而且受李政委邀请组织行政院科技顾问团，此事已详述在本书第十章。

不幸海格底在一九八〇年患胰脏癌，英年早逝。自发现癌症至过世前后只不过几个月左右。在海格底病危时，德仪认为这是海格底个人的「隐私」，所以只有极少数人知道他病危的消息，我那时已在德仪「下山」途中，只知道海格底生病，不知道他病危。倒是在海格底病危期间再度访问德仪，没见到海格底，却被告知海格底病危。于是，在与我聚餐时，倒是他——一个外人——告诉我海格底病危。从我一脸惊异的表情，他也猜到我应已不在德仪核心圈内，并且直爽地问：「你不在经营委员会里了？」我虽痛心，但不否认。

此后两年李政委开始征求我到台湾工作。第一步在一九八一年初，他要求德仪董事长夏伯特「借用」我两星期，要我参观台湾电子工业并对他及行政院院长孙运璿做建议。他第一次做此要求被夏伯特拒绝，夏推说我刚有新任务（品质总监），不肯借；第二次再要时，夏伯特有点不胜其烦，答应了。我在「品质总监」职务内，本就预备在一九八一的三、四月到欧亚各德仪工厂走一遍，现在腾出四月十二至二十二的十天，专门为李政委为台湾电子工业做建议。

这十天中我看了十三家工厂和两个实验室（工研院电子所及交通部电信所），与李政委及工研院方贤齐院长吃了好几次晚餐；从这次起，以后我访问台湾，李政委常邀请当时的经济部部长和财政部部长与我一起晚餐，甚至有一次他说：「我把张博士交给你们了。」这次离台前，我拜会行政院院长孙运璿，口头报告此行的建议。回到达拉斯后写了一份九页的报告给李政委，这份报告我至今还保留，现在把它纲要摘录如下：

**日期：一九八一年五月四日****致：李国鼎政委**台湾电子业在最近十年有爆发性的成长，但几乎所有成长都基于台湾的低工资。当别的比台湾工资更低的地区开始开放，政府的目标——要电子工业从「劳力密集」升级到「技术密集」，非常合时。

「技术密集」与「劳力密集」工业需要很不一样的经济及社会基础设施，也许更重要的，它们需要很不一样的经营者心态。要务不是开发几个个别的技术，而是建立一个奖励创新的社会及经济环境。

Haggerty and the 1981 Taiwan Visit

Minister Li subsequently became acquainted with Eric Haggerty, who had recently retired as TI's Chairman. A year later (1978), at Minister Li's invitation, Haggerty made a week-long visit to Taiwan and, at Minister Li's request, organized the Executive Yuan's Science and Technology Advisory Group (STAG), as detailed in Chapter 10 of this book.

Sadly, Haggerty was diagnosed with pancreatic cancer in 1980 and died young. Only a few months passed between diagnosis and death. When Haggerty was critically ill, TI considered it his "private matter" and very few people knew of his condition. I was already on my "downhill" path at TI by then and only knew that Haggerty was ill, not that he was critical. Ironically, during Haggerty's final illness, Minister Li visited TI again. Not meeting Haggerty, he was told Haggerty was critical. At dinner with me, it was Minister Li — an outsider — who informed me of Haggerty's condition. From my visible shock, he surmised I was no longer in TI's inner circle and bluntly asked: "You're no longer on the Operations Committee?" Though pained, I did not deny it.

Over the next two years, Minister Li began recruiting me to work in Taiwan. The first step came in early 1981, when he asked TI Chairman Shepherd to "borrow" me for two weeks to visit Taiwan's electronics industry and advise him and Premier Sun Yun-suan. The first time he made this request, Shepherd refused, excusing that I had just taken on a new assignment (Quality Director) and could not be spared. The second time, Shepherd, somewhat annoyed, agreed. Within my Quality Director role, I had already planned to visit TI factories across Europe and Asia in March-April 1981. Now I carved out ten days (April 12–22) specifically for Minister Li to advise Taiwan's electronics industry.

During those ten days, I visited thirteen factories and two laboratories (ITRI's Electronics Research Institute and the Ministry of Transportation's Telecommunications Institute). I had several dinners with Minister Li and ITRI President Fang Xianqi. From this trip onward, whenever I visited Taiwan, Minister Li would often invite the current Minister of Economic Affairs and Minister of Finance to join me for dinner. Once he even said: "I'm entrusting Dr. Chang to you."

Before leaving Taiwan, I paid a courtesy call on Premier Sun Yun-suan to give an oral summary of my recommendations. After returning to Dallas, I wrote a nine-page report to Minister Li, which I still preserve today. Its outline follows:

Date: May 4, 1981

To: Minister K.T. Li

Taiwan's electronics industry has experienced explosive growth in the past decade, but nearly all of that growth has been predicated on Taiwan's low wages. As other regions with even lower wages begin to open up, the government's goal — to upgrade the electronics industry from "labor-intensive" to "technology-intensive" — is most timely.

"Technology-intensive" and "labor-intensive" industries require very different economic and social infrastructure. Perhaps more importantly, they require very different managerial mindsets. The task is not to develop a few individual technologies, but to build a social and economic environment that rewards innovation.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Downhill path (下山途中)—张忠谋自况在德仪职业生涯的下行阶段；「下山」隐喻失去核心圈地位、权力逐步被削弱的处境。
Operations Committee (经营委员会)—德仪最高决策机构，由董事长、总裁及核心高阶主管组成；被排除在经营委员会之外，意味着失去对重大决策的参与权。
Labor-intensive → Technology-intensive (劳力密集→技术密集)—产业升级的经典路径——从依赖低成本劳动力转向依赖技术知识；这是台湾在一九八〇年代经济转型的核心命题。

给李政委的报告（一九八一年）

我就四个题目建言，谨建言如下：

**一、自动化**方贤齐院长让我看他的初步工研院自动化技术研发计划，我的问题是：「研发了又如何呢？」「工业界又怎么享受工研院的研发成果？」**二、VLSI计划**VLSI案需要的经费和人才甚巨，可不必做。

**三、电脑**我非常高兴看到小型「电脑相关」公司的蓬勃发展。建言：

1. 硬件制造应限于以微处理器为基础的路板、模组、或个人电脑。 2. 小型电脑公司的经营重点应为：软件开发、硬件适应、比较简单路板或电脑设计及组装，以及售后服务，或提供客户个别需要的服务。 3. 台湾本地市场甚小，大部分营收要从国外来。

**四、一般建言**1. 创业基金（亦称风险基金）。 2. 考虑扩充台湾的证券市场。 3. 考虑如何以租税政策鼓励投资「技术密集」事业。

四十年后重温这报告，我相当惊异我那时的冲劲。当然我那时完全不了解台湾的政治和工业环境（不然不会建议工研院不做自动化及VLSI计划），我也高估了政府对民间企业的影响力（不然不会对政府做对电脑产业的建言），但纯从科技业策略面看，即使今天的我，也不惭愧我四十年前的建言。

事实上，在孙运璿任行政院院长时期，正是政府科技计划最抬头的时期。在我访问台湾之前，政府已决定要工研院做自动化和VLSI计划，我的「不要做」建议，当然无人理会。只有我的「一般建言」——关于创业基金、租税优惠、证券市场方向等等——倒是在以后几年政府陆续开始做，但是这些动作，也已有许多财经专家建议，我的建言只是附和他们一下而已。

几个月后，我就发现李政委「借调」我参观台湾工业，主要目的不是要我建言；「醉翁之意不在酒」，他只是要我进一步了解台湾，他的下一步就是邀请我到台湾工作。

ReadShift 双语翻译

The Report to Minister Li (1981)

I offered recommendations on four topics:

I. Automation

President Fang Xianqi showed me ITRI's preliminary automation R&D plan. My questions: "What happens after the R&D?" "How would industry benefit from ITRI's research results?"

II. VLSI Program

The VLSI program would require massive funding and talent — it need not be done.

III. Computers

I was delighted to see the flourishing of small "computer-related" companies. My recommendations:

1. Hardware manufacturing should be limited to microprocessor-based circuit boards, modules, or personal computers.

2. Small computer companies should focus on: software development, hardware adaptation, relatively simple circuit board or computer design and assembly, after-sales service, and customized client solutions.

3. Taiwan's domestic market is quite small; most revenue must come from abroad.

IV. General Recommendations

1. Venture capital funds (also called risk funds).

2. Consider expanding Taiwan's securities market.

3. Consider tax policies to encourage investment in "technology-intensive" industries.

Revisiting this report forty years later, I am quite amazed by my youthful vigor. Of course, I understood nothing of Taiwan's political and industrial environment at the time (otherwise I wouldn't have advised ITRI against the automation and VLSI programs). I also overestimated the government's influence over private enterprise (otherwise I wouldn't have made recommendations to the government about the computer industry). But purely from a technology strategy standpoint, even today's me feels no shame about the recommendations made forty years ago.

In fact, during Sun Yun-suan's tenure as Premier, government technology programs were at their zenith. Before my visit, the government had already decided to have ITRI pursue automation and VLSI. My "don't do it" advice was, of course, ignored. Only my "general recommendations" — on venture capital, tax incentives, securities market direction, and so forth — were gradually implemented in subsequent years. But by then, many financial experts had already proposed similar ideas; my recommendations merely echoed theirs.

A few months later, I realized that Minister Li's real purpose in "borrowing" me to visit Taiwan's industry was not for my advice. "The drinker's heart is not in the cup" — he simply wanted me to better understand Taiwan. His next step would be to invite me to work there.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
VLSI (Very Large Scale Integration，超大型集成电路)—指将数十万乃至数百万个晶体管集成在一块芯片上的技术；工研院的VLSI计划后来成为台湾半导体产业的重要技术来源。
Venture capital / Risk fund (创业基金/风险基金)—以股权投资方式支持初创公司发展的资金；李国鼎积极推动的创投基金，后来成为台湾科技业蓬勃发展的关键金融基础设施。
Tax incentives for technology-intensive industry (租税优惠)—政府以减免税收方式鼓励企业投资技术密集产业；新竹科学工业园区的租税优惠是吸引高科技厂商入驻的关键政策工具。

一九八二年孙运璿院长的聘雇及我的婉谢

一九八二年一月我的日记：

一月十日（星期日）上午十时去Marriott。M受孙运璿「说客」之托，要我去台湾工作，但他对何工作并不明了，讲了好几小时，不得要领。晚六时半去M家，M受李国鼎托，说李要我组织一个高科技对外贸易公司，其他情形也不详细。

一月十一日 早上电话李国鼎告知他已和潘及M谈过，又告诉他下月会飞去台湾和他详谈。

一月十二日 对彪希（BARR ROL）说李国鼎事。

一月十三日 彪希要我打电话回绝李国鼎，我说和李面谈一次吧，彪希虽答应，但似不高兴。

那时我是德仪的「品质总监」，本来就应到全球德仪工厂视察，所以相当容易安排在台湾逗留几天。后来安排在三月二十四日自东京抵台湾，二十五日在德仪台湾办德仪事，二十六至二十九日与孙院长、李政委、方贤齐院长、潘文渊顾问讨论台湾政府要给我的工作，以及待遇。

孙院长亲自对我讲工作。他说，我可以有三个选择：一是做他的科技顾问，二是做工研院院长，三他让李政委说。

李政委说他想要我主持政府要办的创投基金（就是M在达拉斯说的贸易公司），但这完全只在「想」的阶段，资金的来源都还没有。李政委只是要让我知道：创投基金也是一个可能。

待遇方面，只有潘顾问代孙院长问我最近三年待遇多少？我告诉他：二十五万、二十万、二十二万（均美元）。他请示了孙院长后告诉我：「不会让你吃亏。」

Premier Sun's 1982 Offer and My Decline

From my diary, January 1982:

January 10 (Sunday) — 10 AM went to the Marriott. M, acting as an emissary for Sun Yun-suan, wanted me to work in Taiwan, but he had no clarity about what the job would be. Talked for hours without getting to the point. 6:30 PM went to M's house. M, entrusted by Li Guoding, said Li wanted me to organize a high-tech foreign trade company. Other details were vague.

January 11 — Morning, called Li Guoding, told him I had spoken with Pan and M, and that I would fly to Taiwan next month to discuss in detail.

January 12 — Told Barr about Li Guoding's matter.

January 13 — Barr asked me to call and decline Li Guoding. I said I would meet Li face-to-face once first. Barr agreed but seemed displeased.

At that time I was TI's "Quality Director" and was expected to visit TI factories worldwide, so it was relatively easy to arrange a few days in Taiwan. Eventually, I scheduled my visit: arriving from Tokyo on March 24, handling TI Taiwan business on the 25th, and meeting with Premier Sun, Minister Li, President Fang Xianqi, and consultant Pan Wen-yuan from the 26th to the 29th to discuss the position and compensation the Taiwan government was offering.

Premier Sun personally explained the job to me. He said I had three choices: first, be his technology advisor; second, be ITRI President; third, he would let Minister Li explain.

Minister Li said he wanted me to run a government-sponsored venture capital fund (the trading company M had mentioned in Dallas), but this was still purely at the "thinking" stage — funding sources had not yet been identified. Minister Li simply wanted me to know that the VC fund was also a possibility.

On compensation, only Consultant Pan, on Premier Sun's behalf, asked what my salary had been for the past three years. I told him: $250,000, $200,000, $220,000 (all USD). After consulting Premier Sun, he told me: "We won't let you suffer a loss."

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Quality Director (品质总监)—德仪全球品质与生产力的最高主管；张忠谋在德仪「下山」途中被安排此职，虽仍有全球视察的便利，但已远离核心决策圈。
Venture capital fund (创投基金)—由政府主导、投资于初创科技公司的事业基金；李国鼎的创投构想后来成为台湾科技业资金链的重要一环。
"We won't let you suffer a loss" (不会让你吃亏)—孙运璿院长对张忠谋的待遇承诺；这句话体现了台湾政府揽才的诚意，但也暗示了公部门薪资与跨国企业高管之间的巨大差距。

未成的赴台与一九八五年徐贤修的「三顾茅庐」

一九八二年，我在德仪已到「最后的呐喊」阶段（本书第十一章）。假使我的整个德仪生涯也如我在哈佛的一年，是一个「可带走的盛宴」，那么到了一九八二年，这「盛宴」也已到了杯盘狼藉，主人连连打呵欠，只有我身为客人却还在高谈阔论的阶段。盛宴将终，我的离开德仪，仅是迟早问题；但是迟或早却需要拿捏，因为我还有未到期的「股票承购权」；我还要倚靠这些「股票承购权」赚来的钱，过我未来也许几十年的低薪，或无薪的生活。

当然孙院长答应我在待遇上「不会让我吃亏」，但这话能维持多久？我在德仪的薪水比台湾工研院院长高得太多，虽然孙院长有诚意，但他不会永远当行政院院长，若换了一个新的行政院院长，还会不会延续这个承诺？

有一个办法，假如德仪答应，我可在德仪「留职停薪」；那么，我可在台湾工作，在德仪虽不领薪，但未到期的「股票承购权」可保留；等到「承购权」到期，我把它实现了，才正式自德仪辞职。但这办法需要德仪同意。

回到达拉斯后，我对彪希请示在德仪「留职停薪」。我很坦白地告诉他我想去台湾工作，但希望保留股票承购权。彪希说去问夏伯特，一星期后彪希回话：「不准！我们要留你。」我在五月四日致函孙院长，并将副本寄给李政委及方院长，坦白告诉我的处境：我想来台湾工作，但放弃股票承购权的损失实在太大（我甚至告诉他可能损失的金额），而「留职停薪」的请求又被拒绝。

孙院长及李政委在一个多月后各自回信，两人都表示他们的失望。李政委另提了一个办法：我每年台湾几次，每次一、两星期。

鉴于上次李政委要求「借用」我时夏伯特的不高兴，以及我对夏伯特和彪希性格的了解，我不认为他们会答应李政委的折衷办法，所以也没对他们提。

一九八三年十月三十一日，股票承购权也等到了，我辞职德仪，首先想到的就是台湾。辞职次日就电话李政委，告诉他我已是「自由之身」；意外地，电话后却没有下文。几天内，已有好几个猎头者与我接触，所以我也不再向台湾追踪。为什么这次李政委冷淡，对我至今是一个谜。但一九八五年，徐贤修找我后，李政委又热烈劝我做工研院院长，我接任工研院院长后，他又热烈要我成立台积电。

只是，一九八五年主动到纽约找我当工研院院长的不是我熟识的李国鼎，而是我比较不熟识的徐贤修。
