The Official Document Relay and Formal Approval

I still remember showing my first draft to Minister Li — he shook his head repeatedly. He first instructed me on the proper format. After I rewrote it, he carefully helped me polish the wording. He also told me that as ITRI President, I should not submit a memorandum directly to Premier Yu, but to Minister of Economic Affairs Li Da-hai. After several days of work, I submitted my memorandum to Minister Li on November 27, with the following key points:

(1) Total capital required: $202 million USD — 70% equity, 30% debt.

(2) Equity portion: $145 million. Proposed share allocation: Government $70 million (48.3%); other domestic or foreign investors $35 million (24.1%); Philips investment highly probable.

(3) At least four reasons to establish TSMC today.

(4) The General Manager should be someone with significant management standing in the international VLSI industry, familiar with the latest manufacturing technology, and capable of building close relationships with foreign markets. Likely an American. Need to recruit about 10 people in the U.S. Mid- and lower-level staff can be recruited in Taiwan; the Electronics Institute can transfer about 100 engineering personnel, sufficient for initial needs.

Minister Li Da-hai received my memorandum and waited a full month before forwarding it to Premier Yu on December 30. In addition to summarizing my memorandum, he added: "I respectfully request that the Yuan, after approving, designate relevant agency heads to form a Preparatory Steering Group to coordinate planning and necessary tax incentive measures, and ask ITRI President Chang to serve as Executive Secretary and handle the preparatory work."

After this, the Executive Yuan moved quickly. On January 4, 1986, Secretary-General Wang Zhangqing wrote to the CEPD asking it to "expedite review" of TSMC. On January 8, the CEPD convened, chaired by Chairman Zhao Yaodong with Vice Chair Wang Zhaoming. I recall attending committee members including Minister of Finance Qian Chun, Minister of Economic Affairs Li Da-hai, Minister of Transportation Lian Zhan, and CBC Governor Zhang Jizheng. I presented the innovative "dedicated foundry" model once more, along with the key points from my November 27 memorandum. After the presentation, Chairman Zhao solicited opinions. The exchange I remember most was with Governor Zhang:

Governor Zhang: "What gives you the right to compete with American, Japanese, and Korean companies?"

Me: "We specialize in foundry. I compete on excellent service."

Governor Zhang laughed: "Ha! A Taiwanese company competing on reputation — that's the first I've heard of such a thing."

Though I understood this was a sarcastic remark, I didn't quite grasp it: Don't Taiwanese companies care about reputation? Fortunately, no other committee members took the bait. Governor Zhang's words passed like the wind — gone as soon as spoken.

The next day, Chairman Zhao issued a letter to the Secretary-General: In principle, agree to proceed; agree to form a Preparatory Steering Group; and ask ITRI President Morris Chang to serve as Executive Secretary handling preparatory work.

On January 16, the Executive Yuan plenary adopted the CEPD's conclusion. On January 28, Premier Yu issued a directive to five ministries and ITRI, appointing Chairman Zhao Yaodong and Minister Li Da-hai as co-conveners of the Preparatory Steering Group; Minister of Finance Qian Chun, Minister Chen Lian, and myself as group members, with me also serving as Executive Secretary. This was the so-called "Five-Person Committee."

Minister Li — the person who had done the most to advance TSMC — was not on the Five-Person Committee. Minister Li told me he had asked Premier Yu to exclude him, saying he had "retired after success." From my September 10, 1985 briefing to Premier Yu proposing TSMC, to Premier Yu's January 28, 1986 designation of the Five-Person Committee — this was Act One of TSMC's founding. Act Two was about to begin.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Preparatory Steering Group (筹划指导小组)—行政院为筹备台积电而设的跨部会协调机构；五人小组是台积电得以在官僚体系中快速推进的关键制度设计。
"Competing on reputation" (凭商誉竞争)—张继正总裁对张忠谋「凭服务竞争」的讥讽——台湾公司凭商誉竞争是第一次听闻；这句话反映了当时台湾产业的国际形象。
"Retired after success" (功成身退)—李国鼎主动要求不进入五人小组，自谓「功成身退」；这是中国传统政治智慧的体现——在最成功时退出，避免日后承担责任。
章节

台積電篇一第十七章

张忠谋

台积电篇一·第十七章｜募资

寻找第二主角

俞国华院长指定台积电"五人小组"时，政府已决定出资48%。但是，俞院长有一个条件：我必须先找一家有IC技术的跨国公司，要他们做第二主要投资者；然后，政府才能去找台湾民间，台湾民间也才有信心凑足余额。

俞院长的预言百分之百正确。后来，即使飞利浦同意投资27.6%后，政府还是花了九牛二虎之力，才凑足剩余的24.1%。

一九八五年是世界半导体业历史到那时为止最不景气的一年——成长率是负16%。大部分半导体公司都求生存。在这时刻，我找他们投资一家以前从未尝试过的"专业晶圆代工"公司，而且这家公司位在当时美、日、欧半导体公司都认为是"半导体不毛之地"的台湾！

ReadShift 双语翻译

When Premier Yu Kuo-hua appointed the "Five-Person Committee" for TSMC, the government had already decided to contribute 48% of the capital. However, Premier Yu set one condition: I had to first find a multinational company with IC technology to serve as the second lead investor; only then would the government approach Taiwanese private investors, and only then would they have confidence to raise the remainder.

Premier Yu's prediction proved 100% correct. Later, even after Philips agreed to invest 27.6%, the government still had to expend tremendous effort to raise the remaining 24.1%.

1985 was the worst year in the history of the global semiconductor industry up to that point—growth rate was negative 16%. Most semiconductor companies were merely surviving. At this moment, I approached them to invest in a "dedicated foundry" company—a business model never attempted before—and one located in Taiwan, which American, Japanese, and European semiconductor firms all considered a "semiconductor barren land"!

四处碰壁

在八五年十二月及翌年一月，我还是试了。虽然那时我已相信飞利浦有投资诚意，但一切条件都还未开始谈，我不知道谈得成否。况且，我认为多找几家公司来与飞利浦竞争，绝对对我们有利。我写信或打电话给英特尔、德仪、摩托罗拉、松下、新力、迪吉多、超微、汤姆生等公司的总裁。除了松下是孙运璿先生特别要我接触，其余都是我在德仪及通用时期熟悉的。大部分都有回信，但信是千篇一律的"无兴趣"。

ReadShift 双语翻译

In December 1985 and January 1986, I still tried. Although by then I believed Philips had genuine investment interest, no terms had been discussed yet, and I didn't know if negotiations would succeed. Moreover, I believed that having multiple companies compete with Philips would definitely be to our advantage. I wrote letters or made phone calls to the CEOs of Intel, Texas Instruments, Motorola, Matsushita, Sony, DEC, AMD, and Thomson. Except for Matsushita, which Mr. Sun Yun-suan specifically asked me to approach, the rest were companies I had known well from my TI and GE days. Most responded, but the letters were uniformly "not interested."

德仪与英特尔的拒绝

除了德仪和英特尔。德仪是我的老东家，缘虽断但情犹在。德仪的半导体总经理席克（第十章曾提到他）邀我去达拉斯见面。我去了，对他及几位他的幕僚做了一个简报。当时他就说希望不大，但答应考虑并与总裁夏伯特讨论。几个月后，我与飞利浦已即将成局，席克又邀请我再去达拉斯。这次他没有幕僚陪同，单独告诉我德仪不准备投资。

英特尔的故事相似。我写信给英特尔总裁，也是我的老朋友摩尔。摩尔邀我与他的技术及生产总监巴瑞特（Craig Barrett）相会。我做了半小时左右的简报，并且回答了他的问题。后来几星期音讯全无，我就打电话找巴瑞特，找了好几个地方才找到他。他说：英特尔无兴趣投资。

现在（一九八六年五月）只剩飞利浦了——虽然飞利浦还不知道他们是唯一表达兴趣的投资者。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Except for TI and Intel. TI was my former employer—the bond was broken but the affection remained. TI's semiconductor general manager Sheek (mentioned in Chapter 10) invited me to Dallas. I went and gave a briefing to him and several of his staff. At the time he said the chances weren't great, but agreed to consider it and discuss with president Sheppard. Months later, when my negotiations with Philips were nearly concluded, Sheek invited me to Dallas again. This time he had no staff accompanying him and told me privately that TI would not invest.

Intel's story was similar. I wrote to Intel's president, my old friend Gordon Moore. Moore arranged for me to meet his technology and production director Craig Barrett. I gave about a half-hour briefing and answered his questions. Then weeks went by with no word, so I called Barrett, tracking him down through several locations. He said: Intel was not interested in investing.

By now (May 1986), only Philips remained—though Philips didn't yet know they were the sole investor to express interest.

飞利浦

飞利浦成立于一八九一年，以电灯泡起家。在二十世纪，它陆续进入家电、被动元件、半导体、光电、医疗器材等业。在一九八零年代，它是世界最大跨国公司之一，也是一家有IC技术的公司。

但是在半导体业内，无论从营收规模、技术强度或获利率角度看，飞利浦都非世界第一流。我把它排在二流行列中的第一排。这样排法虽非褒，但亦非贬。因为在我心目中，当时一流的第一排为英特尔独占；德仪、摩托罗拉只是一流的第二排。二流的第一除飞利浦外，还有人。二流的第二排以及三流，人更多。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Philips was founded in 1891, starting with light bulbs. Throughout the twentieth century, it successively entered home appliances, passive components, semiconductors, optoelectronics, and medical equipment. In the 1980s, it was one of the world's largest multinational corporations, and a company with IC technology.

However, within the semiconductor industry—whether measured by revenue scale, technology strength, or profitability—Philips was not world-class first tier. I ranked it in the first row of the second tier. This ranking was neither praise nor criticism. Because in my mind, the first row of first tier was occupied solely by Intel; TI and Motorola were merely the second row of first tier. The first row of second tier, besides Philips, had others. The second row of second tier and third tier had even more.

飞利浦的动机

这个二流一排的半导体公司，为什么在这半导体业萧条年头，别的半导体公司都无兴趣投资台積電之时，单独有兴趣？答案有二。其一：半导体并非飞利浦主业，虽然八五年半导体萧条，但飞利浦别的业务并不萧条，所以总公司仍有足够现金可供投资。答案之二更为重要：那时中国大陆尚未开放，飞利浦总部已决定把台湾作为他们的低工资生产基地。他们本来在台湾就有IC装配测试厂，现在准备在台湾大肆建立被动元件、光电等生产基地；他们正在想如何才能获得台湾政府的青睐，恰巧碰到台湾政府招外商投资台積電，台積電就成为他们台湾扩充计划的第一炮。

把镜头移后几年。果然，在八零年代晚期及九零年代初期，飞利浦在台湾大肆扩充被动元件及光电等生产基地，雇用员工最高达四万余人。但是，九零年代中期大陆开始开放，外国公司蜂拥而入，大陆成为新的世界低工资生产基地。飞利浦也弃旧抱新，很快地从台湾搬到大陆去，在台湾只留下行销人员。今日飞利浦在台湾的员工不到一千人；对台積電的投资，也在获厚利后于二零零八年终结——但这些都是以后的故事。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Why was this tier-2 tier-1 semiconductor company—alone among all semiconductor companies—interested in investing in TSMC during an industry downturn, when others had no interest? There were two answers. First: semiconductors were not Philips' core business. Although the semiconductor sector was in recession in 1985, Philips' other businesses were not, so headquarters still had sufficient cash for investment. The second answer was more important: mainland China had not yet opened up, and Philips headquarters had already decided to make Taiwan their low-wage production base. They already had an IC assembly and test factory in Taiwan, and were now planning to aggressively build production sites for passive components, optoelectronics, and more. They were wondering how to gain the favor of the Taiwanese government—and then, by coincidence, the Taiwanese government sought foreign investment for TSMC. TSMC became the first shot of their Taiwan expansion plan.

Fast forward a few years. Indeed, in the late 1980s and early 1990s, Philips aggressively expanded its passive component and optoelectronics production bases in Taiwan, employing up to 40,000 workers at its peak. But by the mid-1990s, mainland China began opening up; foreign companies poured in, and mainland China became the world's new low-wage production base. Philips also abandoned the old for the new, quickly relocating from Taiwan to mainland China, leaving only marketing staff in Taiwan. Today, Philips employs fewer than a thousand people in Taiwan; its investment in TSMC, after reaping substantial profits, ended in 2008—but these are all stories for later.

初访荷兰

回到一九八五年。李政委告知我飞利浦有兴趣投资后，我就与飞利浦接触，接着遵他们嘱写投资建议书，并在十一月三日至六日访问荷兰飞利浦。我曾在一九六九年以德仪集成电路总经理身份访问荷兰飞利浦。那时德仪稳居世界IC业领袖，飞利浦技术落后，想买德仪的"技术授权"。我受飞利浦之邀，去考察他们是否有接受德仪技术的能力。那次访问，我以"征服者"姿态出现。

但这次却大不相同。这次我是"恳求者"，恳求飞利浦投资。角色转换，沧海桑田，使我晚上在旅舍中唏嘘不已。尤其，这次我并没有见到对方的主角——飞利浦IC总经理克列斯曼（Krigsman），他在美国。

这次访问飞利浦，给我最深印象是飞利浦正在巨额投资建两个IC厂。他们在奈梅亨建IC生产厂，同时在恩荷芬建IC"研发厂"；引导我参观的人告诉我："研发厂的规模与生产厂相似。"亲眼看到这样巨额的投资在进行式中（必在两亿美元以上），我比较放心我们的要求（四千万美元）会被接受。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Back to 1985. After Commissioner Li informed me of Philips' investment interest, I made contact with Philips, then followed their instructions to write an investment proposal, and visited Philips in the Netherlands from November 3 to 6. I had visited Philips in 1969 as TI's integrated circuit general manager. At that time, TI stood firmly as the world leader in the IC industry; Philips was behind technologically and wanted to purchase TI's "technology license." I accepted Philips' invitation to assess whether they had the capability to absorb TI's technology. On that visit, I appeared as a "conqueror."

But this time was completely different. This time I was a "supplicant," begging Philips to invest. The role reversal—the vast change of circumstances—made me sigh in my hotel room at night. Moreover, this time I did not meet the key person on their side—Philips' IC general manager Krigsman. He was in the United States.

What impressed me most during this Philips visit was that they were making enormous investments to build two IC factories. They were building an IC production facility in Nijmegen, and simultaneously an IC "R&D fab" in Eindhoven; the person guiding me told me: "The R&D fab's scale is similar to the production fab." Witnessing such massive investment firsthand (it must have exceeded $200 million), I felt more confident that our request ($40 million) would be accepted.

七个月谈判的开启

十二月二日，我去加州森尼韦尔（Sunnyvale），首次晤克列斯曼，自此展开长达七个月的谈判。在此谈判中，我代表台積電，我背后的决策者是"五人小组"，我主要助手是胡定华、史钦泰以及政府常用的联鼎法律事务所的陈国慈律师。飞利浦方面则有许多谈判者——技术、业务方面由克列斯曼负责，台湾飞利浦技术长罗益强君助理；财务、法务另有荷兰飞利浦专人负责。

ReadShift 双语翻译

On December 2, I went to Sunnyvale, California, and met Krigsman for the first time, launching a negotiation that would last seven months. In this negotiation, I represented TSMC. Behind me, the decision-makers were the "Five-Person Committee." My main assistants were Hu Ding-hua, Shi Qin-tai, and lawyer Chen Guoci of the Lian Ding law firm, commonly used by the government. On the Philips side, there were many negotiators—technology and business aspects were handled by Krigsman, assisted by Mr. Luo Yiqiang, CTO of Philips Taiwan; finance and legal affairs were handled by dedicated personnel from Philips Netherlands.

谈判重点一——公司命名

在第一次对院长简报"共同晶圆厂"时，我已暂时命名新公司为 Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company（TSMC）。我觉得这名字表达了公司的要点：（一）在台湾成立（Taiwan）＋（二）做半导体（Semiconductor）＋（三）做制造（Manufacturing）。后来的投资协议都以英文为主文；一直到公司登记，才有中文名字问题。我的第一个反应就是直译英文："台湾半导体制造公司"，但发现此名已为人登记，所以改成"台湾积体电路制造公司"，简称"台積電"。英文名字及英文简写都不必改，现在TSMC已闻名世界了。

ReadShift 双语翻译

When I first briefed the Premier on the "Common Wafer Fab," I had tentatively named the new company Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC). I felt this name captured the company's essentials: (1) established in Taiwan (Taiwan) + (2) in the semiconductor business (Semiconductor) + (3) in manufacturing (Manufacturing). Subsequent investment agreements used English as the main text; the Chinese name issue didn't arise until company registration. My first instinct was a direct translation: "Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company," but discovered this name was already registered by someone else, so we changed it to "Taiwan Integrated Circuit Manufacturing Company," abbreviated as "TSMC." The English name and acronym didn't need to change—and now TSMC is world-famous.

谈判重点二——营业范围

开始与飞利浦谈判，我就强调"专业晶圆代工"商业模式。飞利浦不但同意，而且说如果台湾要办设计公司或IDM型的公司，他们不会考虑投资，因为设计公司或IDM型公司会是他们的竞争者。既有这样共识，我们在"投资协议纲要"（Heads of Agreement）中，更清楚地界定"专业晶圆代工"的营业范围：

台積電不设计或推销自己的产品，但依照客户的设计，为客户制造IC晶圆，并提供或安排封装测试服务。

ReadShift 双语翻译

From the start of negotiations with Philips, I emphasized the "dedicated foundry" business model. Philips not only agreed, but said that if Taiwan wanted to establish a design house or IDM-type company, they would not consider investing, because a design house or IDM-type company would be their competitor. With this consensus, we more clearly defined the business scope of "dedicated foundry" in the "Heads of Agreement":

TSMC does not design or sell its own products, but manufactures IC wafers according to customers' designs, and provides or arranges packaging and testing services.

谈判重点三——技术

首晤克列斯曼（飞利浦首席谈判员）时，他就要求台積電"完全以飞利浦技术为基础"，我立刻拒绝。我从德仪时期就知道，技术是一个半导体公司的灵魂。怎么能在公司还未组成时，就先出卖他的灵魂？接着，克列斯曼要求飞利浦以技术做股，我也拒绝了。我们要的全额现金投资（李政委还认为我要得太少，因为他预计在台湾民间募资会有困难），任何折扣都会使台湾民间募资更困难。

但是我们的确也要他的技术协助。在一九八六年一月初，工研院的技术团队（副院长胡定华、电子所所长史钦泰、副所长章青驹、组长曾繁城）去恩荷芬领略飞利浦的技术。他们回来的报告是："可以帮助我们自己的开发。"

更重要的是：飞利浦与十几家大型半导体公司交换授权；假使飞利浦拥有二五%以上台積電股权，台積電也在飞利浦的保护伞下。也就是说：台積電不会受到这十几家大公司专利权的干扰。

技术开发的帮助，以及专利权的"保护伞"，都要钱买。飞利浦也毫不客气，要求高价。经过不少折冲，我们（"五人小组"）同意在先进技术（一微米及更先进）营收内，台積電付予飞利浦三分之一权利金。工研院已开发的技术（二微米及以上），台積電不必付权利金。

ReadShift 双语翻译

At my first meeting with Krigsman (Philips' chief negotiator), he demanded that TSMC be "entirely based on Philips technology." I immediately refused. Since my TI days, I had known that technology is the soul of a semiconductor company. How could we sell the soul of a company before it was even formed? Next, Krigsman demanded that Philips contribute technology as equity. I also refused. We wanted full cash investment (Commissioner Li even thought I was asking for too little, because he anticipated difficulties raising funds from Taiwanese private investors)—any discount would make Taiwanese private fundraising even more difficult.

But we did need their technical assistance. In early January 1986, an ITRI technology team (Vice President Hu Ding-hua, Electronics Research Institute Director Shi Qin-tai, Deputy Director Zhang Qingju, and Section Chief Tseng Fan-cheng) went to Eindhoven to survey Philips' technology. Their report upon return: "Can assist our own development."

More importantly: Philips had cross-licensing agreements with over a dozen major semiconductor companies. If Philips owned more than 25% of TSMC's equity, TSMC would also be under Philips' protective umbrella. In other words: TSMC would not be harassed by the patent rights of these dozen-plus major companies.

Help in technology development, and the patent "umbrella," both cost money. Philips, without courtesy, demanded a high price. After considerable negotiations, we (the "Five-Person Committee") agreed that TSMC would pay Philips a one-third royalty on revenue from advanced technology (one micron and below). For technology already developed by ITRI (two microns and above), TSMC would pay no royalty.

谈判重点四——独立性

一旦避免了"以飞利浦技术"做基础，我就要强调台積電的独立性。我不要台積電成为飞利浦的子公司，政府也不要台積電成为"国营"或"国有"公司。所以在"协议纲要"上我们明白说明：

台積電是一个独立事业，她的成长和获利的优先考量，与独立的美国IT C公司一样。

与独立美国ITC公司相比拟，是刚自美国来台湾的我决定的。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Having avoided being "based on Philips technology," I then emphasized TSMC's independence. I did not want TSMC to become a Philips subsidiary, and the government did not want TSMC to become a "state-run" or "state-owned" enterprise. So in the "Heads of Agreement" we clearly stated:

TSMC is an independent enterprise. Its priority considerations for growth and profitability are the same as those of an independent American ITC company.

The comparison to an independent American ITC company was my own decision, as someone who had just come to Taiwan from the United States.

谈判重点五——人事权

人事权在没有异议下达成协议：

董事会十人：政府指派四人，飞利浦指派三人，其余股东指派两人，总经理兼董事一人。

如政府持股在二五%以上，政府指定董事长。最大股东提名总经理，由董事会决定。

总经理为公司行政首长（CEO）。

第二大股东提名财务副总。

监察人三名。政府及飞利浦各指定一人，其他股东指定一人。

总经理并列，而且总经理是行政首长，这些规定都属于标准欧美公司体制——也是飞利浦及我习惯的体制。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Personnel authority was agreed upon without dissent:

The board would consist of ten members: four appointed by the government, three appointed by Philips, two appointed by other shareholders, and one serving as both general manager and director.

If the government held more than 25% of shares, the government would appoint the chairman. The largest shareholder would nominate the general manager, subject to board approval.

The general manager would be the company's chief executive (CEO).

The second largest shareholder would nominate the financial vice president.

Three supervisors: one each appointed by the government and Philips, and one by other shareholders.

That the general manager would also be a board member, and that the general manager would be the chief executive—these provisions were all standard European and American corporate governance—the system both Philips and I were accustomed to.

谈判重点六——飞利浦享受股票承购权

开启飞利浦谈判不久，赵耀东主委就对我说："他们（飞利浦）一定会要求股票承购权。"赵主委富有与国外公司合资经验，他的话也让我有心理准备。果然，在一切都已大致谈定，双方准备签署"协议纲要"时，飞利浦突然提出股票承购权，建议如下：

（一）最早一九八九年九月三十日，飞利浦可提出承购要求，增加飞利浦持股至五一%，"政府股东"及"其他股东"必须转让股票给飞利浦；如"其他股东"不愿，则"政府股东"必须转让给飞利浦。

（二）转让价格依下列两条件，孰者为高而定：（A）转让时之公司资产净值。（B）原始投资价，加银行利率。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Early in the Philips negotiations, Committee Chairman Zhao Yaodong said to me: "They (Philips) will definitely demand a stock option." Chairman Zhao had extensive experience in joint ventures with foreign companies, and his words gave me mental preparation. Sure enough, when everything had been largely negotiated and both parties were preparing to sign the "Heads of Agreement," Philips suddenly raised the stock option issue with the following proposal:

(1) Beginning September 30, 1989 at the earliest, Philips could exercise an option to increase its stake to 51%, and "government shareholders" and "other shareholders" would be obligated to transfer shares to Philips; if "other shareholders" refused, then "government shareholders" must transfer to Philips.

(2) The transfer price would be determined by whichever of the following two conditions was higher: (A) the company's net asset value at the time of transfer, or (B) the original investment price plus bank interest.

反建议与张忠谋的坚持

我接受了（一），但不接受（二）。我对飞利浦的反建议是：

（二）转让价格三条件，等量考虑：（A）转让时之公司资产净值。（B）转让时之公司获利能力及获利预测。（C）在美国证券市场上市之美国半导体公司之本益比。

我的反建议使飞利浦惊愕了。时间已是一九八六年五月二十七日。与飞利浦总裁已订六月九日来台湾签署"协议纲要"。几乎一切别的都已谈定，飞利浦谈判团也不想为了这件可能不会发生的事（如台積電不成功，飞利浦不会要增加持股），阻碍他们以台湾作为主要生产基地的第一步。

匆匆折冲后，最后的转让价格条件是：（A）转让时之公司资产净值。（B）转让时之公司获利能力及获利预测。（C）在美国证券市场上市之美国半导体公司之市价／净值比。

最后的协议与我的反建议相差不远。当时（C）市价／净值比大约二．五倍到十倍，所以最后协议比飞利浦的原建议对开发基金有利得多。飞利浦一向以谈判能力著称，但在这件事上，我们赢了。

ReadShift 双语翻译

I accepted (1) but rejected (2). My counter-proposal to Philips was:

(2) Transfer price determined by three factors given equal consideration: (A) the company's net asset value at transfer. (B) The company's earning power and profit forecast at transfer. (C) The price-to-earnings ratio of American semiconductor companies listed on U.S. stock exchanges.

My counter-proposal stunned Philips. It was May 27, 1986. The Philips president had already scheduled a visit to Taiwan on June 9 to sign the "Heads of Agreement." Almost everything else had been settled, and the Philips negotiation team did not want to let this potentially moot point (if TSMC failed, Philips wouldn't want to increase its stake) block their first step in making Taiwan a primary production base.

After hasty negotiations, the final transfer price conditions were: (A) the company's net asset value at transfer. (B) The company's earning power and profit forecast at transfer. (C) The price-to-book ratio of American semiconductor companies listed on U.S. stock exchanges.

The final agreement was not far from my counter-proposal. At that time, (C) the price-to-book ratio was approximately 2.5x to 10x, so the final agreement was far more favorable to the Development Fund than Philips' original proposal. Philips had always been renowned for its negotiation skills, but on this matter, we won.

谈判重点七——营业计划

我与胡定华、史钦泰等工研院同仁，花了不少时间准备台積電十年详细营业计划。克列斯曼仔细地看了，认为我们的售价太乐观。飞利浦很可能是我们未来客户，他做此言，我认为大有自私意味在，但我无意与他做冗长辩论。我们稍事调整计划内的售价，但仍呈示不错的获利及投资回收。详细的营业计划附录在"协议纲要"里。

在这个计划里，我们前五年的营收年复合成长率为六四%，营业利益率除了在第一年以外，可以由单位数成长到一九九二零年的二五%左右。而实际上，台積電前五年的营收年复合成长率为一三零%，营业利益率除了第一年以及产业不景气的一九九零年以外，都是双位数。

"营业计划"的假设是我们只有一厂及二厂，所以从九二年起，二厂成熟后，营收就不再成长。"真实"的数字代表我们后来继续建三厂、四厂。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Along with ITRI colleagues Hu Ding-hua and Shi Qin-tai, I spent considerable time preparing TSMC's detailed ten-year business plan. Krigsman reviewed it carefully and considered our pricing too optimistic. Philips was likely to be our future customer; in making this comment, I believed there was considerable selfish motivation, but I had no intention of engaging in a lengthy debate with him. We made slight adjustments to the pricing in the plan, but it still showed solid profitability and investment recovery. The detailed business plan was appended to the "Heads of Agreement."

In this plan, our projected compound annual revenue growth rate for the first five years was 64%, and operating margin—except for the first year—could grow from single digits to about 25% by 1992. In reality, TSMC's compound annual revenue growth rate for the first five years was 130%, and operating margins—except for the first year and the industry downturn year of 1990—were all double digits.

The "business plan" assumed we would only have Fab 1 and Fab 2; thus from 1992 onward, once Fab 2 matured, revenue would stop growing. The "actual" figures represent our later decision to continue building Fab 3 and Fab 4.

"投资协议纲要"与"技术合作协议"

七个月的谈判，有时顺利，有时痛苦，但我一直抱着"非谈成不可"的态度。如果谈不成，飞利浦不投资，我们就办不成台積電，工研院的IC计划也会走到山穷水尽地步。抱着这样"可忍则忍"的心怀，终于谈成了与飞利浦的"投资协议纲要"。"五人小组"同意后，我与飞利浦总裁在一九八六年六月签署。

有了飞利浦的投资承诺，我们满足了俞院长的台湾募资条件，政府也就展开了台湾募资。几个月后，股款凑足（一亿四千五百万美元，相当于新台币五十五亿元），全体投资人在十月签署"股东协议书"。这"股东协议书"完全保存了"投资协议纲要"的要点。

也就是说，七个月的谈判造就了台積電，也决定了台積電头六年的经营模式。一直到一九九二年十月，台積電决定申请上市，原始股东在"股东协议书"的私自约定不可能在上市时成立。而且原始股东（包括行政院开发基金及飞利浦）嗅到了上市后股票增值的诱惑，才决定解除原来的"股东协议"。

ReadShift 双语翻译

The seven-month negotiation was sometimes smooth, sometimes painful, but I always maintained an attitude of "this must succeed." If negotiations failed and Philips didn't invest, we couldn't establish TSMC, and ITRI's IC program would reach the end of its road. With this "endure what can be endured" mindset, we finally concluded the "Investment Agreement Heads" with Philips. After approval by the "Five-Person Committee," I signed it with the Philips president in June 1986.

With Philips' investment commitment in hand, we satisfied Premier Yu's condition for Taiwan fundraising, and the government launched its Taiwan fundraising campaign. Months later, the full capital was raised (US$145 million, equivalent to NT$5.5 billion), and all investors signed the "Shareholders Agreement" in October. This "Shareholders Agreement" fully preserved the key points of the "Investment Agreement Heads."

In other words, seven months of negotiation created TSMC and determined TSMC's business model for its first six years. It wasn't until October 1992, when TSMC decided to apply for listing, that the private arrangements in the "Shareholders Agreement" could no longer be sustained upon public listing. Moreover, the original shareholders (including the Executive Yuan Development Fund and Philips) caught the scent of stock appreciation after listing and agreed to terminate the original "Shareholders Agreement."

技术合作合约几乎翻脸

除了"投资协议纲要"，飞利浦要求根据"纲要"内关于飞利浦技术的约定，双方订立"技术合作合约"。为了这个合约，我几乎与飞利浦闹翻。

原因是这样的：飞利浦建议，因为他们富有建IC厂经验，所以台積電的IC厂也由他们设计。看到这个建议，我觉得这已违反台積電的独立原则，我从"可忍则忍"转为"是可忍，孰不可忍"。与飞利浦初步争论无效后，我对"五人小组"报告：也许决裂点已到。赵耀东（素有"铁头"之称）说："决裂就决裂，自己办亦可。"但李达海主张还是请李国鼎周旋一下，也许可以解套。会后我就与李政委商量，他决定写信给飞利浦总裁，要求飞利浦撤回替我们设计IC厂要求。这封信果然有效。几天后飞利浦不再提此要求。我们也就在一九八六年的十二月与飞利浦签署"技术合作合约"。

ReadShift 双语翻译

In addition to the "Investment Agreement Heads," Philips requested that both parties enter into a "Technology Cooperation Agreement" based on the technology-related provisions in the "Heads." Over this agreement, I nearly had a falling out with Philips.

It happened like this: Philips proposed that because they had extensive experience building IC fabs, TSMC's IC fab should also be designed by them. Upon seeing this proposal, I felt it violated TSMC's principle of independence. I shifted from "endure what can be endured" to "this cannot be endured." After initial arguments with Philips proved futile, I reported to the "Five-Person Committee": perhaps the breaking point had arrived. Zhao Yaodong (known as the "Iron Head") said: "Break then break—we can do it ourselves." But Li Dahai advocated having Li Guomiao mediate, perhaps finding a way out. After the meeting I discussed it with Commissioner Li, who decided to write to the Philips president requesting that Philips withdraw its demand to design our IC factory. The letter proved effective. A few days later, Philips no longer raised this demand. We then signed the "Technology Cooperation Agreement" with Philips in December 1986.

台湾募资

一九八六年五月，我对"五人小组"报告：与飞利浦的谈判已大致底定。"五人小组"随即致函台湾区电工器材工业同业公会理事长龚孝勇以及九家公司（台塑、华夏、中美和、声宝、宏碁电脑、神通电脑、大同、新光纺织、台湾聚合）的董事长，告诉他们台積電总股本金额，以及政府及飞利浦的参与金额。主要目的是邀请他们参与投资。

没有一个人打电话给我。"五人小组"也只要求我访问台塑王永庆。至于联成石化，访问相当顺利。苗君曾在英特尔公司担任微处理器设计工程师多年，对IC非常内行。他的投资兴趣是真实的时，苗的父亲苗育秀先生亦在座，而且很明显地是最后决策者。他也相当赞成投资。后来联成石化（亦为苗育秀先生主持）成为台積電原始股东之一。

ReadShift 双语翻译

In May 1986, I reported to the "Five-Person Committee": negotiations with Philips were substantially finalized. The "Five-Person Committee" immediately wrote to Gong Xiaoyong, chairman of the Taiwan Electrical and Electronic Manufacturers' Association, and the chairs of nine major companies (Formosa Plastics, Huaxia, Union Chemical, Tatung, Acer, Mitac, Tatung, Shin Kong Textile, Taiwan Polymer), informing them of TSMC's total capital amount and the participation amounts from the government and Philips. The primary purpose was to invite them to participate in the investment.

Not a single person called me. The "Five-Person Committee" only asked me to visit Formosa Plastics' Wang Yung-ching. As for United Petrochemical (Lien Cheng), the visit went quite smoothly. Mr. Miao (Feng-chiang) had worked at Intel for many years as a microprocessor design engineer and was very knowledgeable about ICs. His investment interest was genuine. When I visited, his father Miao Yuxiu was also present and clearly the final decision-maker. He too was quite supportive. Later, United Petrochemical (also chaired by Miao Yuxiu) became one of TSMC's original shareholders.

台塑王永庆

台塑王永庆董事长却是另一个故事。胡定华曾与王董事长合作过，所以我请他去约见。王董事长表示要请我们吃饭，并邀我们携眷。当时我无眷，但胡、史带着他们的夫人一起去了。

晚宴地点在台塑顶楼，也是王董事长私寓。宴席上王坐主位，夫人李宝珠在旁相陪，王也邀了五、六位台塑人员。胡、史及我有备而来，我们准备答复王董事长任何有关台積電的问题。

席中觥筹交错，宾主尽欢。主菜是"台塑牛排"，吃后王董事长问我喜不喜欢，我当然说喜欢，王董事长就即刻命他家人次日送几块到我家来。

但是，关于台積電的讨论却出奇地少。胡、史和我都已半醉，我们还以为王已决定投资，所以也不多问关于台積電的事。

实情恰恰相反，王董事长已决定不投资。这顿饭只是对我们的努力的回馈而已。几星期后，李达海部长电话王，问他投资意愿，王说他不投资。李部长急了，请俞院长帮忙。俞院长自己打电话给王，王才勉强同意。嘱咐我再访王（"上次你没做好，这次做得好一点"）。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Formosa Plastics chairman Wang Yung-ching was another story. Hu Ding-hua had worked with Chairman Wang before, so I asked him to arrange a meeting. Chairman Wang expressed that he would treat us to dinner and invited us to bring our spouses. I had no spouse at the time, but Hu and Shi brought their wives.

The dinner was held at the top floor of Formosa Plastics—also Chairman Wang's private residence. At the dinner, Wang sat in the host's seat, with his wife Li Baozhu accompanying him, and Wang had also invited five or six Formosa Plastics personnel. Hu, Shi, and I came prepared to answer any questions Chairman Wang might have about TSMC.

Amidst the toasts and cheerful conversation, the main course was "Formosa Plastics steak." After eating it, Chairman Wang asked me whether I liked it. Of course I said I liked it, and Chairman Wang immediately ordered his family to deliver several pieces to my home the next day.

Yet discussion about TSMC was remarkably scarce. Hu, Shi, and I were all half-drunk, and we assumed Wang had already decided to invest, so we didn't press the matter of TSMC further.

The reality was precisely the opposite: Chairman Wang had already decided not to invest. This dinner was merely a gesture reciprocating our efforts. Weeks later, Minister Li Dahai called Wang to ask about his investment intent; Wang said he would not invest. Minister Li panicked and asked Premier Yu for help. Premier Yu personally called Wang, and Wang reluctantly agreed. He instructed me to visit Wang again ("You didn't do well last time—do better this time").

二访王永庆

这次访王仍有饭吃，但气氛与上次完全不同。我单独赴宴，王神态肃杀，席中没有"三娘"，只有两位台塑人员。当我问他投资意愿，他只说："仍有兴趣"，但令我难忘的却是他的另一句话："你为什么找政府办这件事？你早来找我，也许我们已办成了。这种代工……"

令我更难忘的是他的补充："你早来找我，我们甚至可以出你月薪一万美元。"

月薪一万美元，这就是王董事长对我的慷慨评价！王董事长不知道，我也没有理由告诉他——因为告诉他会使他更生气——几个月后我就会开出对台積電第一个美国人总经理的聘书："年薪三十万美元。第一年如达到营运计划，加花红十五万美元。"

后来，王董事长承诺投资五%。当然，关键是俞院长，不是我的两次访问。

八月，李政委对我说：还缺几亿新台币，但决定不再恳求民股，缺额由中央投资（国民党投资机构）补足。

同月，民间股东签"认购书"，纲要如下：荷兰飞利浦出资二七．六%，行政院开发基金出资四八%，其他民间投资人出资二四．一%。

募资大功告成。十二月召开发起人会议，选举第一任董监，选举我为董事长。发起人会议后登记公司。

ReadShift 双语翻译

This second visit still included dinner, but the atmosphere was completely different from the last time. I attended alone. Wang's demeanor was stern. "Third Madame" was not present at the table; only two Formosa Plastics personnel accompanied him. When I asked about his investment intent, he merely said: "Still interested." But what I found even more unforgettable was another thing he said: "Why did you go to the government for this? If you had come to me earlier, perhaps we would have already done it. This foundry model..."

Even more unforgettable was his addendum: "If you had come to me earlier, we might even have offered you a monthly salary of $10,000."

A monthly salary of $10,000—this was Chairman Wang's generous appraisal of me! Chairman Wang didn't know, and I had no reason to tell him—because telling him would make him even angrier—that a few months later I would extend an offer to TSMC's first American general manager: "Annual salary $300,000. If the business plan is met in the first year, add a $150,000 bonus."

Later, Chairman Wang committed to investing 5%. Of course, the decisive factor was Premier Yu, not my two visits.

In August, Commissioner Li told me: we still lacked several hundred million NT dollars, but had decided to stop pleading with private investors—the shortfall would be made up by Central Investment (the KMT's investment arm).

In the same month, private shareholders signed "subscription documents," with the following outline: Philips Netherlands contributed 27.6%, the Executive Yuan Development Fund contributed 48%, and other private investors contributed 24.1%.

Fundraising was successfully completed. In December, the founders' meeting was convened; the first board of directors and supervisors were elected. I was elected chairman. After the founders' meeting, the company was registered.

ReadShift 双语翻译

章节

台積電篇一第十八章

张忠谋

台积电篇一·第十八章｜开辟鸿蒙

定位

一九八六至八七年的冬天，台积电即将组成，台湾媒体在一度热烈报导"政府最大投资案"后，忽然平静下来。我也借这由绚烂趋平淡、而真正考验即将来临的过渡时期，对台积电的创始初期应采取的策略，做了一个检讨。

成立台积电的目的，基本是为工研院已进行十年的IC计划及继承IC计划的VLSI计划建立工业出路，所以创始期的核心团队，就是工研院VLSI计划实验工厂的成员。作为一个要能赚钱的半导体公司，他们的强点是：成熟技术高生产良率；他们的弱点是：没有IC设计技术，制程技术落后两、三代，而且实验工厂只有台湾客户，没有国外客户，甚至连与国外客户的接触都没有。

ReadShift 双语翻译

## Positioning

In the winter of 1986-87, as TSMC was about to be formed, the Taiwanese media—after initially reporting fervently on the "government's largest investment project"—suddenly calmed down. I also took advantage of this transition period, when things were moving from excitement to calm and the real test was yet to come, to review the strategies TSMC should adopt in its early founding period.

The purpose of establishing TSMC was fundamentally to create an industrial outlet for ITRI's ten-year IC program and its successor, the VLSI program. Thus, the founding core team consisted of members from the ITRI VLSI program's experimental factory. As a semiconductor company that needed to be profitable, their strengths were: high production yield with mature technology. Their weaknesses were: no IC design technology, process technology lagging two to three generations behind, and the experimental factory only had Taiwanese clients—no foreign clients, not even any contact with foreign clients.

从"Foundry"到"专业晶圆代工"

我在第十六章已提及，考虑了工研院VLSI计划的强点及弱点，其实它的工业出路只有一条：舍弃设计，只为客户制造。早在七零年代，当时英特尔创办人之一摩尔已为此"不设计，只制造"事业取了一个名字：foundry。只是，摩尔的foundry只是一般又设计、又制造公司（IDM）的副业。把foundry成为专业，自始自台積電始。更具讽刺性的，当我找英特尔投资台積電时（第十七章），英特尔拒绝了，原因是不认为专业foundry能赚钱。

英文的foundry是一个中性名词，无语意亦无贬意，但中文一下子把foundry译成"晶圆代工"，大概因为台湾非常习惯"代工"。即使加上"专业"两字，也不能消除一般"代工"的低技术、低资本的形象。

其实台積電的"专业晶圆代工"自始就"高资本"，自始也不是"低技术"，因为即使我们创始时制程技术落后尖端技术两至三代，但我们的良率很高，而高良率反映了扎实的工程基础。

虽然我不喜欢中文"代工"附带的"低技术"形象，但"代工"是台湾习惯的名词，也不便改。台積電的定位在我心里倒毫无疑问："Dedicated Foundry"，中文翻译成"专业晶圆代工"。

ReadShift 双语翻译

As mentioned in Chapter 16, considering the strengths and weaknesses of ITRI's VLSI program, there was really only one industrial outlet: abandon design, and manufacture only for customers. As early as the 1970s, Gordon Moore, one of Intel's founders, had already given this "don't design, just manufacture" business a name: foundry. However, Moore's foundry was merely a sideline for a company that both designed and manufactured (IDM). Making foundry a specialty—professional foundry—began with TSMC. More ironically, when I sought Intel's investment in TSMC (Chapter 17), Intel refused, its reason being that it did not believe professional foundry could be profitable.

The English word "foundry" is a neutral term, with no semantic nor pejorative connotation. But Chinese immediately translated foundry as "晶圆代工" (wafer foundry), probably because Taiwan was very accustomed to the concept of "代工" (contract manufacturing). Even adding the word "专业" (dedicated/professional) couldn't eliminate the low-technology, low-capital image associated with typical "代工" (contract manufacturing).

In fact, TSMC's "dedicated foundry" was "high-capital" from the start, and never "low-technology" from the start, because even though our process technology lagged the cutting edge by two to three generations at founding, our yield was very high, and high yield reflected solid engineering foundations.

Although I didn't like the "low-technology" image that the Chinese term "代工" carried, "代工" was a term Taiwan was accustomed to and inconvenient to change. TSMC's positioning in my mind was unquestionable: "Dedicated Foundry," translated into Chinese as "专业晶圆代工" (dedicated wafer foundry).

两个策略，一个价值

今日（二零二零年）的台積電以尖端技术（七纳米、五纳米、三纳米）见称。因为台積電领先世界的尖端半导体技术，才成为我所称的"地缘政治策略家的兵家必争之地"。最近有友人问我：

"听说你们创始时的策略是市场营销，而不是达到尖端技术。我以为我一定听错了。"

他没有听错。创办时最大问题是没有客户。一厂开始时的产能是少少的每月一千片（六吋晶圆），第一年整年都没填满。创始时我们就准备建二厂，二厂初期的预计产能是每月一万两千片，从每月几百片跳到每月一万两千片，不但需要想象力，还需要策略以及说服力，才能说服董事会拨款给我们。

所以我们的第一策略是：开关美国，其次欧洲市场。美、欧市场是当时全世界最大的半导体市场。台積電核心团队只熟悉台湾市场。与美、欧市场比，台湾市场真是微乎其微。谁能领导核心团队开关美、欧市场？我认为自己是最佳人选，但在台積電成立时，我任工研院院长才一年多，正火热地要改革工研院，绝无时间或精力再兼一个创新、开关的任务。替代方案就是：雇一个富有半导体经营能力的美国人做总经理。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Today (2020) TSMC is renowned for its cutting-edge technology (7nm, 5nm, 3nm). It is precisely because of TSMC's world-leading advanced semiconductor technology that it has become what I call "a place that geopolitical strategists fight over." Recently a friend asked me:

"I heard that your founding strategy was marketing, not achieving cutting-edge technology. I thought I must have misheard."

He had not misheard. The biggest problem at founding was having no customers. Fab 1 started with a modest capacity of a thousand wafers per month (6-inch), and wasn't fully utilized for the entire first year. At founding, we were already planning to build Fab 2, whose initial projected capacity was twelve thousand wafers per month. Jumping from a few hundred per month to twelve thousand per month required not only imagination but also strategy and persuasiveness to convince the board to appropriate funds to us.

So our first strategy was: open up the U.S. market, then the European market. The U.S. and European markets were the largest semiconductor markets in the world at that time. TSMC's core team was only familiar with the Taiwanese market. Compared to the U.S. and European markets, the Taiwanese market was truly negligible. Who could lead the core team to open up the U.S. and European markets? I considered myself the best candidate, but when TSMC was founded, I had been ITRI president for only a little over a year and was passionately reforming ITRI. I absolutely had no time or energy to also take on the pioneering, market-opening mission. The alternative was: hire an American with semiconductor management capability to be general manager.

第二策略与价值观

第二策略是：加强核心团队已有的高良率能力。高良率是我们创台时的长处，也是我们选择"专业晶圆代工"的原因，但核心团队的高良率建立在当时台湾市场需求的廉价品上（例如电子表IC）。现在我们要开关高、中档美、欧市场。他们对于品质、可靠度、制程监控（Process Control）、制程改变控制（Change Control）等等，要比台湾市场讲究得多。我有相当信心我们核心团队既有的高良率建立在扎实工程基础上，现在要更上一层。

除了这两个策略外，我从我做"客制品"的经历体验到：千金难买客户对你的信任。现在，台積電只做"客制品"。我们必须一开始就赢得客户的信任。不轻易答应，但答应的，一定要不计代价做对。对供应商、对社会，甚至对竞争者，也要诚信以对。不但对客户要诚信，我不相信一个公司能做一个人又是另一面。

ReadShift 双语翻译

The second strategy was: strengthen the core team's existing high-yield capability. High yield was our strength at founding, and the reason we chose the "dedicated foundry" model. But the core team's high yield had been built on low-cost products for the Taiwanese market (e.g., electronic watch ICs). Now we were going to open up the high-end and mid-range U.S. and European markets. Their demands regarding quality, reliability, process control, change control, and so on were far more rigorous than those of the Taiwanese market. I had considerable confidence that our core team's existing high yield was built on solid engineering foundations, and now needed to go one level higher.

Beyond these two strategies, I had learned from my own experience doing "custom products" as TI: customer trust is a thousand pieces of gold cannot buy. Now, TSMC did only "custom products." We had to win customers' trust from the very beginning. Don't promise easily, but once promised, deliver at all costs. To suppliers, to society, even to competitors—conduct with integrity. Not only to customers must we be honest; I don't believe a company can act one way to people and another way otherwise.

商誉竞争

当年我对经建会报告成立台積電，并且说台積電要以"好的服务"竞争时，中央银行总裁曾经哈哈了一声："台湾公司要凭商誉竞争，倒是第一次听闻。"现在，我们真的要做了。

起始台積電的两个策略，后来有增加，最重要的增加就是十二年后（一九九九年）的"技术领先"，也随市场和竞争环境而有所改变，但起始的价值观——诚信，却一直没变过。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Back when I reported to the Council for Economic Planning and Development on establishing TSMC, and said that TSMC would compete on "good service," the Central Bank governor laughed out loud: "A Taiwanese company competing on reputation—that's the first I've heard of it." Now, we were really going to do it.

TSMC's initial two strategies were later augmented—the most important addition being "technology leadership" twelve years later (1999)—and they evolved with the market and competitive environment. But the founding value—integrity—never changed.

戴克斯——第一任总经理

一九八六年秋，台積電募资有谱，我就开始物色美国人总经理。我接触了三、四位我熟悉的德仪前下属，现在已在别的半导体公司任要职。竟无一人有兴趣，连来台湾看一看的兴趣都没有。

就在那时，戴克斯和我接触了。我认识戴克斯，但不熟。一九八五年春，我们曾一起参加过一次美国半导体业协会理事会。那时我代表通用器材；他代表GE半导体公司。一年半后，我已在台湾，即将组成台積電；他仍在GE，但即将失业。他即将失业的原因是：GE总裁威尔许决定关闭GE半导体公司。

威尔许是一九八一九九一年至二零零一年的GE总裁，也是一个风云人物，一度被誉为"二十世纪后半最佳企业总裁"。GE是一个许多事业的集合体。在威尔许接任总裁初期，他检讨了每一事业，对一个在它行业营收排名不高的事业（例如GE半导体公司在半导体行业的营收排名也许是第十几名或第二十几名），威尔许只有一个命令："五年内做到第一或第二名；否则，关门！"对戴克斯而言，要他做到半导体业第一或第二等于要他爬喜马拉雅山，所以结论是关门。拖到一九八六年秋，威尔许的五年时限亦将到临，戴克斯亦将失业，所以戴对台積電总经理这机会大有兴趣。

In the fall of 1986, with TSMC's fundraising looking promising, I began scouting for an American general manager. I approached three or four former TI subordinates whom I knew well, who were now holding senior positions at other semiconductor companies. Not a single one was interested—they weren't even interested in coming to Taiwan to take a look.

Just then, Douglas Dexter made contact with me. I knew Dexter, but not well. In the spring of 1985, we had both attended a meeting of the U.S. Semiconductor Industry Association board of directors. At that time I represented General Electric (G.E.) equipment; he represented GE's semiconductor division. A year and a half later, I was in Taiwan, about to form TSMC; he was still at GE, but about to lose his job. The reason he was about to be unemployed: GE president Jack Welch had decided to shut down GE's semiconductor business.

Welch was GE's president from 1981 to 2001, a legendary figure once hailed as "the best corporate president of the second half of the twentieth century." GE was a collection of many businesses. Early in Welch's tenure as president, he reviewed each business. For a business whose revenue ranking in its industry was not high (e.g., GE Semiconductor's ranking in the semiconductor industry was perhaps fifteenth or twentieth), Welch had only one command: "Become first or second within five years—otherwise, shut it down!" For Dexter, asking him to make GE Semiconductor first or second in the industry was like asking him to climb Mt. Everest, so the conclusion was to shut it down. This dragged on until the fall of 1986, when Welch's five-year deadline was approaching and Dexter was about to lose his job. So Dexter was very interested in the opportunity to be TSMC's general manager.

飞利浦的审核

我在一九八六年十月亲访戴克斯于他居住地——北卡罗来纳州图兰市，相谈甚投契。戴很认同"专业晶圆代工"商业模式以及开关美欧市场策略；戴也在年底来台湾与"五人小组"五人小组相会。"五人小组"没有什么意见，只是戴和我都觉得很奇怪，在晚餐席上"五人小组"除了在介绍时与戴寒暄几句外，只互相中文谈笑，而没有对戴发一言或问一句话。

根据当时的"股东协议"，总经理由最大股东（开发基金）提名，董事会通过后任命。飞利浦在董事会十席内占三席，所以我也请飞利浦在台湾的两位董事与戴克斯面谈，两位都很支持。我以为我已做得很周到了，想不到一星期后我就接到第三位飞利浦董事（克列斯曼）的电话，他数落了我一顿，警告我"必须小心"（Careful）维护飞利浦权益，而且坚持面试戴克斯。我只得嘱戴于一九八七年一月去荷兰见克列斯曼。见戴面后，克列斯曼倒很爽快同意。戴克斯也在二月初来到台湾报到。

In October 1986, I personally visited Dexter at his home—Raleigh, North Carolina. We hit it off well. Dexter also came to Taiwan at the end of the year to meet with the "Five-Person Committee." The committee had no objections, but both Dexter and I thought it was strange: at the dinner, apart from exchanging a few pleasantries during introductions, the committee members only chatted with each other in Chinese and didn't speak a word to Dexter or ask him a single question.

Under the then-existing "Shareholders Agreement," the general manager was nominated by the largest shareholder (the Development Fund) and appointed upon board approval. Philips held three of the board's ten seats, so I also arranged for Philips' two directors in Taiwan to interview Dexter. Both were very supportive. I thought I had been quite thorough, but barely a week later I received a call from a third Philips director (Krigsman), who lectured me, warning me to "be careful" to protect Philips' rights and insisting on interviewing Dexter himself. I had no choice but to ask Dexter to go to the Netherlands in January 1987 to meet Krigsman. After meeting Dexter, Krigsman readily approved. Dexter came to Taiwan to report for duty in early February.

核心团队踟蹰

在一九八五年九月开始构想台積電时，我以为如果办成台積電，一定会有一位工研院高层主管带领一个IC计划核心团队来台積電。后来我开始对胡、史说台積電必须开关美、欧市场，所以第一任总经理应该是美国人；此后我发现胡已无兴趣来台積電，他那时已是交大校长、工研院院长的候选人，已无兴趣担任台積電总经理以下的任何职务；至于史钦泰，我也发现他的兴趣主要还是学术，志愿留在工研院。到台積電即将组成时，看起来，实验工厂厂长曾繁城是唯一可能的核心团队领导人。曾繁城在电子所的职级低所长两级。他的上司是电子所副所长。这位副所长也不愿加入台積電。

但是，在台积电准备开张前两星期，胡定华告知我：连曾繁城也有疑虑，他和核心团队都担心加入台積電后未来的前途。胡定华告诉我："你必须与曾谈。"

When I first conceived of TSMC in September 1985, I thought that if TSMC were successfully established, a senior ITRI manager would definitely lead an IC program core team to come to TSMC. Later, I began telling Hu and Shi that TSMC had to open up the U.S. and European markets, so the first general manager should be American. Afterward, I discovered that Hu was no longer interested in coming to TSMC—he was already a candidate for president of National Chiao Tung University and ITRI president, and he was no longer interested in any position below TSMC general manager. As for Shi Qin-tai, I also discovered that his interests were primarily academic; he wished to stay at ITRI. By the time TSMC was about to be formed, it appeared that Zeng Fan-cheng, the experimental factory director, was the only potential core team leader. Zeng Fan-cheng's rank at the Electronics Research Institute was two levels below the institute director. His immediate boss was the deputy institute director. This deputy director was also unwilling to join TSMC.

However, two weeks before TSMC was preparing to open, Hu Ding-hua informed me: even Zeng Fan-cheng had doubts. He and the core team all worried about their future prospects after joining TSMC. Hu Ding-hua told me: "You must talk with Zeng."

曾繁城的工会领袖姿态

我与曾谈了。后来我与他相熟后，曾经告诉我他那次他对我要求的姿态，简直是工会领袖对资方谈判的姿态！可怜我其实也是"劳方"，为了要办成台積電，只好充当"资方"，消释曾繁城的疑虑。

曾代表核心团队质疑两大点：第一，台積電如何与韩、日公司竞争？他没提美国公司，因为美国公司比韩、日公司更高一筹。韩、日公司我们已不能应付了。这质疑是我在募资期常要应付的。我重复了一遍我的两个倚靠：第一个倚靠是我们的"专业晶圆代工"商业模式。我们不与美、韩、日半导体公司竞争，它们反而是我们的客户。第二个倚靠是核心团队的高良率能力。对第一个倚靠，曾似乎半信半疑。对第二个倚靠，我的信心似乎高于核心团队对自己的信心。

但是，曾让我的辩论通过了。于是曾繁城提出第二个质疑。在此以前我的以为是：既然工研院以财团法人身份，素享高薪美誉，所以核心团队移到台積電，薪资不改；以后，当然再说。

但是，曾给了我一个比较复杂的解释。他说：台湾公司的习惯除发固定薪资外，每年都会视业绩发红利。当然，有的美国公司也发红利，但对一般员工而言，红利只是员工收入的小部分。照曾繁城那天所言，红利可以是收入的大部分。

我听懂了曾繁城的话后，觉得员工红利也不失为对员工的合理补贴。本来台湾工程师的收入远低于欧、美、日本。现在台積電要在世界竞争，应该也在员工收入上做相当程度的看齐。

I talked with Zeng. Later, after we became well acquainted, he told me that his posture during that negotiation with me was simply that of a union leader negotiating with management! The pity was that I was actually also "labor." In order to make TSMC happen, I had no choice but to play "management" and dispel Zeng Fan-cheng's doubts.

Zeng raised two major points on behalf of the core team. First: How would TSMC compete with Korean and Japanese companies? He didn't mention American companies, because American companies were a notch above Korean and Japanese ones. We could already barely handle Korean and Japanese companies. This was a question I frequently had to address during the fundraising period. I repeated my two pillars of reliance: The first was our "dedicated foundry" business model. We didn't compete with American, Korean, or Japanese semiconductor companies—they would actually be our customers. The second was the core team's high-yield capability. Regarding the first pillar, Zeng seemed half-believing. Regarding the second pillar, my confidence seemed higher than the core team's confidence in themselves.

Nevertheless, Zeng let my arguments pass. Then Zeng Fan-cheng raised his second concern. Previously, I had assumed: since ITRI, as a foundation, enjoyed a reputation for high salaries, when the core team transferred to TSMC, their salaries would remain unchanged; and of course, things would be discussed again later.

But Zeng gave me a more nuanced explanation. He said: Taiwanese company practice, in addition to paying a fixed salary, was to issue bonuses according to performance every year. Of course, some American companies also gave bonuses, but for ordinary employees, bonuses were only a small part of income. From what Zeng Fan-cheng said that day, it sounded like bonuses could be the majority of income.

After I understood what Zeng Fan-cheng was saying, I felt employee bonuses were also a reasonable form of compensation for employees. Originally, Taiwanese engineers' incomes were far lower than those in Europe, America, and Japan. Now TSMC was going to compete globally; we should bring employee compensation to a relatively comparable level.

建立"激励制度"

他回去告诉核心团队，核心团队也满意了。总的来说，我们又有总经理，又有核心团队，可以开张了。大约一年后，台積電发出首次员工红利；以后几十年员工红利极少中断；后来又加上员工认股。

二十九年后，大部分核心团队仍在公司，经历多次灾难，也与我并肩打过多次硬战。他们之中产生了一个副董事长、三个资深副总、五个副总。一点怀疑、一点后悔都没有。

每次我想起核心团队加入台積電前的踟蹰，以及曾繁城那天的工会领袖姿态，总不禁怀念初加入德仪的我（"自传上册"第十四章）——多么年轻！多么有信心！多么兴奋地赴那场"与命运的约会"！多么幼稚！多么天真！当时十七岁的我，一点踟蹰都没有，分核心团队加入时和加入德仪时差不多年轻，但他们的心情竟和我的心情大不一样。时、地、人都变了。

He went back and told the core team, and the core team was also satisfied. In sum, we now had both a general manager and a core team—we could open for business. About a year later, TSMC issued its first employee bonus. In the decades since, employee bonuses have rarely been interrupted; later, employee stock options were added.

Twenty-nine years later, most of the core team was still with the company, having weathered multiple crises and fought many hard battles alongside me. Among them emerged one vice chairman, three senior vice presidents, and five vice presidents. Without a trace of doubt or regret.

Whenever I recall the core team's hesitation before joining TSMC, and Zeng Fan-cheng's union leader posture that day, I cannot help but reminisce about myself when I first joined TI ("Autobiography, Volume 1," Chapter 14)—how young! How confident! How excited I was to keep that "rendezvous with destiny"! How naive! How innocent! At seventeen, I had not a trace of hesitation. When portions of the core team joined TSMC, they were about the same age as when I had joined TI, yet their state of mind was so different from mine at that time. Times, places, and people had all changed.

章节

台積電篇一第十九章

张忠谋

台积电篇一·第十九章｜筚路蓝缕

一厂

一九八七年二月底，台积电公司登记完成，就在"一厂"开张营业。一厂是一座两层楼加地下室的工研院建筑。工研院本拟以此作为新的IC实验工厂，现在衍生了台积电，就把此建筑物，连同已买进的若干制造设备，一起租赁给台积电。一楼是工厂。工研院已买进的制造设备并不完整，台积电在头两年花了四千多万美元添置制造设备，把产能凑加到每月一万三千片六吋晶圆。

地下室是员工餐厅，一楼部分及二楼是办公室。除了作业员全时在一楼工厂工作外，其余员工在一、二楼有办公桌，几位高层经理有各自办公室，还有几间公用会议室。这么多人都在一层楼上，相当挤。我的正职仍为工研院院长，虽非常关心台积电，且常来"一厂"开会，但的确不需要在台积电有办公室，当然也不领台积电报酬。一直到一九八八年年底，我成为工研院董事长，就不领工研院任何薪资，只领台积电薪资。
