## Fab 1

At the end of February 1987, TSMC completed its company registration and opened for business in "Fab 1." Fab 1 was a two-story ITRI building with a basement. ITRI had originally intended this building as a new IC experimental factory. Now that TSMC had been spun out, ITRI leased this building to TSMC along with certain manufacturing equipment already purchased. The first floor was the factory. The manufacturing equipment ITRI had purchased was incomplete; TSMC spent over $40 million in the first two years adding manufacturing equipment, bringing capacity up to 13,000 six-inch wafers per month.

The basement was the employee cafeteria; portions of the first floor and the second floor were offices. Except for operators who worked full-time on the factory floor, the rest of the employees had desks on the first and second floors. Several senior managers had their own offices, plus a few shared conference rooms. So many people on one floor rather cramped. My primary position was still ITRI president. Although I was very concerned about TSMC and often came to "Fab 1" for meetings, I really didn't need an office at TSMC and of course drew no salary from TSMC. It wasn't until the end of 1988, when I became ITRI chairman, that I stopped receiving any salary from ITRI and only drew TSMC compensation.

戴克斯上任一把火

在工作积极度上，戴克斯一点都不负我的期望。一上任，他积极推动我的两个策略：开关美国市场和巩固生产能力。他先聘雇美国行销经理，此人名匹列切（Steve Pletcher），是戴在GE时的行销经理。匹住在佛罗里达州，而我们的未来客户大部分都在西岸，所以台积电的第一年，匹几乎每周都飞加州拜访客户，住在加州旅馆里，周末又飞回佛州家。如此一年余，直到第二年（一九八八年），我们才在加州圣荷西城租了办公室，并招雇新的行销工程师。在第一年内，匹每两、三个月来台湾一次，对戴及我报告他的进度。在第一年内他没有带回订单，但每次我问他对我们的"专业晶圆代工"是否可行？他总竖起他的大拇指，乐观地说一定可行。

ReadShift 双语翻译

In terms of work initiative, Dexter did not disappoint my expectations at all. Upon taking office, he aggressively pushed my two strategies: opening up the U.S. market and strengthening production capabilities. He first hired an American marketing manager named Steve Pletcher, who had been Dexter's marketing manager at GE. Pletcher lived in Florida, while most of our future customers were on the West Coast, so for TSMC's first year, Pletcher flew to California almost every week to visit clients, staying in California motels and flying back to Florida on weekends. This continued for over a year, until the second year (1988), when we rented an office in San Jose, California and hired new engineering marketing staff. During the first year, Pletcher came to Taiwan every two to three months to report his progress to Dexter and me. He didn't bring back any orders in the first year, but whenever I asked him whether our "dedicated foundry" model would work, he would always give a thumbs-up and optimistically say it definitely would.

魏谋与核心团队缺口

戴克斯第二个重要聘雇是营运副总魏谋。魏谋德裔美籍，半导体工程博士，在德仪研发单位实验线当主任工程师。我在德仪时魏也在，但他的职阶低我好几级，所以我并不认识他。现在戴克斯把他找来，要我面试，我觉得他无论知识或经验，都足以执行我的第二策略——巩固生产能力，所以同意雇他。他成为以曾繁城为首、从工研院过来的核心团队的上司。起先，曾繁城有点不舒服，但几个月后，也看出在生产技术上，魏有可指导曾及核心团队之处，所以曾原来的不舒服也就消失了。

但是核心团队有一个缺洞——无人做行销。本来工研院的实验工厂就没有行销人员，所有的生意都是客户闻名而来。现在，台积电的名气不如工研院，我们要登客户门求生意。事实上，一九八七年台积电百分之百营收，一九八八年七六%营收均来自台湾客户。我的美欧市场策略，匹列切的大拇指，一直到两年后才有效著效果。这两年，台积电靠蔡志群的行销。后来蔡志群也成为长期台积人，直到二零二二年初，才从台积电亚太行销业务主管职务退休。

虽然戴克斯态度积极而且乐观，但是，没有生意还是没有生意。虽然我们有每月几千片（六吋）产能，第一年每月通常只有几百片生意。记得魏谋加入后几星期，我问他："何时可以填满产能？"他恨恨地回答："和遥遥无期。"

第一年结账，营收四百万美元，只是募资时营业计划的三分之一；营业亏损五百四十万美元，倒低于营业计划的亏损七百三十万美元。这是因为年中就预测营收不能达标，处处节省之故。

这是相当暗淡的一年，以后还有几年暗淡；但是，第一个大突破就在转弯角上。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Dexter's second key hire was COO Wei Mou. Wei Mou was German-American, a Ph.D. in semiconductor engineering who had served as a staff engineer at TI's R&D pilot line. When I was at TI, Wei was also there, but his rank was several levels below mine, so I didn't know him. Now Dexter brought him in for me to interview. I felt that his knowledge and experience were sufficient to execute my second strategy—strengthening production capabilities—so I agreed to hire him. He became the boss of the core team that had come from ITRI with Zeng Fan-cheng at its head. At first, Zeng Fan-cheng felt somewhat uncomfortable, but after a few months, he could see that in production technology, Wei had things to teach Zeng and the core team, so Zeng's initial discomfort dissipated.

However, the core team had a critical gap—no one doing marketing. Originally, ITRI's experimental factory had no marketing personnel at all; all business came to them by reputation. Now, TSMC's reputation was not as strong as ITRI's; we had to go to customers' doors to solicit business. In fact, in 1987, 100% of TSMC's revenue came from Taiwanese clients; in 1988, 76% still came from Taiwan. My U.S.-Europe market strategy and Pletcher's thumbs-up didn't show significant results until two years later. During these two years, TSMC relied on Cai Zhi-qun's marketing. Later, Cai Zhi-qun also became a long-term TSMC employee, retiring only in early 2022 from his position as head of TSMC's Asia-Pacific marketing business.

Although Dexter's attitude was aggressive and optimistic, nonetheless, no business was no business. Although we had capacity of several thousand wafers (6-inch) per month, in the first year we typically only had a few hundred wafers of business per month. I remember a few weeks after Wei Mou joined, I asked him: "When can we fill capacity?" He replied ruefully: "It's nowhere in sight."

First-year revenue was $4 million, only one-third of the business plan's projection at fundraising. Operating loss was $5.4 million, which was actually less than the projected $7.3 million loss, because mid-year we forecast revenue would miss target and cut costs everywhere.

This was a rather bleak year, and there would be more bleak years to come; but the first major breakthrough was just around the corner.

英特尔来敲门

一九八七年十一月，我忽然接到友人虞有澄兄的通知，说安迪·葛洛夫要来台湾，顺便想参观台积电。

虞有澄是当时英特尔资深副总；葛洛夫是当时英特尔执行副总，次年即将接总裁位；而英特尔那时虽尚未是最高营收半导体公司（德仪仍是），但技术领先群伦，已大有业界龙头气势。我与虞及葛洛夫都熟悉，当然不会轻慢虞的要求。只是我纳闷：英特尔去年才拒绝了我们的募资要求，现在我们需要他们的投资仍办成了公司，怎么他们忽然有兴趣要参观我们？难道他们那么快就要用我们了？

当然我要好好接待葛洛夫，但是他要来那天恰巧我已有先约要在美国，所以我仔细交代戴克斯，好在戴与葛洛夫也相当熟悉。

我返台后，戴对我报告：葛的参观非常顺利。看到我们的工厂后，葛惊呼："居然你们真的有一座运转的六吋晶圆厂！"戴让葛看我们的良率纪录，葛也相当佩服，并且透露了一点英特尔"可能用得着台积电"的意愿。

ReadShift 双语翻译

In November 1987, I suddenly received word from my friend You Yicheng (Eugene) that Andy Grove would be coming to Taiwan and wanted to visit TSMC.

You Yicheng was then Intel Senior Vice President; Grove was then Executive Vice President of Intel and would become president the following year. Although Intel was not yet the highest-revenue semiconductor company (TI still was), its technology led by a wide margin and it had already developed an aura of industry leader. I knew both You and Grove well, and of course would not take You's request lightly. But I puzzled: Intel had rejected our fundraising request only last year, and now that we had formed the company without their investment, why were they suddenly interested in visiting us? Could they really need us that quickly?

Of course I needed to receive Grove well, but it happened that on the day he was to visit I already had a prior commitment in the U.S. So I gave Dexter careful instructions, and fortunately Dexter also knew Grove fairly well.

After I returned to Taiwan, Dexter reported to me: Grove's visit went very smoothly. Upon seeing our factory, Grove exclaimed: "You actually do have an operating six-inch fab!" Dexter showed Grove our yield records, which Grove quite admired, and even disclosed a little of Intel's "possible need for TSMC."

英特尔的考验

几个月后，英特尔真的来与我们谈生意了。第一个生意是一.五微米的微控制器，英特尔两代（约三年）前的产品。英特尔因为要把他们的生产资源用在更先进的产品上，所以要我们代工。对我们来说，一.五微米正是我们最先进的技术，所以这是很好的机会让我们量产刚在开发的技术。

葛洛夫非常重视生产。在英特尔自己的工厂里，假使两个厂生产同一产品，他要求这两厂必须使用"完全相同"（copy exactly）的制程。现在要我们生产他三年前出炉的产品，他还是不肯把他的制程告诉我们，而要用我们自己的、刚开发出来的制程"试制"他的产品，让他在良率、品质及可靠度上决定是否及格。这个考试我们通过了。

再下来的对我们更为重要。英特尔要我们建立整套世界级生产制度，包括统计制程控制（Statistical Process Control）、品质控制、设备预防维修等等。我们花了一、两年，但在二厂开始量产时（一九九零年），也完成了。英特尔交给我们第一个产品一年后，又在次年把一.二微米DRAM交给我们代工，要我们走同样的步骤。

英特尔的两宗生意，在台积电创始后的第二及第三年发生。对台积电生产团队，这是一个醍醐灌顶的洗礼！从一个虽良率很高，但只做本地低阶产品的团队，他们证明了他们"继续学习"的能力，他们开始进入"世界级"了。

ReadShift 双语翻译

A few months later, Intel really came to talk business with us. The first deal was a 1.5-micron microcontroller, Intel's product from about two generations (approximately three) years earlier. Intel needed us to manufacture it because they wanted to deploy their production resources on more advanced products. For us, 1.5 microns was our most advanced technology, so this was a great opportunity to mass-produce our newly developed technology.

Grove took manufacturing extremely seriously. In Intel's own fabs, if two fabs made the same product, he demanded that they use "identical" (copy exactly) processes. Now, having us manufacture a product that had debuted three years ago, he still refused to tell us his process. Instead, he wanted us to "trial manufacture" his product using our own, newly developed process, and then he would judge whether we were up to standard in yield, quality, and reliability. We passed this exam.

What followed was even more important for us. Intel required us to establish a complete world-class production system, including Statistical Process Control, quality control, equipment preventive maintenance, and more. This took us a year or two, but by the time Fab 2 began volume production (1990), it was complete. A year after Intel gave us the first product, the following year they also gave us a 1.2-micron DRAM to manufacture, going through the same steps.

Intel's two deals occurred in TSMC's second and third years. For TSMC's production team, this was a revelatory baptism! From a team that, despite having high yield, only made low-end local products, they demonstrated their "ability to continue learning" and began entering the "world-class" ranks.

英特尔的验证

英特尔后，飞利浦、德仪、摩托罗拉陆续找我们代工。德仪和摩托罗拉找我们代工的原因和英特尔相似。飞利浦则是因为我们良率比飞利浦自己厂的良率高。我为台积电募资时看到的荷兰飞利浦新厂，其实是克列斯曼的"最后一搏"。后来向台积电购买的价格比自己制造成本低，克列斯曼的职位也敲起警钟。

英特尔的两宗生意，也是对我们"价值观"的考验。有相当长的时期，这生意赔本。但我们的价值观是"不计代价，实现承诺"，咬紧牙关做下去。英特尔也委托另一家公司代工。那家公司因赔本而半途放弃，总经理还以大拇指及食指做成一个圆圈（象征银钱），对英特尔说："这是我们的价值。"与台积电多么不同！

对我，英特尔的生意是一个莫大的鼓励。它验证了"专业晶圆代工"商业模式；也验证我们"巩固生产能力"及"进军美、欧市场"策略的正确性；它也成功考验了我们的价值观。在创立的三、四年内，台积电已塑造了它未来成功的雏型。八八、八八、八年的业绩还不是很好，但在我心中，台积电的成功已不是一个问号。

ReadShift 双语翻译

After Intel, Philips, TI, and Motorola successively came to us for foundry services. TI and Motorola's reasons for coming were similar to Intel's. Philips came because our yield was higher than that of Philips' own fab. The new Philips fab in the Netherlands that I had seen while fundraising for TSMC was actually Krigsman's "last stand." Later, buying from TSMC cost less than manufacturing it themselves, and Krigsman's position began to ring alarm bells.

Intel's two deals were also a test of our "values." For a considerable period, these deals were conducted at a loss. But our value was "deliver on promises at all costs," so we gritted our teeth and carried on. Intel also outsourced manufacturing to another company. That company gave up midway because of losses; even the general manager made a circle with his thumb and forefinger (symbolizing money) and told Intel: "This is what we value." How different from TSMC!

For me, Intel's business was an enormous encouragement. It validated the "dedicated foundry" business model; it validated the correctness of our "strengthen production capabilities" and "enter U.S. and European markets" strategies; and it successfully tested our values. Within three or four years of founding, TSMC had shaped the prototype of its future success. The performance in '88, '89, '90 was not yet great, but in my heart, TSMC's success was no longer a question mark.

戴克斯犯错

戴克斯是一个不错的总经理，但在第一年底，他犯了一个错误——他低估了飞利浦在台积电的影响力。根据"投资协议"，飞利浦有权任命台积电财务副总。在台积电创始时，飞利浦派了一位以前在飞利浦高雄厂的财务主任H君过来。H对戴克斯报告。第一年底，戴克斯对H表现不满，要换人。他应该先与飞利浦高层商量，但他没有这样做。他直接请H回飞利浦。

H不服，写信给台积电的董监事，诉说戴克斯的不是。此时戴克斯和我想请飞利浦再派一位财务长过来。但飞利浦不肯，他们要先追究戴的错。搞了几个月后，戴在压力下辞职，飞利浦另自荷兰总部派一位财务长来台积电。

戴克斯在压力下辞职，使我相当灰心。两年前，我在三、四个人拒绝我后，才找到戴克斯。戴完全认同我主导的商业模式、策略和价值，而且执行不遗余力。一年后就失去他，一时也找不到适当的人。幸而他已雇了营运副总——魏谋，就让魏谋试做总经理吧！

魏谋是一个工程师，十分认同"巩固生产能力"策略，七、八分认同"专业晶圆代工"模式，对"诚信"价值观也无意见，但他相当轻视市场及行销，好像以为只要有技术、能制造，客户就会自己找上门。反正我们已有美国及台湾行销经理。起初我有点担心匹列切，但匹确实告诉我：他至少短期内不会离开。

戴克斯个人的逆运很快好转。他离台几个月后，忽然飞利浦宣布：已聘戴克斯为Signetics（飞利浦的美国子公司）总经理。Signetics的规模，比当时台积电至少大好几倍，而且位在美国——戴克斯的祖国。所以对戴克斯而言，Signetics不失为好的归宿。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Dexter was a decent general manager, but by the end of his first year, he made a mistake—he underestimated Philips' influence within TSMC. Under the "Investment Agreement," Philips had the right to appoint TSMC's financial vice president. When TSMC was founded, Philips dispatched a former finance manager from its Kaohsiung factory, Mr. H, to TSMC. H reported to Dexter. At the end of the first year, Dexter was dissatisfied with H's performance and wanted to replace him. He should have first consulted with senior Philips management, but he didn't. He directly asked H to return to Philips.

H不服 (was not convinced) and wrote to TSMC's directors and supervisors, complaining about Dexter's wrongdoing. By this time, Dexter and I wanted to ask Philips to send another CFO. But Philips refused; they wanted to first hold Dexter accountable for his mistake. After several months of deadlock, Dexter resigned under pressure, and Philips sent another CFO from its Netherlands headquarters to TSMC.

Dexter's resignation under pressure made me quite disheartened. Two years earlier, only after three or four people had rejected me did I find Dexter. Dexter completely identified with the business model, strategies, and values I championed, and executed them tirelessly. Now after only one year I had lost him, and I couldn't immediately find a suitable replacement. Fortunately, he had already hired the COO—Wei Mou—so let Wei Mou try being general manager!

Wei Mou was an engineer who strongly identified with the "strengthen production capabilities" strategy, identified about 70-80% with the "dedicated foundry" model, and had no issue with the "integrity" value. But he rather looked down on marketing and sales, as though he thought that as long as you had technology and could manufacture, customers would come knocking on their own. In any case, we had both American and Taiwanese marketing managers. At first I worried a bit about Pletcher, but Pletcher assured me that he would not leave, at least in the short term.

Dexter's personal fortunes soon took a for the better. A few months after he left Taiwan, Philips suddenly announced: it had hired Dexter as general manager of Signetics (Philips' American subsidiary). Signetics was at least several times larger than TSMC at the time, and it was located in the U.S.—Dexter's home country. So for Dexter, Signetics was not a bad destination.

二厂的创新

在倡议台积电及募资时，我一直视一厂为过渡厂，而自己设计、建造的二厂为我们头五年的主力。募资金额也以建立及营运二厂所需资本为主。一厂只是初期"练兵"地点而已。所以几乎从一厂开张第一天，我们就开始设计、规划二厂；并且在同年九月，就向董事会提出二厂投资案。

二厂的初期规模是每月（六吋）三万片。在我们对董事会提案二厂时，我们每月生意只有几百片！克列斯曼（代表飞利浦的台积电董事）以为我们发疯，领导全董事会反对，当然不能通过。

董事会三个月一次。被拒的一个半月后，我们重整旗鼓，把提案的包装稍微更改，而且给足克列斯曼面子——我、戴克斯、魏谋、繁城四人特地联袂飞硅谷，访克列斯曼及飞利浦半导体财务长于他们在Signetics的办公室，并花了几小时时间解释美欧生意即将到来，我们需要现在就通过二厂案。这次访问果然奏效。三个月后的董事会，克列斯曼不再反对，二厂投资案也就顺利通过了。

二厂于次年（一九八八年）四月在新竹科学园区动土，一九九零年开始运作，开启了我下篇要讲的台积电"咆哮九零年代"。

使得台积电能够咆哮的原因之一，是二厂的创新。当然，"专业晶圆代工"商业模式是台积电最大的创新，但持续不断技术上、生产上、市场上的创新，自公司创立就开始。二厂就有两个相当重要的决定。

ReadShift 双语翻译

When proposing TSMC and raising funds, I always viewed Fab 1 as a transitional facility, while Fab 2, which we would design and build ourselves, would be our main workhorse for the first five years. The fundraising amount was also based on the capital needed to build and operate Fab 2. Fab 1 was merely an initial "training" site. So almost from Fab 1's first day of operations, we began designing and planning Fab 2, and in September of that same year, we presented the Fab 2 investment proposal to the board.

Fab 2's initial projected capacity was 30,000 wafers (6-inch) per month. When we proposed Fab 2 to the board, our monthly business was only a few hundred wafers! Krigsman (the TSMC director representing Philips) thought we had gone crazy and led the entire board in opposition—naturally, it could not pass.

The board met once every three months. A month and a half after the rejection, we regrouped, slightly adjusted the presentation packaging, and gave Krigesman ample face—Dexter, Wei Mou, Fan-cheng, and I together flew to Silicon Valley and visited Krigesman and the Philips semiconductor CFO at their Signetics offices, spending several hours explaining that U.S. and European business was imminent and we needed to pass the Fab 2 proposal now. This visit proved effective. Three months later at the board meeting, Krigesman no longer opposed, and the Fab 2 investment proposal passed smoothly.

Fab 2 broke ground in Hsinchu Science Park in April the following year (1988), and began operations in 1990, ushering in what I will discuss in the next volume as TSMC's "Roaring '90s."

One of the reasons TSMC was able to roar was Fab 2's innovations. Of course, the "dedicated foundry" business model was TSMC's biggest innovation, but continuous innovation in technology, production, and marketing had begun since the company's founding. Fab 2 alone involved two very important decisions.

第一个决定：SMIF袖珍洁净箱

第一个决定是启用SMIF（Standard Mechanical Interface，袖珍洁净箱）。IC制程必须在"无尘"环境内，如果整个工厂都是"洁净室"，那么排气系统相当昂贵，而且运作时非常费电。SMIF是一家名叫Asyst的硅谷公司所发明，它的妙处是一个"袖珍"洁净箱，可以与生产机器连接。与标准洁净室比较，它既节省排气系统的资本支出，又节省电力，而且据Asyst当时说，"袖珍"洁净环境其实比标准洁净室更为洁净，所以应该提高良率。

魏谋和曾繁城都支持SMIF。我打电话给一位英特尔友人，问他知不知道SMIF？他说，英特尔在实验室试用过，SMIF"很有希望。但是，英特尔是大公司，承担不起大规模使用SMIF的风险。你们是刚开始的小公司，也许承担得起这风险"。

这句无意的轻语（至少我想是无意的），倒提高了我的冒险意愿。毕竟，小公司要赶上大公司，必须在对的地方做大事不愿或不敢做的事。我希望SMIF是一个对的地方。

我们决定用SMIF。台积电的二厂是世界上第一家在量产环境内用SMIF的工厂。此后，所有台积电晶圆厂都用SMIF。后来听说同业也陆续采用SMIF。

ReadShift 双语翻译

The first decision was to adopt SMIF (Standard Mechanical Interface, mini-environments). IC processing must take place in a "dust-free" environment. If the entire factory were a "clean room," the ventilation system would be extremely expensive, and very costly to operate. SMIF was invented by a Silicon Valley company called Asyst. Its clever feature was a "miniature" clean environment that could be connected to production equipment. Compared to a standard clean room, it saved both capital expenditure on ventilation systems and electricity, and moreover, according to Asyst at the time, the "miniature" clean environment was actually cleaner than a standard clean room, so it should improve yield.

Both Wei Mou and Zeng Fan-cheng supported SMIF. I called an Intel friend and asked if he knew about SMIF. He said Intel had trialed it in the lab; SMIF "shows promise. But Intel is a big company and cannot afford the risk of large-scale SMIF adoption. You're a small, new company—maybe you can afford the risk."

This offhand remark (at least I believe it was offhand) actually increased my willingness to take risks. After all, for a small company to catch up to big companies, it must, in the right places, do things that big companies are unwilling or afraid to do. I hoped SMIF was a right place.

We decided to use SMIF. TSMC's Fab 2 was the first factory in the world to use SMIF in a production environment. Thereafter, all TSMC fabs used SMIF. Later I heard that competitors also gradually adopted SMIF.

第二个决定：采用艾司摩尔（ASML）的曝光机

第二个决定是采用艾司摩尔（ASML）的曝光机。曝光机在生产线上诸多机器中最昂贵。在建二厂时日本Nikon以及Canon公司几乎占有全部世界曝光机市场。

艾司摩尔却是一家新公司。巧合的是，它和台积电一样，也是飞利浦投资的公司（飞利浦投资IC相关事业的智慧，实在远胜它自己经营IC事业的智慧）。我还记得在募资时期有一次访问荷兰飞利浦时，一位中年人从空旷走廊的另一端滚球般走过来。与我在一起的飞利浦副总与他打招呼，也对我们说："让我介绍，这位是我们投资的艾司摩尔公司董事长，这位是我们投资的TSMC董事长。"

台积电成立后，Nietzsche、Nikon、ASML高阶经理人员多次来推销各自的曝光机。经过魏谋和曾繁城详细研究，认为艾司摩尔机器有技术优点。唯一问题是：没人用过艾司摩尔机器，台积电会是第一家，的确有相当风险。

我们还是决定用艾司摩尔。在这课题上，我的想法和在SMIF上一样：小公司如要追上大公司必须要冒些险。

此后三十几年，艾司摩尔一直是台积电最主要且最重要的曝光机供应商。同时，艾司摩尔的技术也一直领先Canon与Nikon。艾司摩尔逐渐扩大市占率。至今日，它的市占率已独占鳌头，公司市值也已超过两千亿美元。台积电与艾司摩尔几乎同时诞生，一起成长，一直以伙伴关系相处。

ReadShift 双语翻译

The second decision was to adopt ASML steppers (exposure equipment). Steppers are the most expensive of many machines on a production line. When building Fab 2, Japanese Nikon and Canon virtually dominated the entire world stepper market.

ASML, however, was a startup. Coincidentally, like TSMC, it was also a Philips-invested company (Philips' wisdom in investing in IC-related businesses far exceeded its wisdom in operating its own IC business). I still recall that during the fundraising period, on a visit to Philips in the Netherlands, a middle-aged man came rolling toward us from the other end of a long hallway. The Philips VP walking with me greeted him and said to us: "Let me introduce—this is the chairman of ASML, the company we invested in; this is the chairman of TSMC, the company we invested in."

After TSMC's founding, senior executives from Nikon, Canon, and ASML all came multiple times to pitch their respective steppers. After detailed study by Wei Mou and Zeng Fan-cheng, they concluded that ASML's machines had technical merits. The sole problem was: no one had used ASMM machines before; TSMC would be the first—there was considerable risk.

We decided to go ahead with ASML. My thinking here was the same as with SMIF: if a small company wants to catch up to big companies, it must take some risks.

For the next thirty-plus years, ASML has remained TSMC's primary and most important stepper supplier. At the same time, ASML's technology has consistently stayed ahead of Canon and Nikon. ASML gradually expanded its market share. To this day, its market share is dominant, and its market capitalization has exceeded $200 billion. TSMC and ASML were born almost at the same time, grew together, and have always maintained a partnership relationship.

员工分红、认股

美国企业也有分红，但对绝大部分员工而言，分红仅是固定薪资的一小部分。台湾企业不同，假使景气好，企业盈余高，员工分红可以是固定薪资的一大部分，甚至比固定薪资更高。

一九八零年代中期，联华电子（联电）已有相当丰盛的员工现金分红；一九八七年起，联电开始以股票面值计算的股票分红，更让其他公司员工啧啧称羡。台积电尚未成立时，曾繁城就先几乎以工会领袖的姿态"照会"我：成立台积电后，每年都要有员工分红。

但是成立后我们每月都亏损，当然没有理由分红。一九八八年七月（成立后十七个月），台积电第一次做到当月收支平衡。其实，一个月的不亏损也不是一般公司分红的依据；但鉴于成立前曾繁城的"照会"，以及我"尽早分红"的诺言，我决定于当月结账后就发相当于半个月的奖金。全体同仁皆大欢喜。

八八年底结账，当年营业净利为一亿三千余万元，几乎把八七年的亏损都赚回来了。我们又发了一次奖金，大家更皆大欢喜。

除奖金外，八八年十一月第一次现金增资，我们开始员工认股。此后每次现金增资（八九年十月、九零年六月及十一月、九一年十一月、九二年十一月），员工同时认股。直至最后一次增资，员工已拥有全公司八．五%股权。

ReadShift 双语翻译

American companies also have bonuses, but for the vast majority of employees, bonuses are only a small part of fixed salary. Taiwanese companies are different. When the economy is good and company profits are high, employee bonuses can be a large portion of fixed salary, or even exceed it.

By the mid-1980s, United Microelectronics Corporation (UMC) already had quite generous cash bonuses for employees. From 1987 onward, UMC began issuing stock bonuses calculated at face value, which made employees of other companies green with envy. Before TSMC was even formally established, Zeng Fan-cheng had already "informed" me in the posture of a union leader: after TSMC's founding, there must be employee bonuses every year.

But after founding, we lost money every month—naturally there was no reason for bonuses. In July 1988 (seventeen months after founding), TSMC achieved monthly break-even for the first time. In truth, one month of no loss was not the basis for bonuses at a normal company; but in view of Zeng Fan-cheng's pre-founding "informing" and my promise to "bonus as early as possible," I decided to issue a bonus equivalent to half a month's salary after that month's books closed. Everyone was overjoyed.

At year-end 1988 closing, net operating profit for the year was over NT$130 million, almost earning back all of 1987's losses. We issued another bonus and everyone was even happier.

Besides bonuses, in November 1988 during the first cash capital increase, we began employee stock subscriptions. Thereafter, at each cash capital increase (October 1989, June and November 1990, November 1991, November 1992), employees simultaneously subscribed for stock. By the last capital increase, employees owned 8.5% of the company's total equity.

飞利浦反对员工认股

在我对董事会提出员工认股时，公司已转亏为盈。飞利浦对台积电的看法，也自怀疑、保守转为乐观，所以他们反对员工认股。他们的理由是：（一）此举稀释投资协议内飞利浦股权比例自27.6%至25%左右；（二）飞利浦母公司没有员工认股的先例。

理由（二）当然不成理由——飞利浦不让员工认股，难道台积电也不可以？关于理由（一），在我坚持员工认股下飞利浦的台湾总经理还特地写信给开发基金，说飞利浦被稀释的股权，要在实施股票承购权时补回。经过我和开发基金讨论后，此点开发基金暂时默认。毕竟，飞利浦的股票承购权是下一场战争，我另有战略，此时不必与飞利浦起冲突。

ReadShift 双语翻译

When I proposed employee stock options to the board, the company had already turned profitable. Philips' attitude toward TSMC had also shifted from skeptical and conservative to optimistic, and precisely because of this they opposed employee stock options. Their reasons were: (1) this would dilute Philips' equity stake under the investment agreement from 27.6% to about 25%; (2) Philips parent company had no precedent for employee stock options.

Reason (2) was of course not a valid argument—just because Philips didn't allow employee stock options, should TSMC also not be allowed? Regarding reason (1), under my insistence on employee stock options, the Philips Taiwan general manager even wrote to the Development Fund, saying that Philips' diluted equity would be made up when the stock option was exercised. After discussions between me and the Development Fund, the Development Fund tacitly accepted this for the moment. After all, Philips' stock option was the next battle; I had a separate strategy and saw no need to create a conflict with Philips at this time.

台塑退出

八九年间接听闻台塑已卖出它持有的全部台积电股票，大为震惊。台积是台积电第三大股东（5%，仅次于开发基金及飞利浦），也是募资时俞国华认为"必要"的投资者。怎么在投资还不到三年，公司已开始赚钱时就卖出？况且，无论在卖出前或卖出后，王永庆或他的董事代表王文洋，对我一句交代话都没有。

震惊之余打电话给王文洋，他只冷淡地证实台塑已卖出消息。当时对台湾尚相当天真的我，还在电话上请他继续担任台积电董事，使得我们可以继续从台湾"经营之神"受益。文洋君似乎有点惊讶，但他只冷淡地说："不做了。"事后我才知道台湾法律规定，如一个董事转让他代表的一半（或一半以上）股权，他必须辞董事职。文洋君在电话上没有告诉我这点，大约也是因为他认为我的无知，实在已到了超出"孺子不可教"地步吧？

后来听说台塑把台积电股票卖给了一个证券经纪商，此经纪商又转卖给许多散户。与王文洋通电话后，我已失去继续追逐此事的兴趣。后来台积电多了许多散户，倒是事实。

ReadShift 双语翻译

In 1989, I indirectly heard that Formosa Plastics had sold all its TSMC shares. I was shocked. Formosa Plastics was TSMC's third-largest shareholder (5%, behind only the Development Fund and Philips). It was also the investor that Premier Yu Kuo-hua considered "necessary" during fundraising. Why sell when the company had only been invested for less than three years and had begun to be profitable? Moreover, neither Wang Yung-ching nor his board representative Wang Wen-yang said a single word of explanation to me, either before or after the sale.

Shocked, I called Wang Wen-yang. He only coldly confirmed the news that Formosa Plastics had sold. I, who was still quite naive about Taiwan at the time, even asked him over the phone to continue serving as a TSMC director so we could continue benefiting from Taiwan's "Management God." Wen-yang seemed a bit surprised but only coldly said: "I won't do it anymore." I learned afterward that Taiwanese law stipulates that if a director transfers half (or more) of the shares he represents, he must resign his directorship. Wen-yang didn't tell me this over the phone, probably because he thought my ignorance truly had reached a point beyond "unteachable."

Later I heard that Formosa Plastics had sold the TSMC shares to a securities broker, who then resold them to many retail investors. After the phone call with Wang Wen-yang, I lost interest in pursuing the matter further. That TSMC later gained many retail shareholders, however, is a fact.

飞利浦提出承购要求

根据我们与飞利浦的"协议纲要"，最早一九八九年九月三十日，飞利浦可提出承购要求，增加飞利浦持股至51%（见第十七章）。八九年底，台积电财务长对董事会报告财测：营收有八亿余元，较八八年成长一倍；营业净利四亿余元，是八八年的一倍。听到这样的业务报告后，飞利浦认为实现股票承购权的时机已到，在八九年底正式对开发基金提出承购要求。

现在，以我为首的台积电经理部门面临一场经营权之战。如果飞利浦获得51%股权，台积电将成为飞利浦的子公司——董事经理均将为荷兰所派；新的董事长和总经理也将挑选他们自己的人马。现任的高级经理人将失去职位，或失业。中低阶员工将在"飞利浦式"管理下，如果八八年飞利浦反对台积电员工认股是一个提示，那么在台积电成为飞利浦子公司后，员工不必期待任何认股，更不能奢望后来我们实施的以面值计算的员工股票分红。还有，已开始实施的员工认股，也将失去大部分意义，因为外国公司的子公司不能上市，所以员工认股得到的股票也只有有限的"可卖性"或增值机会。

国内别的股东，也和认股员工在一条船上。

总之，飞利浦子公司台积电绝不会成为今日的台积电。

面对这样严重的挑战，我有办法吗？

有。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Under the "Heads of Agreement" between us and Philips, as early as September 30, 1989, Philips could exercise an option to increase its stake to 51% (see Chapter 17). At year-end 1989, TSMC's CFO reported financial forecasts to the board: revenue would be over NT$800 million, double that of 1988; net operating profit over NT$400 million, double that of 1988. Upon hearing this business report, Philips believed the time was right to exercise the stock option, and formally made the demand to the Development Fund at year-end 1989.

Now, the TSMC management department, led by me, faced a battle for control. If Philips obtained 51% of the equity, TSMC would become a Philips subsidiary—directors and managers would all be dispatched by the Netherlands; the new chairman and general manager would select their own people. Current senior managers would lose their positions, or become unemployed. Junior and mid-level employees would be under "Philips-style" management. If Philips' opposition to TSMC employee stock options in 1988 was any indication, after TSMC became a Philips subsidiary, employees need not expect any stock options, and even less the stock bonuses we later issued at face value. Furthermore, the employee stock subscription program already in place would lose much of its meaning, because a subsidiary of a foreign company cannot go public, so the stock obtained through employee subscription would have only limited "marketability" or appreciation opportunity.

Other domestic shareholders were also in the same boat as the subscribing employees.

In short, a Philips subsidiary TSMC would absolutely never become today's TSMC.

Faced with such a serious challenge, did I have a plan?

Yes.

短期战术与长期战略

我的短期战术，早已埋伏在"协议纲要""转让价格"第三条件内（见第十七章）。第三条件要求的是非常高的转让价格（即是2.5倍到10倍的市价/净值比），即使与第一、第二条件等量考虑，结果也会是飞利浦不能接受的高价。我知道飞利浦不会接受高价转让，所以我短期战术的目的是拖延！

我长期战略是：拖延一、两年后，对原始股东有厚利的"上市"机会，会神像般出现在所有股东眼前，包括飞利浦。那时，我就可以"大家的利，也是飞利浦的利"说服飞利浦，把他们的承购目标，从51%降到可以让台积电上市的比例。

在八九年底，我知道九零年会是不好的年，因为新的二厂增加了大量我们在一年内消化不了的产能。但是我深信，自九一年起，新增的产能更增加我们的威力。如果我们能把飞利浦的承购要求拖延到九一年，飞利浦会看到：让台积电上市会对所有股东，包括飞利浦自己，以及所有员工都有利。

ReadShift 双语翻译

My short-term tactics had long been embedded in the "Heads of Agreement" under the "transfer price" third condition (see Chapter 17). The third condition required a very high transfer price (i.e., 2.5x to 10x price-to-book ratio), so even if considered equally with the first and second conditions, the result would be a price Philips could not accept. I knew Philips would not accept a high-price transfer, so the purpose of my short-term tactic was delay!

My long-term strategy was: after delaying a year or two, the "IPO" opportunity—highly profitable for original shareholders—would appear before all shareholders like a vision, including Philips. At that point, I could convince Philips with "what's good for everyone is also good for Philips," getting them to reduce their subscription target from 51% to a percentage that would allow TSMC to go public.

At year-end 1989, I knew 1990 would be a difficult year because the new Fab 2 added a massive amount of capacity we could not absorb within a year. But I firmly believed that from 1991 onward, the new capacity would further increase our power. If we could delay Philips' subscription demand until 1991, Philips would see that letting TSMC go public would benefit all shareholders, including Philips itself, as well as all employees.

赵扬清与拖延战略

开发基金直接要与飞利浦谈判。开发基金的执行秘书是经济建会主委或财政部部长（在八、九零年代，这两个部会交替接管开发基金），但全时管事的是开发基金副执行秘书。当时副执行秘书是赵扬清女士。在一九九零、九一年两年中，赵女士与飞利浦谈判无数次。每次谈判之前及之后，赵女士都和我讨论开发基金应采取的立场。我从不露面。飞利浦甚至魏谋都认为我是这两年谈判的局外人。赵女士是出战的大将，我是她没人知道的参谋长。我们合作无间，这段合作是我台湾经验中非常愉快的一段。

我们的战术、战略在两年多后都成功了。怎么成功，待下篇再讲吧。

ReadShift 双语翻译

The Development Fund was the one to negotiate directly with Philips. The Development Fund's executive secretary was the chairman of the Council for Economic Planning and Development or the Minister of Finance (in the 1980s and 1990s, these two ministries alternated managing the Development Fund), but the person managing affairs full-time was the deputy executive secretary of the Development Fund. At that time, the deputy executive secretary was Ms. Zhao Yangqing. In 1990 and 1991, Zhao negotiated with Philips countless times. Before and after each negotiation, Zhao would discuss with me the position the Development Fund should take. I never showed my face. Philips and even Wei Mou believed I was an outsider to these two years of negotiations. Zhao was the commanding general who fought the battles; I was her chief of staff that no one knew about. We cooperated seamlessly—this cooperation was a very pleasant chapter of my Taiwan experience.

Our tactics and strategy both succeeded more than two years later. How they succeeded, I will tell in the next volume.

开关美、欧市场，美国行销经理易人

台积电开张第一年（一九八七年）的营收，几乎全部来自台湾，但戴克斯以及他雇的美国行销经理匹列切致力开关美国市场，次年即开始见效果。八八年来自美国的营收占全部营收16.3%，八九年更升高至55%。好几个大型美国半导体公司，如英特尔、德仪、摩托罗拉都赫然在客户之列。我"开关美、欧市场"的第一策略，可说已有成功的开始。

戴克斯于八八年在压力下辞职，几个月后他出任Signetics总经理；几个月后，他也把匹列切带去。如果飞利浦存心要破坏台积电的开关美国市场计划，也不能比这样做来得更彻底吧？幸而我二十几年前的德仪旧同事"高价路克"（John Luke）忽然出现，而且毛遂自荐，要当台积电的美国行销经理。

一九六零年代，我在德仪初任业务单位总经理时，路克是德仪众多"区域行销经理"之一；只是大部分行销经理都销"商品"。路克却销"客制品"，我那时已领会供应商在"客制品"上的议价权比在"商品"上高，而路克也完全同意，所以我们合作相当愉快。那时他告诉我在客户群中他有"高价路克"绰号，而且颇自傲这绰号。

现在，台积电作为"专业晶圆代工"者，产品都是"客制品"，"高价路克"又出现了。经过一、两次话旧及面试，我高兴地雇用电。路克后来在台积电做到一九九八年。他充分参与台积电的"咆哮九零年代"。

TSMC's revenue in its first year of operation (1987) came almost entirely from Taiwan. But Dexter and the American marketing manager he hired, Pletcher, worked aggressively to open up the U.S. market, and results were already visible the following year. In 1988, U.S.-origin revenue accounted for 16.3% of total revenue; in 1989, it rose to 55%. Several major American semiconductor companies—Intel, TI, Motorola—were all prominently among our clients. My first strategy of "opening up U.S. and European markets" could be said to have had a successful start.

Dexter resigned under pressure in 1988. A few months later he became Signetics general manager; a few months after that, he took Pletcher with him. If Philips had wanted to sabotage TSMC's U.S. market opening plan, they could hardly have done it more thoroughly than this! Fortunately, a former TI colleague from over twenty years earlier, "High-Price Luke" (John Luke), suddenly appeared and recommended himself for the position of TSMC's American marketing manager.

In the 1960s, when I had just become general manager of a business unit at TI, Luke was one of TI's many "regional marketing managers." But most marketing managers sold "commodities." Luke sold "custom products." I had already appreciated that a supplier's bargaining power on "custom products" was higher than on "commodities," and Luke completely agreed, so we cooperated quite pleasantly. At that time he told me he had the nickname "High-Price Luke" among his customer base, and he was quite proud of it.

Now, as a "dedicated foundry," TSMC's products were all "custom products," and "High-Price Luke" appeared again. After one or two conversations reminiscing and an interview, I happily hired him. Luke stayed at TSMC until 1998. He was fully involved in TSMC's "Roaring '90s."

欧洲行销与麦克

一九八八年，我也雇了一位以前德仪的老下属，麦克（Siegfried Mack），请他做台积电欧洲行销经理。欧洲市场虽不如美国市场大，但也颇可观，在九零年后，台积电的欧洲营收达到全部营收的8%以上。我尤其享受我与麦克九零年一月的客户之旅。我们驱车自法兰克福至弗莱堡（Freiburg），又至Marin，再去日内瓦，一共三天。麦克是道地德国人，所以我们一路吃、住、行完全德国式。

ReadShift 双语翻译

In 1988, I also hired a former TI subordinate, Siegfried Mack, to be TSMC's European marketing manager. The European market, though not as large as the U.S. market, was also quite substantial. After 1990, TSMC's European revenue reached over 8% of total revenue. I especially enjoyed a customer trip I took with Mack in January 1990. We drove from Frankfurt to Freiburg, then to Marin, then to Geneva, over three days. Mack was German through and through, so our eating, accommodation, and travel along the way were thoroughly German-style.

魏谋辞职

正在业务看好，"筚路蓝缕"时代就要结束，"咆哮"时代即将开始，魏谋突然辞职。其实他的辞职有迹可循，虽非我所促使，但亦非我不欢迎。

魏谋是一个相当杰出的工程师。在台积电的头四年（一九八七至九零年），他对制造工程颇有贡献。他领导台积电的制造团队接受英特尔要求的制造制度，使我们的制造迈上世界级。他也创新——二厂的设计、袖珍洁净箱、采用名不见经传艾司摩尔的曝光机等等。

但是他可对市场、行销一无所知，甚至没有兴趣。这当然不是一位称职总经理应有的态度。我在不得已情况下任命他为总经理，而他在市场、行销上的缺点，在九零年已明显地出现了。

更成问题的是他到处为自己打算的性格。他接任台积电总经理不久后的一天，他的座车（他不在里面）与一辆工研院的车相擦，那时我还是工研院院长，八、九成时间花在工研院上，我的办公室也在工研院里。魏谋的办公室在台积电一厂，是工研院租给台积电的。我忽然接到魏谋电话，我还以为台积电有什么突破，高兴地接起话筒，但是他用责问的口气说："我以台积电总经理的地位，对工研院院长…"

我还是他的上司。为了这样的小事（没人受伤，保险公司理赔），值得用这样的态度对待你的上司吗？

ReadShift 双语翻译

Just when the business was looking up, the "trailblazing" era was about to end, and the "roaring" era was about to begin, Wei Mou suddenly resigned. In truth, his resignation had been foreshadowed. While I had not encouraged it, neither was I unwelcoming of it.

Wei Mou was a quite outstanding engineer. In TSMC's first four years (1987-1990), he made considerable contributions to manufacturing engineering. He led TSMC's manufacturing team to adopt the production systems that Intel required, bringing our manufacturing up to world-class. He also innovated—Fab 2 design, SMIF mini-environments, adoption of the then-unknown ASML steppers, and more.

But he knew nothing about marketing and sales, and was not even interested. This was certainly not an attitude a competent general manager should have. I had appointed him general manager out of necessity, and his shortcomings in marketing became glaringly apparent by 1990.

Even more problematic was his self-serving personality. Not long after taking over as TSMC general manager, one day his car (he was not inside) lightly scraped an ITRI vehicle. At that time I was still ITRI president, spending 80-90% of my time on ITRI matters; my office was also in ITRI. Wei Mou's office was in TSMC Fab 1, leased to TSMC by ITRI. I suddenly received a call from Wei Mou. I thought TSMC had some breakthrough and happily picked up the receiver, but he said in a demanding tone: "As general manager of TSMC, I have a right to say to the ITRI president..."

I was still his boss. For such a minor matter (no one was injured, insurance covered it), was it worth treating your superior with such an attitude?

魏谋对飞利浦输诚

更严重的事发生了。八八九年底，飞利浦提出股权承购要求，魏谋立刻认定飞利浦必定很快成为台积电的主人。他在第一个机会——飞利浦提出申诸后的第一个台积电董事会，私约飞利浦的IC总经理（那时克列斯曼已被撤职，换了一位对我相当友善的哈格曼斯达（Heinz Hagmeister））。魏谋告诉哈氏：飞利浦购并台积电后，他会留下来，所以飞利浦不必担心台积电的稳定性。

连哈格曼斯达都惊奇魏谋这样的提早"输诚"，所以第二天就告诉我魏谋对他说的话——显然哈氏认为与我好关系，比魏谋的输诚更重要。

我没有告诉魏谋我已知道他对飞利浦输诚，但九零年上半年，他几乎每星期问我："承购案进行得怎样？"我不说。我有我的战术和战略，只能与赵扬清讨论，不能对任何人说，更不能对叛逆者说。后来他不耐烦了，凶悍地对我说："我是总经理，为什么不告诉我？"我回答："好好地做你的总经理，此事与你无关。"

ReadShift 双语翻译

Something more serious happened. At year-end 1989, when Philips made its equity subscription demand, Wei Mou immediately concluded that Philips would soon become TSMC's master. At the very first opportunity—the first TSMC board meeting after Philips made its request—he privately met with Philips' IC general manager (by then Krigesman had been removed and replaced by a quite friendly Heinz Hagmeister). Wei Mou told Hagmeister: after Philips acquired TSMC, he would stay, so Philips need not worry about TSMC's stability.

Even Hagmeister was astonished by Wei Mou's premature "surrender," so the next day he told me what Wei Mou had said to him—clearly Hagmeister believed maintaining a good relationship with me was more important than Wei Mou's defection.

I didn't tell Wei Mou that I already knew about his defection to Philips. But in the first half of 1990, he asked me almost weekly: "How is the subscription case progressing?" I didn't tell him. I had my own tactics and strategy, which I could only discuss with Zhao Yangqing—not with anyone else, and certainly not with a defector. Eventually, growing impatient, he said fiercely to me: "I'm the general manager; why won't you tell me?" I replied: "Do your job as general manager properly. This matter doesn't concern you."

魏谋离去

九零年秋，承购案继续在我策略下拖延，魏谋等不住了，刚巧新加坡的"特许半导体公司"要聘他为总经理，他辞职了。我并不惊奇。在他对飞利浦输诚那一刻，他显然以为我已是即将退出舞台的过去人物，而他要保护自己的既有地位。事实上，我不但不是过去人物，我的黄金时代正要开始，而他却与他一生难得的黄金机会擦身而过。

台积电并没亏待魏谋。他离开时，已认了好几次的员工认股。如果他没卖掉这些股票，这些股票应也是一笔小财。我也认为这是他那几年在台积电制造工程上贡献应得的报酬。

ReadShift 双语翻译

In the fall of 1990, with the subscription case continuing to be delayed under my strategy, Wei Mou could wait no longer. As it happened, Singapore's "Chartered Semiconductor" wanted to hire him as general manager, and he resigned. I was not surprised. At the moment he defected to Philips, he apparently believed I was already a fading figure about to exit the stage, and he wanted to protect his own position. In reality, I was not a fading figure at all—my golden era was just beginning—and yet he let the golden opportunity of a lifetime pass him by.

TSMC had not treated Wei Mou poorly. When he left, he had already subscribed to employee stock options several times. If he hadn't sold those shares, they would have been a small fortune. I also felt this was deserved compensation for his contributions to TSMC's manufacturing engineering over the years.

布鲁克接任总经理

一九九零年秋魏谋辞职时，刚巧我自台积电募资时就属意的总经理人选——布鲁克出现，填补了魏谋遗留下来的空缺。

布鲁克是我德仪多年下属。我在一九六六年就认识他，他也是本书第六章里"一个危机，两个英雄"的英雄之一。在"危机"后他在我手下扶摇直上，做到主管MOS的副总裁位。直到一九八三年德仪消费者产品失败而士气低落、人心背离之时，布鲁克离开德仪，跑到一家不很成功的中型半导体公司快捷半导体任该公司总裁。

他在快捷做了几年后，快捷的股东斯伦贝谢公司（Schlumberger）仍不满意的业绩，要把快捷卖掉。布鲁克想把快捷卖给日本电脑及半导体公司富士通（Fujitsu）。但在一九八零年代，日本半导体业很强盛，几乎有超过美国半导体业之势，深为美国政府所忌。因此，美国政府把快捷半导体与富士通的合并计划反对掉了。斯伦贝谢急于脱手，就以低价把快捷卖给另一家美国公司——国家半导体（National Semiconductor）。在买卖的过程中，国家半导体并没有挽留布鲁克。布鲁克就此失业。

ReadShift 双语翻译

In the fall of 1990, when Wei Mou resigned, as it happened the general manager candidate I had favored since TSMC's fundraising days—Brook—appeared, filling the vacancy left by Wei Mou.

Brook had been my subordinate at TI for many years. I met him in 1966. He was also one of the two "heroes" in "One Crisis, Two Heroes" from Chapter 6 of this book. After the "crisis," he rose rapidly under me, reaching the position of vice president in charge of MOS. Until 1983, when TI's consumer products failure caused low morale and talent drain, Brook left TI and went to a middling semiconductor company—National Semiconductor (he became president of the company).

After a few years at National Semiconductor, the company's shareholder, Schlumberger, was still dissatisfied with the performance and wanted to sell the company. Brook wanted to sell the company to the Japanese computer and semiconductor company Fujitsu. But in the 1980s, the Japanese semiconductor industry was so strong it nearly surpassed the American semiconductor industry, which aroused deep concern from the U.S. government. Therefore, the U.S. government opposed the merger plan between National Semiconductor and Fujitsu. Schlumberger, eager to exit, sold off National Semiconductor at a low price to another American company—National Semiconductor (the name was confusing, but it was a different entity). During this transaction, National Semiconductor did not retain Brook. Brook was unemployed.

合适的人选

布鲁克虽是工程出身，但他的长处是市场、行销及经营。他的这些长处正与台积电初期的策略契合，所以在一九八六年台积电募资成功，要找总经理时，我的第一批人选就有他在内。但那时他不愿离开快捷半导体。一九九零年我再去找他时，他已失业两年，当然态度不同，但他虽然接受我的邀请，却对我声明：他不认台积电总经理职位为他长期归宿，而且他也不愿长期住在台湾，但答应我做一年——一年后再说。

一九九零年十二月，我们正式宣布布鲁克为任总经理。我不久前才发生的工研院院长、董事长交接典礼的风光，许多媒体记者都来了，第二天报纸上也有相当显著的登载；那么，现在台积电的新总经理也应有相似的威风吧？我们开了一个晚会，也邀请了不少记者，但是，到的只有一个！我相当沮丧，也对人事经理把晚会及邀请传达得很草率感到不满。人事经理倒很老实地告诉我："不要以为我们是工研院。台湾像我们这样的公司，不知道有几百个。"

ReadShift 双语翻译

Although Brook was trained as an engineer, his strengths were in marketing, sales, and operations. These strengths aligned perfectly with TSMC's initial strategies. So when TSMC's fundraising succeeded in 1986 and we were looking for a general manager, Brook was among my first choices. But at that time he was unwilling to leave National Semiconductor. When I approached him again in 1990, he had been unemployed for two years, so naturally his attitude was different. But although he accepted my invitation, he made it clear: he did not consider the TSMC general manager position his long-term home, and he did not want to live in Taiwan long-term. But he agreed to do it for one year—and then we'd see.

In December 1990, we officially announced Brook as the new general manager. I had just recently had a grand ITRI presidentchairman transition ceremony—many media reporters came, and the next day's newspapers had quite prominent coverage. Surely TSMC's new general manager should have similar fanfare? We held a reception and invited quite a few reporters, but only one showed up! I was quite dejected and unhappy with the sloppiness of the event and the invitations. The personnel manager told me frankly: "Don't think we're ITRI. There are hundreds of companies like us in Taiwan."

"一百亿"呼喊

使我振奋的倒是这晚会的另一个镜头。举行晚会时一九九零年即将结束，当年的营收为新台币二十二亿元。我带领到会的二、三十位台积电高级主管高呼："一百亿！"第一次呼喊时，声量已经很大，但布鲁克——晚会的主角，根本不懂我们喊了什么，急着他旁边的人，我等他听懂后，再带领大家呼喊第二次"一百亿！"布鲁克也喊了，他的美国口音特别令人注意。我再喊一次"一百亿"，大家回应"一百亿！"真的声量如雷，墙壁都似乎震动了。

一九九年底，我已有很强的信心："筚路蓝缕"时代已结束，我们已走上成功之路。不要说一百亿元是一个可达到的目标，即使一千亿元也不是奢求了。

ReadShift 双语翻译

What actually lifted my spirits was another moment from the reception. During the reception, 1990 was about to end, with revenue for the year at NT$2.2 billion. I led the twenty to thirty TSMC senior managers present in shouting: "One hundred billion!" At the first shout, the volume was already loud, but Brook—the guest of honor—had no idea what we were shouting, and asked the person next to him. I waited until he understood, then led everyone in shouting "One hundred billion!" a second time. Brook shouted too, and his American accent was particularly noticeable. I shouted "One hundred billion" once more, and everyone responded "One hundred billion!" The volume was truly thunderous, the walls seemed to shake.

By year-end 1990, I already had a strong confidence: the "trailblazing" era was over, and we were on the path to success. Not to mention that one hundred billion was an achievable target—even one thousand billion would not be an extravagant wish.

黄金年代即将开始

写此书时，已九十岁矣！回忆此生，如以每十年为一单位，则每单位都有高潮和低潮，兴奋和沮丧，期待和失落。读者读至此，应该亦可领会。但如要我挑选我的黄金时代，我毫不犹豫挑选六十至八十五岁那两个半单位。在那时段，我充分保持了青、中年就享受的健康；我精力充沛，每星期工作和上学阅读或写作时间大概总在六十小时以上；出国频繁，大部分是开关新客户或拜访现有客户，但也不少次参加国际会议，和聆听各国政要或专家学者讨论国际大事。

健康和精力固然是黄金时代的必要条件。有了健康和精力后，我深信我的专业知识、经验和判断力在六十到八十五岁时期都已成熟。德仪给了我世界级的训练，虽然在颇快情形下辞职，但它给我的训练，我至今感恩！通用和投资人的经验，也让我看到科技业的金融面——这是我在德仪二十五年没有看到的；工研院又教我不少台湾的"人情世故"，是我后来经营台积电不可或缺的经验。

比知识、经验、判断力更重要的，我坚强了自己的斗志。六十岁以后，三次辞职后，我认为已经退无可退，而必须坚强自己的斗志。其实我六十至八十五岁这时的困难和阻力也不少，但我不再认输不再放弃。

当然，构成我"黄金时代"最重要因素是：台积电成功了！台积电从一个几乎没人看好的开始，在三十年光景，它成为一个没人能忽略的公司。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Writing this book at the age of ninety! Looking back on my life, if we take each decade as a unit, every unit had its highs and lows, excitement and frustration, anticipation and disappointment. Having read this far, the reader should understand. But if I were to pick my golden era, I would unhesitatingly pick those two and a half units from ages sixty to eighty-five. During that period, I fully maintained the health I had enjoyed since youth and middle age. I was energetic, with weekly work and serious reading or writing time totaling about sixty hours. I traveled abroad frequently—mostly to open up new clients or visit existing ones, but also attending international conferences and listening to political leaders and experts from various countries discussing world affairs.

Health and energy were of course necessary conditions for a golden era. With health and energy, I firmly believe my professional knowledge, experience, and judgment all matured during the sixty to eighty-five period. TI gave me world-class training. Although I resigned under hasty circumstances, I remain grateful for the training it gave me! My GE and venture capital experience also showed me the financial side of the technology industry—something I had not seen during my twenty-five years at TI. ITRI taught me much about "human relations and worldly wisdom" in Taiwan, experience indispensable to my later management of TSMC.

More important than knowledge, experience, and judgment was the fact that I strengthened my fighting spirit. After age sixty, after three resignations, I believed I could retreat no further and had to fortify my fighting spirit. In truth, there were plenty of difficulties and obstacles during this sixty to eighty-five period, but I refused to admit defeat and refused to give up.

Of course, the most important factor constituting my "golden era" was: TSMC succeeded! From a beginning that almost no one believed in, within thirty years, it became a company that no one could ignore.

ReadShift 双语翻译

台積電篇二卷首

台积电篇二·卷首｜咆哮九〇年代（一九九一—二零零零）

章节

台積電篇二第二十章

张忠谋

台积电篇二·第二十章｜"专业晶圆代工"商业模式大放异彩

九零年代业绩

一九九一至二零零零年台积电的业绩，列表如下。

ReadShift 双语翻译

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| 年复合年成长率 | 1991 | 1992 | 1993 | 1994 | 1995 | 1996 | 1997 | 1998 | 1999 | 2000 |

| 营收（亿元新台币） | 44.8 | 65.1 | 123.3 | 193.4 | 287.7 | 394.0 | 439.2 | 504.2 | 730.7 | 1,662.0 || 营业净利 | 7.1 | 12.4 | 44.2 | 86.2 | 139.0 | 182.4 | 149.3 | 138.1 | 248.3 | 613.0 |这十年的营收"年复合成长率"是49.4%；营业净利的年复合成长率是64.1%。九六至九八年，是全球半导体业不景气的三，全球半导体业在九六年萎缩8%，在九七年只成长4%，在九八年又萎缩8%。但即使在这不景气的三年，台积电仍有不错的表现。

一旦营收达到十亿美元，创业算成功了。如以此为标准，那么台积电九五年营收达到十一亿美元（当年美金／台币汇率为一比二十六）也可算是创业成功了。

ReadShift 双语翻译

## The '90s Performance

TSMC's performance from 1991 to 2000 is shown in the table below.

| Compound Annual | 1991 | 1992 | 1993 | 1994 | 1995 | 1996 | 1997 | 1998 | 1999 | 2000 | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | Revenue (NT$ B) | 4.48 | 6.51 | 12.33 | 19.34 | 28.77 | 39.40 | 43.92 | 50.42 | 73.07 | 166.20 | | Net Operating Profit | 0.71 | 1.24 | 4.42 | 8.62 | 13.90 | 18.24 | 14.93 | 13.81 | 24.83 | 61.30 |

Revenue compound annual growth rate (CAGR) for this decade was 49.4%; net operating profit CAGR was 64.1%. 1996-1998 were three years of global semiconductor downturn: the global semiconductor industry shrank 8% in 1996, grew only 4% in 1997, and shrank 8% again in 1998. But even during these three recession years, TSMC's performance was still decent.

Once revenue reached $1 billion, the venture could be considered successful. By this standard, TSMC's 1995 revenue of $1.1 billion (at an exchange rate of 1 USD to 26 NT) could also be considered a successful venture.

设计（无晶圆厂）公司风起云涌

台积电成立后头两年（一九八七至八八年）的客户几乎全是台湾的小型设计公司。一九八九年起，先有国外大型IDM（自有晶圆厂公司），如英特尔、摩托罗拉、德仪、飞利浦等，将他们工厂内比较不具经济价值的产品，委托给我们生产，藉以提升这些产品的营业利益。但自一九九一年起，美国设计公司风起云涌地成立。

根据无晶圆厂半导体公司联盟（FSA）在二零零七年给我的资料，在一九九一年中，全球无晶圆厂公司自两百零七家增加至七百五十家；它们的总营收也自一九九三年的二十四亿美元，增加至二零零零年的一百七十亿美元。根据台积电的经验，无晶圆厂一百亿美元大约需要三十四亿美元晶圆代工。而台积电二零零零年营收为一百三十二亿美元，其中约四成来自IDM，即"自有晶圆厂公司"。那么，另外六十成（三十二亿美元）来自"无晶圆厂公司"。这么说来，台积电难道把所有"无晶圆厂公司"的生意都接下来了？我想不见得，FSA可能低估了二零零零年"无晶圆厂公司"的营收。但是，有一点我相信：台积电很早就是"无晶圆厂半导体公司"的首选代工者。

ReadShift 双语翻译

In the first two years after TSMC's founding (1987-88), customers were almost entirely small Taiwanese design houses. From 1989 onward, established foreign IDMs (Integrated Device Manufacturers with their own fabs)—Intel, Motorola, TI, Philips, etc.—began outsourcing less economically viable products from their fabs to us to improve the profitability of those products. But from 1991 onward, American design companies sprang up like a tidal wave.

According to the Fabless Semiconductor Alliance (FSA), which provided me data in 2007, in 1991 the number of fabless companies worldwide grew from 207 to 750; their total revenue also grew from $2.4 billion in 1993 to $17 billion in 2000. Based on TSMC's experience, $10 billion of fabless revenue requires about $3.4 billion of wafer foundry services. TSMC's 2000 revenue was $13.2 billion, of which about 40% came from IDMs. The remaining 60% ($8 billion) came from fabless companies. Did TSMC really take all the business of every fabless company? I think not—FSA may have underestimated fabless company revenue in 2000. But one thing I believe: TSMC was very early on the foundry of choice for fabless semiconductor companies.

IDM转向台积电

我也以为：一旦IDM（自有晶圆厂）公司试用台积电的晶圆代工，他们也会逐渐停止他们自己的晶圆制造，而改用台积电。为什么"自有晶圆厂公司"转向台积电是一个逐渐、而不是很快的过程？第一，"自有晶圆厂公司"有许多制造部员工，他们不会一下子把制造部员工都遣散；第二，"自有晶圆厂公司"也有不少尚未完全折旧，以及即使已完全折旧，仍有剩余价值的生产设备，这些设备也不会被当作废铜烂铁卖掉。

ReadShift 双语翻译

I also believed: once IDMs (integrated device manufacturers) tried TSMC's foundry services, they would gradually cease their own wafer manufacturing and switch to TSMC. Why was the shift of IDMs toward TSMC a gradual rather than rapid process? First, IDMs had many manufacturing department employees; they wouldn't lay them off all at once. Second, IDMs also had considerable production equipment that was not fully depreciated, or even if fully depreciated still had residual value. This equipment wouldn't be sold as scrap iron either.

"服务导向"策略的成功

为什么台积电成为"晶圆代工"的首选？因为我们"专业晶圆代工"商业模式和我们"服务导向"策略完全成功了！在台积电成立之前，"晶圆代工"是许多美国、日本、台湾IDM公司的副业，"副业"的客户不受重视，甚至还遭受委托的"代工"者竞争。台积电的商业模式是"专业晶圆代工"——完全"服务导向"、"为客户赴汤蹈火"。台积电的技术长处是高良率——台积电的一切所为，完全迎合客户的需求。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Why did TSMC become the foundry of choice? Because our "dedicated foundry" business model and our "service-oriented" strategy completely succeeded! Before TSMC's founding, "wafer foundry" was a sideline for many American, Japanese, and Taiwanese IDMs. As a "sideline," customers were not valued and even suffered competition from the very company they outsourced to. TSMC's business model was "dedicated foundry"—thoroughly "service-oriented," "going through fire and water for customers." TSMC's technological strength was high yield—everything TSMC did was completely oriented toward meeting customer needs.

行销美国成功

除了创新的商业模式外，初期台积电另一个重要策略是行销美国。用美国总经理、美国行销人员，加上我自己对美国客户的熟识，台积电来自美国客户的营收自一九八七年（成立年）的零美元，到一九九一年的八千七百万美元（占全部营收53%），到一九九八年的八亿六千万美元（占全部营收57%）。自二零零零年后，台积电来自美国的营收大概都在全部营收六成以上。这与美国蓬勃发展的设计公司有关。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Beyond the innovative business model, another key early TSMC strategy was marketing in the U.S. Using an American general manager, American marketing personnel, plus my own familiarity with American customers, TSMC's revenue from American customers grew from zero in 1987 (the founding year) to $87 million in 1991 (53% of total revenue), to $860 million in 1998 (57% of total revenue). From 2000 onward, TSMC's U.S.-origin revenue has been roughly above 60% of total revenue. This correlates with the flourishing design company ecosystem in the U.S.

日本市场的衰退

相反的是日本市场。日本半导体业在八零年代非常强劲，但后来渐渐衰退，我认为这与日本简直没有IC设计公司有关。记得二零零七年春，我受邀到日本福冈的一个电子业会议致词，在半导体业者座谈会内，业者对我的致词完全没有理会，反而频频要日本政府资助他们建晶圆厂。我对此点提出此已在时不晚矣，但日本半导体业者尚抱守老旧观念。

在我孤独飞返台湾途中，我想：从今以后日本半导体业大概也就不过如此了。

ReadShift 双语翻译

The Japanese market told the opposite story. Japan's semiconductor industry was very strong during the 1980s, but later gradually declined. I believe this was related to the fact that Japan had virtually no IC design companies. I recall that in the spring of 2007, I was invited to give a speech at an electronics industry conference in Fukuoka, Japan. At the semiconductor roundtable, the industry participants completely ignored my speech and instead repeatedly asked the Japanese government to subsidize them in building wafer fabs. I pointed out that it was already too late, but the Japanese semiconductor industry still clung to outdated notions.

On my lonely flight back to Taiwan, I thought: from now on, the Japanese semiconductor industry would probably be just that—ordinary.

ReadShift 双语翻译

章节

台積電篇二第二十一章

张忠谋

台积电篇二·第二十一章｜台积电的经营理念及九零年代策略

经营理念

大约在一九九四、九五年之际，台积电营收已以年复合成长率60-70%气势成长了几年，员工及重要主管人数也急剧地增加，我已不能常常与所有重要主管做理念性讨论。我想：应该把我们基本的价值观，也就是台积电的经营理念，写出来。虽然写理念的过程只有几天，但理念的形成却是几十年家教及学校教育加上职业及社会经验的结果。一共写了十条如下：

**台湾积体电路制造股份有限公司企业经营理念****（一）坚持高度职业道德**这个理念代表公司的品格，是我们最基本也是最重要的理念，也是执行业务时必须遵守的法则。所谓高度职业道德是：第一、我们说真话。第二、我们不夸张、不作秀。第三、对客户我们不轻易承诺，一旦做出承诺，必定不计代价，全力以赴。第四、对同业我们在合法范围内全力竞争时，也尊重同业的智财权。不恶意中伤。第五、对供应商我们以客观、清廉、公正的态度进行挑选及合作。

在公司内部，我们绝不容许贪污；不容许在公司内有派系或小圈圈产生；也不容许"公司政治"（Company Politics）的形成。至于我们用人的首要条件是品格与才能，绝不是"关系"。

ReadShift 双语翻译

## Business Philosophy

Around 1994-95, TSMC's revenue had been growing at a compound annual rate of 60-70% for several years. The number of employees and key managers had also increased sharply. I could no longer frequently engage in philosophical discussions with all key managers. I thought: we should write down our core values—TSMC's business philosophy. Although the process of writing the philosophy took only a few days, the philosophy itself was the result of decades of family upbringing and schooling plus professional and social experience. I wrote ten principles:

**TSMC Business Philosophy**

**(1) Uphold the Highest Professional Ethics**

This principle represents the company's character. It is our most fundamental and most important philosophy, and a code we must follow when conducting business. By highest professional ethics we mean: First, we tell the truth. Second, we do not exaggerate or put on airs. Third, we do not make promises to customers lightly; once a promise is made, we must spare no cost and give our all. Fourth, while competing aggressively within legal bounds, we also respect competitors' intellectual property. We do not maliciously disparage. Fifth, we select and collaborate with suppliers based on objectivity, integrity, and fairness.

Within the company, we absolutely do not tolerate corruption; we do not tolerate factions or cliques within the company; nor do we tolerate the formation of "company politics." As for hiring, the primary criteria are character and competence, definitely not "connections."

**（二）专注于"专业积体电路制造服务"本业**我们的本业是"专业积体电路制造服务"，这个领域发展迅速，只要我们能集中力量，积极从事本业的钻研，发展空间必定无可限量。因此，我们要心无旁骛、全力以赴，在"专业积体电路制造服务"本业中谋求最大的成就。

**（三）放眼世界市场，国际化经营**我们的目标是全球市场，而不局限于东南亚或任何地区。集成电路是一个跨越国界的产业，全球各主要业者无不将目标延伸到世界各地。而我们最强的竞争者也来自国外，如果我们不能够把眼光放远在世界市场中建立竞争力，我们在国内终究也将无法生存。

我们的根在台湾，但要在全世界主要市场建立基地，是国际化经营的意义。而为配合国际多元发展的文化需求，在人才募集方面，我们则不论国籍，唯才是用。

**（四）注意长期策略，追求永续经营**我们确信"人无远虑，必有近忧"的道理，只要我们能做好长期策略规划，并认真地执行，短期较为急就章式的冲刺便会大大减少。因此，除了每年我们都要为未来五年做一个长期策略规划外，在我们的日常工作中，也应有相当高的程度落实于长期的成效与回收。

ReadShift 双语翻译

**(2) Focus on Our Core Business: "Dedicated IC Manufacturing Services"**

Our core business is "dedicated IC manufacturing services." This field is developing rapidly. As long as we concentrate our energy and actively pursue excellence in our core business, the development potential is boundless. Therefore, we must be single-minded and give our all to achieving the greatest success in our core business of "dedicated IC manufacturing services."

**(3) Look to World Markets, Operate Internationally**

Our target is the global market, not limited to Southeast Asia or any single region. Semiconductors are a borderless industry; every major global player has extended its reach to every corner of the world. And our strongest competitors also come from abroad. If we are not able to broaden our vision and establish competitiveness in the world market, we will ultimately be unable to survive domestically either.

Our roots are in Taiwan, but establishing footholds in every major world market is the meaning of international operations. To support international and diverse cultural needs, in terms of talent recruitment we are nationality-blind—we hire solely on merit.

**(4) Pay Attention to Long-Term Strategy, Pursue Sustainable Operation**

We firmly believe in the principle that "if a person does not have long-term considerations, there will be near-term worries." As long as we can do long-term strategy planning well and execute it diligently, short-term hastily-executed sprints will be greatly reduced. Therefore, in addition to the five-year long-term strategy plan we do every year, in our daily work there should also be a high degree of focus on long-term results and returns.

经营理念（续）

**（五）客户是我们的伙伴**我们自始就将客户定位为伙伴，绝不和客户竞争。这个定位是我们过去成功的要素，也是未来继续成长的关键。我们视客户的竞争力为台积公司的竞争力，而客户的成功也是台积公司的成功。

**（六）品质是我们工作与服务的原则**包括公司内部或是外部，每个我们所服务的对象，都是我们的"客户"。而"客户满意度"就是"品质"。在台积公司，品质是每一个员工的责任，我们应坚守岗位，本着追求卓越、精益求精的态度，不但认真地把每一件事、每一件任务做到最好，更要随时检讨，务求改善，追求并维持"客户全面满意"，这就是以"品质是我们工作与服务的原则"的具体实践。

**（七）鼓励在各方面的创新，确保高度企业活力**创新是我们的命脉。如果我们一旦停止创新，将很快地面临没落与失败。我们不但要在技术方面追求创新，在企划、行销、管理等各方面更要强调。自然地，积极建立与累积公司的智能财产权也不可或缺。我们更要常保公司充满蓬勃朝气与活力，随时秉持积极进取、高效率的处事态度，来因应瞬息万变的产业特性。

**（八）营造具挑战性、有乐趣的工作环境**相信对大多数的同仁而言，一个有挑战性，可以持续学习，而又有乐趣的工作环境，比金钱报酬更为重要。我们要齐力塑造并维持这样一个环境，吸引并留住志同道合而且最优秀的人才。

**（九）建立开放型管理模式**我们要营造乐于沟通的环境，以建立开放型管理模式。"开放型"代表同仁间互相以诚信、坦率、合作相待。同仁乐于接受意见，也乐于改进自己。同时，更将透过集思广益的方法接受各方看法，而在做成决定后，就团结一致、不分你我、集中力量朝共同目标全力以赴。

**（十）兼顾员工福利与股东权益，尽力回馈社会**员工与股东同是公司重要的组成分子。我们要提供给员工一个在同业平均水准以上的福利，同时让股东对公司的投资得到平均水准以上的报酬。同时，公司的成长也得力于社会及产业环境的配合，我们要不断尽能力和回馈社会，做一个良好的企业公民。

ReadShift 双语翻译

## Business Philosophy (continued)

**(5) Customers Are Our Partners**

From the beginning, we have positioned customers as partners and never compete with them. This positioning has been a key factor in our past success and continues to be critical for future growth. We view our customers' competitiveness as TSMC's competitiveness, and our customers' success as TSMC's success.

**(6) Quality Is the Principle of Our Work and Service**

Whether internal or external to the company, everyone we serve is our "customer." And "customer satisfaction" is "quality." At TSMC, quality is every employee's responsibility. We should stand fast at our posts, and in the spirit of pursuing excellence and continuous improvement, not only do every task and every job earnestly and to the best of our ability, but also constantly review and seek improvement, pursuing and maintaining "total customer satisfaction." This is the concrete practice of "quality as the principle of our work and service."

**(7) Encourage Innovation in All Areas, Ensure High Corporate Vitality**

Innovation is our lifeblood. If we ever stop innovation, we will quickly face decline and failure. We must pursue innovation not only in technology but also emphasize it in planning, marketing, management, and all other areas. Naturally, actively building and accumulating the company's intellectual property is also indispensable. We must also keep the company full of youthful energy and vitality, and at all times maintain a proactive, efficient attitude to respond to the industry's ever-changing nature.

**(8) Create a Challenging and Enjoyable Work Environment**

We believe that for most colleagues, a challenging, continuously learnable, and enjoyable work environment is more important than financial compensation. We must work together to shape and sustain such an environment—attracting and retaining like-minded and most talented people.

**(9) Establish an Open Management Model**

We must create an environment that encourages communication to establish an open management model. "Open" represents colleagues treating each other with integrity, frankness, and cooperation. Colleagues are open to receiving input and willing to improve themselves. At the same time, we will adopt a brainstorming approach to accept views from all sides, and after decisions are made, unite as one—with no distinction between "you" and "me"—concentrating all forces to charge toward the common goal.

**(10) Balance Employee Welfare and Shareholder Rights, Strive to Give Back to Society**

Employees and shareholders are both important constituents of the company. We must provide employees with welfare above the industry average, while also giving shareholders returns on their investment above the industry average. At the same time, the company's growth also depends on support from society and the industry environment. We must continuously do our best to give back to society and be a good corporate citizen.

不变的十条

这十条中，第一条："坚持高度职业道德"最为基本。我在德仪时，德仪的基本价值是Integrity。此字很难译成中文，我后来把它译成"诚信正直"，也不完美。其实真正的难题是，我在德仪就发现：人的Integrity定义都不一样。在德仪的二十五年中，有好几次我目击面红耳赤的争论，一方开始质疑对方的Integrity，对方先是面色一变，但立刻转冷笑："你有你的Integrity，我有我的。"

所以在台积电的经营理念上，我特地把我认为的"职业道德"诠释了一番。至于为什么只讲"职业"道德，而不是"道德"？解释简单得很。公司无权干涉私德，但有权甚至有社会责任要求职业道德。

我们把这十条经营理念印成小册，分发给所有员工，而且把一大叠放在公司大厅的柜台上，使得客户、供应商、任何访客都可取得。这十条理念自写成后就没有改过，我认为也无须改。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Among these ten principles, the first, "Uphold the Highest Professional Ethics," is the most fundamental. At TI, TI's core value was Integrity. This word is hard to translate into Chinese; I later translated it as "诚信正直" (integrity and honesty), but it wasn't perfect. The real problem is, I discovered at TI: everyone's definition of Integrity is different. During my twenty-five years at TI, on several occasions I witnessed heated arguments where one side began questioning the other's Integrity. The other side's expression would first change, then immediately turn to a sneer: "You have your Integrity, I have mine."

So in TSMC's business philosophy, I specifically elaborated on what I believe "professional ethics" to be. As to why we say "professional" ethics rather than just "ethics"? The explanation is simple. A company has no right to interfere in private morality, but it has the right—even the social responsibility—to demand professional ethics.

We printed these ten principles in a booklet and distributed it to all employees. We also placed a large stack on the lobby counter so that customers, suppliers, or any visitor could pick one up. These ten principles have not been changed since they were written, and I believe they need not be changed.

九零年代策略

台积电初期的策略，我在第十八章《开辟鸿蒙》已略有所述。开始几年，需要执行公司策略的经理人并不多，我就以"耳提面命"方式传授给他们。大家也都能照我的意思执行。这策略的成果非常丰硕。但是到了九零年代中期，重要经理人数急剧增加，要大家齐心一致，不能只靠"耳提面命"，而有必要把公司策略写下来。于是我于一九九八年九月，花了几天时间，亲自写下了"TSMC Strategy"。原文是英文，最近为了写此书要包括此策略，故由台积电公关部门把它译成中文。

台积公司营运策略（一九九八年九月七日）

目标

成为声誉卓著、以服务为导向且能够为客户创造最大整体利益的专业积体电路制造服务公司，借此成为此产业规模最大且获利最高的公司。

客户是我们的伙伴

我们自始就将客户定位为伙伴，绝不和客户竞争。我们视客户的竞争力为台积公司的竞争力，而客户的成功也是台积公司的成功。

背景、当前市场概况和未来展望

台积公司于一九八五年开创了专业积体电路制造服务商业模式。当时专业积体电路制造服务公司并没有稳定的市场，台积公司唯一的商机来自整合元件制造公司周期性的外包业务，以及当时刚进入市场的少数无晶圆厂（晶片设计）公司。尽管初期困难重重，台积公司仍坚持专注于专业积体电路制造服务的商业模式。

我们的信念和努力于八零年代后期和九零年代初期获得了回报，创业家发现台积公司是可信赖的专业积体电路制造服务公司，自此开始成立大量的无晶圆厂公司。无晶圆厂公司透过和台积公司合作，由台积公司为其生产晶片进而获得的初始成功，致使更多的无晶圆厂公司相继成立。如今，于一九九八年，已经有数百间无晶圆厂公司成立，其中最集中的聚落位于硅谷。无晶圆厂公司成为台积公司市场的支柱。

ReadShift 双语翻译

## The '90s Strategies

TSMC's initial strategies, which I briefly described in Chapter 18, "Creation of a New Universe," were passed on to the few managers who needed to execute them in the early years by way of "personal briefings." Everyone was able to execute according to my intentions. The results of these strategies were very fruitful. But by the mid-1990s, the number of senior managers had increased sharply. To achieve unity of effort, it was no longer sufficient to rely on "personal briefings"; it was necessary to write down the company strategy. So in September 1998, I personally spent a few days writing the "TSMC Strategy." The original was in English; recently, to include this strategy in this book, TSMC's public relations department translated it into Chinese.

## TSMC Business Strategy (September 7, 1998)

### Objective

To become a renowned, service-oriented dedicated IC manufacturing services company that creates the greatest total benefit for its customers, thereby becoming the largest and most profitable company in this industry.

### Background, Current Market Overview, and Future Outlook

TSMC pioneered the dedicated IC manufacturing services business model in 1985. At that time, dedicated IC manufacturing services companies did not have a stable market. TSMC's only business opportunity came from periodic outsourcing by integrated device manufacturers (IDMs) from their fabs to us to improve the profitability of those products. Despite the many initial difficulties, TSMC persisted in focusing on the dedicated IC manufacturing services business model.

Our belief and effort were rewarded in the late 1980s and early 1990s. Entrepreneurs found TSMC to be a trustworthy dedicated IC manufacturing services company, and from then on began to establish a large number of fabless companies. Through collaborating with TSMC for their chip production, the initial success achieved by fabless companies led to the successive establishment of more fabless companies. Now, as of 1998, hundreds of fabless companies have been established, with the most concentrated cluster located in Silicon Valley. Fabless companies have become the backbone of TSMC's market.

竞争与挑战

与此同时，台积公司的成功吸引了众多竞争对手投入产业。竞争对手利用台积公司的产能短缺（发生在一九九三—一九九五年和一九九七年部分期间）及相对高的获利率，提供台积公司客户产能和或较低的价格，侵蚀台积公司的市占率。现今（一九九八年）的市场环境特征是竞争激烈，一九九六年起，半导体行业的衰退加剧了此现象，目前仍未见此态势有减弱的迹象。

然而，台积公司专业积体电路制造服务商业模式依旧一如既往，其优势衍生于以下考量：

（1）设计（无晶圆厂）产业——人类创业精神将推动更多无晶圆厂公司成立。某些无晶圆厂公司可能会陷入营运困境甚至因此失败，但是新的公司将进入市场并取而代之。无晶圆厂公司没有大笔投资建厂的负担，相较于大型的整合元件制造公司，他们能够更迅速地市场需求做出反应，也成长得更快。他们在半导体产业的比重将会增加。

（2）整合元件制造公司——晶圆制造技术本身在多数竞争情况下已经不再是决定性的竞争因素。晶圆厂和其他组织（研发、行销、企划等）间的紧密合作仍然相当关键。整合元件制造公司面临耗费巨额资金投资晶圆厂的决策风险，以及日益加剧来自无晶圆厂公司的竞争，将使其选择与晶圆制造服务公司签订制造合约，或成立合资晶圆厂，进而使其风险和资本支出最小化。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Meanwhile, TSMC's success attracted numerous competitors into the industry. Competitors exploited TSMC's capacity shortages (which occurred during 1993-1995 and portions of 1997) and relatively high profitability by offering TSMC's customers capacity and/or lower prices, eroding TSMC's market share. The market environment as of 1998 is characterized by intense competition, a phenomenon exacerbated by the semiconductor industry downturn from 1996 onward, with no sign of this trend weakening.

Nevertheless, TSMC's dedicated IC manufacturing services business model remains as robust as ever, and its advantages stem from the following considerations:

(1) The design (fabless) industry—the entrepreneurial spirit of humankind will drive the founding of more fabless companies. Some fabless companies may find themselves in operational difficulties or even fail, but new companies will enter the market to replace them. Fabless companies do not have the burden of huge capital expenditures for building fabs. Compared to large integrated device manufacturers, they can respond to market demand more rapidly and also grow faster. Their weight in the semiconductor industry will increase.

(2) Integrated device manufacturers—wafer manufacturing technology itself is no longer a decisive competitive factor in most competitive contexts. Close cooperation between fabs and other organizations (R&D, marketing, planning, etc.) remains quite critical. IDMs face the decision risk of spending huge capital on fabs, along with intensifying competition from fabless companies, which will lead them to choose to sign manufacturing contracts with wafer fabrication service companies, or establish joint-venture fabs, thereby minimizing their risks and capital expenditures.

策略I——满足客户需求

客户需要什么？以下列表涵盖绝大多数客户需求，然而个别客户的优先顺序通常有所差异：能使客户脱颖而出、或至少能和对手竞争的技术；台积公司面对客户需求的灵活度；从产品设计定案到量产的周期时间短；能够帮助客户超越竞争对手、或至少能和对手竞争的设计服务；全方位的一站式整合服务；保护客户的智能财产权；能够即时投入且针对可能出现的问题提出解决方案；台积公司对客户的伙伴关系态度和行为。

台积公司的策略是在上述除价格外的所有面向上，能够明显优于竞争对手，方能在价格中赚取价差（price premium）。策略如此制定有双重意义：第一，相较于采取低价策略，以此方式获取的客户忠诚度和长期合作伙伴关系将更为长久。其二，此具有说服力的计算逻辑可以说明：10%的价差获利（10%价差绝非上限）将使我们即使为了更好地服务客户而必须提升营运成本，相较于竞争对手仍可得到更好的获利。

ReadShift 双语翻译

What do customers need? The following list covers the vast majority of customer needs, though the priority order typically varies by individual customer: Technology that enables customers to differentiate themselves, or at least compete with rivals; flexibility of the foundry company in meeting customer needs; short cycle time from product design to mass production; design services that help customers outperform competitors, or at least compete; comprehensive one-stop integration services; protection of customer intellectual property; ability to commit immediately and propose solutions to any problems that may arise; and the foundry company's attitude and behavior toward customer partnership.

TSMC's strategy is to be clearly superior to the competition in all of the above dimensions except price, thereby earning a price premium. This strategic formulation has a dual meaning: First, compared to a low-price approach, the customer loyalty and long-term partnership gained in this way will be more enduring. Second, a compelling logic shows: a 10% price premium (10% is by no means the upper limit) will allow us to achieve better profitability than competitors even when we must increase operating costs to serve customers better.

价格策略与组织策略

再多讲几句我们的价格策略：（1）我们的价格策略是获得价差，但不失去业务。（2）要成功执行此策略，必须拥有绝佳的客户关系。衡量此关系的基准为客户是否让我们看"第一眼和最后一眼"（first and last look）——即最先被客户告知商机，以及最后一个有机会婉拒此商机。如我们看了"最后一眼"，就要竭尽所能（例如采取一次性的交易策略等），避免失去此笔交易。（3）我们可以在一次性的交易上具有弹性，但是当向客户提供此弹性交易时，也需同等对待其他客户——应对其同一领域之直接竞争对手提供类似交易条件。

策略II——组织性地成为市场及服务导向的企业

生产制造或工程导向企业和服务导向企业间存在巨大差异，我们的目标是成为后者，同时保留前者的核心实力。我们的策略是：公司的业务人员（他当然可以是专业工程师、会计、主管等），同时也是公司业务人员。身为业务人员，代表为客户服务。当客户需要服务（例如生产时程变更、技术变更或问题修复等），它必须被视为机会，而不是一种负担。

（2）高阶管理人员（职级三十八以上）除了是优秀的业务和专业人士，更必须是优秀的商业人士（businessmen）。如果他们目前不是，他们应该自我训练、接受训练以成为商业人士。

（3）为了落实我们的定价策略，在很大程度上必须仰赖业务组织的判断。因此，业务组织应全面配有优秀的商业人才（从项目经理到更高职级的同仁）。他们应该完整地接受公司经济面向的相关训练（成本、产能利用率、获利要求等）。因此，他们必须有别于"商品"业务人员且通常具备更高资历。一旦他们的技能和判断达到我们要求的高标准，就应该反映在他们的职级和薪酬上，将其做出对应调整。

ReadShift 双语翻译

A few more words on our pricing strategy: (1) Our pricing strategy is to earn a price premium but not lose business. (2) To successfully execute this strategy, we must have excellent customer relationships. The benchmark for measuring this relationship is whether customers give us the "first and last look"—meaning we are the first to be informed of a business opportunity, and the last to have a chance to decline it. If we're the "last look," we must do everything possible (e.g., adopt one-time deal tactics) to avoid losing that business. (3) We can have flexibility in one-time transactions, but when offering such flexibility to a customer, we must treat other customers the same way—offering similar terms to their direct competitors in the same domain.

## Strategy II — Become a Market- and Service-Oriented Enterprise Organizationally

A great gap exists between production/manufacturing- or engineering-oriented enterprises and market- and service-oriented enterprises. Our goal is to become the latter while retaining the core strengths of the former. Our strategy is:

Personnel in our business organization (who may of course be professional engineers, accountants, managers, etc.) are also businesspeople. As businesspeople, they represent customer service. When a customer needs service (e.g., production schedule changes, technology changes, or problem resolution), it must be viewed as an opportunity, not a burden.

(2) Senior management (level 38 and above) must not only be excellent businesspeople and professionals, but also excellent businessmen. If they are not currently, they should train themselves and receive training to become businessmen.

(3) To implement our pricing strategy, we rely heavily on the judgment of the business organization. Therefore, the business organization should be fully staffed with outstanding talent (from project managers to higher levels). They should receive thorough training in the economic aspects of the business (cost, capacity utilization, profitability requirements, etc.). Thus, they must be distinct from "commodity" salespeople and typically should be of higher caliber. Once their skills and judgment meet the high standards we demand, this should be reflected in their titles and compensation accordingly.

世界级的市场部门

必须建立世界级的市场（Marketing）部门。此部门的职责可列举于下：（a）与研发组织共同确定技术蓝图。（b）建议新服务或技术。（c）与业务单位共同开发新客户。（d）台积公司在不同应用产品（绘图晶片、晶片组等）、不同领域（电脑、手机等）、不同地域、不同客户的行销策略。（e）市场和竞争资讯。（f）战术性定价调整。（g）台积公司的品牌认同。（h）总归来说，成为最高管理者的业务和行销"幕僚长"。

策略III——扩大核心实力

（1）我们的核心优势在工程技术和制造能力。我们必须在这些领域扩大领先优势，具体来说，必须持续努力追求良率、生产周期、生产力、资产利用率等。（2）积极取得公司内部和外部的智能财产权，除数量，更应该重视其品质。

策略IV——无晶圆厂、整合元件制造公司及系统厂商

我们的策略是积极追求所有潜在客户，包括无晶圆厂、整合元件制造公司及系统厂商。

策略VI——财务策略

（1）维持保守的负债/权益结构：35%债务/65%权益。（2）保守管理财务资产。（3）仅投资与我们的核心业务直接相关的业务——晶圆制造服务。（4）在不得已的情况下才会考虑合资成立晶圆制造厂。

ReadShift 双语翻译

A world-class Marketing department must be built. Its responsibilities can include: (a) Collaborate with R&D to determine the technology roadmap. (b) Recommend new services or technologies. (c) Collaborate with business units to develop new customers. (d) TSMC's marketing strategies for different applications (graphics chips, chipsets, etc.), different segments (computers, mobile phones, etc.), different geographies, and different customer types (within the same market or product space). (e) Market and competitive intelligence. (f) Tactical pricing adjustment. (g) TSMC's brand identity. (h) In summary, serve as the chief of staff for business and marketing to top management.

### Strategy III — Build Core Strengths

(1) Our core strengths are engineering technology and manufacturing capability. We must broaden our leading advantage in these areas, specifically by relentlessly pursuing yield improvement, cycle time, productivity, asset utilization, and the like. (2) Actively acquire intellectual property both internal and external to the company. Beyond quantity, quality should be emphasized.

### Strategy IV — Fabless, IDM, and System Companies

Our strategy is to aggressively pursue all potential customers, including fabless, IDM, and system companies.

### Strategy VI — Financial Strategy

(1) Maintain a conservative debt/equity structure: 35% debt/65% equity. (2) Prudently manage financial assets. (3) Only invest in businesses directly related to our core business—wafer manufacturing services. (4) Consider joint-venture fabs only as a last resort.

策略VII——企业文化

我们的企业文化表述于十大经营理念中，其内涵和本策略彼此一致且相互依赖。十大经营理念和本策略应相辅相成。

理想的量化成果

同仁们将此视为成功执行此策略应有的成果，而不是目标本身：成为全球最大的积体电路制造服务公司，营收领先第二大晶圆制造公司比例至少为二比一。（3）二零一零年之前，营收达美金百亿元。

策略的总结

这策略的重点是：运用台积电的核心优势——工程技术及制造能力，而使它成为一个服务公司。以"优质服务"为导向，以"为客户创造最大整体利益"为卖点，毫不犹豫地要求"价差"。而且，"10%价差绝非上限"。这样大胆的策略，不但在台湾制造业没听闻过（不记得张继正总裁在台积电募资时的评语吗？"台湾公司要凭商誉竞争，倒是第一次听闻。"见第十六章），即使在全世界也很少见。

但是，这策略出奇地成功了，不但在九零年代成功，而且一直到我退休，还是继续成功。当然我们在一九九九年，就加了"技术领先"一项。起初也是"耳提面命"，后来正式成为我们"商标"的一部分："技术领先！制造优越！客户信任！"

"技术领先"的果实在二零一一年开始出现（二十八纳米），到二零一八年，也就是我退休的那年，台积电的尖端技术（七纳米）已到了独家领先世界、供不应求的地步。

虽然"技术领先"是今日台积电的重要支柱，但我从未忘记，台积电的基础是"服务导向"打下来的。

ReadShift 双语翻译

## Strategy VII — Corporate Culture

Our corporate culture is captured in the Ten Business Philosophies, whose content and this strategy are consistent with and dependent on each other. The Ten Philosophies and this strategy should complement each other.

### Ideal Quantitative Results: The Outcome, Not the Goal

Colleagues should view these as the fruits that should result from successful execution of this strategy, not as goals per se: Become the world's largest IC manufacturing services company, with revenue lead over the second-largest foundry at least 2:1. (3) Achieve revenue of $10 billion USD by 2010.

### Summary of Strategy

The essence of this strategy is: leverage TSMC's core strengths—engineering technology and manufacturing capability—to transform it into a service company. Oriented around "superior service," with "creating the greatest total benefit for customers" as the selling point, unapologetically demanding a "price premium." And "10% premium is by no means the upper limit." Such a bold strategy had not been heard of in Taiwan's manufacturing industry (don't you remember President Zhang Jizheng's comment during TSMC's fundraising? "A Taiwanese company competing on reputation—that's the first I've heard of it." See Chapter 16). Even globally, such a strategy was rare.

But this strategy succeeded remarkably—not only in the '90s, but continued to be successful all the way through my retirement. Of course, in 1999 we added "technology leadership." At first, it too was transmitted by "personal briefings," and later it formally became part of our "trademark": "Technology Leadership! Manufacturing Excellence! Customer Trust!"

The fruits of "technology leadership" began to appear in 2011 (28nm), and by 2018—the year I retired—TSMC's cutting-edge technology (7nm) had reached a stage of exclusive world dominance, with supply falling short of demand.

Although "technology leadership" is an important pillar of today's TSMC, I have never forgotten: TSMC's foundation was laid down by being "service-oriented."

台積電篇二第二十二章

张忠谋

台积电篇二·第二十二章｜经营权之战落幕，在台湾、美国上市

拖延战术

在第十九章《筚路蓝缕》内，我已叙述在一九八九年底台积电业绩初露曙光时，飞利浦就提出增加股权至51%要求。我也叙述我认此为要求为台积电的"经营权之战"——也是我事业人生的生死战。如果飞利浦成功增股至51%，我很难想像他们会让我继续充分自主地经营台积电；我将面临十年内继德仪、通用、工研院后的第四次失败；我的唯一的未来，恐怕是回美国创业、或教书。即使原始股东的股权会因为飞利浦经营下的台积电而增值不少，但他们的前途也会在失去专业经理人的带领下而比较没有保障。

其实对我而言，台积电"经营权之战"赢了，我的事业前途才有希望。为了抵抗飞利浦增加股权至51%要求，我的初期战术是拖延——拖延战术。在投资协定中，飞利浦的承购价格以三个因素"等量考虑"决定。这三因素中，第二："转让时之公司获利能力及获利预测"及第三："在美国证券市场上市之美国半导体公司之市价/净值比"都有相当主观性，因此可以各有各的看法。果然，在一九八九至一九九零年飞利浦与开发基金一共七次的会议中，飞利浦提出的承购价格总只是十几元，甚至二十元，而开发基金提出的都是七、八元。这样大的差距无法妥协，双方就停止开会了一年。
