## Delay Tactics

In Chapter 19, "Trailblazing," I described how, at year-end 1989 when TSMC's performance first showed promise, Philips demanded an increase in its stake to 51%. I also described how I considered this demand as TSMC's "battle for control"—and a battle for my own professional life and death. If Philips succeeded in increasing its stake to 51%, I could hardly imagine they would let me continue running TSMC with full autonomy. I would face my fourth career failure in a decade—after TI, GE, and ITRI. My only future would probably be returning to the U.S. to start a business or teach. Even though the original shareholders' equity would appreciate considerably under Philips-managed TSMC, their prospects would also be less secure with the loss of professional management.

In fact, for me, only by winning TSMC's "battle for control" would my professional future have hope. To resist Philips' demand to increase equity to 51%, my initial tactic was delay. Under the investment agreement, Philips' purchase price was determined by three factors given "equal consideration." Among these three factors, the second, "the company's earning power and profit forecast at transfer" and the third, "the price-to-book ratio of U.S. semiconductor companies listed on the U.S. stock market," both had considerable room for subjective judgment, so each side could hold its own view. Sure enough, in seven meetings between Philips and the Development Fund during 1989-1990, Philips always proposed a purchase price of only NT$10-20, while the Development Fund proposed NT$7-8. Such a large gap could not be bridged, and both sides stopped meeting for a year.

上市准备

在协商僵持的两年中，台积电的业绩已有飞跃式的成长——营业净利自八九年的四亿五千万元跃至九一年的十二亿四千万元。同时，我也开始做上市准备。九一年四月，我透过开发基金的推荐，打了一通电话给当时大华证券的总经理张孝威，告诉他想委托大华证券担任我们上市承销商，并请他到我办公室商议。

张孝威来了，我把台积电的股东投资协议给他看。这上面有谁派几名董事，谁派董事长，谁派总经理，财务副总等等……孝威说："让我回去研究一下，再跟你回复。"

一个月后，孝威又来了。这次他带了一张皱皱的便条，上面有十几项"必须改"，例如：谁都不能派董事长、总经理，谁都不能派董或监察人……更重要的，不能有一个超过半数股权的股东。

孝威告诉我的，其实是：必须废止当年为了台积电募资时吸引飞利浦投资的"股东协议书"，不然，不要想上市。

ReadShift 双语翻译

During the two years of negotiation deadlock, TSMC's performance had grown by leaps and bounds—net operating profit jumped from NT$450 million in 1989 to NT$1.24 billion in 1991. Meanwhile, I began preparing for an IPO. In April 1991, through a Development Fund referral, I made a phone call to Zhang Xiaowei, then general manager of Grand Cathay Securities, telling him we wanted to engage Grand Cathay as our IPO underwriter and inviting him to my office to discuss.

Zhang Xiaowei came. I showed him TSMC's shareholders' investment agreement. It specified who appointed how many directors, who appointed the chairman, who appointed the general manager, who appointed the financial vice president, and so on. Xiaowei said: "Let me go back and study this, and I'll get back to you."

A month later, Xiaowei came back. This time he brought a crumpled note listing over a dozen "must change" items, e.g.: no one can appoint the chairman or general manager; no one can appoint directors or supervisors. . . . More importantly: there cannot be a shareholder holding more than 50% of equity.

What Xiaowei was really telling me was: the "Shareholders Agreement" that had been crafted to attract Philips' investment during TSMC's fundraising must be annulled—otherwise, don't even think about an IPO.

致函飞利浦

一九九一年九月，开发基金及飞利浦的"承购权"谈判已僵持了一年余，我也自大华证券了解：如台积电要上市，最大股东的股权必须限制在一半以下。我想：台积电向上市迈进一大步的时机已到。我就致函飞利浦的台湾总经理罗益强。罗氏同时亦为台积电董事（飞利浦法人代表）。在此函内，我告诉他若台积电股票上市，原始股东可能有好几倍的投资回收，但飞利浦的股权必须限制在40%以内。

这"40%"的数字是我选的，我认为40%既符合上市规定，又是飞利浦可以接受的。罗益强请示飞利荷兰总部，荷兰总部原则上接受降低承购股权至40%，但双方还是需要同意一个"合理"的承购价格。

鸭子几乎已经煮熟，我想，最后一步还是让开发基金来走吧。开发基金当时归财政部管，主任委员职亦为时任财政部的部长王建煊兼任。我就在九一年十月走访王部长，请教如何化解飞利浦对承购价的僵局。王部长果然提出"锦囊妙计"：成立两个独立的"TSMC股价评审小组"，每组七位委员，均应是台湾社会贤达或金融专家，开发基金及飞利浦各提名约一半。

ReadShift 双语翻译

In September 1991, the "subscription rights" negotiations between the Development Fund and飞利浦 had been deadlocked for over a year. I also learned from Grand Cathay Securities: if TSMC wanted to go public, the largest shareholder's equity must be limited to below 50%. I thought: the time had come for TSMC to take a major step toward listing. I wrote to Luo Yiqiang, the general manager of Philips Taiwan, who was also a TSMC director (Philips' representative). In the letter, I told him that if TSMC stock went public, original shareholders might realize several times their investment return, but Philips' equity would need to be limited to within 40%.

The "40%" figure was my choice. I believed 40% both complied with IPO regulations and was acceptable to Philips. Luo Yiqiang consulted Philips Netherlands headquarters, which in principle accepted reducing the subscription equity to 40%, but both sides still needed to agree on a "reasonable" purchase price.

The duck was almost cooked. I thought: the last step should be left to the Development Fund. At that time, the Development Fund was under the Ministry of Finance, and the chairmanship was held concurrently by the Minister of Finance, Wang Jianxuan. In October 1991, I visited Minister Wang, seeking his advice on breaking the deadlock with Philips over the purchase price. Minister Wang indeed produced a "secret plan": establish two independent "TSMC Stock Price Evaluation Committees" of seven members each, consisting of distinguished members of Taiwanese society or financial experts, with the Development Fund and Philips each nominating about half.

股价评审小组

王部长的建议很快地被飞利浦接受。两个小组也很快地成立。事实上，飞利浦只提名了一位委员：曹嶽维。曹君是当时中欧贸易促进会理事长。开发基金和我很快地把两个小组组成，每组召集人及委员如下：

第一组——曹嶽维（召集人）、施振荣、黄言章、马秀如、李麟、江万龄、徐小波第二组——江万龄（召集人）、黄茂雄、徐小波、张春雄、杜荣、王建煊（后由他人代）

台积电提供两小组需要的财务及财务预测资料，我也指定林坤禧副总为台积电联络人。自九一年十一月至九二年四月，这两小组经过多次讨论，各自达到结论。第二小组先在九二年四月二十一日提报告，建议承购股价20.44元；第一小组在四月二十八日提报告，建议承购股价17.84至19.18元。两小组的建议股价相当接近，那段时期台积电的"未上市股票参考价"也在十七至十八元左右。

在成立两个"TSMC股价评审小组"前，开发基金及飞利浦均同意：小组建议不具约束力，只提供双方参考。所以要完成承购仍要开发基金和飞利浦正式协商；这在九二年八月发生，最后协商价为21.79元，飞利浦增加股权至40%，但更重要的是同意废止一九八六年的"股东协议书"。

至此台积电上市的路已铺好了！但最后还有一步路要走。台积电在九二年十月三十日开始"公开发行"。根据证交法规定，"公开发行"两年后方可上市。

Minister Wang's suggestion was quickly accepted by Philips. The two committees were also quickly formed. In fact, Philips nominated only one member: Cao Yuewei, who was then chairman of the Association for the Promotion of Trade with Central and Eastern Europe. The Development Fund and I quickly formed the two committees, each with the following convenor and members:

Committee 1—Cao Yuewei (Convenor), Shi Zhengrong, Huang Yanzhang, Ma Xiuru, Lin Li, Jiang Wanling, Xu Xiaobo Committee 2—Jiang Wanling (Convenor), Huang Maoxiong, Xu Xiaobo, Zhang Chunxiong, Du Rong, Wang Jianxuan (later replaced)

TSMC provided both committees with needed financial and financial forecast data. I also designated Vice President Lin Kunxi as TSMC's contact person. From November 1991 to April 1992, after extensive discussion, each committee reached its conclusion. The second committee submitted its report on April 21, 1992, recommending a purchase price of NT$20.44. The first committee submitted its report on April 28, 1992, recommending a purchase price of NT$17.84-19.18. The two committees' recommended prices were quite close, and during this period TSMC's "unlisted stock reference price" was also around NT$17-18.

Before the two "TSMC Stock Price Evaluation Committees" were established, the Development Fund and Philips had both agreed: the committee recommendations were non-binding, for reference only. So to complete the subscription, the Development Fund and Philips still needed to negotiate formally. This occurred in August 1992. The final negotiated price was NT$21.79, Philips increased its equity to 40%, but more importantly, both parties agreed to annul the 1986 "Shareholders Agreement."

Now the road to TSMC's listing was paved! But there was still one more step. TSMC began its "public offering" on October 30, 1992. Under securities regulations, listing could occur two years after the "public offering."

台湾上市

小插曲不妨在此一提。根据一九八六年的"股东协议书"，飞利浦要求承购时，任何原始股东均可把拥有的股票卖给飞利浦；如无人要卖，开发基金就是"最后必须卖方"。九二年十月，当一切都谈妥后，王部长以公文征询所有原始股东，是否愿以21.79元股价转让给飞利浦？结果竟是无一股东愿意。在股价已涨了一倍多后，他们此刻不愿出售股票的意志，与六年前他们不愿意投资台积电的意志一样坚强。

我不知现在台湾公司上市是否还是很难？但一九九四年台积电绝对是"民"恳求"官"。台积电在二月二十八日提出上市申请，证交所人员于三月十六、十七两天来公司查核，并且面试我。不少质问：当年为什么要政府（开发基金）出资成立台积电？为什么要飞利浦投资，让"肥水"外流？为什么租工研院的实验工厂？他们对当时台积电在极少人看好的情况下募资（一九八五至八六年）的困难，几乎一无所知——或者，装成一无所知？被面试的我，感觉像是个罪犯。真的，在台湾做事竟是这么难！

面试后被嘱咐写一篇《台积公司成立沿革》。在我的工作日程上，我在三月二十三日记着：整日写台积成立沿革。

当然，证交所的质问，至少还有俞国华、李国鼎可以为我作证。但是，九四年是李登辉任总统的第七年，他的权力基础已很稳固。相对地，俞、李这两位"老臣"已释权多年，我也不想再去麻烦他们援助。

幸而这次倒也不需要他们的援救。《台积公司成立沿革》缴卷后，证交所似已满意。六月二十四日，证交所通过我们的上市案。九月五日，台积电以90元股价上市，但却是"有价无市"，此后六交易日，每天都"无量涨停"。直至九月十二日，股价涨到142.5元才开始有交易。对原始股东而言，如果他们在九四年九月十二日卖出，投资回收是14倍。

ReadShift 双语翻译

An interesting aside: Under the 1986 "Shareholders Agreement," when Philips demanded subscription, any original shareholder could sell their shares to Philips; if no one wanted to sell, the Development Fund was the "last must-sell party." In October 1992, after everything was agreed, Minister Wang sent an official letter to all original shareholders asking whether they were willing to transfer shares to Philips at the NT$21.79 price. The result: not a single shareholder was willing. After the stock price had more than doubled, their resolve not to sell at this moment was as strong as their resolve not to invest in TSMC six years earlier.

I don't know if it's still very difficult for Taiwanese companies to go public, but in 1994, TSMC was definitely the "private sector" begging the "government." TSMC submitted its IPO application on February 28. SEC investigators came to the company on March 16-17 for audits and interviewed me. Many questions: Why did we need the government (Development Fund) to fund TSMC's establishment? Why let Philips invest, allowing "fertile water" to flow to outsiders? Why rent ITRI's experimental factory? They knew almost nothing about the difficulties of fundraising for TSMC when very few believed in it (1985-86)—or perhaps they were pretending not to know? Being interviewed, I felt like a criminal. Really, doing something in Taiwan was that hard!

After the interview, I was instructed to write a piece on "The Founding History of TSMC." In my work diary, on March 23 I noted: "Spent the whole day write TSMC founding history."

Of course, for the SEC's questioning, at least Yu Kuo-hua and Li Guoding could testify on my behalf. But 1994 was the seventh year of Lee Teng-hui's presidency, and his power base was already quite solid. Relatively speaking, Yu and Li, these two "senior ministers," had been out of power for years, and I didn't want to trouble them for their assistance.

Fortunately, this time their rescue wasn't needed. After submitting "The Founding History of TSMC," the SEC seemed satisfied. On June 24, the SEC approved our listing. On September 5, TSMC listed at an IPO price of NT$90, but it was "priced with no market"—for the next six trading days, it hit the daily price limit up with "no volume" every day. It wasn't until September 12, when the price rose to NT$142.50, that trading began. For original shareholders, if they sold on September 12, 1994, their investment return was 14x. Of course, better—and much better—returns lay ahead.

美国ADR上市

台积电在台湾上市的证券商是大华证券，但在正式上市时，原来对我做建议的张孝威总经理已离职，由宋学仁接替。台积电上市后宋也离开大华而加入美商高盛银行（Goldman Sachs）。宋学仁虽然在大华只待了短时期，但在这短时期内刚好碰到台积电在台湾上市。他很看好的前景，况且他初入高盛，还不是"Partner"，正想快快立功升级为"合伙人"。如能说服台积电在美国上市，将是不小的功劳。

有此背景，宋学仁在我们已通过台湾上市、而尚未承销之际，就开始游说我以ADR（American Depositary Receipt）方式在美国上市。对此我起初很冷淡；我刚经历在台湾上市，已对上市前的准备工作感觉疲倦；况且，在美国上市又有什么好处？

后来的几个月，终于打动了我。他的理由是：飞利浦与开发基金都想出脱台积电股票，而台湾股票市场交易量低；如飞利浦或开发基金大量释股，将遭遇"愈卖愈贱"的恶运。相对的，美国市场远较活泼。所以，在美国上市可视为让飞利浦与开发基金卖股票的一个好渠道。

在飞利浦同意降低承购权至40%，并废止"投资协议"时，我已认定飞利浦已放弃原先要控制及经营台积电的意向，而转为要赚钱。但是，假如他们因为卖股不易，仍长期继续保持相当高的股权，那他们的股权仍会像"达摩克利斯之剑"一般，悬挂在我头上。何不给他们一条快速售股的捷径？

ReadShift 双语翻译

Grand Cathay Securities was the underwriter for TSMC's Taiwan listing, but by the time of the formal listing, general manager Zhang Xiaowei, who had originally advised me, had left and was replaced by Song Xueren. After TSMC's listing, Song also left Grand Cathay to join the American investment bank Goldman Sachs. Although Song Xueren was only at Grand Cathay for a brief period, it happened to coincide with TSMC's Taiwan listing. He was very bullish on TSMC's prospects. Moreover, having just joined Goldman Sachs, he was not yet a "Partner" and was eager to achieve merit and get promoted to "partner" quickly. Persuading TSMC to list in the U.S. would be no small accomplishment.

Against this background, while we had already passed Taiwan listing but not yet been underwritten, Song Xueren began lobbying me to list in the U.S. via ADR (American Depositary Receipt). I was initially quite cool to this. I had just gone through the Taiwan IPO and felt exhausted by the preparatory work; moreover, what was the benefit of listing in the U.S.?

In the following months, he finally moved me. His reasoning was: both the Development Fund and Philips wanted to sell TSMC stock, but the Taiwan stock market had low trading volume. If飞利浦 or the Development Fund sold large quantities, they would face the nightmare of "the more you sell, the cheaper it gets." The U.S. market was far more active. Therefore, listing in the U.S. could be seen as a good channel for飞利浦 and the Development Fund to sell their shares.

By the time Philips agreed to reduce its subscription rights to 40% and annul the "Investment Agreement," I had already concluded that Philips had abandoned its original intention to control and operate TSMC and switched to wanting to make money. But if they continued to hold a rather high equity stake long-term because selling shares was difficult, their equity would still hang over my head like the "Sword of Damocles." Why not give them a fast track to sell shares?

高盛长久合作

我对"在美国上市"的看法转为积极后，就与宋学仁说我要与高盛高层建立直接关系；我心里想的不只是这次在美国上市，而是在长久的未来，如果台积能如我那时已期许地成功，就的确需要一家关系密切的世界级投资银行，而高盛恰可充当这角色。宋学仁很配合，把高盛关键人物，包括最高层，都介绍给我。此后几十年，高盛几乎是台积电的唯一投资银行，而且把这工作做得很好。

台积电ADR于一九九七年十月八日在纽约证券交易所以代号TSM上市。台积电每一单位ADR代表台湾的五股。ADR交易远较台股交易活泼。以目前情形来说，ADR大约占全部股权20%，平均每天交易量为一千万ADR，相当于五千万台股；台股占全部股权80%，平均每天交易量只是三千万股；所以ADR交易之活泼度，是台股的六倍多！

我的主要目的——让飞利浦尽快释股，以消灭挂在经营者头上的"达摩克利斯之剑"——也逐渐实现。ADR上市前，飞利浦尚拥有31%股权；八年后（二零零五年）已减至16.4%。二零零八年八月全部出清。

ReadShift 双语翻译

After my view of "listing in the U.S." turned positive, I told Song Xueren that I wanted to establish direct relationships with Goldman Sachs senior management. What I had in mind was not just this U.S. listing, but for the long-term future: if TSMC could succeed as I already envisioned at that time, we would indeed need a close relationship with a world-class investment bank—and Goldman Sachs could precisely play that role. Song Xueren was very cooperative and introduced me to Goldman Sachs key figures, including the highest levels. For decades thereafter, Goldman Sachs has been virtually TSMC's sole investment banking partner, and they did the job very well.

TSMC's ADR was listed on the New York Stock Exchange on October 8, 1997 under the ticker TSM. Each TSMC ADR represents five shares traded in Taiwan. ADR trading is far more active than Taiwan share trading. As of now, ADRs account for about 20% of total equity, with average daily trading volume of 10 million ADRs (equivalent to 50 million Taiwan shares). Taiwan shares account for 80% of total equity, with average daily trading volume of only 30 million shares. So the activity level of ADR trading is more than six times that of Taiwan shares!

My primary goal—allowing飞利浦 to quickly release shares, to eliminate the "Sword of Damocles" hanging over management—was gradually achieved. Before the ADR listing,飞利浦 still owned 31% equity; eight years later (2005), it had reduced to 16.4%. In August 2008, it fully exited.

投资回收与反思

飞利浦在台积电投资上赚了多少钱？我们估计了一下：它的投资是三十亿元，总回收（包括股利及出售股票获利）是四千零三十八亿元——二十一年内一百三十五倍回收！非常好的回收！但是他们原来要经营台积电，要把台积电拥为己有的野心却落空了。他们本以为台积电只是一个台湾性、台湾级的公司，而飞利浦却是世界级的公司。他们在台积电成立四、五年后才发现：这家公司会比他们自己更"世界级"。

开发基金呢？他们一直遵守了"不干涉经营"的原则，但他们卖台积电股票的力道，比飞利浦还大。他们在飞利浦执行承购权后，仍拥有30.8%台积电，但在之后的六年内，就在台湾市场卖得只剩17.4%。ADR上市后，他们更是痛快地卖，卖到二零零五年九月，只剩6.4%。

开发基金赚了多少钱？它的投资是二十二亿元。出售股票收入及截至二零二二年一月底股利收入为两千七百六十七亿元。现在尚握有的6.4%，如以目前股价（约六百三十元）计，约值一兆零四百一十八亿元。也就是说，如果现在出清台积电股票，他们的总投资回收约六百倍。

当然，真正的回收还不能用金钱算。今日台积电的技术和产品，已渗入世界几十亿人民的工作和生活，以及几十万公司、组织的作业中。如果台积电忽然消失，世界几十亿人民的生活肯定会受影响。当年李国鼎、俞国华要成立台积电，为的是要发展台湾半导体工业，至于投资回收，我想他们的目标有限——只要小赚就不对了。

我必须承认，没有政府的投资和协助，我办不起来台积电。在一片"市场经济"呼声中，有些事情还是要由政府来做的。

ReadShift 双语翻译

How much did Philips make on its TSMC investment? We estimated: its investment was NT$3 billion, total recovery (including dividends and stock sale profits) was NT$403.8 billion—a 135x return in 21 years! An excellent return! But their ambition to operate TSMC and claim it as their own was defeated. They originally thought TSMC would be a Taiwan-level company, while Philips was a world-class company. Only four or five years after TSMC's founding did they realize: this company would be even more "world-class" than they were themselves.

The Development Fund? They consistently adhered to the principle of "non-interference in operations," but their selling of TSMC stock was even more aggressive than Philips. After Philips executed its subscription rights, the Development Fund still held 30.8% of TSMC, but within the next six years they sold down to 17.4% on the Taiwan market. After the ADR listing, they sold even more vigorously, down to 6.4% by September 2005.

How much did the Development Fund earn? Its investment was NT$2.2 billion. Stock sale proceeds plus dividend income through end of January 2022 totaled NT$276.7 billion. The 6.4% still held, at the current stock price (about NT$630), would be valued at approximately NT$1.0418 trillion. In other words, if they liquidated their TSMC stock now, their total investment return would be about 600x.

Of course, the true return cannot even be measured in money. Today TSMC's technology and products have permeated the work and lives of billions of people around the world, as well as the operations of hundreds of thousands of companies and organizations. If TSMC suddenly disappeared, the lives of billions of people would certainly be affected. Back then Li Guoding and Yu Kuo-hua wanted to establish TSMC to develop Taiwan's semiconductor industry. As for investment return, I think their goals were limited—just a small profit would have been fine.

I must admit: without the government's investment and assistance, I could not have started TSMC. Amidst the chorus calls for "market economy," there are still things that need to be done by the government.

章节

台積電篇二第二十三章

张忠谋

台积电篇二·第二十三章｜记忆体的诱惑──世界先进和德碁

记忆体的诱惑

本书读者应该对记忆体这名词不陌生。记忆体是德仪半导体重产品之一，在第九章内"记忆体的奋斗"一节，我详述我在德仪经手记忆体事业的甜酸苦辣；老实说，在那时期，不如意的日子超过如意的日子；所以在办台积电时，我已不想碰记忆体。想不到，命运捉弄人，在台积电创办七年后，我又被推人记忆体的漩涡中。到底是怎么发生的？

虽然记忆体对我没有什么吸引力，但正想进入半导体业者特别有诱惑力，因为粗看起来，进入记忆体的门槛似乎较其他半导体产品为低。记忆体的市场大，竞争者少。全球IC市场80%是逻辑，有几百家竞争者；20%是记忆体，只有几家竞争者，而且大部分"记忆体"都是标准型的"商品"，只要依样炮制，就卖得出去。

但是，我几十年经营半导体公司的经验告诉我：虽然记忆体竞争者少，但竞争者都是强大，而且大部分是专做记忆体的公司——七零、八零年代是日本公司，九零年代以后是韩国公司。他们绝对不好惹。

我的经验也告诉我："客制化"产品（Custom Products）通常比标准型商品容易赚钱。还有很重要的一点：记忆体的设计和制程开发必须密切配合。八零年代米德（Carver Mead）与康威（Lynn Conway）把逻辑设计标准化，点出了逻辑晶圆代工的可能。但记忆体设计从未标准化。所以，要成立一家有竞争力的记忆体公司，必须具备设计与制程都强的能力。

ReadShift 双语翻译

## The Lure of Memory

Readers of this book should be familiar with the term "memory." Memory was one of TI's major semiconductor products. In Chapter 9, in a section titled "The Struggle of Memory," I detailed the ups and downs of my experience running the memory business at TI. Frankly, during that period, there were more bad days than good. So when founding TSMC, I had no desire to touch memory again. Who would have thought—fate plays tricks on people—seven years after founding TSMC, I was pushed back into the memory vortex. How did this happen?

Although memory held no attraction for me, it was particularly alluring for those wanting to enter the semiconductor business, because at first glance the barrier to entry into memory seemed lower than for other semiconductor products. The memory market was large with few competitors. 80% of the global IC market was logic, with hundreds of competitors; 20% was memory, with only a few competitors. Moreover, most "memory" products were standard "commodities"—you could just replicate them and they'd sell.

But my decades of experience running semiconductor companies told me: although memory had fewer competitors, those competitors were formidable, and most specialized in memory—Japanese companies in the 70s and 80s, Korean companies after the 90s. They were absolutely not to be trifled with.

My experience also taught me: "custom" products usually make money more easily than standard commodities. There was another very important point: memory design and process development had to work hand in glove. In the 1980s, Carver Mead and Lynn Conway standardized logic design, pointing to the possibility of logic wafer foundry. But memory design was never standardized. So to build a competitive memory company, one needed to be strong in both design and process technology.

德碁的起源

在一九八八、八九，全球记忆体市场已经好几年缺货，记忆体价格居高不下，日、韩的记忆体公司都赚了翻了，此时台湾就有两位关键人士，中了记忆体的诱惑。

一位是宏碁集团施振荣董事长。一九八八年七月，施董事长告诉我：宏碁电脑需要大量记忆体，记忆体是它成本的一大块，所以施董事长预备在宏碁集团下成立一家记忆体公司，既可自给，又可省钱，甚至还可卖给别的客户赚钱。

但是设计和制程技术呢？施董事长说可以从德仪移转。当然这要付德仪相当高的技术费。董事长的计画犯了我的大忌：技术不自主！但是在他告诉我他的记忆体计画时，我已接近任工研院院长的终点。我在工研院的三大改革，至少两个已失败；我的副院长已辞职，我已"众叛亲离"；我的两个上司：经济部部长和行政院院长，都已说我"不善处理人事"。

在这样的处境下，我实在不想质疑台湾电脑界的大老施董事长。于是，我只讲了几句不著边际的话。事后证明，我这样做是对的，因为七个月后（一九八九年二月），施要对经济部长陈履安报告他的记忆体公司（PEGE）计画，陈部长嘱我参与，我听了德仪移转技术的详细条件后，觉得实在苛刻，就在会中表达。陈部长立刻打断我的话说："这是宏碁的事，你不必过问。"后来陈部长做结论时说："政府既不投资，乐观其成。"

ReadShift 双语翻译

In 1988-89, the global memory market had been in shortage for several years. Memory prices stayed high, and Japanese and Korean memory companies were making a killing. At this time, two key figures in Taiwan fell to the lure of memory.

One was Acer Group Chairman Shi Zhengrong (Stan Shih). In July 1988, Chairman Shi told me: Acer needed large quantities of memory; memory accounted for a big chunk of its cost. So Chairman Shi planned to establish a memory company under the Acer Group—both self-serving and cost-saving, and potentially selling to other customers for profit.

But what about design and process technology? Chairman Shi said it could be transferred from TI. Of course, this would require paying TI quite high technology fees. Chairman Shi's plan violated my cardinal rule: technological non-autonomy! But when he told me about his memory plan, I was nearing the end of my tenure as ITRI president. Two of my three major ITRI reforms had failed; my vice president had resigned; I had been "deserted by friends and followers." My two superiors—the Minister of Economic Affairs and the Premier—had both said I was "poor at handling people."

In this situation, I really didn't want to question Chairman Shi, an elder of Taiwan's computer industry. So I said only a few noncommittal words. It turned out that my approach was correct. Seven months later (February 1989), Shi reported to Economic Minister Chen Lian-an on his memory company (PEGE) plan. Minister Chen asked me to participate. After hearing the detailed terms of TI's technology transfer, I felt they were truly harsh and said so at the meeting. Minister Chen immediately cut me off: "This is Acer's business; you need not interfere." Later Minister Chen concluded: "The government won't invest; we're happy to see it succeed."

世界先进的起源

第二位中了记忆体诱惑的是当时工研院副院长史钦泰。钦泰是我在规画台积电时亲密度仅次于胡定华的同事，但在工研院衍生公司这课题上，他的看法与我很不一样。我认为衍生公司，人要移过去；他却不放人，认为工研院的半导体计画不只衍生一个公司，而是要衍生一个产业。

一个妈妈，要生许多孩子，而且这许多孩子要各有特色；不然，他们会互相竞争、互相残杀。这样的妈妈，工研院能做吗？

假使有人问我，我的答复会是斩钉截铁的"不能"。但是，我在八八年十二月已被调任为无权、不领薪、也没有什么事的工研院董事长，钦泰已不必问我。大概他知道如果问我，我会反对，所以也不问。

另一方面，工研院的"美洲技术顾问团"在八九竭力推荐记忆体为工研院"下一个半导体计画"。于是，以记忆体为载具的"次微米计画"就在九零年上路。这计画有一特点：自始就预备衍生一家记忆体公司。所以，它的"实验室"就盖在新竹科学园区，实际上是一座厂房——以便"衍生"新公司后立刻可成为工厂。

我在九零年才陆续知道"次微米计画"的内容，立刻就认为这是一个野心极大的计画。它的目的是五年后（一九九五年）衍生一个记忆体公司；既然要衍生一个公司，这公司当然要有竞争力，那么，从制程技术面来说，"次微米计画"必须紧紧跟随"摩尔定律"——这是它的前身（VLSI计画）在十年内都没做到的事；除制程技术外，记忆体公司还需要记忆体设计技术。工研院一直就没有好好发展设计技术，而且发展的只有简单的逻辑设计，几乎从未涉猎记忆体设计。

ReadShift 双语翻译

The second person to fall to the lure of memory was then-ITRI Vice President Shi Qin-tai (Shih Ching-tai). Qin-tai was my closest colleague in planning TSMC after Hu Ding-hua. But on the topic of ITRI spin-offs, his view was quite different from mine. I believed that when spinning off companies, people should move over. He didn't want to release people; he believed ITRI's semiconductor program should spin off not just one company but an entire industry.

One mother giving birth to many children—and these many children each having distinctive characteristics, otherwise they would compete with each other and kill each other. Could ITRI be that mother?

Had anyone asked me, my answer would have been a resounding "no." But in December 1988, I had been reassigned as ITRI chairman with no power, no salary, and nothing to do, so Qin-tai no longer needed to ask me. He probably knew I would oppose it, so he didn't bother asking.

On another front, ITRI's "Americas Technical Advisory Committee" vigorously pushed memory as ITRI's "next semiconductor program" in 1989. Thus, the memory-vehicle "Submicron Program" was launched in 1990. This program had one characteristic: from the start, it was designed to spin off a memory company. So its "laboratory" was built in Hsinchu Science Park—actually a fab building—so that after the new company was spun off, it could immediately become a fab.

I didn't learn the details of the "Submicron Program" until 1990. I immediately saw this as an extremely ambitious program. Its goal was to spin off a memory company five years later (1995). Since a company was to be spun off, it would of course need competitiveness. From a process technology standpoint, the "Submicron Program" had to keep pace with "Moore's Law"—something its predecessor (the VLSI Program) had not accomplished in ten years. Beyond process technology, a memory company also needed memory design technology. ITRI had never properly developed design technology, and what it had developed was only simple logic design—it had barely touched memory design.

李健熙的早餐

一九八九年一月，我刚卸任工研院院长职；施振荣董事长已告诉我他想自德仪购买记忆体技术、成立德碁记忆体公司的大致构想；但"次微米计画"还在史钦泰副院长心中酝酿，我尚不知情。此时我忽然接到韩国三星电子公司台北办事处的电话邀请：董事长李健熙正在台湾，想邀请我早餐。

当时大部分美国半导体公司已退出记忆体业，日本公司仍占据大部分记忆体市场，但因为《广场协议》和自，日币在一九五至八八年的三年内升值了一倍有余，所以日本记忆体公司已渐渐不支；相反地，韩国三星公司渐露锋芒。

我为了好奇而赴约——毕竟台积电不做记忆体，为什么李健熙要请我吃早餐？

我同时也邀施振荣和史钦泰一同前往。邀施，是因为我也知道他正在想办记忆体公司；邀史，是因为他是我成立台积电的重要助手，也是工研院研发重心的代表人物。见面后发现，原来这次李健熙的角色是"说客"。他认为记忆体业需要很大资本、很多人才。台湾出不起这资本、聚不到这人才；所以，还是死了进入记忆体业的心吧！为了要让我们见识三星已投入的资本和人才，他邀请我们前往韩国访问三星。

我事后才知道，李健熙在邀我早餐时，已知道施董事长要办德碁（李的情报可能来自德仪管道）。至于为什么用我做媒介？大概他从我在德仪的经历以及之后在台积电创立"专业晶圆代工"商业模式，知道我是一个"内行的半导体经营者"。

ReadShift 双语翻译

In January 1989, I had just stepped down as ITRI president. Chairman Shi Zhengrong had already told me his general vision of buying memory technology from TI to form a Tepro memory company. But the "Submicron Program" was still brewing in Vice President Shi Qin-tai's mind, and I was unaware of it. Then I suddenly received a phone call from the Taipei office of Korea's Samsung Electronics: Chairman Lee Kun-hee was in Taiwan and wanted to invite me to breakfast.

At that time, most American semiconductor companies had exited the memory business. Japanese companies still dominated most of the memory market, but because of the Plaza Accord, the Japanese yen had more than doubled in value against the USD between 1985 and 1988, so Japanese memory companies were gradually losing ground. Conversely, Korea's Samsung was emerging.

I attended out of curiosity—after all, TSMC didn't do memory; why would Lee Kun-hee want to buy me breakfast?

I also invited both Shi Zhengrong and Shi Qin-tai to come along. I invited Shi Zhengrong because I also knew he was thinking of starting a memory company. I invited Shi Qin-tai because he was an important aide in establishing TSMC and a representative figure of ITRI's R&D center of gravity. At the meeting, it turned out that Lee Kun-hee's role this time was as a "lobbyist." He believed the memory industry required huge capital and much talent. Taiwan couldn't afford the capital or gather the talent—so give up the idea of entering the memory industry! To show us the capital and talent Samsung had already invested, he invited us to visit Samsung in Korea.

I learned afterward that Lee Kun-hee already knew about Chairman Shi's plan to establish Tepro when he invited me to breakfast (Lee's intelligence may have come through TI channels). As for why he used me as an intermediary—probably from my experience at TI and afterward in creating the "dedicated foundry" business model at TSMC, he knew I was a "knowledgeable semiconductor operator."

访问三星

总之，我和史、施接受了李健熙的邀请访问三星，也在两个半月后（一九八九年四月十三至十五日）实践了我们的访问。在韩国受到了三星诚恳的款待。十三日晚上到达首尔，住进三星开办的旅馆；十四日参观三星记忆体工厂。在此之前，我已看过不少记忆体工厂——德仪日本、德仪美国、还有好几个日本记忆体公司。的确，与我看过德日、德仪美的工厂相比，三星的工厂毫不逊色。三星的工程师和经理人相当熟谙他们的工作，也都相当诚恳回答我们的问题。

十五日上午，李健熙在一个布置华丽的大会客室接见我们。也有几位三星经理人员陪同。我们人见，在我脑海中一瞬即逝的印象是：有点像古代中国边疆酋长进贡时拜见中国皇帝。

李健熙问我们：怎么样，你们看到了吧？记忆体需要很大资本、很多人才。我已不记得我们的详细答复，总之是谢谢他，也说了些很佩服三星成就之类的话。当天下午我们就登机回台北。

这次访问，丝毫没有改变施董事长、史副院长对记忆体的看法。施董事长的德碁计画木已成舟，他在与李健熙早餐（一月）及访问三星（四月）中间，已在二月对经济部长报告要成立德碁。看了三星后，他还是继续积极进行德碁的开办。

史副院长在与李早餐前，已开始在心中酝酿以记忆体为载具、以五年内衍生记忆体公司为目标的"次微米计画"。访问三星后，他更积极对经济部倡议"次微米计画"。终于在一年多后，一九九零年七月，此计画正式开始。

ReadShift 双语翻译

In any case, Shi, Shi, and I accepted Lee Kun-hee's invitation to visit Samsung, and two and a half months later (April 13-15, 1989), we fulfilled our visit. We received warm hospitality from Samsung in Korea. On the evening of the 13th we arrived in Seoul and checked into a Samsung-operated hotel. On the 14th we toured Samsung's memory fab. Before this, I had seen quite a few memory fabs—TI Japan, TI U.S., and several Japanese memory companies. Indeed, compared to the TI Japanese, TI U.S. fabs I had seen, Samsung's fab was in no way inferior. Samsung's engineers and managers were highly knowledgeable about their work and answered our questions quite frankly.

On the morning of the 15th, Lee Kun-hee received us in a magnificently decorated boardroom. Several Samsung managers also accompanied him. A fleeting impression in my mind was: somewhat like a frontier tribal chief paying tribute to the Chinese emperor in ancient times.

Lee Kun-hee asked us: Well, did you see? Memory requires huge capital and lots of talent. I don't remember our exact replies—in any case, we thanked him, and said things like how much we admired Samsung's achievements. That afternoon we boarded a plane back to Taipei.

This visit didn't change Chairman Shi's or Vice President Shi's views of memory at all. Chairman Shi's Tepro plan was already a done deal—between the breakfast with Lee Kun-hee (January) and the Samsung visit (April), he had already reported to the Economic Minister in February about establishing Tepro. After seeing Samsung, he continued actively pursuing Tepro's founding.

Vice President Shi, before the breakfast with Lee, had already begun brewing in his mind the "Submicron Program" with memory as its vehicle and the goal of spinning off a memory company within five years. After visiting Samsung, he became more active in advocating for the "Submicron Program" to the Ministry of Economic Affairs. Finally, over a year later, in July 1990, the program officially began.

次微米计划与投标

工研院的"次微米计画"在九零年七月正式开始。史钦泰副院长深知开发记忆体需要设计及制程人才密切配合，他亲到美国求才，找到了卢志远、卢超群两兄弟。哥哥卢志远在贝尔实验室开发制程，弟弟卢超群在IBM设计——两人在各自领域都相当杰出，把他们两人找进"次微米计画"的确会是一个不错的安排。

但是问题发生了。志远愿意受聘为电子所副所长，并主持"次微米计画"，但超群志在创业，要在台湾开一家记忆体设计公司（即是后来的钰创科技），所以只愿意做"次微米计画"的设计承办者。史副院长在没有更好选择情形下，也同意了这安排。

这安排在第一个产品的开发相当成功，四年后（九四年中期），电子所和钰创团队已成功开发4M DRAM。但这安排的另一任务却被忽略了。4M DRAM的设计可以由钰创承办，但是下一个产品呢？本来要在"次微米计画"下建立自己的设计团队，但是等到真的要做，就发现有基本的矛盾和困难。台湾的IC设计人才本来就少，遇到好的，谁雇他（她）？是电子所还是钰创？何况竞争雇设计人才的公司还不只钰创，九三年又另一家记忆体设计公司从"钰创"衍生出去。

总之，直至九四年，在世界先进衍生的前夕，隶属工研院"次微米计画"的DRAM设计工程师只有两、三位。

ReadShift 双语翻译

ITRI's "Submicron Program" officially began in July 1990. Vice President Shi Qin-tai, keenly aware that memory development required close cooperation between design and process talent, personally went to the U.S. to recruit, finding the brothers Lu Chih-yuan and Lu Chao-chun. The elder brother Lu Chih-yuan developed processes at Bell Labs; the younger brother Lu Chao-chun designed at IBM—both were quite outstanding in their respective fields. Recruiting both into the "Submicron Program" was indeed a good arrangement.

But a problem emerged. Chih-yuan was willing to serve as deputy director of the Electronics Research Institute and lead the "Submicron Program." But Chao-chun aspired to start his own business—he wanted to open a memory design company in Taiwan (which later became ProMOS Technologies)—so he was only willing to be the design contractor for the "Submicron Program." Vice President Shi, lacking a better alternative, also agreed to this arrangement.

This arrangement was quite successful in developing the first product. Four years later (mid-1994), the ERI and ProMOS teams had successfully developed 4M DRAM. But another mission of this arrangement was neglected. The 4M DRAM design could be contracted to ProMOS, but what about the next product? The original intent was to build the program's own design team under the "Submicron Program," but when it came time to actually do it, fundamental contradictions and difficulties emerged. Taiwan's IC design talent was already scarce. When you found good talent, who hired them—ERI or ProMOS? Moreover, ProMOS wasn't the only company competing to hire design talent; in 1993 another memory design company "spun off" from ProMOS.

In any case, by 1994, on the eve of Vanguard International's spin-off, the DRAM design engineers belonging to ITRI's "Submicron Program" numbered only two or three.

"无法拒绝的机会"

更巧的，九四年秋，台积电在台湾上市，上市几天后股价涨到142.5元，是原始投资成本的十几倍（见第二十二章）。不少台积电的原始团队都发了一笔不大不小的财，被"次微米计画"的团队羡慕。"他们能，为什么我们不能？"

赶快衍一家公司！赶快量！赶快上市！赶快发财！

在"次微米计画"团队急著要量4M DRAM、工研院电子所绝对看好衍生公司的情绪下，经济部在九三年底决定以"招标"方式决定谁主导衍生公司。

台积电呢？如我在本章开端说，我离开德仪后，已不想碰记忆体。九四年台积电的总经理是布鲁克；布鲁克是我德仪属下手当初他也不想再碰记忆体。但是，当时台积电第三号人物——营运副总，也是原来核心团队之首繁城，虽不太了解记忆体业，却十分看好"次微米计画"团队，认为我们必须"竞标"。

即使我和布鲁克能够说服曾繁城的热忱，我也认为如不投标，对台积电和我都会是很大的负数。原因有二：第一，自八九年至九四年，我是工研院董事长，虽然在"次微米计画"酝酿时未被征询，但在此计画执行时我也自以为要尽董事长责任，充分支持此计画，现在又怎么能在即将产生成果时撒手？

第二，当初我替工研院的VLSI计画找出路，衍生了台积电，而台积电又非常成功。现在工研院又要衍生一个半导体公司，难道我拒绝参与？正因为是台积电成功，大家才会有这样的期待。

现在，又一个"无法拒绝的机会"出现。还是去吧！不负大家的期望。再募一次资，再办一个公司。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Coincidentally, in the fall of 1994, TSMC listed in Taiwan. Within a few days of listing, the stock price rose to NT$142.5, more than ten times the original investment cost (see Chapter 22). Many of TSMC's founding team members made a modest fortune, which was envied by the "Submicron Program" team. "They can do it, why can't we?"

Spin off a company quickly! Ramp production quickly! Go public quickly! Get rich quickly!

Amid the "Submicron Program" team's eagerness to ramp 4M DRAM production, and ERI's unwavering optimism about the spin-off company, the Ministry of Economic Affairs decided at year-end 1993 to determine who would lead the spin-off company through a "bidding" process.

As for TSMC? As I said at the beginning of this chapter, after leaving TI I had no desire to touch memory again. In 1994, TSMC's general manager was Brook; Brook was my former TI subordinate who had experienced the ups and downs of memory with me, and he didn't want to touch memory again either. But the then-third-ranking figure at TSMC—COO and also leader of the original core team Fan-cheng—though not very knowledgeable about the memory business, was extremely bullish on the "Submicron Program" team and believed we must "bid."

Even if Brook and I could have convinced Fan-cheng to temper his enthusiasm, I also believed that not bidding would be a significant negative for both TSMC and me. There were two reasons: First, from 1989 to 1994, I was ITRI chairman. Although I wasn't consulted when the "Submicron Program" was brewing, during the program's execution I felt it my duty as chairman to fully support it. How could I now abandon it when results were about to bear fruit?

Second, originally I had found an outlet for ITRI's VLSI program by spinning off TSMC, and TSMC had become hugely successful. Now ITRI wanted to spin off another semiconductor company—could I refuse to participate? Precisely because TSMC had succeeded, people had these expectations of me.

Now, another "offer I couldn't refuse" appeared. Let's just go! Live up to everyone's expectations. Raise funds again, build another company.

成立世界先进半导体公司

九四年为记忆体公司募资，比八五至八六年为台积电募资容易得多了。重要原因是台积电在成立后的七年内已有爆发性的成长（九三年营收新台币一百二十三亿元，营业净利四十四亿元），投资人新的记忆体公司也会同样成功。新公司在几个月内就募集到一百二十二亿元。投资者由台积电领衔（四十二亿元），包括联华、台聚等十三家公司以及工研院与台积电的员工。与八五至八六年的台积电募资相比，台积电当年只募到五十五亿元。

下一步要"投标"，也就是要决定以多少新公司的股票回馈政府。在投标前，业界盛传至少台积电与联电会投标，所以投标的数字必须保守机密。所有投资人都授权我决定，不必告诉他们。想了几天后，我合理的回馈就是政府对"次微米计画"真实的经费付出。这数字是57亿5500万元（5亿7550万股）。

开标了。我们得标。惊奇的是：我们是唯一投标者！联电董事长立刻发布：他成功地抬高了我对政府的回馈。当时我虽稍有被玩弄的不快，但这不快很快地过去，毕竟，更大的挑战还在后面。

得标后，立刻成立新公司，初期资本总额一百八十亿元。新公司的名字，世界先进，是后来卢志远取的。志远也同时带领"次微米计画"同仁共两百余人过来到新公司，成为新公司的核心团队。志远成为新公司的营运副总。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Raising capital for a memory company in 1994 was much easier than it had been for TSMC in 1985-86. The important reason: TSMC had experienced explosive growth within seven years of its founding (1993 revenue NT$12.3 billion, net operating profit NT$4.4 billion). Investors believed the new memory company would succeed similarly. The new company raised NT$12.2 billion within a few months. Investors, led by TSMC (NT$4.2 billion), included thirteen companies such as UMC and Taisu Core, plus ITRI and TSMC employees. Compared to TSMC's fundraising in 1985-86, when TSMC had only raised NT$5.5 billion.

Next came the "bidding"—determining how much of the new company's stock to give the government in return. Before bidding, industry rumors said at least TSMC and UMC would bid, so the bid numbers had to be kept strictly confidential. All investors authorized me to decide without informing them. After thinking for a few days, I decided the reasonable return to the government was the actual funding the government had contributed to the "Submicron Program." This figure was NT$575.5 million (57.55 million shares).

The bids were opened. We won the bid. Surprisingly: we were the only bidder! UMC's chairman immediately announced that he had successfully driven up our return to the government. Although I felt a slight displeasure at being played, this displeasure quickly passed—after all, the bigger challenges still lay ahead.

After winning, the new company was immediately formed, with initial total capital of NT$18 billion. The new company's name, Vanguard International, was later coined by Lu Chih-yuan. Chih-yuan also led over 200 colleagues from the "Submicron Program" to the new company, becoming its core team. Chih-yuan became the new company's COO.

艾凡斯与波折

我自经济部决定要招标时，就开始物色总经理。第一人史钦泰。他是"次微米计画之父"，也是台湾资深半导体研发者，所以是当然人选。史在九三年底也答应接受此职。但九四年初，史忽然被升任为工研院院长，他就告诉我：他宁愿当工研院院长，而不来世界先进做总经理了。

我的第二人选是孔毅（Roger Kung），当时在美国摩托罗拉担任。经过面后，孔同意参加。但当他辞职时，摩托罗拉给了新职位。他宁留摩托罗拉，不来世界先进了。

第三人选是一位德仪旧属，当时在英特尔当副。但考虑了几天后，也回绝了我。

三个人回绝我后，我有点著急了。我想到老朋友艾凡斯。他曾任IBM副总裁多年，后来参加H&Q创业投资基金。我想他虽不曾经营半导体事业，但对半导体不陌生，而且他多年电脑企业高阶经验，应该能领导世界先进的年轻一辈。艾凡斯欣然接受我的聘请，在九五年一月报到。

此后十个月世界先进在兴奋的忙碌中度过——忙碌扩厂，购置制造设备。4M DRAM是世先唯一能量产的产品，市价持续高于十二美元，而制造成本约五、六美元。营收从第一季几乎零，到第二季四亿元，第三季度十五亿元！到八月，公司首次收支平衡。艾凡斯模仿台积电首月收支平衡的做法，宣布员工分红！

但是好景不长。九六年四月的一个周末，艾凡斯约我午餐，告诉我4M DRAM价格迅速下降，因为下一代记忆体：十六M DRAM来了。但世界先进的十六M DRAM还在开发中，离量产还远得很。

ReadShift 双语翻译

When the Ministry of Economic Affairs decided on bidding, I began scouting for a general manager. My first choice was Shi Qin-tai. He was the "father of the Submicron Program" and Taiwan's senior semiconductor R&D leader—he was the natural choice. Shi had agreed to accept the position at year-end 1993. But in early 1994, Shi was suddenly promoted to ITRI president. He told me: he would rather be ITRI president than come to Vanguard as general manager.

My second choice was Roger Kung, then at Motorola in the U.S. After interviews, Kung agreed to join. But when he resigned, Motorola offered him a new position. He chose to stay at Motorola instead.

My third choice was a former TI subordinate who was then a vice president at Intel. But after considering for a few days, he also declined.

After three people rejected me, I was getting anxious. I thought of an old friend— Evans. He had served as an IBM vice president for many years, later joining H&Q venture capital. I thought that although he had never run a semiconductor business, he was no stranger to semiconductors. Moreover, with his many years of senior computer industry experience, he should be able to lead Vanguard's younger generation. Evans gladly accepted my offer and reported for duty in January 1995.

For the next ten months, Vanguard passed in excited busyness—busy expanding the fab, purchasing manufacturing equipment. 4M DRAM was Vanguard's only volume product, with market price consistently above $12 while manufacturing cost was about $5-6. Revenue went from almost zero in Q1 to NT$400 million in Q2, NT$1.5 billion in Q3! By August, the company achieved break-even for the first time. Evans imitated TSMC's practice after its first break-even month and announced an employee bonus!

But the good times didn't last. On a weekend in April 1996, Evans asked me to lunch and told me that 4M DRAM prices were falling rapidly because the next generation—16M DRAM—was arriving. But Vanguard's 16M DRAM was still in development, far from volume production.

曾繁城接手与转型

九六年新年假后，4M DRAM市价继续崩跌；第一季平均价格是7.57美元，第二季3.94美元，第三季2.29美元。自第二季起，世界先进进入亏损状态，而且生产愈多，亏损愈大。艾凡斯撑不住了。

我怜悯这位老朋友，但同时也决定他不能继续做世界先进总经理了。刚巧那时台积电营运副总曾繁城我不满他的总经理布鲁克，想从台积电辞职。我对曾说："你不必辞职，暂时去世界先进当总经理吧。"曾欣然同意。五月八日我就对世界先进干部宣布艾凡斯辞职，繁城（大家都称他为FC）任总经理。

再一年，世界先进亏损更大，FC更急著要回台积电。九八年五月，我宣布FC回台积电任总经理职，卢志远暂代世界先进总经理。同时我竭力鼓励当时台积电营运副总蔡力行去世界先进当总经理。蔡很不愿意，但经我力劝后，他终于同意。

蔡力行只做了十三个月（一九九九年二月至二零零零年三月）世界先进总经理，但他做了一件很重要的事——他对我说："世界先进若记忆体没有希望，把它转型成专业晶圆代工！与台积电一样。那么，台积电可以帮助它慢慢再站起来。"

我同意。自二零零年起，我们把世界先进转型。二零零一至二零零二年全球半导体业不景气，台积电和世界先进都不能幸免，但二零零三年后，世界先进的晶圆代工业务就慢慢茁壮。这十几年来，世界先进已是一个很健康的专业晶圆代工公司。

ReadShift 双语翻译

After the 1996 New Year holiday, 4M DRAM market prices continued to crash. Q1 average price: $7.57; Q2: $3.94; Q3: $2.29. From Q2 onward, Vanguard entered a loss position—the more they produced, the more they lost. Evans couldn't hold out anymore.

I pitied this old friend, but also decided he couldn't continue as Vanguard's general manager. As it happened, TSMC's COO Zeng Fan-cheng was dissatisfied with his general manager Brook and wanted to resign from TSMC. I said to Zeng: "You needn't resign—go to Vanguard as general manager for now." Zeng gladly agreed. On May 8, I announced to Vanguard executives that Evans had resigned and Fan-cheng (everyone called him FC) was now general manager.

One year later, Vanguard's losses grew even larger, and FC was even more anxious to return to TSMC. In May 1998, I announced FC's return to TSMC as general manager, with Lu Chih-yuan acting as Vanguard general manager. At the same time, I strongly encouraged TSMC COO Cai Lixing to go to Vanguard as general manager. Cai was very reluctant, but after my earnest urging, he finally agreed.

Cai Lixing served as Vanguard general manager for only thirteen months (February 1999 to March 2000), but he did one very important thing—he said to me: "If Vanguard has no future in memory, transform it into a dedicated foundry! Like TSMC. Then TSMC can help it slowly stand up again."

I agreed. From 2000, we transformed Vanguard. The 2001-2002 global semiconductor downturn hit both TSMC and Vanguard, but after 2003, Vanguard's foundry business gradually grew stronger. For over a decade now, Vanguard has been a healthy dedicated foundry company.

记忆体梦碎

德碁比世界先进早五年开始，但它的命运与世界先进相似。世界先进虽有自主记忆体技术，但技术跟不上竞争者，所以失败。德碁没有自主记忆体技术，它的技术来源——德仪，在九零年代决定退出。幸而在九九年台积电因为自己来不急扩充产能，决定为增加产能而购并德碁。自此德碁的招牌消失，它的工厂变成台积电的晶圆七厂。

九零年代德碁和世界先进在记忆体上的努力，是台湾企图强力进入记忆体业的勇敢一搏。但"爱拼才会赢"，世界先进和德碁拼了，而没有赢。幸而有台积电这一支救兵，才不致"死伤惨重"。

当年李健熙的"忠"告："台湾出不起记忆体业需要的资本，也没有足够人才……要是真的要做记忆体，还是与三星合作"，至少有一半是对的。的确，德碁和世界先进人才、资本都不够，但是李健熙漏了另一个重点："学习曲线"！在九零年代德碁和世界先进开始做记忆体时，三星已远在"学习曲线"的前面。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Tepro started five years earlier than Vanguard, but its fate was similar to Vanguard's. Although Vanguard had independent memory technology, the technology couldn't keep up with competitors, so it failed. Tepro had no independent memory technology at all, and its technology source—TI—decided to exit the memory business in the 1990s. Fortunately, in 1999, TSMC, unable to expand its own capacity fast enough, decided to acquire Tepro to increase capacity. From then on, Tepro's brand disappeared, and its fabs became TSMC's Fab 7.

The efforts of Tepro and Vanguard in memory in the 1990s were a bold attempt by Taiwan to forcefully enter the memory industry. But "only those who fight will win"—Vanguard and Tepro fought, but didn't win. Fortunately TSMC existed as a rescue force, preventing "heavy casualties."

Lee Kun-hee's "sincere" advice—"Taiwan cannot afford the capital needed for the memory industry, nor does it have enough talent... if you really want to do memory, better to cooperate with Samsung"—was at least half right. Indeed, Tepro and Vanguard lacked both talent and capital. But Lee Kun-hee missed another critical point: the "learning curve"! When Tepro and Vanguard started making memory in the 1990s, Samsung was already far ahead on the learning curve.

章节

台積電篇二第二十四章

张忠谋

台积电篇二·第二十四章｜争取客户信任

九零年代产能供不应求

现在回想起来，台积电的三块基石：制造优越、客户信任、技术领先；前两者在九零年代都已奠定。第三块：技术领先，也在九零年代后期开始成形。在这章中，我想谈谈台积电如何在九零年代奠定"客户信任"的基础。

台积电一厂是规模甚小的厂，但在开张两年后才有足够订单把它填满。二厂在一九八九年落成，九零年开始量产，虽然并不是很快就产能满载，但是客户自工厂落成后就给我们很乐观的需求预测，使得我们也很乐观。果然，九二年他们的实际需求甚至超过他们原先以为乐观的预测。同时，新的无晶圆厂IC设计公司纷纷成立，成为我们客户。这真是我们兴奋的时光！我们立刻决定建三厂，三厂在九五年落成。

事实上，除了九六、九七、九八这三年世界半导体业不景气，台积电营收也只能以36%、18%、15%成长率稍缓成长外，整个九零年代台积电都在产能不足、供不应求状态中。在这情形下，客户最殷切的要求就是要我们大胆建新厂，积极扩产。这点，我们做到了。三厂在九五年落成时，我们立刻为四厂、五厂动土。

ReadShift 双语翻译

## Capacity Demand Exceeded Supply Throughout the '90s

Looking back now, TSMC's three cornerstones—manufacturing excellence, customer trust, and technology leadership—the first two were already laid in the 1990s. The third, technology leadership, also began taking shape in the late 1990s. In this chapter, I want to discuss how TSMC laid the foundation of "customer trust" in the 1990s.

TSMC Fab 1 was a rather small facility, but it took two years after opening before there were enough orders to fill it. Fab 2 was completed in 1989 and began volume production in 1990. Although it didn't reach full capacity quickly, customers gave us optimistic demand projections after the fab was completed, which made us optimistic too. Sure enough, in 1992 their actual demand even exceeded what they had originally considered optimistic forecasts. Meanwhile, new fabless IC design companies were springing up and becoming our customers. These were exciting times! We immediately decided to build Fab 3, which was completed in 1995.

In fact, except for 1996, 1997, and 1998—three years of global semiconductor downturn when TSMC revenue grew at more modest rates of 36%, 18%, and 15%—throughout the 1990s TSMC was in a state of insufficient capacity and demand exceeding supply. Under these circumstances, customers' most urgent request was for us to boldly build new fabs and aggressively expand capacity. This we did. When Fab 3 was completed in 1995, we immediately broke ground for Fabs 4 and 5.

台南科学园区

一九九六年国科会宣布建立台南科学园区。这是政府对科技业的重要德政。台积电是最早加入的公司之一。我在九七年接受《中国时报》专访时表示：

"十年前我在台湾成立台积电时，当时我看到一个趋势，许多小型的集成电路设计公司即将成立，但晶圆制造工厂是一种资金非常大的投资。这些设计公司多半没有太多资本用来兴建自己的制造工厂，我相信这就是专业晶圆制造工厂生存的空间。

现在，我又看到第二波正在形成，也是南科制造中心的基本出发点。这个新的趋势是，目前即使大的集成电路公司也不见得有能力或意愿兴建自己的晶圆制造工厂。但对台积电这种专业晶圆制造工厂来说，我们的客户不只一家，当某一种半导体产品不景气时，我们可以为其他半导体客户服务，这是'专业集成电路制造服务工厂的优势。"

一九九七年四月，我宣布台积电将在未来十年在南科投资四千亿元，并将提供五千个以上就业机会。当时台塑集团王永庆董事长讥我的投资计画为"膨风"。王先生错了，此后十年台积电在南科投资六千余亿元，提供就业机会七千个。

ReadShift 双语翻译

In 1996, the National Science Council announced the establishment of Tainan Science Park. This was an important government benefaction to the technology industry. TSMC was one of the earliest companies to join. In a 1997 exclusive interview with the China Times, I stated:

"Ten years ago when I established TSMC in Taiwan, I saw a trend at that time: many small IC design companies were about to be established, but wafer manufacturing fabs require very large capital investments. Most of these design companies didn't have much capital to build their own manufacturing fabs. I believed this was the survival space for professional wafer manufacturing fabs.

Now, I see a second wave forming, which is also the fundamental starting point of the Tainan Science Park manufacturing center. This new trend is: currently, even large IC companies may not have the capability or willingness to build their own wafer fabs. But for a professional wafer manufacturing fab like TSMC, we have more than one customer. When a certain semiconductor product is in a downturn, we can serve other semiconductor customers. This is the advantage of a 'professional IC manufacturing services fab.'"

In April 1997, I announced that TSMC would invest NT$400 billion in Tainan Science Park over the next ten years, creating over 5,000 jobs. At that time, Formosa Plastics Chairman Wang Yung-ching mocked my investment plan as "puffery." Mr. Wang was wrong—over the next ten years, TSMC invested over NT$600 billion in Tainan Science Park, creating 7,000 jobs.

WaferTech的教训

一九九零到一九九五年当中，台积电营收的平均年成长率超过67%。一九九五年营收接近十一亿美元，客户唯一的抱怨是我们产能不足。我和总经理布鲁克自信心最高之时，感觉即看我们台湾厂48%的营业净利率，只要给我们的厂的获利率应该不会太差。恰巧九五年时，新竹园区已没有土地可给我们，台南科学园区又还没有成立。我与布鲁克就在这阴错阳差之际，决定与Altera、亚德诺半导体（Analog Devices, Inc., ADI）、ISSI（矽成）这三个客户合资在美国华盛顿州卡马斯（Camas）建设一座八吋晶圆厂，并命名为WaferTech。

我们雇了史密斯（Kenneth G. Smith）为总经理。他以他的资历，应该可以胜任这个新厂总经理职。同时，我们在卡马斯买了四倍立即需要的土地，以备以后扩充，随后于九六年七月开始动土兴建八吋晶圆厂。

雇了总经理，动土后的五年间WaferTech连续不断地给我"惊奇"。这惊奇分两类：

第一类是"成本"的惊奇。一言以蔽之："什么都比原先估计的贵。"在台积电九五年已有很专业的成本估计单位，但是这个单位的专长是估算台湾的成本，对美国成本估算外行。在九六至二零零零年五年中，工厂及洁净室建筑等远超过预算，接着是制造设备、薪酬、甚至办公室用具等等，都超出原来预算。

第二类更令我沮丧的是"人事"的惊奇。WaferTech是我和布鲁克的共同决定，我们征询新竹的营运团队，所以在我们宣布要在美国设厂时，新竹的营运团队就有反弹。我更大的惊奇来自美国方面。雇史密斯不久後，我就发现他不太尊重台积电的制造技术，也不太尊重台积电的既有成就。至于台积电的经理人，除了布鲁克和我外，他一个都不服。

ReadShift 双语翻译

From 1990 to 1995, TSMC's average annual revenue growth exceeded 67%. In 1995, revenue approached $1.1 billion, and customers' only complaint was our insufficient capacity. At the peak of confidence for me and General Manager Brook, looking at our Taiwan fabs' 48% operating margin, we assumed a U.S. fab's profitability wouldn't be too bad. As it happened, by 1995 there was no more land available in Hsinchu Science Park, and Tainan Science Park had not yet been established. Brook and I, by this twist of fate, decided to form a joint venture with three customers—Altera, Analog Devices, ISSI—to build an 8-inch fab in Camas, Washington, U.S.A., named WaferTech.

We hired Kenneth G. Smith as general manager, qualified by the role. At the same time, we purchased four times the immediately needed land in Camas for future expansion, then broke ground in July 1996 to build the 8-inch fab.

After hiring the general manager and breaking ground, WaferTech continuously gave me "surprises" over the next five years. These surprises fell into two categories:

The first category was "cost" surprises. In short: "Everything was much more expensive than originally estimated." Although TSMC already had a highly specialized cost estimation unit in 1995, their expertise was estimating Taiwan costs—they were laymen at U.S. cost estimation. During the five years 1996-2000, first factory and cleanroom construction far exceeded budget, then manufacturing equipment, salaries, even office supplies—everything exceeded the original budget.

The second category, which frustrated me even more, was "people" surprises. WaferTech was a joint decision by Brook and me; we hadn't consulted the Hsinchu operations team. So when we announced building a fab in the U.S., the Hsinchu operations team had significant pushback. My bigger surprise came from the American side. Not long after hiring Smith, I discovered he didn't much respect TSMC's manufacturing technology, nor TSMC's existing accomplishments. As for TSMC managers, heBrook and I, he was unconvinced by any of them.

收拾残局

WaferTech自九八年开始量产後，亏损加剧，又与新和总部不和。到了二零零零年，已成为台积电的烂摊子，需要行动了。

我的第一步行动是买回合资伙伴的股份，而且让他们稍赚一点。在买回时，合资夥伴已因为WaferTech的亏损正在担心他们的投资。我让他们在获利条件下出脱这投资，他们都很高兴。本来以合资方式成立WaferTech的目的，也就是要巩固我们与客户的关系。现在WaferTech虽没有成功，客户关系还是巩固了。

第二步是解雇史密斯。新竹和WaferTech不能合作，人事不和是主要原因。第三步是派台积电营运资深副总左大川出任WaferTech总经理，并直接对台积电总经理曾繁城负责。此后数年，新竹派了不少工程师和经理人员到WaferTech协助。

左大川在WaferTech待了几乎四年，WaferTech营运渐趋稳定。"稳定"的意义是：在同样的产品、同样的售价上，WaferTech的毛利率大约比台湾厂的毛利率低20至25个百分点。通常台湾厂的毛利率是45%，WaferTech的毛利率是20%至25%，但是WaferTech的营业净利还是正的。既然还有正的营业净利，我们决定把它维持下去，但是我们不扩充了。直至今日，WaferTech仍是台积电的一部分。

SSMC新加坡合资

九七中期，飞利浦忽然对我要求合资在新加坡建SSMC。这是飞利浦内部已规画有些时日的方案，飞利浦已得到新加坡政府经济发展局（EDB）同意，亦为合资夥伴。根据飞利浦的建议，最后的结局会是台积电出资39%，飞利浦61%。总经理由飞利浦指派，营运副总由台积电指派。八吋技术由台积电供应。

我听了这建议立刻的反应是：飞利浦又想讨我们便宜。我婉拒了。但是飞利浦名在此之後两次台积电董人代表重复提此建议，对我施加高度压力。

从"政治"层面看，飞利浦在九七年仍拥有台积电28.2%股权，占十席董事的四席；如果因为他们真的因为这件事而与我作对，倒也是一件麻烦事。从正面看，我很欣赏新加坡的生产力，接受飞利浦的建议可以当作台积电在费最小力气下，增加一个小工厂。至于台积电对SSMC的技术移转？八技术发展已近尾声。

在考虑各种得失後，我决定接受飞利浦的SSMC合资建议。SSMC在九九年动土，二零零零年开始量产。後来成绩颇佳。

ReadShift 双语翻译

After WaferTech started Volume production in 1998, losses intensified and discord with Hsinchu headquarters continued. By 2000, WaferTech had become TSMC's mess that needed action.

My first move was to buy out the joint venture partners' shares, letting them earn a small profit. At the time of buyout, the joint venture partners were already worried about their investment due to WaferTech's losses. I let them exit the investment under profitable conditions, and they were all happy. The original purpose of forming WaferTech as a joint venture was precisely to strengthen relationships with customers. Now although WaferTech hadn't succeeded, customer relationships were strengthened.

The second move was firing Smith. The inability of Hsinchu and WaferTech to cooperate—personnel discord was the main reason. The third move was dispatching TSMC Senior VP of Operations Zuo Dachuan as WaferTech general manager, reporting directly to TSMC General Manager Zeng Fan-cheng. In the following years, Hsinchu sent many engineers and managers to assist WaferTech.

Zuo Dachuan stayed at WaferTech for almost four years, and WaferTech's operations gradually stabilized. "Stable" meant: with the same products and the same selling prices, WaferTech's gross margin was about 20-25 percentage points lower than Taiwan fabs'. Typically Taiwan fabs had gross margins of 45%, while WaferTech's was 20-25%, but WaferTech's net operating profit was still positive. Since there was still positive net operating profit, we decided to keep it running, but we wouldn't expand it. To this day, WaferTech remains part of TSMC.

### SSMC Singapore Joint Venture

In mid-1997, Philips suddenly asked me to form a joint venture to build SSMC in Singapore. This was a plan Philips had already been developing for some time. Philips had obtained the agreement of Singapore's Economic Development Board (EDB) to also be a joint venture partner. Per Philips' proposal, the final arrangement would be TSMC contributing 39%, Philips 61%. The general manager would be assigned by Philips; the COO by TSMC. 8-inch technology would be supplied by TSMC.

My immediate reaction to this suggestion: Philips was trying to take advantage of us again. I declined. But Philips pursued it tenaciously; twice after that, Chairman of the TSMC board repeated this proposal, putting high pressure on me.

From a "politics" perspective, Philips still owned 28.2% of TSMC in 1997 and held four of the ten board seats; if they really opposed me over this matter, it would be troublesome. On the positive side, I had long admired Singapore's productivity. Accepting Philips' proposal could be viewed as adding a small factory with minimal effort. As for TSMC's technology transfer to SSMC? 8-inch technology development was nearing its end.

After weighing the pros and cons, I decided to accept Philips' SSMC joint venture proposal. SSMC broke ground in 1999 and began Volume production in 2000. It performed quite well thereafter.

购并德碁及世大

一九九八年曾繁城刚自世界先进回台积电任总经理不久，公司事务又因为严重的"供不应求"而繁忙起来。九九年初的某一晚，繁城忽然说他要早点走，去"看看"德碁的工厂。如上章所述，德碁那时已因为德仪决定退出记忆体，而丧失了技术来源；在实际营运上，也已在严重亏损状态中。

在这晚繁城突然告诉我他要"看看"德碁前，我和他早已谈过购并德碁的可能，但德碁是一记忆体公司，把记忆体产能转成晶圆代工产能，要添加不少设备，费时又费钱，也不能立刻解决台积的产能问题，所以我们搁置了购并德碁之议。现在，客户的压力不断增加，繁城认为必须重新检讨购并德碁。

在这卖方不但想卖、甚至必须卖的情形下，只要买方肯出合理的价钱，谈判可以很快顺利结束。九十九年六月台积电与德碁签约：台积电先买德碁30%股权，并开始经营德碁为晶圆代工公司；如没有"惊奇"，台积在一年后购并全部德碁股权。签约後，我们立刻派陈健邦为德碁总经理。

我们与德碁的签约启动了另一家公司也要卖给我们的要求。那另一家公司是世大（世大积体电路股份有限公司）。它成立于一九九六年。创办人张汐京从前在建厂工作，并无经营半导体事业经验，但看到台积电的成功，也想成立一家晶圆代工公司。他找到了中华开发银行及其他几家台湾公司成为世大的大股东。

九九年底，正是我们最缺产能的时期，中华开发总经理胡定吾（亦为世大副董事长）抓对了时机，又制造了一个若有若无的竞对者（联对我们的开出高价。

当时我无意与胡定吾纠缠。我们的大方向都是对的；我们正全速驰向世界半导体业中自五零年代德仪、七零年代英特尔、八零年代三星以来最大的成功；我们不能因为要在所有细节上都不吃亏而降低我们的动能。

台积电在二零零零年初宣布购并世大案。当时飞利浦仍是拥有28.2%股权的台积电最大股东。我在与世大谈判时并未征询飞利浦意见，但在宣布当天打电话荷兰飞利浦总部做口头报告。飞利浦对我们要付的价钱表示高度震惊。我挂电话後想飞利浦的情绪要及早安抚，不然他们可能在董事会杯葛。遂在次日立刻派遣台积电总经理曾繁城、会计长何丽梅前去荷兰解释为甚件购并案是我们在赢取客户信任策略中必须做的事。此行颇成功。

世大购并案又掀起的波澜。我本来以为已结案的德碁购并案，现在因为我们宣布购并世大的价格高于原来议定的德碁价格，德碁股东聚会集体抗议，并要求德碁董事长施振荣重议购并价格。为了抚平他们，我们只得又调整德碁的购并价。

二零零零年七月，德碁和世大购并案正式生效。德碁和世大的招牌从此消失。德碁的晶圆厂变成台积电的七厂；世大的晶圆厂变成台积电的八厂。

ReadShift 双语翻译

In 1998, not long after Zeng Fan-cheng returned from Vanguard International to serve as TSMC general manager, the company was again swamped with business due to severe "demand exceeding supply." One evening in early 1999, Fan-cheng suddenly said he needed to leave early to "take a look at" Tepro's fab. As described in the previous chapter, Tepro had lost its technology source when TI decided to exit memory and was operating at a heavy loss.

Before the evening when Fan-cheng suddenly told me he wanted to "see" Tepro, he and I had already discussed the possibility of acquiring Tepro. But Tepro was a memory company; converting memory capacity to foundry capacity would require adding considerable equipment, costing time and money, and wouldn't immediately solve TSMC's capacity problems, so we had shelved the Tepro acquisition. Now, with mounting customer pressure, Fan-cheng believed we must revisit the Tepro acquisition.

When the seller not only wants to sell but must sell, negotiations can conclude quickly and smoothly as long as the buyer offers a reasonable price. In June 1999, TSMC signed an agreement with Tepro: TSMC first purchased 30% of Tepro's equity and began operating Tepro as a foundry company. If there were no "surprises," TSMC would acquire all Tepro equity a year later. After signing, we immediately assigned Chen Jianbang as Tepro's general manager.

Our signing with Tepro triggered another company wanting to sell to us as well. That other company was WSMC (WaferTech Semiconductor Corporation, actually 世大积体电路). It was established in 1996. Its founder Zhang Xijing had previously been in charge of fab construction at TI and had no experience running a semiconductor business, but seeing TSMC's success, also wanted to start a foundry company. He enlisted China Development Bank and several other Taiwanese companies as WSMC's major shareholders.

At year-end 1999, when we were most short of capacity, China Development General Manager Hu Dingwu (also WSMC's vice chairman) seized the right moment and, by manufacturing a potential competitor (UMC), set a high price for us.

At the time, I had no intention of tangling with Hu Dingwu. Our general direction was right; we were at full throttle toward the biggest success in the global semiconductor world since TI in the '50s, Intel in the '70s, and Samsung in the '80s. We couldn't sacrifice our momentum just to avoid losing on every detail.

In early 2000, TSMC announced the WSMC acquisition. At that time, Philips was still TSMC's largest shareholder with 28.2% equity. I hadn't consulted Philips during WSMC negotiations, but on the day of the announcement, I called Philips Netherlands headquarters to give a verbal report. Philips expressed high shock at the price we were going to pay. After hanging up, I thought Philips' emotions needed to be calmed soon, otherwise they might filibuster in the board meeting. The next day, I immediately dispatched TSMC General Manager Zeng Fan-cheng and CFO He Limei to the Netherlands to explain why this acquisition was a must-do in our strategy of winning customer trust. This trip was quite successful.

The WSMC acquisition stirred up another ripple. Our already-concluded TSMC acquisition was now jeopardized because we announced a WSMC purchase price higher than the originally agreed Tepro price. Tepro shareholders gathered to collectively protest and demanded that Tepro Chairman Shi Zhengrong renegotiate the acquisition price. To appease them, we had to adjust Tepro's acquisition price upward.

In July 2000, the Tepro and WSMC acquisitions formally took effect. The Tepro and WSMC brands disappeared from then on. Tepro's fabs became TSMC's Fab 7; WSMC's fabs became TSMC's Fab 8.

麦肯锡顾问公司的发现

一九九六年，总经理布鲁克与我有一个关于公司组织的争执。台积电自成立后，一直都是"功能式"组织，即：营运（制造）部、研发部、市场行销部……等。布鲁克认为应采取德仪形式"业务单位"组织。我则相当坚决认为"业务单位"组织不适用于台积电。布鲁克不服，要找国际级顾问公司的意见。

麦肯锡花了两、三个月时间，先在内部了解我们的业务後，再与我们的十几个主要客户谈。结论是完全同意我的看法："业务单位"组织不适于台积电，还是继续"功能式"组织较好。

麦肯锡的结论解决了我和布鲁克在组织上的争执，但正如一般国际级顾问公司的做法：回答你给他的问题後，他会发现一个新问题，让他再为你效劳。这次，麦肯锡说："在我们与你们的客户讨论你们组织问题时，我们发现你们客户与你们的关系不是很好。"

这样的说辞，当然引起我的高度注意。十几年来，争取客户信任一直是我们主要目标之一，怎会关系不好？麦肯锡说他无法做详细的回答，但推荐另一家专做客户满意度调查的顾问公司。

自一九九七年起，我们就雇这家顾问公司，每年为我们做客户满意度调查。每年调查报告总是厚厚的一本，包括了所有我们为客户服务的项目：产能足够否？反应度够快否？价格合理否？交货如期否？……等等。作为第三者，这家顾问公司较我们自己更会听到客户的真话。每年我都亲自聆听顾问公司的报告，并主持报告後的检讨会议。每年总有许许多多大小的改进项目，我与高阶主管指定需要改进的单位。

这套制度——每年专业性找出客户不满意处、认明需要采取改进行动的单位、追踪改进——的确增强客户对我们的信任。自一九九七年起，我们年年都做，到我退休，已做了二十一年矣。

ReadShift 双语翻译

In 1996, General Manager Brook and I had a dispute about company organization. Since its founding, TSMC had always used a "functional" organization: Operations (Manufacturing) Department, R&D Department, Marketing Department, etc. Brook believed we should adopt TI's "business unit" organization. I was quite adamant that "business unit" organization was not suitable for TSMC. Brook disagreed and wanted the opinion of an international consulting firm.

McKinsey spent two to three months first understanding our business internally, then talking to a dozen or so of our major customers. The conclusion completely agreed with my view: "business unit" organization was not suitable for TSMC; continuing with the "functional" organization was better.

McKinsey's conclusion resolved the organizational dispute between Brook and me. But as is common among international consulting firms: after answering the question you gave them, they discover a new problem to be of further service. This time, McKinsey said: "While discussing your organizational issues with your customers, we found that your customer relationships were not that great."

Such a statement naturally drew my high attention. For over a decade, winning customer trust had been one of our primary objectives—how could the relationships be not good? McKinsey said they couldn't provide a detailed answer but recommended another consulting firm specializing in customer satisfaction surveys.

From 1997 onward, we hired this firm to conduct annual customer satisfaction surveys for us. Each annual report was a thick volume covering all aspects of our customer service: Is capacity sufficient? Is responsiveness fast enough? Are prices reasonable? Is delivery on time? . . . and more. As a third party, this consulting firm could hear customers' true feelings better than we could ourselves. Every year I personally listened to the consulting firm's report and chaired the post-report review meeting. Every year there were numerous improvement projects of various sizes, and I and senior management assigned the units needing improvement.

This entire system—professionally identifying customer dissatisfaction annually, designating units to take improvement action, tracking improvements—indeed strengthened customer trust in us. We did this every year from 1997 through my retirement, for 21 years in total.

一九九九年九二一大地震迅速恢复

一九九九年九月二十一日凌晨一时余，我在台北寓所睡梦中被地震惊醒，直觉认为楼下较安全，狼狈下楼，在楼梯中间遇到第二震，比第一震更厉害。拼命抓扶手时，听见楼上楼下啪啦啪啦东西掉在地板上的声音，真的以为这是末日了。但是过了一会，倒又不震了——这还不是末日。

二十一日上午我得知凌晨的地震强度达芮氏规模7.3，是台湾百年来最强地震。我也接到初步报告：（1）台积电和世界先进两家公司的人员都安全；（2）地震後两家公司的每个工厂都有许多该厂员工立刻回工厂看他们能做什么。听到这点，我非常感动。曾经在德仪长达二十五年的我，觉得德仪的工程师和经理人员，在同样情形下，不会这么热心；（3）全部工厂和办公室都断电，所以在停顿状态。

二十二日我到新竹，又有新的坏消息：美国纳斯达克（NASDAQ）股价大跌，原因是害怕台湾地震会使美国科技公司的半导体供应断链。此後几天我与同仁在没有电力、当然也没有冷气的闷热会议室商量对策。第一要解决的问题是恢复电力。

谢天谢地，二十四日我们获得近六成需求的稳定电力，二十七日五成生产设备恢复正常运作并逐步出货，三十日九成以上产能恢复正常。纳斯达克股市也很快涨回。

九二一芮氏规模7.3的大地震，起先引起客户的大恐慌。但是，我们在两星期内几乎完全复原，客户对我们的信任增加不少。政府的高效率恢复供电固然是重要因素，但同样重要的是全体同仁对危机的反应：各就其位，不辞辛劳，镇定应付。

ReadShift 双语翻译

At around 1 a.m. on September 21, 1999, I was jolted awake by an earthquake in my Taipei residence. My instinct told me the ground floor was safer. I hurried downstairs in disarray, and midway down the stairs encountered the second aftershock—even stronger than the first. Clutching the railing for dear life, I heard things crashing to the floor from upstairs and downstairs—I truly thought it was doomsday. But after a while, the shaking stopped—it wasn't doomsday after all.

On the morning of the 21st I learned the overnight earthquake measured 7.3 on the Richter scale—the strongest in Taiwan in a hundred years. I also received initial reports: (1) All employees of TSMC and Vanguard were safe. (2) After the earthquake, many employees at each fab of both companies immediately returned their fabs to see what they could do. Hearing this, I was deeply moved. Having spent 25 years at TI, I felt TI's engineers and managers wouldn't have been so enthusiastic under the same circumstances. (3) All factories and offices had lost power, so operations were at a standstill.

On the 22nd I went to Hsinchu, where there was new bad news: U.S. NASDAQ stock prices had fallen sharply, for fear that the Taiwan earthquake would disrupt semiconductor supply to American Tech companies. Over the following days, my colleagues and I met in meeting rooms without electricity—and of course without air conditioning—to discuss countermeasures. The first priority was restoring power.

Thank God, on the 24th we obtained stable power meeting nearly 60% of demand; on the 27th, 50% of production equipment resumed normal operation and we gradually began shipping; by the 30th, over 90% of capacity was back to normal. NASDAQ stock prices also bounced back quickly.

The 921 earthquake, magnitude 7.3 on the Richter scale, initially caused great panic among customers. But we recovered almost completely within two weeks, and customer trust in us increased considerably. The government's efficient power restoration was certainly an important factor, but equally important was all colleagues' response to the crisis: everyone in their positions, tirelessly and calmly handling the situation.

客户"实质上的"晶圆厂

我在德仪的经验告诉自己：自己拥有晶圆厂的IDM公司，其设计部门与晶圆制造部门因互不隶属，常常各玩"公司政治"，争风吃醋，鲜少合作。倒是台积电，作为纯粹晶圆制造公司，可以与IDM客户的设计部门合作无间。当然，无晶圆厂的设计公司更是我们真诚合作的客户暨夥伴。

在九零年代中期，我们对所有客户进一步宣示要成为大家"实质上的"晶圆厂（Virtual Fab）。既然是"实质上的"晶圆厂，那么与客户，尤其客户的设计部门应该沟通无碍。就在九零年代中后期，我对重要客户以及公司内部提倡与客户"多层面"沟通。所谓"多层面"沟通，就是除了我及行销部门外，我亦鼓励客户的设计部门与台积电为他们晶圆的部门沟通。

虽然我们自九零年代中期就有一百家以上客户，二零零零年後更有数百家客户，但在每一时期，最大的十五至二十家客户总是占台积电营收80%。我在九七年自兼总经理後，就把熟悉这十五至二十家大客户的CEO当作是我的重要责任。他们几乎都在美国与台湾，大部分密集在加州。我每年访问每位CEO至少一、两次，他们也常来台湾访问他们"实质上的"晶圆厂。尽管如，我自一九九七年自兼台积电总经理至二零一八年退休的二十年中，虽常与这些大客户的CEO会面，但与"老朋友"叙旧的场面却不多见。因不只大客户常常变，大客户的CEO也常变。我自定的与他们"熟悉"的标准是：假设有事，双方随时打电话给对方，而对方一定会接。

至于"多层面"沟通，大部分在有问题时发生，但有时也在制程研发阶段发生。总之，客户工程师与我们工程师的直接沟通，省了许多第三者代言的误会，也增强不少互信。

ReadShift 双语翻译

My experience at TI told me: IDM companies that own their own fabs often have their design and wafer manufacturing departments playing "company politics" and jealous of each other because the departments belong to different chains of command—they rarely cooperate. TSMC, as a pure wafer manufacturing company, could cooperate seamlessly with IDM customers' design departments. Of course, fabless design companies were even more so our genuinely cooperative customers and partners.

In the mid-'90s, we further declared to all customers that we wanted to be their "virtual fab." Since we were a "virtual fab," we should be able to communicate with customers, especially their design departments, without barriers. Around the mid-to-late '90s, I began advocating "multi-level" communication with key customers and internally.

Although we had over a hundred customers by the mid-'90s and several hundred after 2000, in each period the top 15-20 customers always accounted for 80% of TSMC revenue. After I took over as my own general manager in 1997, I made it an important responsibility to become familiar with the CEOs of these 15-20 major customers. They were almost all in the U.S. and Taiwan, mostly concentrated in California. I visited each CEO at least once or twice a year, and they also often visited Taiwan to see their "virtual fab." Nevertheless, during the twenty years from 1997, when I was TSMC general manager, until my retirement in 2018, although I often met with these major customers' CEOs, opportunities to "catch up with old friends" were rare. Because not only did major customers change often, but major customers' CEOs also changed frequently. My own standard for being "familiar" with them was: if something came up, both parties could call the other at any time, and the other party would definitely answer.

Regarding "multi-level" communication, it mostly occurred when there were manufacturing problems, but sometimes also during process R&D stages. In any case, direct communication between customer engineers and our engineers saved many misunderstandings caused by third-party intermediaries and built considerable mutual trust.

章节

台積電篇二第二十五章

张忠谋

台积电篇二·第二十五章｜作者及教授

作序与写自传

一九九五年初，友人虞有澄寄了一本他写的、但尚未出版的《我看英代爾》给我，并嘱我为他作序。我问他要他说：两千字左右吧。

我花了一整天的时间读《我看英代爾》，读後百感交集。一九九五年正是英代爾"如日中天"的年代。有澄很早就加入英代爾，所以他讲的英代爾故事的前一段正是我在德州仪器竭力与英代爾竞争的时候（见第九章）。当时胜负未分，但我离开德仪後，英代爾领先了。当年这段"德仪（TI）对英代爾（Intel）"的故事，无论是公司对公司对国家，在历史上不断出现，也带来不少可歌可泣的事迹。

我读了虞著《我看英代爾》後，又花了一整天时间为有澄写序。几十年来的中文"长篇"，写起来还算顺手。

想不到这篇序竟成了我成为作者的"进身阶"。虞书出版後几个月，天下文化创办人高希均教授就来看我，劝我写自传。其实我认识高教授已有好几年，但他大概一直以为我一身洋气，不可能写中文，直到看了我爲虞写的序後，才决定"试"一下。我贸然答应了。

接下来是几乎两年的前熬。回忆是享受，动笔却是煎熬。但那时我只六十几岁，体力旺盛，有时感情来了，边写边泣，可以写到深夜二、三时，第二天照样上班。终于在九七年年底，《张忠谋自传：上册——一九三一一一九六四》完成。九八年三月出版。

书发表会里，有人问高希均创办人，对我的"中文打几分"？高教授耸从他的肩膀，不经意地说："七十分左右。"

虽然高教授只打七十分，"自传上册"倒很受欢迎。它是二十几年来台湾最畅销书之一，直至今日，我还不时地拿两、三万元的版税。美国文豪海明威对想做作家青年的忠告："简单的字句，真实的感情"，似乎很有道理。

## Writing a Foreword and Writing an Autobiography

In early 1995, my friend You Yicheng sent me a pre-publication copy of his book "My View of Intel" and asked me to write a foreword. I asked him how long it should be. He said: "About two thousand words."

I spent an entire day reading "My View of Intel," and after reading it, a hundred feelings welled up. 1995 was the heyday of Intel. You Yicheng had joined Intel very early, so the earlier part of the Intel story he told was precisely the time when I was fiercely competing with Intel at Texas Instruments (see Chapter 9). At that time, the winner had not yet been decided, but after I left TI, Intel took the lead. This backthen story of "TI vs. Intel," whether company-to-country or country-to-country, has appeared repeatedly in history and given rise to many epic and moving stories.

After reading You's "My View of Intel," I spent another entire day writing the foreword for him. It was a rare "long" Chinese piece for me in decades, but it flowed smoothly enough.

I never expected this foreword would become my "stepping stone" to becoming an author. A few months after You's book was published, Mr. Commonwealth Publishing founder Professor Kao Hsi-chun came to see me and urged me to write an autobiography. Actually, I had known Professor Kao for several years, but he probably always thought I was too "Westernized" to write in Chinese. Only after reading the foreword I wrote for You did he decide to "test" me. I rashly agreed.

What followed was nearly two years of suffering. Reminiscing was enjoyable, but the actual writing was torment. But at that time I was only in my early sixties, with abundant energy. Sometimes when emotions came over me, I would write through tears until 2 or 3 in the morning, then go to work as usual the next day. Finally, at the end of 1997, "The Autobiography of Morris Chang: Volume 1—1931-1964" was completed. It was published in March 1998.

At the book launch, someone asked founder Professor Kao what "score" he would give my Chinese. Professor Kao shrugged his shoulders nonchalantly and said: "About 70 points."

Although Professor Kao only gave it 70 points, "Autobiography Volume 1" turned out to be very popular. It was one of Taiwan's best-selling books for over 20 years. To this day, I still occasionally receive twenty to thirty thousand NT dollars in royalties. The American literary giant Ernest Hemingway's advice to aspiring writers—"simple words, true feelings"—seems to make a lot of sense.

对台积电内部讲授"经营"

九六、九七年，公司规横渐大，中阶管理人员中已出现不少我不认识的面孔，我想：应该趁这时机对中、高级经理做一系列的"经营台积电"讲授；现在讲，可能十分之二、三听课的人还会注意听，甚至传授给他们的手下；现在不讲，将来公司更大，没有机会了。

于是我开课了，每星期一小时。所有高、中阶的主管都被邀请参加，共七、八十人。我很喜欢教书，但又不喜欢准备。每次上课，我都有一个题目，然後以自然会话方式讲这题目。黑板或白板是我唯一工具。有时我的教材缺乏整理和次序，但我认为一个好学生应该在自己脑子中做这整理，这样他才更有收获。

这样的讲授，大约也举行了二、三十次吧。有收获吗？有。但恐怕不在经营技术上。毕竟台积电的组织是"功能型"的——研发部、制造部……等等。各部的经营都相当专业，而我的讲授却是"一般性"的——价值、愿景、策略……等等。最大的收获是：我们在这快速成长的关键年头，把台积电的价值观，也是我们的"经营理念"落实了。

在台积电三十一年，我和公司同仁都犯了不少错误，但绝少触犯这十条"经营理念"；在极少数触犯的案例上，我们都施予严厉的惩处。

ReadShift 双语翻译

In 1996-97, the company was growing rapidly, and among middle-level managers there were already many faces I didn't recognize. I thought: I should take this opportunity to give a series of "Managing TSMC" lectures to middle and senior managers. If I lectured now, perhaps 20-30% of the audience would still pay attention and even pass it on to their subordinates. If I didn't lecture now, when the company got even bigger, there would be no opportunity.

So I started the class, one hour every week. All senior and middle-level managers were invited, totaling 70-80 people. I very much enjoyed teaching, but disliked preparation. Each class I had a topic, which I would discuss in a natural conversational manner. The blackboard or whiteboard was my only tool. Sometimes my material lacked organization and order, but I believed a good student should do this organization in his own mind—that way he would gain more.

This kind of lecturing was held perhaps twenty to thirty times. Was there gain? Yes. But probably not in management technique. After all, TSMC's organization was "functional"—R&D Department, Manufacturing Department, etc. Each department's operations were quite professional, while my lectures were "general"—values, vision, strategy, etc. The biggest gain was: during this critical year of rapid growth, we instilled TSMC's values—our "business philosophy."

During my 31 years at TSMC, my colleagues and I made many mistakes, but we rarely violated these ten "business philosophies." In the rare cases where they were violated, we imposed severe punishment.

当交大"荣誉管理讲座"教授

我在台积电内部讲授"经营"的消息，很快地传到同在新竹的交通大学。张俊彦校长及管理科学系朱博涌教授都很热心要我开一门有学分的课，朱教授还自愿做我的"助教"。"经营管理专题"课就在九八年秋季学期出现。大约有一百位学生报名，其中一大半是EMBA学生，一小半是管理科学系大学生或别的学系学生，还有几位旁听生。每星期一堂课，每堂课两小时，当中休息几分钟。我一共教了十二堂，还有两堂考试——考试都由朱教授负责，打分也由他负责。我只负责讲十二堂。

这十二堂的题目是：（一）企业愿景；（二）企业文化；（三）组织结构与计；（四）决策与授权；（五）功能性组织；（六）沟通；（七）激励；（八）绩效评估；（九）学习曲线与市场占有率；（十）策略与年度规画；（十一）开会；（十二）世界级企业。

这十二堂课包含了我所有经营经验及心得，从德仪到通用到工研院到台积电。当然，许多经验和心得是负面的，但我认为负面的教训往往比正面的经验更铭心刻骨。知道不做什麼与知道做什麼一样重要。

在我开始这门课时，我对我的约一百位学生说："假如十年後，有十位学生觉得我在此讲的对他有一点用处，对我这已是很好的回馈。"

如今二十余年过去，我还未遇见任何人对我说："啊，我是你当年的交大学生。"更没有人对我说："啊，你当年讲的对我很有用。"事实上，想想我自己，不要讲小学了，从初中到博士班，我也有过一百位以上老师，其中好几位影响我後来的人生。我曾经告诉过他们吗？没有。大部分在课程结束後，就变成陌生人了。

ReadShift 双语翻译

News of my internal "management" lectures at TSMC quickly spread to nearby National Chiao Tung University (NCTU) in Hsinchu. President Zhang Junyan and Professor Zhu Boyong of the Department of Management Science were very enthusiastic about having me teach a for-credit course. Professor Zhu even volunteered to be my "teaching assistant." The "Special Topics in Business Management" course appeared in the fall semester of 1998. About a hundred students enrolled, of whom more than half were EMBA students, less than half were undergraduate students from the Department of Management Science or other departments, and a few were auditors. One class per week, two hours per class, with a short break in between. I taught twelve sessions total, plus two exams—both exams were administered and graded by Professor Zhu. I was only responsible for the twelve lectures.

The twelve session topics were: (1) Corporate Vision; (2) Corporate Culture; (3) Organizational Structure and Design; (4) Decision Making and Delegation; (5) Functional Organization; (6) Communication; (7) Motivation; (8) Performance Appraisal; (9) Learning Curve and Market Share; (10) Strategy and Annual Planning; (11) Meetings; (12) World-Class Enterprise.

These twelve sessions contained all my management experience and insights, from TI to GE to ITRI to TSMC. Of course, much of the experience and many insights were negative, but I believe negative lessons are often more indelibly memorable than positive experiences. Knowing what not to do is as important as knowing what to do.

When I started this course, I told my approximately 100 students: "If, ten years from now, ten students feel that what I taught here was of some use to them, that would already be a great reward for me."

Now more than twenty years have passed, and I have still not met anyone who said to me: "Ah, I was your student at NCTU." Still less has anyone said: "Ah, what you taught back then was very useful to me." In fact, thinking about myself—not to mention elementary school—from middle school through Ph.D. programs, I too had over a hundred teachers, several of whom influenced my later life. Did I ever tell them? No. Most became strangers after the course ended.

後记

後记：补充一段在此章之初，我写到当年这段"现存强权（德仪）对新兴挑战者（英代爾）"的故事时，所感受到的强烈讽刺意味：四、五十年後的英代爾，这个几十年半导体霸主，正在面对新兴的台积电。虽然鹿死谁手尚未可测，但台积电占有优势却是明显的事实，只要台积电不自踩自己脚，应该胜算在握。难道这是我的"复仇记"吗？我没有这个意思。反正上次英代爾领先时，我已离开德仪；这次尽管我情系台积电，但无论谁得胜，我也已经退休多时了。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Epilogue: A supplementary note. Earlier in this chapter, when I wrote about the irony of the "established power (TI) vs. emerging challenger (Intel)" story from those days: forty or fifty years later, Intel, the semiconductor hegemon for decades, is now facing an emerging TSMC. Although it is still uncertain who will prevail, TSMC holds a clear advantage—as long as TSMC doesn't shoot itself in the foot, victory should be within grasp. Is this my "revenge story"? I have no such intention. After all, when Intel took the lead last time, I had already left TI. This time, although my heart is with TSMC, whoever wins, I retired long ago.

ReadShift 双语翻译
