台积电篇三·第三十二章｜老骥伏枥，志在千里

二○○九年六月，在「假淘汰、真裁员」风波平息后，我重新兼任台积电CEO。那一年我七十八岁。许多人问我：为什么还要回来？我的回答是：台积电正面临关键时刻，四十纳米良率问题未解、客户关系紧张、内部士气低落——这些都需要有人出来承担。

「老骥伏枥，志在千里」——这句曹操的诗，正是我当时心境的最佳写照。

ReadShift 双语翻译

In June 2009, after the 'fake elimination, real layoffs' controversy had subsided, I resumed the CEO role at TSMC. I was seventy-eight years old. Many people asked me why I had come back. My answer was that TSMC was facing a critical moment: the forty-nanometer yield problem remained unsolved, customer relations were strained, and internal morale was low—all of which required someone to step up.

'The old steed in the stable still dreams of galloping a thousand li'—that line from Cao Cao's poetry was the perfect expression of my state of mind at the time.

解决四十纳米良率问题（二○○九年）

就在我重返CEO职前的几个月，台积电的最新节点技术——四十纳米——已开始量产，但并不顺利：良率过低，且有品质问题。我似乎又回到了一九六八年的德仪（见第六章），但四十一年前的经验也给了二○○九年的我可用的教训。

二○○九年的我已远离生产技术的细节，所以绝不一九六八年我的上司彪希所为——「帮忙」远过于「帮忙」。我把信心寄托在生产团队主管秦永沛副总上，从不参加他的技术会议，只是随时都抽出时间听取他主动给我的报告。

我还做了一件「公关」事。在我重返CEO职的二○○九年六月时，台积电的「四十纳米生产问题」已广为投资人所知。二○○九年七月底，在我返任CEO后的第一次「法人说明会」上，财务长做了每季的例行报告后，我站起来宣布：

「大家都很关心四十纳米的生产问题，我们也很努力要解决这问题。现在我想请负责营运的资深副总刘德音博士报告生产线现状——但他在生产线工作太忙，不能亲自来此，所以我们以网络直播联机方式，请他做此报告。」接着，会场的屏幕上出现德音穿着白色实验室长袍，站在洁净室门前，开始做他的专业性报告。我看一百多听众的脸色：又惊异又感动。我想：这是一个吉兆。

果然，几个月后，四十纳米良率问题解决，一切回归正常。我对刘德音、秦永沛以及他们生产团队的信心没有白费。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Several months before I resumed the CEO post, TSMC's newest node technology—forty nanometers—had begun mass production, but not smoothly: yield was too low, and there were quality issues. I seemed to have returned to TI in 1968 (see Chapter 6), but the experience from forty-one years earlier also provided lessons I could apply in 2009.

In 2009, I was far removed from the details of production technology, so I would never repeat what my boss Bush did in 1968—'helping' far beyond what was helpful. I placed my confidence in Vice President Yong-pei Chin, who led the production team, and never attended his technical meetings; I simply made time whenever he主动 brought me reports.

I also did something of a 'public relations' nature. By June 2009, when I resumed the CEO role, TSMC's 'forty-nanometer production problem' was well known to investors. In late July 2009, at the first investor conference after my return, after the CFO had delivered the quarterly report, I stood up and announced:

'Everyone is concerned about the forty-nanometer production problem, and we are working hard to resolve it. I would now like to ask Dr. Aric Liu, senior vice president in charge of operations, to report on the production line status—but he is too busy on the production floor to come here in person, so we will connect via live video.'

Next, Dr. Liu appeared on the screen at the venue, wearing a white lab coat and standing before the cleanroom door, beginning his technical report. I watched the expressions of the more than one hundred listeners: a mixture of surprise and being moved. I thought: this was a favorable omen.

As it turned out, a few months later, the forty-nanometer yield problem was resolved and everything returned to normal. My confidence in Aric Liu, Yong-pei Chin, and their production team was not misplaced.

解决与辉达的悬案（二○○九年七月）

辉达是台积电四十纳米节点技术的主要伙伴及客户。台积电在四十纳米初期的生产问题使辉达遭受了严重损失。辉达在我返任CEO一年前就开始与台积电争议，但一直没有结论。

我返任CEO后的头几天，几乎全部时间都在电话上告诉重要客户我返任的消息。在与辉达CEO黄仁勋（Jensen Huang）通话时，他也特别提醒我们两家公司之间的悬案，并要求尽速解决。

此后三星期，我花了几十小时与公司内有关同仁深入探讨此案。二○○九年七月初，我认为我已清楚了解此事并且有解决方案，我电邮Jensen：「我下星期来硅谷，拟于七月十五日下午六点半到你家吃沙拉和披萨。」那时我和Jensen已是十几年的老友，也常去他家吃沙拉和披萨。但这次他接到我的电邮著急了——我们两家公司间有这么严重的争论，怎么我只管吃沙拉和披萨？他回电邮说：「那么，我们什么时候谈正事？」我立刻回复：「六点半到你家，先和你全家吃披萨，八点整我和你到你的书房谈生意。」七月十五日我准时到Jensen家，与他全家有一个简单而愉快的披萨晚餐。八点整，我对Jensen说：「我们去你书房吧。」进书房后我们关起门来开始严肃的谈话。我提出我与台积电同仁研究了三星期的和解建议——上亿美元的赔偿金，并且强调：这建议是我们唯一的建议，它的有效期是四十八小时，如你在四十八小时内仍不同意，我们只得找仲裁人了。

Jensen在两天内同意了。直到现在辉达仍是台积电最大客户之一，而且Jensen与他夫人Lori仍是我与Sophie的好友。

ReadShift 双语翻译

NVIDIA was TSMC's primary partner and customer for the forty-nanometer node. TSMC's early production problems at forty nanometers caused NVIDIA significant losses. NVIDIA had begun disputing with TSMC a year before my return as CEO, but no resolution had been reached.

In the first few days after resuming the CEO role, I spent almost all my time on the phone informing key customers of my return. When I spoke with NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang, he specifically called attention to the outstanding dispute between our two companies and urged a swift resolution.

For the next three weeks, I spent dozens of hours in deep discussion with relevant colleagues within the company. In early July 2009, I felt I understood the matter clearly and had a solution. I emailed Jensen: 'I will come to Silicon Valley next week and plan to join your family for salad and pizza at 6:30 p.m. on July 15.'

By then Jensen and I had been friends for over a decade, and I had often dined at his home on salad and pizza. But this time he was alarmed by my email—given how serious the dispute was between our companies, why was I only thinking about salad and pizza? He emailed back: 'Then when are we going to discuss business?'

I replied immediately: 'I'll come to your home at six-thirty, have pizza with your family first, and at eight o'clock sharp, you and I will go to your study to discuss business.'

On July 15 I arrived on time at Jensen's home and had a simple and pleasant pizza dinner with his family. At eight o'clock sharp, I said to Jensen, 'Let's go to your study.' Once inside, we closed the door and began a serious conversation. I presented a settlement recommendation that I and my TSMC colleagues had studied for three weeks—over one hundred million dollars in compensation—and emphasized that this was our only proposal, valid for forty-eight hours; if he did not agree within forty-eight hours, we would have no choice but to seek arbitration.

Jensen agreed within two days. To this day, NVIDIA remains one of TSMC's largest customers, and Jensen and his wife Lori remain friends of Sophie and me.

调整降价速度（二○一○年及以后）

经验和「学习曲线」理论都告诉我们：同一节点技术晶圆的单位成本会随累积产量而下降。再加上「抢单」竞争激烈，半导体的降价已成惯例。

只是二○○五至二○○九年蔡力行任CEO期间，台积电降价的幅度超过了成本降低的幅度，以致毛利率降低。在这期间，管理团队又提出了一个营收大幅增加、但利润不增加、无法接受的五年计划。我只得把这五年计划原封退还，要求管理团队再提。

二○○九年六月我回任CEO后的首要工作之一就是降低降价速度，使得我们的毛利率能逐步上升。通常台积电每年的价格在前一年底就和客户商定，所以我在二○○九年六月中已无能为力，我只能致力于二○一○年的价格。经过半年我自己、总部「订价」幕僚单位以及全球营销组织的努力，使得二○一○年的降幅缩小到二○○九年降幅的三分之二；后一年的降幅再进一步降低到二○○九年降幅的一半。

随着售价比较稳定，「减低成本」运动又每时每刻都在推行，我们的毛利率也有显著的进步。二○○九至二○一八年都在四十五％至五十％间。五年内毛利率有五个百分点的进步！

多位「派遣人力」为「正职同仁」（二○一○年）

在同一地区内，如果雇主候用的人员有「同工不同酬」现象，这个雇主是自找麻烦——小则士气不振，大则工会干涉、群体抗议。

我在返任CEO后发现台积电约有两万两千位「正职员工」，却有三千两百位「派遣人力」。其中约五百位「派遣人力」是属于一些不同于一般「正职员工」的专业（保全、医护、团膳等），但绝大部分约两千七百位「派遣人力」的原因是为了降低成本。

在二○○九年底发现这问题后，我找了五位与此问题有关的副总成立「专案小组」，要求他们拟出办法以「正职员工」取代「派遣人力」。二○一○年三月我们对全体同仁公布此办法，并在六月至九月执行。办法是在原本两千七百多位工作与既有「正职员工」相似的「派遣人力」中，遴选两千四百位新任「正职同仁」。未经遴选的三百多位，台积电也经中介公司为他们找到新工作，或领取我们提供的「关怀金」离去。

此「替代案」还有一个我未预料但也不惊讶的后果——两千四百位自「派遣人力」改为「正职同仁」的生产力，竟与原来两千七百位「派遣人力」的生产力一样。我们不需要多添人。

若对的事，常有好报。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Both experience and the 'learning curve' theory tell us that the unit cost of wafers at the same node technology declines as cumulative output increases. Coupled with fierce competition for orders, price reductions in semiconductors had become customary.

However, during Ming-Lieh Tsai's tenure as CEO from 2005 to 2009, TSMC's price cuts exceeded the rate of cost reduction, causing gross margins to decline. During this period, the management team also proposed an unacceptable five-year plan that would significantly increase revenue but not profit. I had no choice but to return the plan unopened and ask the team to resubmit.

One of my first tasks after resuming the CEO role in June 2009 was to slow the pace of price cuts so that our gross margins could gradually recover. Because TSMC's prices for the coming year were typically agreed upon with customers at the end of the preceding year, I could do nothing for 2009 by mid-June; I could only focus on 2010 pricing. After six months of effort by myself, the headquarters pricing staff, and the global marketing organization, the price decline for 2010 was reduced to two-thirds of the 2009 decline; the following year's decline was reduced further to half of the 2009 decline.

As selling prices stabilized and the campaign to reduce costs continued around the clock, our gross margin also improved significantly. From 2009 to 2018, it remained between forty-five and fifty percent—a five percentage point improvement over five years!

Within the same workplace, if employees doing the same work receive different pay, the employer is inviting trouble—on the small scale, demoralization; on the large scale, union interference and collective protest.

After resuming the CEO role, I discovered that TSMC had approximately 22,000 'regular employees' but 3,200 'dispatched workers.' Of these, about 500 dispatched workers were in specialized roles different from regular employees (security, medical, catering, etc.), but the vast majority—approximately 2,700—were dispatched workers hired primarily to reduce costs.

After discovering this issue at the end of 2009, I assembled five vice presidents associated with this matter into a 'special project team' and asked them to devise a plan to replace dispatched workers with regular employees. We announced this plan to all employees in March 2010 and implemented it from June to September. From the original 2,700+ dispatched workers whose jobs were similar to existing regular employees, we selected 2,400 to become new 'regular colleagues.' For the remaining 300+ not selected, TSMC also helped them find new jobs through intermediary companies or provided them with 'care payments' to leave.

This 'substitution plan' had one consequence I had not anticipated but was not surprised by—the productivity of the 2,400 who were converted from dispatched workers to regular employees was the same as that of the original 2,700 dispatched workers. We did not need to add any headcount.

合并先进技术事业组织及主流技术事业组织（二○○九年十月）

在蔡力行任CEO期间，他成立了先进技术事业组织及主流技术事业组织。这两个单位的主力都是生产线（在台积电，我们亦称生产为「营运」），先进组织负责十二吋厂，主流组织负责六吋及八吋厂。

力行的事业组织其实也是一九九六年布鲁克主意的重演（见第二十四章）。一九九六年我否决了布鲁克的主意，十几年后没有否决力行。我想是因为布鲁克只是「总经理」不是CEO，而力行是CEO，应该给CEO更多空间。

但现在我回来做CEO，这个错误也应该改掉了。所以在处理最急迫问题（调整降价速度、解决与辉达的悬案）后，我就把先进组织和主流组织的业务发展单位抽出来，再把这两个组织合并为全公司的营运组织。

接着，合并两个抽出来的业务发展单位，并且赋予它新的使命——台积电的Marketing Department。

欧美大公司通常把行销（Sales）和Marketing放在一起。台湾企业界了解行销，但常忽视Marketing，甚至连好的译名都没有。我查英汉辞典，它对Marketing的译名是：市场学。其实Marketing岂止是一门学问！对以「客制」产品为主的台积电，它是每天都要执行的专业。

既然Marketing没有好的译名，我们就称它为Business Development吧。这名字译成中文容易，就是「业务发展」。

业务发展组织的使命是：

（一）了解并预测世界晶圆代工市场。

（二）了解台积电前三十大客户（约占台积电总营收的八十％）。

（三）了解台积电自己的研发及制造能力，因而配合客户的新产品要求，提高台积电的市占率。

（四）因为要做到（一）、（二）、（三），所以要常与客户接触。

我对CEO（包括自己）的期许是：把外面的世界带进公司里面，动员公司的人力、财力资源来应付外来的挑战及机会。其实，业务发展组织的负责人就是一个小型的CEO。

ReadShift 双语翻译

During Ming-Lieh Tsai's tenure as CEO, he established an Advanced Technology Business Organization and a Mainstream Technology Business Organization. Both units were centered on production lines (at TSMC, we also call production 'operations'); the Advanced unit was responsible for twelve-inch fabs, and the Mainstream unit for six-inch and eight-inch fabs.

Tsai's business organization was essentially a replay of Brook's idea from 1996 (see Chapter 24). In 1996 I had rejected Brook's proposal, but more than a decade later I did not reject Tsai's. I suppose it was because Brook was only a 'general manager,' not CEO, whereas Tsai was CEO, and a CEO should be given more latitude.

But now that I had returned as CEO, this mistake也应该 be corrected. So after addressing the most urgent issues (adjusting the pace of price cuts and resolving the outstanding dispute with NVIDIA), I pulled out the business development units from both the Advanced and Mainstream organizations and merged the two into a single company-wide operations organization.

Next, I merged the two extracted business development units and endowed them with a new mission—TSMC's Marketing Department.

Large companies in Europe and the United States typically group Sales and Marketing together. The Taiwanese business community understands 'sales' but often neglects 'marketing,' to the point that there is not even a good translation. I looked up marketing in an English-Chinese dictionary, and the translation given was 'market studies.' But marketing is far more than an academic discipline! For TSMC, which is primarily a custom-product company, it is a professional function practiced every day.

Since marketing had no good Chinese translation, we called it Business Development. Translating that name into Chinese was easy: 'business development.'

The mission of the business development organization was:

(1) Understand and forecast the global foundry market.

(2) Understand TSMC's top thirty customers (accounting for approximately eighty percent of TSMC's total revenue).

(3) Understand TSMC's own research and development and manufacturing capabilities, thereby aligning with customers' new product requirements to increase TSMC's market share.

(4) To accomplish (1), (2), and (3), it was necessary to maintain frequent contact with customers.

My expectation for a CEO (including myself) was to bring the outside world into the company and mobilize the company's human and financial resources to meet external challenges and opportunities. In essence, the head of the business development organization was a small CEO.

任命魏哲家与刘德音

蔡力行已把公司里最被看好的两位经理人——刘德音和魏哲家——分别担任先进技术组织和主流技术组织的负责人。现在我把这两个组织合并了，又把业务发展单位抽出来成立新组织（约六、七十人），我怎么善待德音和哲家？

这两位过去都有相当丰富的研发及营运经验，但都缺乏营销、市场及客户接触经验。新的业务发展组织会是一个新的学习机会和经验。我先把业务发展组织的职位征询两位中较资深的刘德音，但他拒绝了：「我现在（先进技术事业组织）就有一万多名员工，怎么要我接受只有六、七十名员工的位置？」事实上，以员工数目衡量主管职位的重要性是一个错误的迷思。高层接触机会也许是更好的衡量。

接着我征询魏哲家，他倒欣然接受业务发展组织的职位。那么就当然定了。当然，刘德音也得到了他所要的营运组织职位。

召回蒋尚义（二○○九年九月）

蒋尚义在一九九七年加入台积电，是第一个我赋予「技术领先」使命的研发主管（见第二十七章）。但是他在蔡力行任CEO期内选择退休。我认为他是不可多得的研发主管人才，所以在我回任CEO后，请他到我的新竹办公室共进牛肉面午餐，并要求他回台积电重任研发主管一职。尚义欣然答应，并于二○○九年十月初——亦即我回任CEO后不到四个月——重任研发资深副总。

Tsai had already placed the company's two most promising managers—Aric Liu and CC Wei—as heads of the Advanced Technology and Mainstream Technology organizations, respectively. Now that I had merged these two organizations and extracted the business development unit to form a new organization (about 60 to 70 people), how should I treat Liu and Wei fairly?

Both had considerable experience in research and development and operations, but neither had experience in marketing, market analysis, or customer engagement. The new business development organization would be a new learning opportunity. I first approached the more senior of the two, Aric Liu, about the position, but he declined: 'I already manage over ten thousand employees in the Advanced Technology Business Organization. How can you ask me to take a position with only 60 or 70 employees?'

In fact, measuring the importance of a managerial position by the number of subordinates is a misconception. Opportunities for senior-level engagement might be a better measure.

I then approached CC Wei, who readily accepted the position. So it was settled. Of course, Aric Liu also received the operations organization position he wanted.

Shang-yi Chiang joined TSMC in 1997 and was the first research and development executive I entrusted with the mission of 'technology leadership' (see Chapter 27). But he chose to retire during Tsai's CEO tenure. I considered him an exceptionally rare R&D executive talent, so after I resumed the CEO role, I invited him to my Hsinchu office for beef noodle soup lunch and asked him to return to TSMC as head of R&D. Chiang gladly accepted and, in early October 2009—less than four months after my return—resumed his role as senior vice president of R&D.

确定营收八％为研发费用（二○一○年）

蒋尚义回任后，台积电的研发经费已相当充足，研发同仁也没有埋怨经费不足。但我想：应该把我们对研发承诺数量化。

在那「滚滚新世纪」的头十年，我常常追忆我在德仪任全球半导体集团总经理时，想把德仪的半导体研发经费自营收的四.七％增加至五.五％，而累被拒绝的痛苦（见第九章）。在二○○九年回顾台积电的研发经费占营收比例，自一九九七年至二○○九年一直在五％至六％范围内。我想：还有增加的空间！就随手把「营收的八％」作为我们研发经费占营收的目标。

果然，二○一一年以后，几乎每年研发经费都是当年营收的八％左右。随着营收的成长，研发经费也达到了二○二三年的五十六亿美元（新台币一千八百亿元），相当可观的数字，已超过麻省理工学院整年的总经费！当然，我们只做制程的研发，如果与客户伙伴的设计研发经费一并算起来，又有哪家半导体IDM公司的研发经费可以与我们相比？

ReadShift 双语翻译

After Shang-yi Chiang returned, TSMC's R&D funding was already quite adequate, and R&D colleagues had no complaints about insufficient funding. But I thought: we should quantify our commitment to R&D.

In the first decade of the 'surging new century,' I often recalled the frustration I had experienced at TI when I tried to increase TI's semiconductor R&D spending from 4.7 percent to 5.5 percent of revenue, only to be repeatedly rejected (see Chapter 9). In 2009, reviewing TSMC's R&D spending as a percentage of revenue, I found that from 1997 to 2009 it had remained in the five to six percent range. I thought: there is room to increase! So I casually set the target at 'eight percent of revenue.'

As it turned out, from 2011 onward, R&D spending was approximately eight percent of revenue almost every year. With revenue growth, R&D spending reached 5.6 billion dollars (180 billion New Taiwan dollars) in 2023—a considerable figure, exceeding the entire annual budget of MIT! Of course, we only conduct process R&D. If we add the design R&D spending of our customer partners, which semiconductor IDM company's R&D spending could compare with ours?

二○一○至二○一八年

二○○八年的不景气来得急，但也恢复得快。与二○○一年的不景气相比，台积电营收自二○○一年第一季急降，一直到二○○三年第三季才回到二○○○年第四季的水准——不景气时期共十一季。

ReadShift 双语翻译

> There is a tide in the affairs of men, > Which, taken at the flood, leads on to fortune; > Omitted, all the voyage of their life > Is bound in shallows and in miseries.

二○○八年台积电营收自第四季急降，但二○○九年第四季就已几乎回到二○○八年第三季水准——不景气时期只有四季。事后看起来，二○○八年的半导体市场不景气完全因为金融危机——投资工具过于氾滥而使得金融机构的槓桿太高，其实与半导体的基本需求无关。一旦各国政府出手拯救金融业，半导体需求不但复原，而且比「不景气」前成长更快。

这就是我在二○○九年六月复任CEO后看到的。幸运地，同时我们逐渐解决了四十纳米的良率问题。更好的消息：研发单位报告在下一个节点技术上（二十八纳米），他们有很快的进展。二十八纳米是一个关键技术，如果能在两年内开始量产，正在迅速发展的智慧型手机内的半导体将是我们的天下！

这是一个莎士比亚的「高潮」时刻：

世事的起伏本来是波浪式的，人们要是能够趁著高潮一往直前，一定可以功成名就；要是不能把握时机，就要终身蹭蹬，一事无成。

ReadShift 双语翻译

The 2008 downturn arrived quickly and also recovered quickly. Compared with the 2001 downturn, TSMC's revenue plummeted in the first quarter of 2001 and did not return to the fourth-quarter 2000 level until the third quarter of 2003—a downturn period of eleven quarters.

In 2008, TSMC's revenue dropped sharply in the fourth quarter, but by the fourth quarter of 2009 it had almost recovered to the third-quarter 2008 level—a downturn of only four quarters. Looking back, the 2008 semiconductor downturn was entirely caused by the financial crisis—the excessive proliferation of investment vehicles had pushed financial institutions' leverage too high—which had nothing to do with the fundamental demand for semiconductors. Once governments around the world moved to rescue the financial sector, semiconductor demand not only recovered but grew faster than before the 'downturn.'

This was what I saw after resuming the CEO role in June 2009. Fortuitously, we were simultaneously resolving the forty-nanometer yield problem. Even better news: the R&D organization reported rapid progress on the next node technology (twenty-eight nanometers). Twenty-eight nanometers is a critical node; if we could begin mass production within two years, the semiconductors in rapidly growing smartphones would be ours for the taking.

This was a Shakespearean 'climax' moment:

'The course of true affairs is wave-like; if people can press forward with the tide, they will surely achieve success; but if they fail to seize the moment, they will stumble through life and accomplish nothing.'

赶上高潮：加大投资（二○一○至二○一八年）

怎么才能跨上这高潮？我们必须立刻投资四十及二十八纳米的产能！

在「滚滚新世纪」内，自二○○一至二○○九年，台积电的资本投资相当稳定，每年大致在二十至二十五亿美元范围内。二○一○年，我发狠了。我要跨上我想象中的、新节点技术给我们的高潮。我加倍产能投资到五十九亿美元，比二○○九年的两倍还多！

我的发狠是因为我看到了台积电的机会。但当我发出此一讯息——二○一○年第一季董事会议程——好几位独立董事担心了，要在会前与我通电话。在他们心目中，市场景气还未完全恢复，怎么就投资那么多产能？二○一○年一月二十六日，台湾的晚上八点、美国的清晨、英国的下仗，我和三位在台湾、美国和英国的独立董电话会议。他们质问我要投资那么多，我告诉他们四十及二十八纳米技术的机会。他们半信半疑。最后我说：「这件事让我做吧，毕竟我是公司的负责人。」他们这才不再反对。

二○○九至二○一○年我看到的是四十及二十八纳米的机会。但随着台积电研发经费继续增加，研发能力继续增强，新技术层出不穷，以后营收及获利成长机会愈来愈多、也愈大。在二○一○至二○一八年八年内，台积电的资本投资自前述二○一○年的五十九亿美元成长到二○一八年的一百零五亿美元。营收自二○一○年的一百三十三亿美元成长到二○一八年三百四十二亿美元；获利也自二○一○年的五十一亿美元成长到二○一八年的一百一十六亿美元。

How do we seize this climax? We must invest immediately in capacity for forty- and twenty-eight-nanometer technology!

During the 'surging new century,' from 2001 to 2009, TSMC's capital investment was relatively stable, averaging between 2 and 2.5 billion dollars annually. In 2010, I went all in. I wanted to ride the wave that I saw coming from the new node technologies. I doubled capacity investment to 5.9 billion dollars—more than double the 2009 level.

My determination came from seeing TSMC's opportunity. But when I put this on the agenda for the first-quarter 2010 board meeting, several independent directors grew concerned and called me before the meeting. In their view, the market had not fully recovered—why invest so much capacity? On January 26, 2010, at 8 p.m. in Taiwan, early morning in the United States, and the evening in the United Kingdom, I held a teleconference with three independent directors in Taiwan, the United States, and the United Kingdom. They questioned why I wanted to invest so much. I told them about the forty- and twenty-eight-nanometer technology opportunities. They were half-convinced, half-doubtful. In the end, I said, 'Let me make this decision. After all, I am the person in charge.'

Only then did they cease their opposition. In 2009 and 2010, I saw the opportunity in forty- and twenty-eight-nanometer technologies. But as TSMC's R&D funding continued to increase and R&D capabilities strengthened, with new technologies emerging one after another, the opportunities for revenue and earnings growth became ever greater. Over the eight years from 2010 to 2018, TSMC's capital investment grew from the aforementioned 5.9 billion dollars in 2010 to 10.5 billion dollars in 2018. Revenue grew from 13.3 billion dollars in 2010 to 34.2 billion dollars in 2018; earnings grew from 5.1 billion dollars in 2010 to 11.6 billion dollars in 2018.

二十八纳米的汗与泪

我们当时以为大胆对二十八纳米产能力的投资，事后看来还嫌太少。但二十八纳米的大客户——高通，也拥有相当大的责任。当我们试产成功准备二○一二年量产时，高通起初估计他们二○一二年全年的需求是四万片晶圆。几个月后（二○一一年八月）他们发现给客户的样品受到超过预期的欢迎，就修改需求估计到十二万片。对台积电而言，一下子增加一个新产品三倍已是很艰难的任务，但高通的需求还继续增加——最后达到三十万片。

二○一二年二月九日，当高通的需求与我们的供应能力已有相当落差时，高通董事长及总裁联袂来访，他们的开场白就是：「我们只是要多点芯片，我们愿意付较高的价钱。」我了好几位副总帮忙：涨价无补于事，我们也不会做，我们已正在尽全力增加产能及产量。

一小时后，他们恨恨而去，临走前撂下一句狠话：为了对他们股东负责，他们必须再找另一个供应来源。我回答：「等到你们新的来源可以供应时，我们也可以供应你们完全的需要了。」高通的确找了另一个来源——格罗方德（GlobalFoundries），但我的预言是准确的。二○一二年九月十三日，我去高通的美国加州圣地牙哥总部访问高通总裁，他微微叹息似地说：「你说的话是对的，现在我们的新来源可以供应我们的边际需要，但你们也可以供应了。」结果二十八纳米产能过剩了。我们另一位客户也跑来对我说：「现在二十八纳米有新的来源，而且价钱比你们便宜，所以我们要在这边减单了。」我又气又惊，因为这位客户是我们一直认为忠诚的伙伴。他倒振振有辞：「这个新的来源不是我们建立的，而是高通建立的。既然高通建立了这个来源，你总不能说他不能用吧？」

ReadShift 双语翻译

What we had considered a bold investment in twenty-eight-nanometer capacity later appeared, in retrospect, to have been insufficient. But Qualcomm, TSMC's major customer at the twenty-eight-nanometer node, also bore considerable responsibility. When we successfully completed trial production and prepared for 2012 mass production, Qualcomm initially estimated their full-year 2012 demand at 40,000 wafers. A few months later (August 2011), they found that the samples provided to their customers were more popular than expected, and they revised their demand estimate to 120,000 wafers. For TSMC, tripling output for a new product at once was already a formidable task, but Qualcomm's demand continued to grow—eventually reaching 300,000 wafers.

On February 9, 2012, when Qualcomm's demand had diverged considerably from our supply capacity, Qualcomm's chairman and president visited together. Their opening words were: 'We just need more chips. We are willing to pay a higher price.'

I asked several vice presidents to assist: raising prices would not help, and we would not do it. We were already doing our utmost to increase capacity and output.

An hour later, they left in frustration, but not before delivering a parting threat: to be responsible to their shareholders, they had to find another supply source. I replied: 'By the time your new source can supply you, we will also be able to supply your complete needs.'

Qualcomm did find another source—GlobalFoundries—but my prediction proved accurate. On September 13, 2012, I visited Qualcomm's headquarters in San Diego, California, and spoke with the president. He sighed slightly and said, 'What you said was correct. Now our new source can supply our marginal needs, but so can you.'

The result was that twenty-eight-nanometer capacity became oversupplied. Another one of our customers came to me and said: 'Now there is a new source for twenty-eight nanometers, and the price is cheaper than yours, so we are reducing our orders here.'

I was both angry and startled, because this customer had always been considered a loyal partner. He replied calmly: 'This new source was not established by us, but by Qualcomm. Since Qualcomm established it, can you really say they should not be allowed to use it?'

二○二四年记：多年后，每次我想起二○一二年二十八纳米的故事，情绪总还是有点激动。但再借莎士比亚的话吧：「有好结果的事都是好事（All's well that ends well）。」二十八纳米的故事有很好的结果。

二十八纳米是台积电打进智慧型手机世界的第一代技术。上文所述的「产能过剩」也只是暂时性的。自二十八纳米后，手机应用成为台积电的最大市场——直至最近。如果我们没有二十八纳米的成功，我的自传恐怕也不会有下一章。

章节

台積電篇三第三十三章

张忠谋

台积电篇三·第三十三章｜苹果来敲门

二○一○年的一个秋日夜晚，苹果公司的营运长杰夫·威廉斯（Jeff Williams）突然成了我家的不速之客——由我太太Sophie的表弟郭台铭（鸿海集团创办人）带领，亲自到我家拜访。此举掀开了苹果与台积电合作关系的序幕，也成为台积电进军智慧型手机芯片市场的里程碑。

然而，从「苹果来敲们」到真正拿到订单，中间经历了两年的艰辛谈判、财务规划和技术挑战。苹果不仅要求台积电承诺庞大的产能，更在台积电与三星之间做了一番取舍。这段故事，既有商业博弈的紧张，也有两家公司价值观碰撞后的契合。

ReadShift 双语翻译

On an autumn evening in 2010, Jeff Williams, Apple's operations chief, suddenly became an unexpected guest at my home—accompanied by my wife Sophie's cousin, Terry Gou (founder of the Foxconn Group), who personally visited our home. This visit opened the prelude to the Apple–TSMC partnership and became a milestone in TSMC's entry into the smartphone chip market.

However, from 'Apple knocking at our door' to actually receiving orders, there was a two-year journey of arduous negotiations, financial planning, and technical challenges. Apple not only demanded that TSMC commit to massive capacity but also made TSMC choose between it and Samsung. This story contained both the tension of business negotiation and the alignment of values between the two companies.

苹果的背景

苹果自一九七六年成立后，一直就是一个传奇性的科技公司。一九八○年它的股票在美国上市，苹果市值立刻比历史悠久、规模巨大的福特汽车公司还高。记得苹果上市后不久，我正访问台湾，对李国鼎政务委员提起苹果与福市的市值比较，李政委频频摇头，并説：「怎么有这样的事？」我回答：「这就是现代科技公司的神妙。」一九八五年，苹果创办人贾伯斯（Steve Jobs）因公司政治被迫辞职。九○年代苹果一度家道中落。一九九七年贾伯斯返任，苹果又复兴，尤其在二○○七年推出智慧型手机，惊动世界，几乎人手一支，也改变了千千万万人的生活习惯。后来苹果的智慧型手机及个人电脑产品，市值曾达三兆美元，高居世界前两名。

智慧型手机是一个相当「半导体密集」的产品。所以台积电自二○○七年后就以苹果为潜在的大客户。只是苹果除了以创新成名外，也是一个非常保密的公司。那时我们只听到它已开始设计自用的积体电路，而且找韩国的三星电子代工。三星本来就是世界最大的记忆体公司（见第二十三章），一定也是苹果的存储器供应商；所以苹果找它代工逻辑产品也不稀奇。

只是，苹果打开智慧型手机市场后不久，雄心勃勃的三星会长李健熙忽然宣布三星也要做智慧型手机了。三星既是苹果的主要供应商，也变成苹果的主要竞争者。

假使我是贾伯斯，我一定会有「是可忍，孰不可忍」的感觉。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Since its founding in 1976, Apple had always been a legendary technology company. When its stock went public in the United States in 1980, Apple's market capitalization immediately exceeded that of Ford Motor Company, a firm with a long history and massive scale. I remember that shortly after Apple's listing, I was visiting Taiwan and mentioned the comparison of Apple and Ford's market values to Vice Premier Kuo-Ting Li. Premier Li shook his head repeatedly and said, 'How can such a thing exist?' I replied, 'That is the marvel of modern technology companies.'

In 1985, Apple's founder Steve Jobs was forced to resign due to corporate politics. During the 1990s, Apple fell on difficult times. Jobs returned in 1997, and Apple revived, especially with the 2007 launch of the smartphone, which stunned the world. Nearly everyone carried one, and it changed the daily habits of hundreds of millions of people. Later, Apple's smartphone and personal computer products at one point reached a market capitalization of three trillion dollars, ranking among the top two in the world.

Smartphones are products that are quite 'semiconductor-intensive.' So after 2007, TSMC regarded Apple as a potential major customer. But Apple, known for its innovation, was also an exceptionally secretive company. At that time, we only heard that it had begun designing its own integrated circuits and was having them fabricated by Samsung Electronics of Korea. Samsung was already the world's largest memory company (see Chapter 23) and certainly also Apple's memory supplier; so it was not surprising that Apple turned to it for logic product fabrication as well.

But soon after Apple opened the smartphone market, the ambitious Samsung chairman Kun-Hee Lee suddenly announced that Samsung would also make smartphones. Samsung, already Apple's primary supplier, had become Apple's primary competitor.

If I were Steve Jobs, I would certainly have felt that 'if this can be tolerated, nothing cannot be tolerated.'

晚餐桌上的不速之客（二○一○年十一月）

台积电的机会来了，但我们仍找不到进入苹果的门。

二○一○年十一月九日是一个星期二。下午六时，我刚在台积电台北办事处结束了为期两天的第四季董事会。六时半回到台北家，Sophie在家门口截住我，説：「郭台铭下午来了一个电话，説他晚上带一个苹果副总到我们家吃饭，八点到。」郭台铭是Sophie的表弟，我们常有亲戚间的往来。他也是鸿海集团的创办人和董事长。鸿海是苹果的主要装配商，与苹果有密切的关系。一听到Sophie的话，我就知道苹果副总的来意——原来担心苹果无门可入，现在苹果来敲门了。

台铭带来的是杰夫·威廉斯（Jeff Williams），他在苹果的地位不只是副总，而是营运长。

为了有两位客人，Sophie添了几道菜。坐定后，杰夫单刀直入：説要台积电替苹果生产苹果自己设计的逻辑晶片。他显然已对台积电做了相当研究，知道台积电不是他习惯合作的「单位毛利率」组装工厂，所以他说：「会让你享有四十％毛利率。」其实台积电的毛利率在他来之前就已达四十多至四十五％，而且我正想把它推到五十％。所以他的这句话，在他来说是要我们放心，他不会在价格上太苛刻；我听了倒是提高警觉：在价格上他不会很大方。

当场我没説什么，这只是第一次见面，双方要讨论的事情多得很，价格问题尽可留到最后。

杰夫要求次日就与台积电高阶主管集会。十一月十日上午我到办公室后，就召集台积电高阶主管，为下午二时半与杰夫开会做好准备。会议中杰夫要求苹果的设计、技术以及采购人员尽早到台积电开始讨论双方的合作。

虽然十一月下旬就是美国的感恩节，此后又接着有耶诞节及新年，未来两个月正是美国人喜欢度假的时期，但他仍拟在感恩节后、耶诞节与台积电人员开始密切沟通。

对我来说，苹果来敲门也带来一个额外的安慰：我在前一年任命魏哲家建立了业务发展组织（见第三十二章），现在派上大用。在这个新的客户关系上，他们发挥了很大的功能。

I asked one question: 'Is it twenty-eight nanometer?'

Jeff answered that it was twenty nanometer, with mass production planned one year later. I began to calculate in my head. Twenty nanometer was merely a half-node; pursuing it would be a detour, because we were already trial-producing twenty-half nanometer, and the true next node was sixteen nanometer.

Jeff requested a meeting with TSMC's senior management the following day. On the morning of November 10, after arriving at the office, I convened TSMC's senior team in preparation for the two-thirty meeting with Jeff. During the session Jeff asked Apple's design, technology, and procurement personnel to come to TSMC as soon as possible to begin discussing the cooperation.

Although Thanksgiving fell in late November and was followed by Christmas and the New Year—the two-month period when Americans most favored holidays—he still intended to begin close communications with TSMC's staff after Thanksgiving and before Christmas.

In the end, on December 15 and 16, key personnel from Apple and TSMC held two days of intensive discussions in Hsinchu. Thus began the Apple-TSMC cooperative relationship.

For me, Apple's coming to our door also brought an additional comfort: the business development organization that I had asked Morris Wei to establish the previous year (see Chapter 32) was now proving enormously valuable. They played a major role in this new customer relationship.

两个月「暂停协商」（二○一一年三月五日至五月五日）

正当苹果与台积电双向沟通如火如荼时，忽然，在二○一一年三月三日，我接到杰夫·威廉斯的电话：「英特尔的最高层与提姆·库克（Tim Cook，苹果总裁）接触后，提姆答应了。所以我要我们之间的协商暂停两个月。」虽然这个要求来得突然，但二○一一年的英特尔已无它在上世纪末期令人闻其名即肃然起敬的威风。挂了电话后，我默思我们和英特尔的比较：我觉得我们在技术上不输英特尔（这是二○一一年，再过几年我就会认为我们在技术上胜过英特尔）；在制造成本及客户服务上都胜过英特尔——苹果没有理由弃台积电而选英特尔！

虽然充满自信，但对苹果表示关切总不会是错吧？所以四月我的硅谷之行中，我于四月五日约访杰夫。杰夫回电：他那天不在办公室，但总裁提姆·库克在，已经安排好让我见他。

四月五日我赴苹果总部与提姆共进午餐。提姆很热诚地接待我。我们先到苹果自助餐厅拿了些食物，再回到他的办公室用餐。提姆一开始就叫我不必担心。他没有提英特尔的技术或製造成本，只淡淡地说：「他们不擅做代工。」五月五日，准确地在杰夫「暂停协商」电话两个月后，杰夫来电话：「恢复协商。」

Just as Apple and TSMC were communicating in both directions with growing intensity, suddenly on March 3, 2011, I received a call from Jeff Williams. 'Intel's top management has approached Tim Cook, Apple's president, and Tim has agreed. So I need to pause our negotiations for two months.'

Although the request came suddenly, Intel in 2011 no longer possessed the formidable prestige it had commanded in the late twentieth century, when its name alone inspired respect. After hanging up, I reflected on a comparison between us and Intel. I believed that our technology was not inferior to Intel's—in 2011 I held that view; in the years that followed I came to believe we surpassed Intel. In manufacturing cost and customer service, we outperformed Intel. Apple had no reason to abandon TSMC for Intel.

Confident as I was, I thought it not amiss to express our concern to Apple. During my trip to Silicon Valley in April, I asked to see Jeff on April 5. Jeff called back: he would not be in the office that day, but President Tim Cook was, and he had arranged for me to meet with him.

On April 5 I went to Apple's headquarters and had lunch with Tim. He received me very warmly. We first went to the Apple cafeteria to get some food, then returned to his office to eat. From the start Tim told me not to worry. He did not mention Intel's technology or manufacturing cost. He simply said, in a detached tone, 'They are not good at contract manufacturing.'

On May 5, exactly two months after Jeff's 'pause negotiation' call, Jeff phoned: 'Resuming negotiations.'

多年後，大约二○二一年吧，英特尔又换了一个总裁（十年内的第四个），传出话来説当年没接苹果生意是一个大错误，但原因是嫌苹果出的价格太低。听起来这与提姆对我説的「他们不擅做代工」似乎不很一样，但其实是一样的——不肯接受客户能接受的价格等于「不擅做代工」。台积电的本领就是在客户能接受的价格中赚取合理利润。

台积电的制造及财务规划（二○一一年）

在二○一一年之前，台积电经由营业活动产生的现金，经常都足以发股利及投资未来厂房及生产设备。但二○一一年，苹果给了我们一个相当高的二○一四年晶片需求估计。如果要能完全供应他们估计的需求，台积电必须在未来几年内投资厂房及设备约两百亿美元。这已超出我一向保持的「审慎的」（prudent）财务规划范围。

台积电可采行的应付方案有以下几项：

（一）告诉苹果我们只能承诺为他们生产估计需求的一部分。客户不需要投资产能，所以常倾向于高估他们未来需求。如果台积电「照单全收」所有客户未来需求估计，又照他们的估计投资产能，结果一定是产能过剩。台积电赢得客户信任的办法是：对客户做他能接受、我们在尽力下也能实现的承诺，然后不计代价实现这承诺。

（二）停止或减少每年的股利。

（三）在股票市场做现金增资（卖新股票）。

（四）举公司债。

多年後，大约二○二一年吧，英特尔又换了一个总裁（十年内的第四个），传出话来説当年没接苹果生意是一个大错误，但原因是嫌苹果出的价格太低。听起来这与提姆对我説的「他们不擅做代工」似乎不很一样，但其实是一样的——不肯接受客户能接受的价格等于「不擅做代工」。台积电的本领就是在客户能接受的价格中赚取合理利润。

在二○一一年之前，台积电经由营业活动产生的现金，经常都足以发股利及投资未来厂房及生产设备。但二○一一年，苹果给了我们一个相当高的二○一四年晶片需求估计。如果要能完全供应他们估计的需求，台积电必须在未来几年内投资厂房及设备约两百亿美元。这已超出我一向保持的「审慎的」（prudent）财务规划范围。

台积电可采行的应付方案有以下几项：

（一）告诉苹果我们只能承诺为他们生产估计需求的一部分。客户不需要投资产能，所以常倾向于高估他们未来需求。如果台积电「照单全收」所有客户未来需求估计，又照他们的估计投资产能，结果一定是产能过剩。台积电赢得客户信任的办法是：对客户做他能接受、我们在尽力下也能实现的承诺，然后不计代价实现这承诺。

（二）停止或减少每年的股利。

（三）在股票市场做现金增资（卖新股票）。

Years later, around 2021, Intel appointed yet another president—its fourth in a decade—and word leaked that failing to take Apple's business that year was a major mistake. The reason given, however, was that Apple's price was too low. This sounds somewhat different from what Tim told me—'They are not good at contract manufacturing.' In fact the two statements are the same. Refusing to accept a price the customer can accept is tantamount to being unskilled at contract manufacturing. TSMC's strength lies in earning a reasonable profit within the price the customer can accept.

Prior to 2011, the cash TSMC generated from operating activities was usually sufficient to pay dividends and to invest in future fabs and production equipment. But in 2011 Apple gave us a very high estimate of its chip demand for 2014. If we were to fully supply their estimated demand, TSMC would need to invest roughly twenty billion dollars in fabs and equipment over the following years. That already exceeded the prudent financial planning range I had always maintained.

TSMC could pursue several options:

(1) Tell Apple that we could only commit to producing a portion of their estimated demand. Customers who do not need to invest in capacity tend to overestimate their future demand. If TSMC were to accept every customer's demand estimate and then invest in capacity accordingly, the result would certainly be overcapacity. The way TSMC wins customer trust is to make commitments we can deliver on and that the customer can accept, and then to honor those commitments at all costs.

(2) Suspend or reduce the annual dividend.

(3) Raise cash in the equity market through a seasoned offering.

二○一一年，我们的财务单位以及九○年代就建立的「市场预测」单位已相当成熟。前者有高盛集团的后援，后者不但预测半导体市场，也预测使用半导体的主要电子产品（例如智慧型手机）市场。我在几星期内与这两幕僚单位及有关高阶主管讨论后，决定采取（一）与（四）。

关于（一），我们决定只承诺约一半苹果给我们需求估计。魏哲家，这位上任才一年余的业务发展组织主管，被给予最先告诉苹果这消息的「荣誉」。他去苹果的回应是：「你们疯啦？只接受我们给你们需求的一半？」我们没有疯，这是我们做过「审慎的」财务规划之后的决定。二○一一年六月，我亲自去加州拜访杰夫，重复哲家已告诉他们基层的消息。杰夫只是轻描淡写地説：「其实你们可以暂时停发股利，我想你们股东也会理解。」我也轻描淡写地回答：「我们股东成分中也有不少（事实是三十％左右）满重视股利的。」他就不再多说什么。

苹果只承诺Demand需求一半的晶圆。即使数量减了一半，台积电仍须举公司债七十一亿美元。经过财务部门与高盛讨论后，决定于二○一一、二○一二、二○一三年内在台湾共发行新台币一千六百六十二亿元公司债；此外还要于二○一三年在纽约发行十五亿美元公司债。

In 2011, our finance organization and the 'market forecasting' unit established in the 1990s had both become quite mature. The former had the backing of Goldman Sachs; the latter not only forecast the semiconductor market but also the major electronic-product markets that used semiconductors, such as smartphones. Within a few weeks of discussing matters with both advisory units and relevant senior managers, I decided to pursue options (1) and (4).

Regarding option (1), we decided to commit to only about half of the demand estimate Apple had given us. Morris Wei, who had been leading the business development organization for just over a year, was given the 'honor' of being the first to tell Apple the news. His response at Apple was: 'Are you crazy? You are only accepting half of our demand estimate?'

We were not crazy. This was the decision we reached after conducting prudent financial planning. In June 2011, I personally went to California to meet with Jeff and repeated the message Morris had already delivered to his team. Jeff merely remarked, in a casual tone, 'You could always suspend dividends for a while. I think your shareholders would understand.' I responded in kind: 'A significant portion of our shareholders—roughly thirty percent in fact—place considerable importance on dividends.' He then said no more.

Apple committed only to half its estimated demand in wafers. Even with the quantity halved, TSMC still needed to issue seven-point-one billion dollars in corporate bonds. After discussions between our finance department and Goldman Sachs, we decided to issue a total of one hundred sixty-two billion New Taiwan dollars in corporate bonds across Taiwan in 2011, 2012, and 2013, and additionally to issue fifteen billion dollars in corporate bonds in New York in 2013.

晶圆售价呢？在与苹果充分沟通规格、台积电成本及订价部门横算竖算后，我们已胸有成竹。二○一一年九月十四日，杰夫亲自来新竹，议定就在那天议定了。当天晚上我和他到米其林三星级的颐驊餐厅吃饭。杰夫开玩笑説：「啊，讲定了价。假如没有讲定，我想你会请我们去吃麦当劳。」在製造及财务面上，以上的准备可说相当充足。技术面呢？

二十奈米开发成功，但十六奈米延宕

二○一○年十一月苹果告诉我：苹果在二○一四年要二十奈米。我们正在试产二十奈米，但是在我的做目中，二十奈米只是一个「半节点」——真正的下一个节点是十六奈米。如果做二十奈米，会是一个「绕道」。但是苹果要求，我别无选择，必须先为苹果开发二十奈米。

二十奈米的开发并非百分之百顺利。在二○一二至二○一三年，我曾试过三位共同营运长（Co-COO）——蒋尚义、刘德音、魏哲家轮流接管公司的三大块业务——研发、生产、营销及业务发展。但是一遇到二十奈米的开发有问题，我就立刻把正在享受新工作的蒋尚义召回研发，全破坏了原来设计的轮调制度。

虽不完全顺利，二十奈米还是如苹果要求开发出来。但十六奈米的研发却延宕了。

What about the price per wafer? After extensive discussions with Apple on specifications and careful cost and pricing calculations by TSMC's cost and pricing teams, we felt well prepared. On September 14, 2011, Jeff came to Hsinchu in person, and the price was settled that very day. That evening Jeff and I dined at a three-Michelin-star restaurant. Jeff joked, 'Ah, the price is set. If we had not agreed on a price, I suppose you would have taken us to McDonald's.'

From a manufacturing and financial standpoint, the preparations above could be regarded as quite adequate. What about the technology side?

In November 2010 Apple told us that it wanted twenty nanometer in 2014. We were already trial-producing twenty nanometer, but in my judgment twenty nanometer was merely a half-node—the true next node was sixteen nanometer. Pursuing twenty nanometer would be a detour. But Apple had asked, and I had no choice but to develop twenty nanometer for Apple first.

The twenty-nanometer development was not entirely smooth. Between 2012 and 2013, I tried a rotating system among three co-chief operating officers—Sandi Jin, Tim Liu, and Morris Wei—who would take charge of the company's three major business divisions: R&D, manufacturing, and marketing and business development. But whenever problems arose in the twenty-nanometer development, I would immediately recall Sandi, who was enjoying his new assignment, back to R&D. That completely disrupted the originally designed rotation system.

Although not entirely smooth, twenty nanometer was developed to Apple's specification. But the R&D for sixteen nanometer was delayed.

二○一三年七月，正在我们准备开始量产二十奈米时，苹果忽然对十六奈米需求投标。我们投了标。苹果的回应是：他们决定先向三星购买十六奈米的晶圆。

我急了！几年来为苹果投入这么多人力、财力、物力，难道只做一节点、只做一、两年的生意？

立刻致电邮给杰夫：「我们为了替苹果做二十奈米，投资了一百多亿美元的厂房设备。这些厂房和设备大部分都可用在十六奈米上。现在你不要我们的十六奈米，你要我们怎么办？」杰夫来电要我放心。二○一三年八月二十七日他亲自来新竹对我们解释：三星可以立刻供应十六奈米（他们不必绕道先做二十奈米），所以苹果先买他们的。但一旦台积电可以顺利供应，苹果就会用台积电的十六奈米。

后来不但结果的确如此，台积电也从这经验中开始了一个新做法：同时开发下一个半节点和下当然，每年都在增加的研发经费以及每年都在茁壮的研发团队是一个大帮助。

In July 2013, just as we were preparing to begin mass production of twenty nanometer, Apple unexpectedly issued a bid request for sixteen nanometer. We submitted a bid. Apple's response was that it had decided to purchase sixteen-nanometer wafers from Samsung first.

I grew anxious! We had invested so much manpower, capital, and resources in Apple over the preceding years. Were we to do only one node, only one or two years of business?

I immediately sent Jeff an e-mail: 'To manufacture twenty nanometer for Apple, we invested over ten billion dollars in fabs and equipment. Most of those fabs and equipment can also be used for sixteen nanometer. Now you do not want our sixteen-nanometer wafers. What do you expect us to do?'

Jeff called back to put my mind at ease. On August 27, 2013, he came to Hsinchu in person to explain: Samsung could supply sixteen nanometer immediately (they did not need to take the detour through twenty nanometer first), so Apple chose to buy from them. But once TSMC could supply sixteen nanometer smoothly, Apple would switch to TSMC.

The outcome proved him correct. Moreover, TSMC began a new practice from this experience: developing both the next half-node and the full next node simultaneously. The steadily increasing R&D budget and the growing R&D team each year were of great help.

苹果是「伙伴」

台积电的核心价值：诚信正直、承诺、创新、客户信任，在我们与苹果的建交中受到了考验。同时，我们也考验了苹果的价值。结果，两家公司都安全通过了考验。

我自二○一八年从台积电退休后，就鲜少与苹果接触。但二○二四年二月，杰夫·威廉斯专程来看我。距离二○一○年他做我家的「不速之客」已十三年多。他仍英俊挺拔。我们共同享用我办公室楼上餐厅提供的广东点心。他说了一句让我窝心的话：「台积电是苹果非常少数的最好伙伴之一。」

**Cheat Sheet｜商业词汇**

| 词汇 | 英文 | 含义 |

| 营运长 | Chief Operating Officer (COO) | 负责公司日常运营的高级主管 | | 审慎的 | Prudent | 保守、审慎的财务态度 | | 半节点 | Half-node | 介于两个全节点之间的技术世代 | | 绕道 | Detour | 走不必要的弯路 | | 现金增资 | Seasoned Equity Offering | 发行新股票以筹集资金 | | 公司债 | Corporate Bond | 公司发行的债券 | | 单位毛利率 | Unit Gross Margin | 单位产品的毛利 |

**背景知识延伸｜苹果与三星的爱恨关系**

苹果与三星的关系是商业史上最复杂的「亦敌亦友」案例之一。三星既是苹果重要的零组件供应商（存储器、面板），又是智慧型手机市场的直接竞争对手。这种「供应商+竞争者」的双重身份，促使苹果寻找替代供应来源——这就是台积电进入苹果供应链的历史契机。

**修辞赏析｜「不速之客」的双重含义**

「不速之客」原指不请自来的客人，通常带贬义。在这里张忠谋用这个词来形容杰夫·威廉斯，字面上是「意外来访的客人」，但字里行间其实充满了欣慰——苹果终于主动来敲门了。「不速之客」一词，在张忠谋的精采笔法下，从一个略带贬义的成语转化为充满期待的戏剧性时刻。

章节

台積電篇三第三十四章

张忠谋

台积电篇三·第三十四章｜交棒的规划、退休

交棒的规划（二○○五至二○一七年）

我在二○○五年就开始规划台积电董事长及CEO的交棒。当时的计划是先释出CEO职给蔡力行，但仍保留董事长职。如果力行接CEO位顺利，几年后我就可以完全退休。只是接下来几年，台积电业务及人事并不很顺利，于是在二○○九年我又重兼CEO职，仍未放弃力行未来继承我的可能，所以任命他为台积电新事业总经理。可惜后来台积电的新事业也不很成功，力行也于二○一四年辞职，出任中华电信董事长，后来在二○一七年又转任为联发科共同执行长。他在联发科做得很好，现在已是副董事長暨执行长。

二○一二年任命三位「共同营运长」

重兼CEO几年后，到二○一二年，我认为已将台积电带回康庄大道（见第三十二、三十三章），于是接班人的考量在心中复萌。蔡力行仍是可能人选，他的薪、阶仍是台积电CEO的薪、阶。但几年已经过去，应该再提拔几位可能的接班人。

在二○一二年，公司内部最明显的领导人才是（依姓氏笔画排列）：（一）蒋尚义——当时负责研究开发；（二）刘德音——当时负责制造；（三）魏哲家——当时负责业务发展组织。

二○一二年三月，我摧升蒋、刘、魏三位为共同营运长（Co-Chief Operating Officer）。也许更重要的，我告诉他们：「你们三位轮流负责公司的三个重要领域」——也就是上段所述的研发、制造，及业务发展。一开始，我就把蒋尚义调离研发，让他负责制造。

I began planning the succession of TSMC's chairman and CEO positions as early as 2005. The original plan was to first release the CEO role to Morris Cai, while I retained the chairmanship. If Morris succeeded smoothly as CEO, I could retire completely after a few years. But business and personnel matters at TSMC did not go smoothly in the following years, so in 2009 I resumed the CEO role. I never abandoned the possibility that Morris would eventually succeed me, so I appointed him general manager of TSMC's new businesses. Unfortunately, TSMC's new businesses did not fare well, and Morris resigned in 2014 to become chairman of Chunghwa Telecom. He later moved to MediaTek in 2017 as co-CEO, where he performed excellently and is now vice chairman and CEO.

After resuming the CEO role for several years, by 2012 I felt that TSMC had been brought back onto a solid path (see Chapters 32 and 33). The question of succession arose again in my mind. Morris Cai was still a possible candidate; his pay and rank remained those of TSMC's CEO. But years had passed, and a few more potential successors should be promoted.

In 2012, the most obvious leadership talents within the company were, in alphabetical order by surname: (1) Sandi Jin—then in charge of R&D; (2) Tim Liu—then in charge of manufacturing; (3) Morris Wei—then in charge of the business development organization.

In March 2012, I promoted Sandi, Tim, and Morris to co-chief operating officers. Perhaps more importantly, I told them: 'The three of you will rotate responsibility for the company's three major domains'—namely R&D, manufacturing, and business development, as described above. From the start, I transferred Sandi away from R&D and assigned him to manufacturing.

如果真的在二○一二年能落实三人轮替三个重要领域制度，也许六年后（我在二○一八年退休）台积电的接班会不一样。当然，这也只是「也许」而已——世事变化无穷，非任何人能预料。

只是，我没有落实我起初想做的「轮流」制度。二○一二年正值台积电研发部门努力开发苹果需要的第一个制程——二十奈米，而二十奈米又是一个相当有挑战性的制程。把尚义调离研发后，二十奈米研发问题不断出现（其实这是新技术开发工作的本质），我似乎总不放心。算了，还是把尚义送回研发吧！尚义回原任，倒是德音和哲家互调了——德音管行銷及业务发展，哲家管制造。

二○一三年征询黄仁勋对台积电CEO职的兴趣

当然我相当熟悉公司内的人才，但是在公司外的，还有一个人，无论在品格、视野、半导体专业经验及知识……各种条件下，都值得考虑为台积电的接班人，我也应该跟他谈谈。

这人是Jensen Huang（黄仁勋）。二○一三年时，我已熟悉他十六七年。于是我问他，对台积电CEO职有无兴趣，如有兴趣，我们可以进一步讨论。

我花了大约十分钟时间对Jensen扼要地解释我对台积电的深切期许，也对他解释台积电CEO的报酬——虽没有台积电股票，但固定薪津以及依公司每年净利而订的花红，一定比他当时的收入为高。

Jensen似乎很有耐心地听了，但他没问问题。我讲完后，他也没直接拒绝我，只是简单地回答：「我已有工作。」

If the system of three rotating leaders across the three major domains had been fully implemented in 2012, perhaps TSMC's succession six years later—when I retired in 2018—would have been different. Of course, this is only a 'perhaps.' The course of events is infinite and cannot be predicted by anyone.

What I failed to implement was the 'rotation' system I had initially intended. In 2012, TSMC's R&D department was working hard to develop the first process node required by Apple—twenty nanometer—a quite challenging node. After transferring Sandi away from R&D, problems kept arising in the twenty-nanometer development (which is inherent to new technology development). I seemed never fully at ease. I decided, never mind, to send Sandi back to R&D. Sandi returned to his original post, while Tim and Morris swapped: Tim took over marketing and business development, and Morris took over manufacturing.

Of course I am quite familiar with the talents within the company. But there was one person outside the company, and under every condition—in character, vision, and expertise and knowledge in semiconductors—worth considering as a TSMC successor. I should also talk to him.

That person was Jensen Huang. By 2013 I had known him for sixteen or seventeen years. So I asked him whether he had any interest in the TSMC CEO position, and if so, we could discuss further.

I spent about ten minutes giving Jensen a concise explanation of my deep expectations for TSMC, and also explained the compensation for TSMC's CEO—although there were no TSMC shares, the fixed salary plus the annual bonus tied to company net profit would certainly exceed his then-current income.

Jensen seemed to listen patiently, but he did not ask any questions. When I finished, he did not directly refuse me either. He simply answered: 'I already have a job.'

过几个星期我再打电话问他，他还是同样的回答：「我已有工作。」在二○二四年的今天，当Jensen创办的辉达公司已是全球最高市值公司之一、Jensen个人也已是千亿美元富豪之时，读者或许以为我在二○一三年试图「高攀」了。其实，二○一三年底辉达的市值只是九十亿美元，而台积电的市值已是九百亿美元——辉达的十倍。Jensen在二○一三年的财富也只是辉达市值的百分之单位数而已。我没有「高攀」。

Jensen对我的回答倒是诚实的——他「已有工作」。他的工作就是在十一年后，把辉达提升到今天的辉达！

二○一三年蒋尚义退休

蒋尚义是一个非常聪明、有相当强的技术方向感，也有领导力的半导体研发人才。但是他也很敏感。他自一九九七年加入台积电时就是台积电的研发主管，也是一进台积电我就授以「技术领先」任务的研发主管，我非常敬重他。但是他在二○一六年蔡力行任CEO时就选择自台积电退休。我在二○一九年重兼CEO职，又在「一顿牛肉面」中把他找回来（见第三十二章）。二○一二年我任命了三位「共同营运长」，尚义也是其中之一，但我后来没有落实「三人轮调」制度，尚义显然有点失望——我想因为他原熟悉研发，被调去不甚熟悉的领域。

二○一三年蒋尚义感觉到我为了规划自己的退休，也许要做下一步的组织调整，而他可能不是下一步调整的主角，所以要求我在他满六十七岁退休前，不做任何改变组织的宣告。我也答应了。

尚义在二○一三年十月三十一日退休，我们给了他一个温馨的退休晚会。我也给了他一个「功在台积」的牌子——这是我用这个赞词的唯一一块牌子。

A few weeks later I called him again, and he gave the same answer: 'I already have a job.'

In 2024, when the company Jensen founded, NVIDIA, has become one of the world's most valuable companies and Jensen himself a billionaire worth hundreds of billions of dollars, readers may think I was attempting to 'reach above my station' in 2013. In fact, at the end of 2013 NVIDIA's market capitalization was only nine billion dollars, while TSMC's was already ninety billion—ten times NVIDIA's. Jensen's personal wealth in 2013 was only in the single-digit percentage range of NVIDIA's market cap. I was not reaching above my station.

Jensen was honest in his answer—he 'already had a job.' His job was to build NVIDIA into what it is today, eleven years later.

Sandi Jin was a very smart semiconductor R&D talent with strong technical direction sense and leadership. But he was also sensitive. He joined TSMC in 1997 as the head of R&D, and from the start I charged him with the mission of 'technology leadership.' I deeply respected him. But when Morris Cai became CEO in 2016, Sandi chose to retire from TSMC. I resumed the CEO role in 2019 and brought him back over 'a bowl of beef noodles' (see Chapter 32). In 2012 I had appointed three co-COOs, and Sandi was one of them, but I never implemented the 'three-person rotation' system. Sandi was evidently somewhat disappointed—I believe because he was originally familiar with R&D and was transferred to an unfamiliar domain.

In 2013 Sandi sensed that, in planning my own retirement, I might make further organizational adjustments, and that he might not be the central figure in the next round. He asked me not to announce any organizational changes before he reached the mandatory retirement age of sixty-seven. I agreed.

Sandi retired on October 31, 2013. We held a warm retirement dinner for him. I also presented him with a plaque inscribed 'Merit to TSMC'—the only plaque I have ever used that phrasing.

尚义退休后，我在十一月十二日宣布刘德音及魏哲家为台积电的共同CEO（Co-CEO）。刘、魏两位自二○○五年蔡力行时任CEO、各为先进技术事业组织及主流技术事业的资深副总经理后，一直都是台积电重要的经理人。

这个组织一直维持到二○一八年我退休。

决定退休（二○一七年）

我的退休决定倒是在二○一七年就做了。自二○一九年重在公司扮演积极角色，直至二○一七年我做退休决定时，台积电内部士气高昂，对外强劲发展——营收自二○一九年的一千零三十亿元成长至二○一七年的九千七百七十四亿元；营业净利自二○一九年的一千九百五十六亿元成长至二○一七年接近历史高档。

技术方面，这九年内台积电相继推出四十、二十八、二十、十六、十二、十奈米，在二○一七年也已准备在次年量产七奈米——这大大领先竞争者。同时在晶片封装技术方面，我们也推出了InFO及CoWoS——前者对智慧型手机重要，后者对人工智慧（AI）重要。

这九年也使我到了八十六岁。心想：人生无常，应该趁我还很健康的时候完全自台积电退休，去做些一直想做但却还没做的事：（一）写「自传下册」；（二）介绍给Sophie我中年在德仪时期常去也最喜欢的地方——巴黎及法国里维埃拉还有蒙地卡罗、瑞士、伦敦、义大利北部；（三）尽兴满足我自大学时代就有的嗜好——专业外的阅读、听古典音乐，以及「竞技桥牌」。

After Sandi's retirement, I announced on November 12 that Tim Liu and Morris Wei would serve as TSMC's co-CEOs. Since 2005, when Morris Cai was CEO and they each served as senior vice president in charge of the Advanced Technology Business and Mainstream Technology Business respectively, both Tim and Morris had been among TSMC's most important managers.

This organizational structure remained in place until I retired in 2018.

My retirement decision, however, had been made in 2017. From 2010, when I resumed an active role at the company, through to 2017 when I made my retirement decision, TSMC's internal morale was high and its external growth was strong. Revenue grew from 103 billion NT dollars in 2010 to 977.4 billion in 2017; operating profit grew from 195.6 billion in 2010 to near a historical high in 2017.

On the technology side, during these nine years TSMC sequentially launched forty, twenty-eight, twenty, sixteen, twelve, and ten nanometer nodes. By 2017 we were also preparing to mass-produce seven nanometer the following year—a head start that greatly outpaced our competitors. Meanwhile, in chip packaging technology, we launched InFO and CoWoS—the former critical for smartphones, the latter for artificial intelligence.

These nine years also brought me to the age of eighty-six. I reflected that life is impermanent, and I should take advantage of my continued good health to retire fully from TSMC and do the things I had always wanted to do but had not yet: (1) write the second volume of my autobiography; (2) introduce to Sophie the places I frequently visited and loved most during my years at TI—Paris, the French Riviera, Monaco, Switzerland, London, and northern Italy; (3) indulgently satisfy my hobbies from university days: reading outside my professional field, listening to classical music, and competitive bridge.

规划「双首长制」

许多欧美公司都采取「双首长制」。总裁（CEO）是公司的领导人；董事长领导董事会，监督总裁，而且因公司重要决定必须董事会通过，董事长也成为公司决策最后把关者。如果董事长及总裁两人能密切合作，两人都以公司利益放为最上，而把个人利益放在一边，「双首长制」应该是很好的制度。

以二○一七年台积电的特殊情形而言，两位「共同执行长」在位已四年，如今董事长要退休，可行的接班制度恐怕也只有「双首长制」，否则两人间必有一人离开公司。这又是我所不愿见的。

何况，两位「Co-CEO」在过去四年似乎合作得中满不错，这也给我相当信心：在双首长制下，他们也能为台积电前景继续合作。

在决定对董事会提议我的交棒计划前，我唯一咨询对象是副董事長曾繁城。他也完全认同我的想法。

交棒计划原文

（一）mc（我的英文名字缩写）将完成这任期董事長及董事职，而在二○一八年六月股东大会结束时完全自公司退休。

（二）二○一八年股东大会选出来新的董事会将选出公司「双首长」：刘德音为董事長，魏哲家为總裁。

（三）董事長及总裁将有同样职阶及待遇（包括薪酬及分红）。

**董事长的任务**（一）领导董事会。（二）公司对社会及政府的最高代表。（三）公司决策最后把关者。（四）全时工作。

nc建议：董事长应该继续主持「资本投资」会议，参加「订价会议」、「行销週」、「法说会」，而且应与总裁无缝双向沟通。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Many Western companies adopt a 'dual-leadership' system. The president and CEO is the company's operational leader; the chairman leads the board of directors, supervises the president, and because important company decisions require board approval, the chairman also becomes the final gatekeeper of corporate decisions. If the chairman and president can cooperate closely, each placing the company's interests above all and setting personal interests aside, the dual-leadership system should be an excellent arrangement.

In TSMC's special circumstances in 2017, the two co-CEOs had been in place for four years, and with the chairman about to retire, the viable succession system was恐怕 nothing other than dual leadership; otherwise one of the two would have to leave the company. That was something I was unwilling to see.

Moreover, the two co-CEOs had seemed to cooperate quite well over the past four years, which gave me considerable confidence that they could continue to work together for TSMC's future under the dual-leadership system.

Before deciding to propose my succession plan to the board, the only person I consulted was Vice Chairman Fan-Che Tseng. He fully agreed with my thinking.

(1) MC (the initials of my English name) would complete this term as chairman and director, and retire completely from the company at the conclusion of the June 2018 shareholders' meeting.

(2) The new board elected at the 2018 shareholders' meeting would select the company's 'dual leaders': Tim Liu as chairman, Morris Wei as president.

(3) The chairman and president would hold equal rank and compensation (including salary and dividends).

**Duties of the Chairman** (1) Lead the board of directors. (2) Serve as the company's highest representative to society and government. (3) Act as the final gatekeeper of company decisions. (4) Hold a full-time position.

I suggested that the chairman should continue to chair the 'capital investment' meetings, attend the 'pricing meetings,' 'Marketing Week,' and earnings calls, and maintain seamless two-way communication with the president.

**总裁的任务**（一）在董事会指导方针下，领导及经营公司，无论在战略面、营运面、行銷面或财务面。（二）对董事会报告，不对董事長报告。（三）全公司对总裁报告。

为了强调「双首长制」不是「董事長制」或「总裁制」，我刻意把两人的职阶及待遇画上等号，并且强调董事长是「全时」职，甚至建议董事长应该「主持」或「参加」我任董事长时颇为依赖的会议。

二○一七年七月二日，我召集德音、哲家两人，示以他们以上三文件，并征求他们的同意。两人都感到很兴奋，也无意见地同意。

二○一七年八月七、八日是董事会第三季会期。八月六日晚是我与独立董事的例行晚餐。由于我要讨论我拟定的交棒计划，我特地在晚餐前下午四时以书面提出。大家讨论相当热烈——除了五位独立董事，还有开发基金代表、曾繁城、刘德音及魏哲家。我也于九月二十八日亲自去开发基金向陈美伶说明，并得到她的同意。

二○一七年九月二十八日，我向董事会正式提出「交棒计划」、「董事长的任务」、「总裁的任务」三文件。最后对文字做了小小的修改后，获得全体在场董事一致通过。我也宣布下一届（二○一八年六月至二○二一年五月）董事提名名单：这一届十位董事中，除了我准备退休，另有一位独立董事因健康关系也拟退休，其余八位均提名连任。

换句话说，二○一八年六月的「交棒计划」可以说在二○一七年九月就已获这届及下届董事会同意，也获刘德音及魏哲家这两位接班人的热烈接受。

ReadShift 双语翻译

**Duties of the President** (1) Lead and operate the company under the board's strategic guidance, across strategy, operations, marketing, and finance. (2) Report to the board of directors, not to the chairman. (3) The entire company reports to the president.

To emphasize that the dual-leadership system was neither a 'chairman system' nor a 'president system,' I deliberately placed the two roles on equal footing in rank and compensation, and stressed that the chairmanship was a full-time position. I even suggested that the chairman should 'chair' or 'attend' the meetings on which I had relied heavily during my tenure as chairman.

On July 2, 2017, I convened Tim and Morris, showed them the three documents above, and sought their consent. Both were deeply excited and agreed without hesitation.

August 7–8, 2017, were the board's third-quarter meeting dates. On the evening of August 6, I had my regular dinner with the independent directors. Because I needed to discuss the succession plan I had drafted, I specifically submitted it in writing at 4 p.m. before dinner. The discussion was quite vigorous—besides the five independent directors, attendees included representatives of the Development Fund, Fan-Che Tseng, Tim Liu, and Morris Wei. I also visited the Development Fund in person on September 28 to explain the plan to Mei-ling Chen and received her agreement.

On September 28, 2017, I formally presented the board with three documents: the 'Succession Plan,' 'Duties of the Chairman,' and 'Duties of the President.' After minor textual revisions, the documents were approved unanimously by all directors present. I also announced the director nominations for the next term (June 2018 through May 2021): among the ten directors, besides myself preparing to retire and one independent director retiring for health reasons, the remaining eight were all nominated for re-election.

In other words, the June 2018 succession plan had, by September 2017, already received the approval of both the current and incoming boards, and had been enthusiastically accepted by the two successors, Tim Liu and Morris Wei.

台积电三十週年记

台积电在一九八七年成立，此后每十週年我们都会举行庆祝。二十週年、三十週年均邀请了全球重要客户、供应商以及有合作关係的伙伴一起来分享喜悦。

一九九七年十週年庆时，台积电虽已相当发达，但规模仍属中型，我们邀请了国内的交响曲演奏贝多《第九号交响曲》（合唱）。二○○七及二○一七年，台积电已是一个大规模的公司，我们分别邀请国际著名的乐团演奏贝多芬《第九号交响曲》（合唱）。我热爱这首交响曲，因为它既美丽又雄壮，而且需要八十人以上的大交响乐团及九十人以上的大合唱团才能有好的演出。每个十年庆祝日以此结束，正足以表达台积电的雄心壮志。

二○一七的三十年庆早已订在十月二十三日举行。既然在九月我们就定了次年的交棒计划，我就决定在「三十年庆」之前的十月初就将交棒计划公开宣布。这样做可以提早让伙伴更深认识我的接班人，也可以避免庆祝日后才宣布的可能困扰。

十月二日下午二时，我首先对台积电内部宣布「交棒计划」、「董事长的任务」以及「总裁的任务」；四时半召开记者会对外宣布。十月五、六日，我又分别接受包括日本《经济新闻》及美国彭博新闻社（Bloomberg News）在内的七个国内外媒体的专访。

ReadShift 双语翻译

TSMC was founded in 1987, and every ten years since then we have held a celebration. For the twentieth and thirtieth anniversaries, we invited important global customers, suppliers, and partner organizations to share in the joy.

For the tenth anniversary in 1997, TSMC was already quite prosperous but still a mid-scale company. We invited a domestic symphony orchestra to perform Beethoven's Ninth Symphony (with choir). In 2007 and 2017, TSMC had become a large-scale company, and we invited internationally renowned orchestras to perform Beethoven's Ninth Symphony (with choir). I love this symphony because it is both beautiful and majestic, and requires a full symphony orchestra of over eighty players and a choir of over ninety to deliver a fine performance. Ending each decade celebration with this work was a fitting expression of TSMC's ambition.

The 2017 thirtieth-anniversary celebration was already scheduled for October 23. Since we had finalized the succession plan for the following year in September, I decided to announce it publicly in early October, before the anniversary. This would allow partners to become better acquainted with my successor earlier, and avoid any possible complications arising from an announcement after the celebration.

On the afternoon of October 2, at 2 p.m., I first announced the succession plan, the duties of the chairman, and the duties of the president to TSMC's internal staff. At 4:30 p.m. I held a press conference to make the announcement publicly. On October 5 and 6, I gave interviews to seven domestic and international media outlets, including Japan's Nikkei and Bloomberg News.

十月二十三日是三十週年庆祝日。上午我分别与几位大客户谈我们的合作。由于我的退休早已不是新闻，我们可以如常讨论当前的问题——我很庆幸我们提早宣布交棒计划是对的。

下午座谈会与谈人有辉达、高通、博通、艾司摩尔（ASML）、亚德诺半导体、安谋（ARM）的总裁，以及苹果的营运长——内容相当精彩。

尤其令我欣慰的是晚上的音乐会。在中场休息、贝多芬第九号交响曲即将开始时，我破例地走上舞台，以英文对来宾说了一段退休的感言。说完后，首先几位大客户的总裁起立鼓掌；接着全体来宾都起立鼓掌，掌声如雷。对整个事业生涯都以客户为伙伴的我，他们的掌声真是莫大的回报！

退休

二○一七年十月我宣布我的退休及刘、魏的接班计划后，我对内、对外仍如常工作。二○一八年四、五月，公司内部有几场大规模的惜别会：新竹、台南、台中各办一场，每场都有数百到上千位同仁参加。行销单位同仁大部分来自国外，也趁他们四月在新竹的季会时期为我举办惜别晚会。

二○一八年六月五日的股东大会终于到临。我如计划在股东大会选出新届董事时退休；新一届的董事们也如先前计划选出刘德音为董事長、魏哲家为总裁，开始台积电的「双首长制」。

ReadShift 双语翻译

October 23 was the thirtieth-anniversary celebration. In the morning I met separately with several key customers to discuss our cooperation. Because my retirement was already no longer news, we could discuss current issues as usual. I was glad we had announced the succession plan early.

The afternoon symposium featured presidents from NVIDIA, Qualcomm, Broadcom, ASML, Analog Devices, ARM, and Apple's COO—the discussions were quite splendid.

What delighted me most was the evening concert. During the intermission, just before Beethoven's Ninth Symphony was about to begin, I broke with tradition and walked onto the stage to deliver a retirement address in English. After I finished, the presidents of several key customers rose to applaud first; then the entire audience rose to their feet, thunderous in their applause. For a career in which I regarded customers as partners above all, their applause was a magnificent reward.

After I announced my retirement and the succession plan for Liu and Wei in October 2017, I continued to work normally both internally and externally. In April and May 2018, the company held several large farewell gatherings: one each in Hsinchu, Tainan, and Taichung, each attended by hundreds to thousands of colleagues. Marketing staff, most of whom were based abroad, also took the opportunity of their April quarterly meeting in Hsinchu to host a farewell evening for me.

The shareholders' meeting on June 5, 2018, finally arrived. I retired as planned upon the election of the new board. The newly elected directors, as previously arranged, selected Tim Liu as chairman and Morris Wei as president, launching TSMC's dual-leadership system.

我在五月底就在新竹办公室及新竹家開始打包；办公室在六月五日让给新的董事長，新竹家是自己买的，但Sophie不等我退休就已售出了。

自二十四岁到八十七岁的六十三年事业生涯，就此结束。我原来没想工作那么久。在德仪时，我一心想在六十五岁退休。到台湾时五十四岁，仍想在六十五岁退休。但开始办台积电后，愈办愈成功，我的兴致和期待也愈来愈高，到后来简直是「欲罢不能」。

六十三年的职业生涯中，三年在希凡尼亚（一九五五至一九五八年），二十五年在德仪（一九五八至一九八三年），三十二年在台积电（一九八五至二○一八年，包含筹划及募资的两年）。六十三年几乎全部都在半导体业内；除了德仪的后期几年外，也几乎全部都是积极的、前进的。

我最成功的工作，明显地是我最后一个——台积电。台积电现在已是世界「必需」的公司，而且世界的「需要」——尤其在人工智慧方面——正快速地成长。台积电一定要紧紧追随这需求的成长；在成本方面，台积电也不能放松。

台积电的责任，已落在我的接班人肩膀上。我对他们寄予深切的期待、虔诚的祝福。

ReadShift 双语翻译

I had begun packing in my Hsinchu office and at our Hsinchu home as early as late May. The office was handed over to the new chairman on June 5. Our Hsinchu home had been purchased by me, but Sophie sold it before my retirement.

My sixty-three-year career, from age twenty-four to eighty-seven, thus came to an end. I had never intended to work so long. At TI, I had always hoped to retire at sixty-five. When I came to Taiwan at fifty-four, I still hoped to retire at sixty-five. But after founding TSMC, the more successful it became, the higher my enthusiasm and expectations rose, until eventually I simply could not bring myself to stop.

In my sixty-three-year career—three years at Sylvania (1955–1958), twenty-five at TI (1958–1983), and thirty-two at TSMC (1985–2018, including the two years of planning and fundraising)—almost all of it was in the semiconductor industry. Except for the later years at TI, it was almost entirely active and forward-moving.

My most successful undertaking was obviously my last one—TSMC. TSMC is now a 'must-have' company in the world, and the world's 'need'—especially in artificial intelligence—is growing rapidly. TSMC must closely follow this growth in demand, and it cannot relax on cost.

The responsibility for TSMC now rests on my successors' shoulders. I hold them in the deepest expectation and offer them my most sincere blessings.

ReadShift 双语翻译

**rebook-translation** **Planning for the Handover and Retirement** My succession planning began in 2005 with the release of the CEO role to Tsai Li-hsing while I remained chairman. But after difficulties led me to reclaim the CEO role in 2009, the succession path shifted. In 2012, I promoted three Co-COOs—Shang-yi Chiang, Liu De-yin, and Wei Che-chia—tasking them with rotating responsibility for R&D, manufacturing, and business development. When Chiang retired in 2013, Liu and Wei were named Co-CEOs.

ReadShift 双语翻译

In 2017, now eighty-six, I made my retirement decision. TSMC's operational and technological momentum was strong. I crafted a "dual-key" succession plan: Liu De-yin as chairman and Wei Che-chia as president, with equal rank and compensation. The board approved in September 2017, and in October I announced the plan publicly, culminating in a memorable thirtieth-anniversary celebration where, after my retirement remarks, the audience rose to their feet in thunderous applause—a tribute from the customers who had been my partners for decades.

On June 5, 2018, I retired. My sixty-three-year career in semiconductors—from Sylvania to Texas Instruments to TSMC—had come to an end. TSMC's burden now rested on my successors' shoulders.

**Cheat Sheet｜商业词汇**

| 词汇 | 英文 | 含义 |

| 交棒计划 | Succession Plan | 规画领导职位的传承 | | 共同营运长 | Co-Chief Operating Officer (Co-COO) | 共享运营职责的高阶主管 | | 双首长制 | Dual-Key / Two-Key System | 董事长与总裁权力对等的制度 | | 共同CEO | Co-CEO | 两位执行长共享最高经营权力 | | 功能 | Function | 公司内部的专业単位 | | 订价会议 | Pricing Meeting | 议定产品售价的会议 | | 行销週 | Marketing Week | 定期举行的行销策略检讨会 |

**背景知识延伸｜台积电的「双首长制」实验**

台积电在二○一八年实施的双首长制，在台湾大型企业中是开创性的实验。刘德音作为董事長主责董事会领导与外部代表；魏哲家作为总裁主责公司营运。两人权力对等、互不隶属——这种制度是否能长久运行，是台湾公司治理的重要观察指标。二○二四年刘德音退休、魏哲家独自接下董事長兼总裁后，「双首长制」功成身退。

**修辞赏析｜「欲罢不能」的张力**

张忠谋以「欲罢不能」来描述他成功后无法轻言退休的心态，这四个字恰到好处地呈现了企业创办人面对自己一手打造的公司时的矛盾——明明已经到了该退的时刻，但成功的滋味和持续的梦想让他无法放下。这与他对台积电的深厚情感一脉相承。

**修辞赏析｜「欲罢不能」的张力**

张忠谋以「欲罢不能」来描述他成功后无法轻言退休的心态，这四个字恰到好处地呈现了企业创办人面对自己一手打造的公司时的矛盾——明明已经到了该退的时刻，但成功的滋味和持续的梦想让他无法放下。这与他对台积电的深厚情感一脉相承。

后记：领导力与传承

交棒与退休，是每一位企业领导者最终的考验。张忠谋从二○○五年就开始规划，历时十三年，历经蔡力行的起伏、三位共同营运长的尝试、蒋尚义的黯然退场，最终找到了刘德音和魏哲家这一对「双首长」交出了自已手中三十二年的棒子。

交棒之所以困难，不仅在于找到能力合适的接班人，更在于创办人是否愿意真正「放手」。张忠谋在二○一二年一度想把蒋尚义调离研发，但自己先不放心——这段「调了又调回来」的小插曲，正是领导人「欲罢不能」心态的真实写照。最终他用「双首长制」完成了交棒，也为台湾企业的传承树立了一个先例。

Succession and retirement represent the final test for every business leader. Morris Chang began planning in 2005. Over thirteen years, through Morris Cai's setbacks, the experiment with three co-COOs, and Sandi Jin's quiet departure, he ultimately found in Tim Liu and Morris Wei a pair of 'dual leaders' to whom he could hand over the baton he had carried for thirty-two years.

Succession is difficult not only because of the challenge of finding a successor with adequate ability, but more so because of whether the founder is willing to truly 'let go.' In 2012, Morris Chang once tried to transfer Sandi Jin away from R&D, but could not bring himself to feel at ease—and this brief episode of 'transfer and then transfer back' is a true portrait of a leader's inability to let go. In the end, he accomplished succession through the dual-leadership system and set a precedent for corporate succession in Taiwan.

【注释】[1] 六十七岁是台积电规定的退休年龄，但董事不在此规定内。

# Morris Chang Chronology

## Early Years (1930–1955)

| 年 | 年龄 | 大事 |

|---|---|---|

| 一九三○年 | 出生 | 出生于浙江宁波 |

| 一九三二年 | 1岁 | 随父母迁南京 |

| 一九三六年 | 5岁 | 在南京入小学 |

| 一九三七年 | 6岁 | 抗日战争开始，随父母赴香港 |

| 一九四一年 | 10岁 | 珍珠港事变发生，日军占领香港 |

| 一九四二年 | 11岁 | 自小学毕业 |

| 一九四三年 | 12岁 | 随父母长途跋涉至重庆，入沙坪坝南开中学 |

| 一九四五年 | 14岁 | 抗战胜利，随父母赴上海 |

| 一九四八年 | 17岁 | 毕业于上海南洋模范中学。年底共军进占上海，随父母居香港 |

| 一九四九年 | 18岁 | 赴美国哈佛大学入大学一年级 |

| 一九五○年 | 19岁 | 转学麻省理工学院二年级 |

| 一九五二年 | 21岁 | 获麻省理工学院机械学士学位 |

**背景知识延伸｜张忠谋与APEC**

张忠谋在二○○六至二○二三年间七度担任台湾APEC经济领袖代表，创下纪录。他在国际场合以流利英语和对全球经济的深入理解，为台湾发声。这也是张忠谋从企业家转型为公众人物的标志——退休后的他，影响力不仅限于半导体产业，更延伸至国际外交场合。

**修辞赏析｜大事年表的叙事功能**

大事年表看似只是流水账，实际上是一种高效的叙事策略。通过时间线的铺排，读者可以快速掌握张忠谋一生的关键节点，形成完整的「英雄旅程」框架——从宁波少年到全球半导体教父。每一行大事记背后都是一段精彩的人生故事。

## Supplementary Notes

This chronology covers Morris Chang's important life milestones from birth through 2024. Each age-corresponding entry was originally recorded in traditional Chinese. In compiling this text, I preserved the format and content of the original records as closely as possible, making only corrections to typesetting and a few typographical errors.

The following points warrant special note:

1. The original text calculates age using the traditional East Asian reckoning system, in which a person is one year old at birth.

2. All Republic of China calendar dates in the original have been uniformly converted to the Common Era.

3. Some years have gaps in recorded events (such as the relatively sparse records from 1936 to 1940). These gaps reflect the state of the original source material.

4. The post-retirement APEC records in the original were sparse; supplementary entries here are based on publicly available information.

交棒后的台积电（二○一八至二○二四年）

张忠谋于二○一八年退休后，台积电在刘德音和魏哲家的「双首长制」领导下继续蓬勃发展：

- 二○一九：台积电领先全球量产七纳米强化版（7+） - 二○二○：台积电宣布投资约一百二十亿美元在美国亚利桑那州设立先进晶圆厂- 二○二一：台积电与日本索尼合资在熊本县设立晶圆厂（JASM） - 二○二二：台积电领先全球量产三纳米- 二○二四：刘德音宣布退休，魏哲家接任董事長兼总裁，台积电进入「单一首长制」张忠谋在自传下冊二○二四年记中写道：看到台积电在接班人领导下屡创高峰，是他最大的安慰。

## TSMC After the Succession (2018–2024)

After Morris Chang retired in 2018, TSMC continued to flourish under the dual-leadership of Tim Liu and Morris Wei:

- 2019: TSMC led the industry in mass-producing enhanced seven-nanometer (7+) technology

- 2020: TSMC announced an investment of approximately twelve billion dollars to build an advanced fab in Arizona, USA

- 2021: TSMC and Japan's Sony established a joint-venture fab in Kumamoto Prefecture (JASM)

- 2022: TSMC led the industry in mass-producing three-nanometer technology

- 2024: Tim Liu announced his retirement; Morris Wei succeeded him as both chairman and president, and TSMC entered a single-leadership system

In the second volume of his autobiography, written in 2024, Morris Chang wrote: seeing TSMC reach new heights under the leadership of his successors was his greatest comfort.

结语

「滚滚新世纪」已进入第五个年头。从二○二○年代的AI浪潮到地缘政治的风云变幻，台积电站在历史的十字路口。

张忠谋在二○一八年交棒时说：台积电的「需要」在快速成长。五年后，这句话得到了超乎预期的验证——生成式AI对先进制程的需求，让台积电成为全球科技产业最重要的战略资源。

从一九三五到二○二四，台积电从一个政府主导的「政策工具」，蜕变为全球不可或缺的「技术平台」。张忠谋用三十年时间，缔造了一个真正的世界级企业。

「自传下冊」——关于理想、关于坚持、关于创新与传承的故事，至此划下句号。

## Epilogue

The 'rolling new century' has entered its fifth year. From the AI wave of the 2020s to the shifting winds of geopolitics, TSMC stands at a historical crossroads.

When Morris Chang handed over the baton in 2018, he said TSMC's 'need' was growing rapidly. Five years later, that statement has been validated beyond expectation—generative AI's demand for advanced process nodes has made TSMC the most critical strategic asset in the global technology industry.

From 1987 to 2024, TSMC transformed from a government-directed 'policy tool' into a globally indispensable 'technology platform.' Morris Chang spent thirty years building a genuine world-class enterprise.

The 'Autobiography, Volume II'—a story about ideals, perseverance, innovation, and succession—comes to its close here.

（全文完）

In May 2009, when the global economy was just emerging from the financial crisis, I had a dialogue with Nobel economics laureate Paul Krugman. Krugman said he was cautiously optimistic about the short-term outlook, quite pessimistic about the medium term, but very optimistic about the long term of fifteen to twenty years out. At that time, Krugman's "long term" would find me in my nineties, so I couldn't help but quote another famous economist, John Maynard Keynes: "In the long run, we are all dead." The audience burst into laughter. (Business Weekly)

2014年4月母校史丹福大学选我为"工程英雄"之一，并邀请我演讲。斯坦福校长（中）除亲自主持外，还请同为校友又是我的好友黄仁生来介绍我。

ReadShift 双语翻译

In November 2013, NTU President Yang Yang-chi visited. I still recall Father visiting a friend's home and seeing a scroll reading "Five sons, four PhDs." Upon returning home, Father said he too could write "One son, one PhD," to which Mother replied: "That's a bit weak." Had my parents still been alive today, it could be written as "One son, nine PhDs," and Mother would probably stop saying "That's a bit weak." Alas, they are both gone — too late. (CNA)

In April 2014, my alma mater Stanford selected me as one of its "Engineering Heroes" and invited me to speak. The Stanford president (center) not only hosted personally but also invited fellow alumnus and my good friend Jensen Huang to introduce me.

修辞赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

"一子九博士"故事中母亲的"比较弱了"令人莞尔，而后"太晚了"陡然转折，从幽默变为遗憾，情感落差令人动容。

随着《二十一世纪资本论》在全球热销，作者法国皮凯提来台聚焦于"成长与公平"的论坛演讲。我认为皮凯提不通，因为资本会衔跑。（联合报系提供、人承轮摄影）

2013年5月美国前联准会主席柏南奇来台访问，我与他对谈。柏南奇少年时家境不攻好，与美国做大学生时相似，但是我们两人后来都实现了"美国梦"。我问他："现在美国梦还有可能实现吗？"他回答："还是可能，但我们那时部了。"（《商业周刊》提供）

ReadShift 双语翻译

Following the global bestseller "Capital in the Twenty-First Century," author Thomas Piketty visited Taiwan to speak at a forum on "Growth and Equity." I believe Piketty misses the point, because capital runs away. (UDN, photographer Ren Cheng-lun)

In May 2013, former Fed Chairman Ben Bernanke visited Taiwan for a dialogue with me. Bernanke came from a modest background in his youth, similar to my college days in the U.S., yet we both achieved the "American Dream." I asked him: "Is the American Dream still achievable?" He replied: "It's still possible, but harder than in our day." (Business Weekly)

修辞赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

"资本会衔跑"简洁地表达了资本流动性对分配正义的消解作用，与皮凯提观点形成直接交锋。

2015年4月民进党主席蔡英文以总统候选人身份展开"希记台积电"。（联合报系提供）

Sophie和我捐了这座大楼给MIT。Morris and Sophie Chang Building现在是MIT经济系的家。经济系很厚爱我，送我大楼照片，附六位得诺贝尔奖的现任教授的名片。MIT经济系竟有六位现任教授曾获诺贝尔经济学奖，实为罕见。

ReadShift 双语翻译

In April 2015, DPP Chairperson Tsai Ing-wen, as presidential candidate, began her "visiting TSMC" campaign trail. (UDN)

Sophie and I donated this building to MIT. The Morris and Sophie Chang Building is now home to MIT's Economics department. The department was kind enough to send me a photo of the building along with business cards of six current professors who have won Nobel Prizes. MIT's Economics Department having six current Nobel laureates on faculty is truly rare.

2017年9月我在台积电介绍订户整骨规画。次年10月南京记怖利量产，开启了中国大陆16奈米半罕骨制程新纪元。

2017年10月我在公司举行记者会，宣布将于次年6月股东大会后退休。届时，台积电将由董事长张德音（右）、总经理白家（左）两人平行领导人。（《商业周刊》提供）

ReadShift 双语翻译

In September 2017, I presented TSMC's customer planning at an investor conference. In October of the following year, Nanjing operations began mass production, inaugurating a new era of 16nm semiconductor manufacturing in mainland China.

In October 2017, I held a press conference announcing my retirement following the shareholders meeting the coming June. Going forward, TSMC would be led jointly by Chairman Chang De-yin (right) and CEO Pai Chia (left). (Business Weekly)

修辞赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

两次宣布——一次是事业扩张，一次是个人退休——形成强烈的戏剧张力。

一年一度的台积电运动会，都是我最兴奋的一天。我看到台积同仁高昂的士气、团队精神和运动员精神，我就更为深深地相信，我们台积电一定会成功！

2017年1月我主持了退休前的最后一次运动会。我向同仁们宣布台积电成立于1987年，当年底全公司只有238位同仁，令人珍惜的十年后仍有24位在职、其中一位就是我。我很高兴颁发"三十年年资服务奖"给这些同仁。

ReadShift 双语翻译

TSMC's annual sports day has always been my most exciting day of the year. Seeing TSMC employees' high morale, teamwork, and sportsmanship, I become even more deeply convinced that TSMC will succeed!

In January 2017, I presided over my final sports day before retirement. I announced that TSMC was founded in 1987, and at year's end, the company had only 238 employees. Ten years later, 24 of them remained — including me. It was my pleasure to present "30-Year Service Awards" to these colleagues.

修辞赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

"最令人珍惜的十年"点出十年是一段漫长而珍贵的岁月，从238人到24人的变化，既诉说了创业的艰辛，也体现了张忠谋对长期坚持的敬意。

米勒的著作《芯片战争》于2022年出版，广受各界注目，他在书中说我的人生故事反映了整个半导体产业的发展。2023年3月我（左）与米勒（右）在台北对谈，我说自己是征战半导体的沙场老兵。阅读《芯片战争》无异是一场怀旧之旅，书中的主要战士我都认得。（中央社提供）

Reading "Chip War" was like a nostalgic journey — I knew almost all the main fighters in the book. (CNA)
